We pay $20 extra for utilities (water, sewage and trash, I think). The office staff is really nice! Maintenance comes the first time you call to put a work order in (it may take them a couple days to get to you depending on how many people have called before you). Nice carpet, nice floor plans, comes with full washer and dryer, fridge has an ice maker, lots of windows, fireplace, nice neighbors, and a convenient location (near Meijer on Southport Road). They have recycling bins for plastic, metal, and glass. Cons: I had to find a temporary new home for my cat because the pet fee here is outrageous. They charge $350 up front and $20 per month for cats. (Not sure what they charge for dogs). Also, if I did bring my cat, there is no good place to put the litter box. The fitness center is lacking, but not the worst I've seen. There are 3 treadmills (but one is broken), a recumbent bike, an elliptical machine, and several weight machines. There is also an outdoor pool, sand volleyball, tennis, and basketball courts. The kitchen is small with very little counter space.

text: A Restaurant Week Review: *Note: online RW menu isn't reliable* I so badly wanted to give Smokin' Betty's 5 stars! But I couldn't... As phenomenal as their BBQ was, two things kinda bugged me: 1) We were seated fairly close to the bar on the 2nd floor. It was pretty full, and quite loud. If you have the chance, ask your waitress for a table further from the bar. 2) The womens bathroom on the 2nd floor... absolutely disgusting. Not only were 1/3 of the stalls "Out of Order", the working ones were really dirty and one lacked toilet paper. Hopefully they'll clean it up soon! On the more yummy sides of things, Smokin' Betty's offered us the best Restaurant Week experience we've had yet. And possibly some of the BEST BBQ in the Center City area... Service - Our waiter was so sweet and attentive. The best service I've had in a loooong time. Thanks guys! Drinks - Good, yet selective beer selection. - Fun, refreshing cocktails (try the Raspberry Lemonade Cocktail). First Course - Cheesesteak Springroll: I was skeptical at first, but WOW. The spicy ketchup that they offer for dipping is realllly good too. Any cheesesteak buff has to try these. And the best part... they're 1/2 off during their happy hour! - BBQ Sliders: YUM. The carolina pulled pork had an amazing mesquite zest; just the best kind of "spicy." My favorite, hickory smoked beef brisket, had a sweet and tangy BBQ flavor. Then the caribbean pulled chicken, though tasty, lacked the kind of awesome flavor the other two had. But all of them were cooked to yummy, tender perfection... Second Course - Soup of the Day, Portobello Mushroom & Sage: When we walked up to Smokin' Betty's I noticed this special on their board outside. I absolutely love mushroom soup, I got so excited! Rich, creamy, loads of mushrooms :)This was, hands down, the best mushroom soup I've EVER had. For a soup of the day at a BBQ joint, I was very impressed... - Mixed Green Salad: Tasty, crisp salad. But the balsamic vinaigrette it was served with was WAY over-powering on the bitter factor! Some people like their vinaigrette that way, but definitely not me. Third Course - Hickory Smoked St. Louis Ribs: I don't even know what to say or where to begin... These BBQ ribs were jaw dropping-ly, UHmazing. Again, I got my favorite of the BBQ sauces (sweet and tangy, hickory smoked BBQ goodness). But the even better part... the juicy, tender meat pulled right off the bone *insert Homer's drool here.* I'm just gonna leave it at that. The ribs were served with two sides, like most of the entree items, we got asparagus (perfectly cooked with a nice crunch) and... MAC & CHEESE*!! Fourth Course - Triple Chocolate Layer Cake Typical chocolate mousse and ganache cake. Nothing special. If you really want a treat, go with the... - Chocolate Mousse served w/ mixed berries I prefer my mousse to be light and fluffy. But Betty's thick mousse was still insanely YUMMY. The strawberries, raspberries, and black berries were key :) Overall Smokin' Betty's Restaurant Week menu, offered an extremely tasty selection with hearty portions, for that price we all love... $35. I'm super excited to come back and try some more of their menu items!! *Mac & Cheese: But before we get too excited, I have to admit... I was kind of disappointed. So here's the scoop... I learned that Smokin' Betty's is owned by the same guy who owns Devil's Alley (I knew their mac & cheese tasted familiar... I'm not a fan of Devil's Alley's mac & cheese either). The noodles are always over cooked to me (I prefer the more al dente kind) and the cheese sauce, though nice and thick, has a kind of gritty texture. Then instead of a tomato jam on-top, there were bread crumbs with a hint of garlic flavor to them (which was the best part of this mac & cheese). Though it has potential, I wasn't a fan...
label: POS

text: Another great spot to go when you're visiting Tucson and want to see some of the beauty the desert has to offer. Though actually, Sabino canyon is more oasis than desert, the highlight being the stream (almost a river) lined by huge boulders, cottonwoods, ash, oaks and willows. The narrow, cement road through the canyon was built in the 1930's as a dam access road, but thankfully the dam was never built, and the whole area later became a protected park. Now it is only accessible by a light tram (running every half hour) or on foot. On our visit here with our extended family we chose to take the tram to the turnaround at the top of the canyon and walk down with the kids, who took frequent side trips to the stream to explore, climb the rocks, and stick their toes in the sand. Of course, part of me worried about them turning an ankle or falling in one of the many deep, icy-cold pools. Happily there were no mishaps and I was able to control my protective instincts and let them have fun. We were a bit sad that we had failed to bring snacks, and that the visitor center below failed to stock any kid-friendly ones as well. So, make sure to bring snacks of your own if you plan to spend more than a few hours in the canyon. If I ever visit Tucson again sans kids then this would be a great place to hike the day away, starting early by hiking up Sabino canyon (about 3.5 miles) and returning via Bear canyon (anouther 4-5 miles)

text: We were on our way to another Mexican Restaurant and thought we'd give this place a try instead because it was closer. We should have kept driving. We were seated quickly and given menus. I'm always suspicious of places that have pictures of the food in their menus and this place reinforced that again. The waiters were friendly and attentive and service was good The chips are mass produced and some store bought brands are better than what was served. The salsa was the consistency of tomato soup and definitely not memorable. I ordered the carnitas which turned out to be 1/4" slices of a pork roast and judging from the taste it had been precooked a few days in advance and then rewarmed in a pan. Real carnitas are served in chunks and are fresh and don't have a rewarmed taste. The accompanying rice was bland but flaky. The refried beans were on the soupy side and not memorable. The guacamole was no more than a teaspoon full, bland, l and it was served on a bit of shredded lettuce to make it seem like more. Considering it is specially mentioned on the menu I would expect a bit more. I ordered corn tortillas and they were just reheated out of the bag and served in a plastic tortilla warmer. Definitely mass produced and not good quality I got the impression that they were skimping on portions and quality of ingredients in comparison to other restaurants in town. My companions ordered fish tacos and a tamales. Neither were terrible with the fish getting good marks for the seasoning. One of my companions ordered a margarita. I was surprised when the waiter didn't even ask if my companion wanted it blended and with salt on the rim. The drink really had not noticeable alcohol and was served in an uncharacteristic hurricane style glass. Overall, there are much better restaurants in Sparks and Reno. This place will probably survive because there isn't much else available near its location. Next time I'll drive 5 more minutes.

text: We went to Catahoula on Saturday, since it seems to be Yelp's new spot of the moment and I've heard mostly good things in reviews. Unfortunately, my experience was undesirable. There was also a hair in it. Personally, I'm not one to cause a commotion over stuff like that, especially in an empty bar/restaurant, I just figure I'll put it all into my review. Needless to say, it was gross. Per the server's recommendation, I ordered the oyster po' boy and Mike got "their" burger. He enjoyed his burger for the most part, although it was a little heavy on the goat cheese, but the accoutrement was mostly good. He ordered it medium and said when he took a bite of the burger itself it tasted a little like a McDonald's burger. I haven't had a burger in so long, I don't really remember what they should taste like, but I do have a vague memory of the flavor of a McDonald's patty in my brain and it's delicious. So whether or not this is a negative or a positive is for you to decide, reader. My oyster po' boy was kind of a crisis. It started off good. The fries were tasty, the roll was soft, the lettuce was shredded just right, the first oyster was crispy but soft and not wet, the remoulade tasted authentic. Enjoyable. Then I took a bite into the second oyster. I'm not sure if it was a bad oyster, undercooked/underfried, or I just don't have an appreciation for true oyster flavor, but it erupted with putrid juice and I wanted to throw up. I took a few more bites of bread but the sandwich was soaking wet and had to stop. I felt queasy all the way back to the car. Mike had to drive. He took me for my favorite food (Capogiro) and a walk around Northern Liberties and I felt better. The prices were fair, the server was hard to hear, but friendly, the location and ambiance are pleasant, the TVs are HD and the menu seems decent. Maybe our experience just wasn't the best, but I probably won't go back.

text: We decided to visit Chinatown on a Sunday to find some breakfast. There were not many choices for breakfast in the Reading Terminal Market. We walked into KC's Pastries and picked the peanut butter with mochi bread, coconut pineapple bread and a slice of mocha roll. The bread was soft and not overly sweet, better than some of the bakeries in Taipei and better than any of the Asian pastry shops I tried in the DC area. For 80 cents each, the bread was a bargain. In the DC area, it would cost anywhere from $1.10 to $1.65 each. There was a lot of mochi/coconut inside of the bread. The pineapple crust on top of the bread was really delicious, too. The mocha roll was very disappointing. It did not have any coffee taste, not sweet at all and there was too much cream. Since the cream had no taste, it tasted a bit like soften butter (in a bad way). We went back and bought six more bread (3 sweet and 3 savory). We loved the sweet buns but did not care for any of the savory ones (we got staty beef, roasted pork, curry chicken). The bubble tea seemed very popular here, but I didn't get a chance to try.
label: POS

text: I have to agree with everyone about Frank -- it's hard not to get a great first impression when this guy is so nice and hilarious. We stayed here for New Years and were very satisfied with the experience. Pros * Great location. East Beach is great for volleyball and lounging. Also right along waterfront shuttle stops. *Cute retro boutique hotel. Stands out from cookie cutter white behemoths in the area. *Updated rooms with modern fixtures, good water pressure, and quality TVs. Wireless internet was adequate. *Great prices available through Trip Advisor. Cons *Cramped feel if you plan on hanging out at hotel -- Tiny pool area with rooms practically on top of lounge chairs. *Rooms are not noise proof. We had a small child next door that you could hear when crying. *Not within walking distance of bars or State Street. Still a short cab ride -- we had no issues. Also, try eating at the Cabrillo Beach/Bath House across the street along the beach. They have the best blueberry and banana pancakes. Yum!

text: My family and I went to this restaurant/take-out place, where it appeared slightly dirty... but first impressions usually aren't completely right. For New Orleans standards, this place was well kept up, and the food was pretty good. The shrimp & oyster po-boy was really good... so good I ate it in about a minute. We also tried the gumbo and red bean & rice combination, and both are good choices, with the gumbo being mildly spicy and the red bean for those who like a more Asian flavor.. The only problem was that the gumbo was lacking considerable amounts of seafood (only a few shrimps to be found in the quart-size container, the rest was sausages and onions), which seemed to me a cost-cutting measure. Overall, not bad though... the flavor was more than enough to win me over :) They also gave us a few garlic bread pieces.. which I presumed went with the gumbo. This place also offers Chinese food, so those who want even more Asian food can go to this place. The combination plate w/ broccoli was okay.. not great, but not bad either. The fried rice on the other hand, was a bit stale. Good effort on the Chinese food, but I think that area could use some work :)

text: Super nice new digs on the West Bank for desserts and breakfast! The new building complex is huge and gorgeous and super spacious!!! I love the fact that parking is behind the building so the experience is slow-paced and relaxed, none of that hustle and bustle! Parrot Pete's is really nice inside, great tables all spaced adequately with those Carribean-esque wicker chairs. the magazines on display are for purchase, no reading! So definitely not a Barnes and Nobles experience. The layout is a bit confusing though. When you enter, head straight and you will hit a dessert case. Turn right to purchase your icecreams/milkshakes. But more than likely you will get dessert and a cup of joe. Coffee here...$2!!! It's a good brew, although a bit watery for my tastes. Had the berry cake...it was delicious! Yellow cake w/ a whipped topping with blueberries and strawberries..it was moist and absolutely delicious - not sweet at all! love it...friend had lemon bar..it was okay. fountain drinks - $2.00!!! my gosh! they totally get you on drinks! The prices for the desserts are a bit steep - a mini wedding cake was $6.00!!! A slice of cake - $5.00!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! My goodness! Breakfast here starts @ 8.00....lunch will definitely run you at least $15! But the environment is relaxed and the workers seem to be so happy. Haven't tried foods yet, but the specialty at Parrot Pete's is the Kitchen Sink...a huge icecream sundae meant for sharing w/ lots of folks, served in a huge bowl w/ a "faucet" and "taps". ...the kids faces totally lit up - very cute..up to the point they got their sugar rush and put their mouths on everything (eww). I'd be back here for brunch..it's nice, it's clean, the workers/cooks seem genuinely happy...that's always a plus! Not sure if there is WI-FI available..but a few folks had laptops out...

text: Love theatre? Want to see great talent? Want to sit comfortably during the show? Don't want to pay an arm and a leg? Don't want to swelter in the summer heat of the Muny? Stages is your answer. Saw last night's production of "The Drowsy Chaperone" and was absolutely blown away!! Let me start by saying I'm a huge theatre snob. Especially when it comes to musicals. I know what I like and I like shows as they're done on Broadway with the best talent. Not only did Stages meet my expectations, but it blew them out of the water!! The theatre was a good size. Large enough to accommodate a large audience, but still small enough that you get the intimate theatre experience like I love about Broadway. On top of that, the space between the seats is large enough that you have room to comfortably sit without your knees hitting the back of the chairs in front of you. Affordable tickets are another huge plus. The talent was definitely equal to any of the casts that come through the Fox, but three of us went for what it would normally cost for one to go see something at the Fox. I left the theatre with a huge smile on my face with that feeling that only comes with having seen a great piece of theatre. (Plus, it was out in time to grab custard at The Custard Station!) I would absolutely return to see just about any show that Stages does.

text: Last Sunday I arrived into Philadelphia 3 hours late due to a flight delay. I stood at the curb waiting for the Budget shuttle, no less than 15 minutes while all the other car rental companies came by multiple times. When I arrived to the rental office, only one clerk was working and there was a line. Again, I waited. I presented my reservation to the clerk and reminded her that my company had authorized payment to their corporate credit card and that my personal card should not be authorized. She did not have that information - apparently their District Manager did not input the information into the system. So I presented my MC debit card. Oh no, they don't accept debit cards. Well, if District Manager would have done his job, it wouldn't have been an issue. She authorized the rental and in another 15 minutes I was on my way. On Monday morning I contacted my corporate office who contacted the District Manager who again said that he would straighten it out and make sure that my account was not charged. My corporate office faxed him the credit card information, the signature authorization, and confirmed with him that he received everything. Fast forward to Friday - I return the car and guess who's account was charged? Mine! The same clerk was there at the counter and with the same blank look said the information wasn't in the system and the District Manager had done nothing and was not there. I DON'T CARE IF THEY ARE CHEAPER - THEIR CUSTOMER SERVICE IS AWFUL AND I WOULD NEVER (NOR WOULD MY COMPANY) EVER RENT FROM THEM AGAIN!!! Beware - they're unprofessional and unreliable, oh and WATCH OUT FOR THEIR INSURANCE FEE'S should you elect to opt for insurance - they were more than the actual daily rent of the car.

text: Doobie's is BY FAR my absolute favorite bar in Philadelphia. I'm there at least once a week with my co-workers and honestly don't plan on changing that trend. I really don't have anything to complain about. I probably should start off by saying that Doobie's is a dive. It's dark, kitschy, has Christmas lights up year-round, and the bathroom doors are notorious for lots of graffiti (Check out the KCL = 3 Lushkateers tag in the ladies bathroom...that's right, I did that). But honestly, it's the bar that I always hoped I'd find. I walk in there and I'm guarenteed to know or recognize at least 3 people because everyone there is so friendly. The wait staff is also really nice and a few of them I've come to consider friends as opposed to just people I see out. By the way, check out the box of board games they keep by the back door. It contains the majority of games from you childhood and, while that may not sound fun to some, drunken games of Scrabble or Life are basically the best 45 minutes to an hour spent. The jukebox is also pretty good. It's one of those rare jukes that doesn't download the music from the internet and contains gems such as The Pixies, Tom Waites, and Ella Fitzgerald. In terms of food and beverages, it's on par. The really nice thing about Doobie's is that they definitely cater to vegetarians. I was honestly surprised to see the amount of vegan food they serve on both their regular menu and their specials menu. Some of it is kind of bland, but when you're hammered and the drunchies kick in then it's exactly what you need. They also have a pretty decent beer selection and offer pitchers, something that can be rare these days. They won't empty your wallet but be warned - it's cash only. I highly recommend this place to everyone. It may not look like much at first but I promise you that it's great. Also - if you're there Sunday nights then come say hi. I'm the huge nerd playing Scrabble :D
label: POS

It appears to be exhibitions-only with no permanent exhibits. This makes it hit or miss and the 3 artists on view today were a miss for me. All of the bands we have seen there have been top-notch (The Big Package Band and the The Mandells Band were both notable). text: While home for Thanksgiving, my mom suggested we get dinner one night at Avalon. I had never been there before, but was interested in trying somewhere new. My mom and I arrived a few minutes early and waited for my sister to arrive. It was almost empty at 5:50pm on a Sunday, but was pretty busy by the time we left. The restaurant was already tastefully decorated for Christmas, even though it was only 3 days after Thanksgiving. They had a fireplace going, and the restaurant was very cozy. It is a BYOB, so our waiter came over and opened our wine bottles for us ($2 corkage fee per bottle) and put our white wine on ice. I took a few minutes to study the delicious-sounding but slightly confusing menu. The waiter did come over after my sister arrived and asked us if we wanted him to explain the menu, so that was a nice touch. Also, based on the other reviews on Yelp, it looks like at least part of their menu changes seasonally. When my sister arrived, they brought out complimentary aperitifs- yummy sangria. My mom ordered the caesar salad and some kind of meaty ravioli (they came back later to tell her it was now being served over papardelle, which she said was okay). I ordered the arancinni and the ricotta gnocchi. My sister ordered the bruschetta and the gnocchi as well. The appetizers ran about $8-10 and the entrees ran about $17-27. The arancini was amazing. It was basically fried risotto balls with short ribs and gorgonzola in a red sauce. It looked like meatballs on my plate, but tasted like heaven! My sister's bruschetta was amazing as well- it had mushroom ragu and truffled ricotta. My mom really liked her caesar salad as well. My mom's pasta arrived and it was HUGE. There was basically just piles of meat on top of pasta. We all tasted it and liked it, and she ended up taking half of it home for dinner the next night! The gnocchi was interesting. It is served with little squares of spiced butternut squash and brown butter. When eating a gnocchi alone, it was a bit bland, but when eating it with a few of the butternut squash squares, it was the perfect combination. The serving looked small, but was quite rich- my sister and I struggled to finish our plates (but of course, we did!). For dessert, my sister ordered the crepes and my mom and I shared a cheese plate. The crepes were small (not a sharing dessert if you're still hungry!) and my sister inhaled them in about 3 minutes, so I'm guessing they were good :-). For the cheese plate, you could choose from about 10-11 cheeses and 5 or 6 meats. For 3 cheeses, it was $17, and for 5 cheeses, $25. My mom and I chose the Reggiano, Queso Leonora and the Sottocenere. The Queso Lenora was a bit stinky for my mom's taste (I liked it), but we both loved the Reggiano. The Sottocenere is one that you have to try- it is cow's milk with some truffles inside. The kitchen also drizzled a bit of honey over it. The cheese came on a cute cheese board with some aged balsamic vinegar and a fruit (cherry?) spread. I'd highly suggest the cheese plate if you come here to eat. The service was perfect- not intrusive or rushed, but not MIA either. The restaurant is cash only, which is a fairly big minus for me. My mother said they used to have an ATM by the door, but they don't anymore- so come with plenty of cash. But the extra trip to the bank is definitely worth it- the ambiance was cozy and the food was delicious!!
label: POS

I was a little confused whether there was a difference between what they call "pita bread" versus "naan" -- it seemed the same to me -- but it was tasty, so I'm not complaining. We had a nice Greek red wine with our appetizer plate and dinner. The dining room manager came to our table to open the bottle of wine. I was a bit surprised to hear him say "ya'll" and I mentioned this -- he graciously told me that he's originally from Texas. He told us a bit about the start up of the restaurant and some improvements they have made. All of the wait staff we encountered were friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable. For entrees, I ordered the koobedeh (beef & lamb mixture) kabab plate, which came with rice and roasted veggies (yellow squash, onion, tomato, red pepper, and asparagus). Hubby ordered the beef fillet entree. Both entrees tasted great. The filet was very tender with a good seasoning. I wish they gave us more roasted veggies and less rice -- next time I'll make that request. The place had a nice ambiance. The decor had a rich and warm feel. Our only gripe was the itsy bitsy table at which we were seated. Next time I'll request a larger table. Overall, great experience. We will be back. text: It's no secret that the S&H Kebab House, on P'Unk just off South St., has opened to rave reviews for the grilled skewers & all around well-done Turkish food. It was a gorgeous summer day when we decided to have lunch at S&H...the part of P'Unk isn't heavily traveled, so you can actually enjoy your meal w/o the car exhaust. Plus, for $8 you get plenty of satisfying food...both a platter and an accompanying salad or appetizer. We started with the Tabbouleh salad & the Haydari, a dip made with yogurt, garlic, dill and walnut pieces. The Tabbouleh was well seasoned and full of veggies...diced red pepper, scallions, tomato & parsley. The Haydari, slathered over warmed pita slices, was addictive...the yogurt+dill is a familiar flavor, but the walnut pieces gave the spread a pleasing bite. The main attraction for us was the news that the lamb kebabs were char-grilled...here's a close-up of the Sis Kebap, marinated lamb cubes. Each platter came with grilled pepppers & tomato, two kinds of rice( a spiced short-grain rice and a buttery medium grain) and a slaw of cabbage & carrot. The lamb Doner combines hearty char-grilled lamb flavor in delicately sliced portions. The balance of marinated meat flavors and accompanying veg made for a great summer lunch. Although the desserts looked just as summer-ready, we were stuffed. As we lunched, passers-by commented to one another about S&H, either pointing out that they had eaten there or needed to drop in soon.

text: Most places have to REALLY piss me off to earn a one-star review. Mind you, diBruno's has NOT really pissed me off, they just do *so* many things in piss-poor fashion. I found myself subtracting a star for this, a star for that, and finally I'm just left realizing I do not like this place at all, for the sum of its mismanaged parts, and I have no more stars to give. One and a half stars lost for my putting $1 in your tip jar, and then finding out you did not prepare my bagel for me. Butter packets, a flimsy knife (not conducive to spreading ice cold butter at ALL) and a bagel in a bag? Uhm, why did I put a dollar in your tip jar for a $1.25 bagel??? I specifically buy bagels out rather than prepare them in my home for this convenience alone. I have an aversion to getting my hands all greasy preparing a bagel while I'm trying to shoulder my bags and not have my scarf swoop through messy foil butter packets. Butter my damn bagel, please!!! Another 1.5 star removal for pre-prepared sandwiches. Bread gets soggy, OK? And I like stuff freshly prepared, especially if I'm paying diBruno prices for it. I specifically ordered my caprese sandwich on sesame bread because I saw that combination was not in the pre-prepared sad stack. They merely took (wasted) one of the pre-prepared sandwiches, moved its fillings to the sesame bread, grilled it (aaaah! I didn't want it heated!) and handed it to me. Other times I've asked if they can prepare one fresh, and they look at me like I have two heads before telling me they don't have mozz to do that with. Uhm, hello, you are an Italian cheese shop. You don't have a ball of fresh mozz in the place?! The sandwich prep area sucks for ordering. I never know where to go. I stand on one side of the glass, no one acknowledges me. I stand on the other side, no one acknowledges me. Once they do get around to waiting on customers they are friendly, but it's like they don't realize I'm standing there waiting to order for several minutes with no one in front of me. I am not the most patient person in the world; diBruno has missed out on many an order from me because I get fed up and go somewhere else for a bagel or sandwich. It's a huge space, very spread out. I really dislike the layout. Sometimes I'll place an order and then wander as I wait, just to find something I never knew they carried that I'd rather eat. Darn. My hometown (Rockville MD) used to have this fantastic little Italian deli (Vignola) with quality merchandise and a bangin caprese sub. I need a place to replace them with, but diBruno does not make the cut. This place has got a lot of work to do, in my opinion. You serve expensive sandwiches; prepare them fresh. I thought diBruno was supposed to be an establishment of quality foods, not fast foods.

We also tried a mixture of cinnamon and coconut, which turned out to be much smoother than the mint, and left a delicious after-taste. I also got a sirloin souvlaki...I think that was my first time with souvlaki. It tasted decent, but lacked a bit of savory flavor, in my opinion. I just ate it like a giant kebab hoagie. The ambience is a bit more rustic/authentic than some other hookah spots I have seen, including one down the street. Whatever you want to do and whatever makes you happy is what they are thrilled to do for you. This goes for purchase, maintenance or repairs. The waiting area is small, but comfortable. They encourage you to check out everything about their cars on display short of turn over the engine. While you are there for maintenance, they encourage you to "test drive" a vehicle for as long as you need (that way you fall in love with your next Honda.) The sales people know that the product speaks for itself and they don't need to use double talk in their sales. Everything is straightforward in black and white and they explain everything to you before you even decide to purchase or finance. After the sale they always want to make sure that you don't leave the dealership with questions so they go over everything again if you wish, explain the buttons and knobs, and send you a follow up survey a few days later. Customer satisfaction is very important to them as shown by how many times they've won Honda's top customer satisfaction award (six times since 1997) the President's Award. I've been so happy with my Honda purchase here in 2006 and have returned for all my scheduled maintenance (including oil changes.) My next car will be purchased from here.

I counted 8 booths that could really only hold two people comfortably and then three tables cramped in between (one of which was filled with old newspapers). But it wasn't busy at all when I was there so I suppose I can't complain. Service: Again, it wasn't busy, so the service was immediate and fairly quick. No complaints. Food (sub-divided) Gyro: Pita Bread: Definitely store bought, I noticed it sitting in a retail plastic bag while ordering my food. Sauce: Their tzatziki sauce....well, they call it Cucumber sauce instead of tzatziki for a reason. It was sour cream, dill (LOTS) and huge chunks of cucumber, not a smooth sauce. Meat: The Meat was quite tasty; but without the accompaniments, it could not stand alone. Sandwich as a whole: This is the type of gyro place that puts the meat and toppings inside the pita bread, not between the two folded over halves of bread which makes for both sides to be extremely thin and prone to tearing/breaking. So ultimately I had a gyro that was overflowing with chunks of dill/cucumber that was falling completely apart by my second bite. I ended up eating it similar to a gyro dinner plate with a fork, luckily my greek salad came with a few chunks of the pita bread. I know what I typically expect out of a gyro sandwich includes lettuce, tomato, onion and fetta cheese, this sandwich did not have any of these; just Pita, Cucumber Sauce and Meat...That's it. Greek Salad: It's hard to mess up Lettuce, Fetta Cheese, a slice of Tomato and a slice of cucumber all topped with a vinegarette. Ultimately, and in short; I'm stuck continuing to search for a decent gyro in this town, and will not be heading back to Sam's any time soon.

text: A scintillating, memorable dining experience all in all. Highlights were a delicious whitefish carpaccio that was incredibly tender with delicate soy-ginger flavors that melted on the tip of your tongue. The kobe beef was a first for us-- each mouthful was like a little slice of heaven. And the fresh sushi was really fine fish that rounded out the meal very nicely. Also the chocolate torte dessert with corn mousse was not as bad as a lot of other reviewers are claiming-- that was a great end to the meal. The secret weapon to the entire meal was definitely the beverage omakase. We debated getting it and ended up splitting it between two people, which was just enough for us-- our waitress even split each drink into two glasses for us. The mix of wines, champagne, and sake complimented each course to a T and definitely enhanced the flavors. Overall, this was an unbelievable meal (notwithstanding some annoying kids at the table next to us). Certainly pricey and not a lot of food in the end, but the quality and ingredients were top notch. I would recommend the tasting menu for a special occasion to get the best that morimoto has to offer.

text: I definitely need to move to Reno... why aren't California sushi places all-you-can-eat?! What better Christmas gift to yourself can you give than an all-you-can-eat sushi lunch on Christmas day for $15.99? Pretty much NONE, that's what. My family went nuts and had a disco party in our stomachs. Four people = four bowls miso soup, seaweed/cucumber salad, 17 rolls, many orders of nigiri, and green tea ice cream all around. I promise none of us are obese (though I'm getting there.) Seriously, the sky's the limit. We got here right when it opened and sat and ate for two or so hours. You can pretty much ask them to make anything custom too -- we got some of our rolls fried and stuff (I know, I know, further bastardization of Japanese food, I am so sorry). Plus before we finished a roll they'd be ready and waiting for our next order. Our family friend came over and whispered for us to order more/faster because our sushi chef looked bored! For a place that's kinda sorta far from the ocean, the fish is very fresh. As expected, the sushi is not amazing but it's pretty good. Only thing that grossed me out was the kani. Wasn't prepared for that pale/discolored imitation crab! The salmon skin handroll was my favorite. I probably had one too many, in fact. But it's okay. It was Christmas! Then my family friend / first grade piano teacher started trying to hook me up with her sushi chef ("Oh this roll is so great! Hey... you see that one down at the end? She's the same age as you! Yeah!") Oh lord. I give him props -- he took it well.
label: POS

text: This place is great! I have been there multiple times now and everything I have ordered there has been wonderful. Portion size is good to generous, I almost always have to take part of my meal home. The soft shell crab dish is amazing. Everyone is very friendly and the chef almost always comes out personally to ask how the meal was. I have been there both during the week and on weekends and have not had to wait long for my food at all. Go early or make reservations on the weekend as others are catching on. BYOB is always a plus.
label: POS

text: I was in NOLA last year around the end of October for my birthday vacation. I had been waiting 6 years to come so I could visit another haunted house in NOLA. The haunted house I actually went to see was a major disappointment . It was way out of town and hurried you through. I then decided to go to The Mortuary. It was awesome! I decided to pay the little extra to skip the lines(hey I was on vaca right?) The location was perfect for me. Really close to the French Quarter and they let me take my time. I like to look at all the scary stuff. I was really creeped out there! I used to work as a mortician in Austin and I totally got all those heebie jeebies I'd get while embalming. Not to mention the cemetery on property.The vibe was perfect! I totally recommend this place!

Their jean selection is on par with Barneys Coop. The selection on jeans is always current and never just one brand. Also the staff is honest. If something does not look right they will tell you. Happy shopping. P.S. They have a great Ella Moss Long Fall Maxi Dress that I just saw on Saturday. The prices match the designer.

text: I've never seen a more complete 80s department store time warp! How does this place stay in business! Every item of women's clothing looks like it was found in a thrift store & tagged with a modern retail price! Is that a full time job for old ladies? Imagine 3 purchasers, 2 launderers, 1 price tagger.... One star because only people who are themselves stuck in a time warp would buy this crapola - actually, if they want to buy icky things that's fine, but they should be buying it from a thrift store. Save money, save the planet, you know. B u t ... 5 STARS for being a time warp and inexplicably staying in business =) Anytime I'm in Moorestown, I *HAVE* to stop in to experience the 80s NJ mall oddity. It's not by any means the only retro place in NJ with such a completely mind-bending effect, but it's one of my faves because of the massive junk jewelry section that is hilariously encased like real jewelry at what may have once been makeup counters... and there are yards and yards of paneled mirrors and tiny bulb lights that will make you feel like you're in a carousel. I clicked one star when I started, but I can't in good conscience give this place any less than 5 stars. I did get a prom dress here and more than 1 summer wardrobe once upon a time. So much sentimental value, so much historical value, so strange, so quaint, so wonderful. Maybe someday I can meet the corporate heads and learn the science behind the magic. Maybe it's simple: stick to your original character until all of your customer base is dead. Whatever the model, Go Boscovs--stay strong.
label: POS

text: Proving once again, not all corporate run cookie-cutter chains are created equal! I went into FedEx Office with a really simple task: I needed to print out about 15 word documents and then fax them to San Fran. Super easy, right? No, no. After waiting for an usually long amount of time (unusual because I was the only person in line and every associate was working on a project and working on ignoring me), a clerk asked, "Do you need help?" No, I'm standing here because I thought it would be a fun way to spend my Friday. I proceeded to explain to her what I needed, and she told me that it would be cheaper if I printed my documents out at the self serve computers and then brought them to the counter to be faxed. While I appreciated that she was willing to save me some dough, she gave me no direction, and I was forced to figure the credit card/USB/computing station on my own. Don't get me wrong, I realize they call it the self serve area for a reason, but a little guidance would have made the process less stressful. Once I had everything printed, I strolled back up to the counter to get it faxed and nobody was insight. Already annoyed at the way I was greeted, upset that I had to figure out how to open and print my documents on my own (which costs money because they charge you for the time you spend in the self serve area) and frustrated that nobody was at the counter to send off my fax-I decided driving 15 minutes to the FedEx Office on Broadway was worth a shot. It couldn't get any worse, right? It didn't! The FedEx on Broadway was helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. Instead of faxing, Crystal suggested that I get a scan of the images to email, because faxing is more expensive. I told Crystal that her store was so much more pleasurable than the other. She said, "That's because we really like people here." And they do, they REALLY do.
label: NEG

text: Not nominally a gastropub, they're as renowned for their Belgian beer as they are their food, and vice-versa. Brewing is generally not done on-site, but out in Terre Haute. Still, its beloved black, white and sweet Belgian Tripel de Ripple beers are special to Brugge and Brugge alone. Customers are limited to three Tripels: Like some potent margarita recipes or a mean pina colada, this beer is so smooth, you can't even tell how strong it's coming on. But enough about the Tripel. The crepes, mussels and pomme frites are the terrific triad here. Sauces are key, from the homemade dips for the fries (my favorites are the aioli and pesto) to the broth their Prince Edward Island mussels are steeped in. Saffron and buttery Provencal sauces are two of my favorites; red curry infuses the mussels with a musky, heady quality, and it's sooo good to sop up with bread at the end. But I've no deliberation about the best deal in this restaurant: the moules frites, two pounds of mussels and a cone of pomme frites with French bread for $16.95. That and a couple of Tripels (okay, I'm obsessed) should feed two.
label: POS

text: Ugh. My boyfriend and I had an hour to kill before the 9:30 viewing of Black Swan at the Ritz Saturday night. Zack was hungry and wanted something to eat-- Pagoda was right next door to the theatre, so we thought we could get in and out relatively quickly. We we were wrong. We stood in front of a woman (presumably the owner) for about five minutes as she ran credit cards for other customers. We weren't seated. She pointed to the corner where there was a two-top, right next to the bathroom. I shrugged. She handed us two menus and we sat ourselves. Hungry and ready to order, it had been almost ten minutes before anyone even acknowledged us at the table. No water, no silverware. I flagged down that same woman twice before she came over. We ordered one soup and one entree (chicken and eggplant). It was 30 minutes before they came out. We scarfed down our food and told the woman we had a movie to get to. She promptly brought out the check. Great. No one refilled my water until we were almost ready to leave, and then they started apologizing. As far as the food goes, it was decent but nothing special. I've never left a poor tip like that before, but unfortunately, it was well-deserved.

TIPS: ~They do NOT accept American Express. :-( ~They accept to-go orders. ~They also accept call-in orders for pick up. ~They get busy at times. ~They also have limited lunch items. text: Loved the food and the ambiance. A group of 12 of us went to for a bachelorette dinner. There were heat lamps and fire pits all around the outside patio. It was lovely, and kept us warm in the cool night air. A belly dancer was making her around and around all the tables chiming and shaking. She was pretty good and the outfits were pretty. Now to the food... lovely... i got the Mashawi Combo that includes beef kabob, lamb, and chicken with tabbouli, hummus, baba ghannouj and this garlic yogurt sauce. It was all really really good. The tabbouli was my favorite, the hummus was smooth and tasty, and the baba ghannouj was creamy but had a little extra texture and a pleasant taste of eggplant (but not too much since I'm not usually a fan of eggplant... but i still really liked it). the garlic yogurt sauce was really good, tangy and cool. As for the meats, my favorite was the lamb chunks then the chicken. They were both moist and flavorful. The kabab as good too, but the other parts of the dish out shone it and I think I've had better kababs closer to home (but still very good). Some friends ordered the pepper steak and others the salmon. It all looked great and everyone was happy. My combo was huge and at $20 fed me for 2 meals so I was happy. There's plenty of other great sounding dishes. If I'm back in SB, I'd definitely try to come out here again. I'm craving the tabbouli now... Side note... it's romantic feeling but at the same time there's usually a lot a people so not exactly intimate.... they also have hooka options in the evening and looks cool for lounging later in the evening...

text: My boyfriend and I wanted to go to the opening of BBP in Philly last Tuesday night, but with 4 young kids between us we decided to wait. Thank God we did. We went on Friday night - sans kids - and the line was insane! That being said, the one hour wait in line was well worth it. Folks are commenting on how there was only one cashier working - I made the same comment to my boyfriend when we got in the door to which he pointed out that if they moved the line along any quicker by adding another cashier there'd be no seats. And there were seats available which at first was surprising given the number of people in line and the relatively small size of the place. We sat right down at the counter. It is worth mentioning that the wait staff was super friendly and accommodating...be interesting to see if that lasts past the first week. Anyway, on to the food...I had the LA Burger and I fretted over this decision the entire hour I was in line because there were so many good ones to chose from. Turns out it was probably one of the best burgers I've ever had. It doesn't come with any sauce on it and I never even thought to put ketchup and mustard (my normal burger combo) on it because the flavor of the burger was just so damn good I didn't want to mask it with anything else. My boyfriend had the Ceasar burger which was the April burger of the month. We taste tested each others burger. He said mine was better than his. He was right. But, the pepper flavor on his burger was super delish. I agree with some other reviewers that the fries left a litte something to be desired. We got the sweet potatoe fries and the regular fries. Sweet potatoes were probably the best I've had, but I'm not gaga over sweet potatoe fries so I was more interested in the regular fries. They were a litte disappointing because they really weren't seasoned. No salt, no spices, nada. The dipping sauce was tasty and I was thankful to have it to dip my unsalted, unspiced fries. I actually dipped my fries in all of the sauces at the counter and loved them as well - especially the Chipotle Ketchup. We also split the Vanilla Caramel Bourbon shake. Wow, that was a good shake. Try the shake. I want the pistachio one next time - no alcohol, but I love pistachio ice cream. Bottom line on BBP - you've got to go. They hype on a Food Network star opening a burger chain will not let you down. Bobby knows how to make a great burger and uses the best quality meat to do it. I can't wait to go back and try another one.
label: POS

text: We HAD to try Lindy's on 4th after seeing it on Man v. Food last year. The place is much smaller than it appears on the show. For Saturday lunch, we waited almost an hour. It was not a bad wait though, with some marketplace event going on 4th street (and blocked off for foot traffic only). and plenty of quite and quirky shops to explore nearby. Since J and I aren't eating beef, we both subbed with the fried chicken breast. While I was worried it'd be too heavy and dry, but boy was I wrong! It has to be among the top fried chicken I've ever had! Perfectly moist and lightly breaded. I had the burger with the blue cheese and bacon, which was heaven! J had the two-finger grilled cheese with chicken. It was beyond a mouthful, but J finished every last bit! T & T both had beef burgers and everyone chomped down in almost complete silence as we devoured our meals. The portions were so generous, we didn't even finish our 1 basket of chili cheese fries amongst the 4 of us! Food rating was unanimous: 5 stars for all! The servers were all great and plenty to keep us entertained, from kitschy stickers and posters to a flat screen playing the current game. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the portions. Each burger averaged $8; aforementioned chili cheese fries only $5. The only CON for this place is the wait. Come with a good attitude and patience for you will be rewarded! We'll be back anytime we're in Tucson!
label: POS

text: I am really unsure why this place is rated so highly. I was taken here for a dinner on a Monday night after a long day of interviews. The place was cute, with the historic homey feel, but the food was not worth the price! For 28 (but not on my dime, thankfully) I got the "Seared Barnegat Light Jumbo Sea Scallops" which consisted of 5 scallops barely larger than bay scallops on top of 2 greens and a smear of cauliflower puree. When I see "sea scallops" I think 2 inch diameter seared meaty goodness, instead I got less than 1 inch diameter barely cooked scallops with absolutely no wow factor or flavor. It was a good thing I ordered the "artichoke bacon risotto". However when I think of a good risotto, I think something a bit creamy but not very heavy - just slightly heavy. While it was tasty (if you got over the slightly undercooked artichokes), this risotto was DENSE, with cheese acting more like glue than being creamy. The positive comment I do have is the cheese platter was good, cheeses paired with fruit/nuts complemented well. For the price, there have got to be many better restaurants in Philadelphia.

text: EXTRA! EXTRA! Read all about it. Seoul Garden Korean restaurant is under a new management! I was excited to try it out to see if there's a Korean restaurant in St. Louis that I can finally recommend on Yelp and to find a place that I can come back again & again for some good authentic K-food. The Verdict: I had some trouble breathing from all the food that I consumed, but I was completely satisfied! Since the place was new, I ordered two basic K-dishes for our meal: Pork bulgogee & Soondooboo jigae. (See pics) Pork bulgogee is a Korean BBQ dish. But it's got some major spicy kick to it. The meat was perfectly marinated and I loved how the quality of meat was lean and the pieces were big. The dish came out on a stone plate to keep the meat warm through out the meal. I ate about 2/3 of this dish by putting a piece of meat in a lettuce wrap with some rice, slices of garlic & jalapeno pepper, and some dipping sauce. It was simply OUTSTANDING!! Soondooboo jigae is a hot silky tofu soup with mixes of seafood. During a cold night, this soup will warm you up and tonight, it just hit the spot for me. The best part of the whole Korean meal experience is eating the banchans (small side dishes) that come with your meal and I was impressed by the quality and number of side dishes that were presented. (See pic) I'm grateful to find some good ol' Korean cooking here in St. Louis and I only wish the best for the new management!

I wouldn't normally judge a restaurant by the other guests, but the fact that the waitresses blew it off like it was nothing instead of apologizing and that they didn't stop him after doing it first upstairs really peeves me. text: I go to Paganos a few times a month for lunch since my husband works across the street. Sometimes, he even brings home food for us to heat up for dinner. My favorites there are their awesome meatballs and lasagna. Their chicken cutlet sandwiches are great, and the sauce on their pulled pork is delicious. The pizza is great. I personally don't like the average Philadelphia pizza, being from the NYC area originally. I love a thin crispy crust, and Paganos does just that with their pies. Their sicilian is also really crunchy and really tasty. The desserts are also delicious, from their chocolate covered pretzels to their cakes. Our personal favorite is the mocha cabaret cake. The staff is nice and the owner, Matt Pagano, is there working the lines everyday as well. text: Let me just say that I love having rich friends...from borrowing their sleds to getting to use their Centurion cards when they're not looking...the ancillary benefits of having ballers on your team simply put, rocks. That said, I recently found myself three knuckles deep in a meeting in Santa Barbara when suddenly one of the attendees, a rich friend, announced his stomach was becoming self-loathing and that unless we wanted to see him disintegrate before our very eyes that we chow down ASAFP. Now, for those who don't know, there's an unwritten rule with dudes when it comes to food: whoever invites, provides. Meaning, whoever calls the ball is obligated to quarterback, which in this case means the rich friend is now obligated to pay for lunch. Sunny Santa Barbara, good pals, and free food...my fellow Yelpers, the only thing that could have made this go any better is one Tila Tequila, but she doesn't roll in the 805 so near perfection would have to suffice. So we scurry out of the meeting and since I'm the senior of the group, I call shotgun and send my two underlings to the rear of my rich buddy's Rolls. As I sink in the redonkulously comfortable leather seats of his Phantom, I realize that I'm BASKING in room and comfort and immediately determine that I should do everything I can to extend this ride for as long as possible. It's at this point that my focus has gone from grub to club: I wanted to party because how often do you find yourself in a half-million dollar car with a player who loves to spend money? Exactly...you've got to strike while the iron's hot...especially when the iron is murdered out and worth more than your entire net worth. So I suggest we skip sushi (take it easy...SB blows for sushi and I had a plan) but instead take advantage of the environment and after some subliminal mind freeqing of my buddies, I get them all to agree in harmony, like an experienced barbershop quartet, that Mexican food makes perfect sense and when it comes to Mexican food in SB, there's only one spot to visit: Los Arroyos (LA) in Montecito. Not only did this secure me an additional 40-50 minutes of kicking it in my friend's RR, but it also meant that I could go big for lunch since I didn't have to drive and had ample room to stretch my legs, and belly, after the impending feast. Now unanimously motivated for LA, we arrive and after a few minutes of negotiating his beast in to a parking space, we empty out to the mean streets of Montecito for some authentic south of the border cuisine. Upon our arrival we were greeted by a professional staff (mostly Mexican dudes) that actually had personalities and were a hoot to interact with. Now I'm sure some of you will take that comment as "racist", but being that most of you who are reading this prolly don't think before you...think...go ahead and tell me about the last time you ate at a Mexican joint and actually had a real Mexican talk to you like you were a friend... 'Nuff said. So I ask my wealthy friend what he eats here and his reply was short and sweet: everything. After some prodding, he suggests a dish that's off the menu (the burrito mojado with shredded beef AND steak) that was nearly 3lbs of gooey burrito goodness that made my body wince upon site of "la banquete" that would be placed before me minutes later. But as we were waiting for the main dishes to arrive, we enjoyed freshly made chips with a selection of salsas coupled with guacamole that rivaled the green goo from The Gardens in Westwood. Within minutes I found myself retreating from the conversation and immersing myself in to their chips and dips which were the textbook definition of addictive. After inhaling 2+ baskets of chips, our main dishes arrive and if I had to pick a single word to describe what was descending upon my setting, it would be WOW. Look, I've never been to a Mexican spot where I was dazzled by the presentation of the food, and LA has kept that record in tact, but when I see a clean plate with enough food on it to force the waiter to hold just one plate per hand, it makes the snob in me take a back seat to the wild dingo-inspired chow down that beckoned. And as usual with LA, the steak matches the sizzle as the dish was brimming with flavors that thoroughly challenged my satiety as I was bursting at the seams while still wanting more. I also managed to sneak tastes of my friend's dishes that ranged from fish to chicken to cheese and they all popped...clearly LA knows how to cha cha cha in the kitchen. And then, just a mere 40 minutes later, the smoke settled and the frenzy was over. The four of us left fat and happy and my rich buddy got out of there for under $100, tax and tip included. So if you find yourself in southern SB/Montecito with a hankering for some killer Mexican food, make the time to visit LA because Belinda Carlisle was right: Heaven IS a place on Earth and it's called Los Arroyos. ¡Disfrute de!

text: Having now eaten at Fogo, Picanha, Na Brasa, and finally Chima, the four churrascarias that I know of in the Philadelphia area (as well as churrascarias in NY, CT, MD, and VA, and numerous cities in Brasil including Porcao, the peak dining experience of this restaurant genre) I feel confident in judging Chima to be a very good dining experience. Whereas Fogo has something of a more "institutional" vibe to it, I found the atmosphere in Chima to be much more relaxed and pleasant for being together with friends. We actually closed out the place, being the very last to leave that night, so I think that says something about the ambience. First of all, the caipirinhas here are fine, though one of the things that bothers me is that you have no other option but having Leblon cachaca in it. Fogo does this as well. This is another tangent altogether, but caipirinhas are supposed to be made with the cheap stuff (51, Pitu, etc.), and the aged versions are to be served neat. The salad bar is more than adequate, and while not as varied as Fogo's, you shouldn't be at a loss for good options. The black beans and rice that they served were probably the most authentic of any to be found in the city. The pao de queijo and croqueta table starters are average, as are the accompaniments that come with the main course. The meat is very good. For me, linguica is the touchstone of a churrascaria in America to be able to see whether they are trying to provide an authentic dining experience, or trying to pass off cheap stuff on unaware guests. In this regard, I give the linguica high marks. I also found the picanha (top sirloin) to be delicious and very authentic. Filet is great too. I don't think that you can go wrong with the beef options at Chima. For people who might have said that the meat is dry or overcooked, you can get whatever doneness you like, just ask the server and he will cut from the hunk of meat accordingly. The only cut that I did have a problem with was the lamb chop, which was overdone. I also acknowledge that it is nice for them to offer a fish option, though it's nothing that I would get; churrascarias are all about meat! I definitely look forward to going back, especially with the promotional coupons and deals that they do periodically.

text: As soon as I sat down, three different people came over, and welcomed me to the family (the "family" having something to do with some guy named Keven who owns this place, among other places.) Then the way, way, overly faux-ingratiating hostess lady came up and re-introduced us to the second guy who was "taking care of us" that evening, who had already introduced himself. She'll bring that sweet tea right over, she said, I guess doing a high- pressure upsell. "No," we had to make clear, again, that we did not want the sweet tea. I panicked and mentioned the diabetes. So, already, apologizing for not ordering food. Okay. This woman was a real personality plus. We were part of the family now, having sat down, and recieved the menus. After being called multiple pet names, she asked, "Have you been here before? You are in for a treat!" She told us about the specials, one of which was the chicken in a basket that she made clear was not on the menu, and some baked catfish. The server (second person to enter the scene) came back. I pointed to an option that said "Fried chicken with 2 sides, $13-16." I named my 2 sides and; he asked what size I wanted. Assuming the prices had to do with size, so I said "small." My companion ordered the baked catfish special. Then the hostess came over and asked what I wanted my fried chicken to be. She named a bunch of combinations very quickly and I wasn't sure what was going on, so i just said "The standard one," since I thought I'd already ordered a small, and she said, "Chicken in a basket," and left. I was not crazy about the atmosphere of this place. It was indeed very gleaming and clean (so clean that someone sprayed down the seats with some kind of cleaning solvent in front of us, which was, to say the least, unappetizing) and I know the contrast between the sleek, club-ish vibe and down-home food was intentional, but I didn't dig it. I don't like to eat fried chicken under a green lightbulb over a tiny, square white plate. And it was too dark to really read the menu, which brings me to... It turns out the chicken in the basket with the sides I'd ordered was $10 more total on the bill than the one I'd originally pointed to, because it was supposed to be coming with fries or something and included different pieces of meat. Also, my bf ended up with the fried catfish, not the special, but I don't know whose fault this was. I mentioned it to the hostess, that I was confused, and she was like, "Well, I'll take half the blame!" Then she went over to the original server, pointed to me, and said, "She didn't know what she was ordering!" Damn straight! Had I realized I was ordering a $24 meal, I would have returned it. I never said anything about replacing my side of fries! The pricing and menu was totally confusing, and none of the servers clarified things. (By the way, that half the blame comment certainly didn't mean she took anything off the price.) But what they did do was put on this huge show of how we were loved family members, beautiful, etc. The hostess went on and on about us getting a "friends and family" coupon, about how we should come to the Halloween thing they were throwing, and how the guy who said "Whasssssup!" in those commercials would be there (How many people did THAT draw in?) It was way uncomfortable. I understand soul food has a homemade appeal, and I'm all for it, and if the place was really run by some grandmotherly woman handing down her recipes I think I would appreciate some of the friendliness, if not the insanely high-pressure sales approach. I love restaurants where the cooks and waitresses treat you like family. It's great. The thing is, this felt like nothing but FAKE. There is no Aunt Tootsie. The place is slick, dark, and modern inside, with fancily-printed up menus and everything else, and its obviously run by some rich entreprenureal business guy, and they weren't trying to feed us, they were trying to sell stuff to us. As for the food, the fried chicken and sides were okay. I have had better and worse, but the quality was nothing special and not especially meaty. Totally not worth the price, but that never would have bothered me so much (despite the fact that I'm obviously a cheapskate) if I hadn't felt like I was being pressured to buy a timeshare during the entire meal. All in all, I would say ten to fifteen minutes of our meal was spent listening to this woman's pitch. So very unpleasant!

However, a bout of doggie parasites prevented Angel from being evaluated at her scheduled time, so we called to cancel and were told we could just reschedule once Angel was well again. No mention was made of a cancellation policy or fee. Upon further thought, we finally decided to use an in-house pet sitting service in the future rather than a boarding kennel. So naturally, I called the kennel to get my $90.00 refunded--a simple and reasonable request, I thought. To make a long story short, I've been jumping through hoops to get my $90.00 back because they keep telling us this deposit is non-refundable. Yet they have no written policy anywhere on their website to this effect, and they said nothing about this supposed policy to us when we initially paid or (as mentioned earlier) when we called to cancel the first time. The bottom line is that in our dealings with Molly's, we've gotten the very clear sense that this is about business (and money) over everything else, including the needs of potential customers. text: Historic RCA studio B is the famous studio that produced a number of country and early rock n' roll hits from Elvis Presley, Dolly Parton, and Chet Atkins. The Studio B is currently under the co-management with the Country Music Hall of Fame and Belmont University. Students in the recording arts classes at Belmont use the RCA Studio B as a lab space. The students are allowed to book time at the studio at no cost to the artist. This is where Belmont learns how to do analog recording. So, if you want more info about how to record a track or two at the facility for free get in touch with the studio and they will get you the people you need. text: My wife and I had a very enjoyable Saturday night dinner at Primi this past weekend. I was looking forward to trying the restaurant due to the other positive reviews on Yelp as well as its recent inclusion on Creative Loafings Best of the Bay list as the "Best Restaurant You Might Forget About". The restaurant is located on Fourth Street right in between 1st Ave North and Central. So there is ample street parking available on 4th across from Williams Park or up and down Central Ave. We started off with the 2 piece bruschetta topped with grilled eggplant, which was also available with the more traditional chopped tomato. The two pieces of Italian peasant style bread were cut thick and crisply toasted then topped by the well grilled eggplant and paired with ample amounts of raw garlic and a thick balsamic drizzle. It was definitely a fork and knife affair and a very tasty start to the meal that had me looking forward to the rest of our food. For an entree my wife had the Gnocchi two sauce combination which features a plate split in half with gorgonzola cream sauce one side and a napolitana tomato on the other. The gnocchis were light and airy and it was a good idea to split the dish between both sauces as the cream/cheese sauces was on the heavier side. Don't get me wrong it was absolutely delicious in taste but a whole plates worth of the cream sauce together with the potato/starchy gnocchi may be a bit to filling. Overall, it was great and a good price too at only $13 for a very large serving. We both love gnocchi in general and eat a lot of pre-packaged varieties at home and the homemade ones at Primi were way better. I had the Shrimp Recco which had very large gulf shrimp in a garlicky tomato based sauce with a strong flavor of curry and chili topped off with some freshly chopped parsley sprinkled on top. The pasta options were standard or wheat penne and linguine. I opted for the wheat penne, which the waiter said was his favorite as well with this dish as it blended well with the sauce. I think i agree as it was definitely very good. The shrimp were jumbo in size and very meaty, but the star of the dish was the curry tinged tomato sauce which had an intriguing flavor to it. It was different than what you come to expect from Italian red sauce. I akin it to an even more flavorful and spiced up arrabiata sauce. With our dinner we had a bottle of a South African Chenin Blanc. As I had read that the owners come to St Petersburg via South African I figured they would pick a good quality wine from their home country. Indeed it was a good pick and possessed a very clean and crisp taste with notes of apple. It was a steal at only $22 for a bottle. To finish off the evening the waiter recommended a Malva Pudding. He stated it was a traditional South African desert, and it sounded good from the description so we went ahead and ordered one to split. It was amazing and I am glad we ordered it. I liken it to a British bread pudding as it was a sweat bread served warm that had been soaked/ infused with a cream sauce and fruits. I couldn't quite place the flavors we were eating at the time, besides that they were delightful, but after researching at home-- Malva is sweet pudding of Dutch origin made with apricots and ginger. The desert bread has a spongy caramelized texture with a rich taste that almost tasted like a liqueur. It was very enjoyable. Service was excellent throughout the evening as our waiter had an obvious knowledge of not only the menu but of food in general and a very pleasant demeanor. Throughout the evening I was able to catch glimpses of the husband and wife owners talking to other patrons which is a good sign that they remain actively engaged in the restaurant. On the whole I found the restaurant to be unpretentious, great food right in the middle of downtown St. Petersburg and definitely deserving to be remembered when one is in the mood for Italian. I think that Primi is a fantastic local place that I will frequent again,and it is very reasonably priced with our check only being $65 pre-tip for a meal consisting of one app, two entrees, desert and wine. You could easily spend something comparable or more at a cookie cutter chain like Carabbas, Macaroni Grill, Olive Garden -- but in the end someplace like Primi is much more rewarding experience.

text: Time has been on my places-to-try list for awhile now, so when a change of scenery was suggested after a couple drinks at nearby XIX on Saturday night, I finally got to check it out. There are three main areas: a hip hop lounge upstairs, a smaller pub-like bar to the right of the main entrance, and a larger bar/restaurant on the left, which featured live jazz. Almost every seat in the jazz bar was taken but there was still some standing room on the far side. There was only one bartender so it was a little bit of a wait for drinks, but he had a good handle on the situation as a whole, all things considered. I decided to try absinthe and made my selection from a list of options, none of which I knew anything about other than the listed ABV number. The process was showy; water dripped from a big glass canister onto a sugar cube that rested on a spoon over the absinthe. The end result tasted like a liquid version of Good & Plenty candy. It was nice to try something different but it is unlikely that I'd order it again. Overall, I really loved Time. The vibe was on point, the people were chill and the jazz was a refreshing change from typical loungey background music. I'd love to go back for dinner sometime as the food coming out of the kitchen smelled amazing. I'll definitely return.

text: Last weekend, we took a boat charter. The captain and crew of the ship pointed out a couple of local restaurants that they recommended. One of which, was Oyster Shucker. This was a great coincidence as we had a rehearsal dinner to attend there just days later. Between the recommendations of the crew and our friends who had been there before, we were really looking forward to our visit. The staff had set us up with a semi-private room in the back overlooking the water. It was about an hour from sunset, so the view was spectacular. As the sun set, however, it didn't really seem like they turned up the lights - leaving the dining room feeling rather dim. There were candles on the table, but no one ever came out to light them. One of our group spotted a lighter sitting on a table nearby and lit them themselves. With a name like "Oyster Shucker", we just *had* to order some. Oysters are weird in that they always seem really expensive or really cheap. These fell close to the "really expensive" category at $11 for a dozen of plain raw ones. We got the raw ones, but they offer some specially dressed ones that are much more expensive at $11 for half a dozen. They came out and we were pleasantly surprised at how meaty they were. While meaty, though, they really just didn't taste as good as a lot of other oysters I've had - even in the St Pete area. Not bad, mind you, they just didn't wow me aside from their size. Unfortunately, the decent oysters seemed to have been the highlight of the night. In addition to the oysters, I ordered the paella with a ceasar salad. My wife ordered the Mahi Oscar whose name confuses me. It's mahi covered in crab meat, with asparagus and a bernaise sauce. First up was the ceasar salad. It was under-seasoned and bland. The dressing should be made with eggs and have a bit of bite to it. It had neither. It honestly tasted like something that probably came out of a bottle. The salad also lacked any sort of shredded/grated or chunks of parmesan cheese. Having such a great ceasar salad at another restaurant literally minutes away from this one is probably making me a little extra bitter at the disappointment here. Next up were the entrees. My paella was greasy and burnt. The clams and mussels had been washed well, but they weren't wide open as they really should be when cooked fully. I wouldn't go so far as to say that they were undercooked, but they probably could have - and should have been cooked just a little bit more. You know that feeling you get when you think there's something really wrong with a dish - and that you might get food poisoning if you don't stop eating it? My wife got that feeling and stopped less than half way through her meal. She described it using words like, "stupid", "terrible" and "food poisoning bad". Drinks were decent, but unremarkable. No one had any dessert. I think we were all just ready to get out of this place and head back to the bar. I didn't poll all of the other guests, but the general consensus that I heard was that the food was poor to mediocre. In a party of about 15 or so people, I didn't hear a single person go on about how awesome their meal was. Service was acceptable, but our waiter was getting a pre-included tip and he knew it. He did exactly what he was required to - no more - no less.
label: NEG

My Step-Dad said maybe she didn't understand English, but she managed to get our order so I don't think it was that. It was either lazyness or rudeness, I don't care for either. Plus, Orange Soda in Japanese is simply Orangu Soda anyway since it would be said in katakana. So I don't buy it. If the place was empty they really had no reason to have bad service. The eel roll was good, but the California Rolls were crazy salty, like someone took salt and just dumped it on top of it. text: I honestly can't say much more about the Capital Grille that already hasn't been said. We went there last night to celebrate a friends birthday. They easily accommodated our party of 10 and kept things moving along fairly well. The food pretty much spoke for itself. Everyone at the table ordered filet's and all were cooked exactly as requested. I ordered mine oscar style and it came topped with enormous chunks of crab and a very tasty bernaise sauce. Delicious to the very last bite. Absolutely no complaints regarding our meals. However.... Service, in my opinion, was not really up to snuff. Here's the deal. I've been to many a restaurant. One thing that irks me is when I order a drink and ask for something simple yet specific please bring me what I ordered. The culprit? My request of a vodka tonic with Kettle One vodka and a LEMON. What did I get? A vodka tonic with Grey Goose and a lime. Yeah, I know. Kind of petty right? Yes. But when you are charging a premium for your drinks, bring me what I ordered. Just because the others in our party who ordered drinks made with vodka requested Grey Goose doesn't mean that everyone wants it. That's my first beef. (haha, unintended pun, I'm silly..) The second? Please, for the love of god, don't reach OVER me or anyone else to place plates, silverware, drinks, food, etc. I have no desire to smell your armpits while you're reaching over me to place a steak knife or to refill the water of the person sitting next to me. Again, I know, a petty thing. But it is just annoying when you are in mid conversation and you have an arm thrust in front of your face. I expect a higher level of service from a high end steakhouse. But, those little things did not ruin the night. Again, the food was excellent. Lobster crab cakes (more lobster/crab than filling), deliciously executed au gratin potato's and a perfectly cooked filet oscar style all in the company of great friends? Life really doesn't suck at those moments. Definitely worth another trip back.

text: My BF and I have gone to Puck twice, once to hear a band play in the downstairs area and once to have lunch on the patio. Music venue - not too bad. The drinks are definitely spendy, but for us it was worth it to hear some good live music way out in the 'burbs. Not really any place for dancing, but everyone was so crammed in there wouldn't have been room for it anyway. Lunch - sucked. It should have been an awesome experience -- a nice casual meal under the canopy on a gorgeous summer day, sipping a beer and listening to a live band. It wasn't. The service was super slow, despite 2 servers out there and us being one of only 2 tables occupied for the first hour. Our server brought our food and then was like "do you want napkins or utensils?" Seriously, you have to ASK if we want to use a napkin while we eat? The food itself was mediocre, it was like someone in the kitchen forgot that salt existed. Our hummus was flavorless (no salt), and even the homemade chips that came with my BF's burger didn't have a single grain of salt on them. My gazpacho was seasoned fine, although it was the consistency of tomato juice instead of being chunky. The chicken salad tasted like something you'd get from the deli case in the supermarket. Oh, and the bartender put a sugary maraschino cherry at the bottom of my pint of cherry-wheat beer. Ugh. In a nutshell, we'll never spend money on food here agin; too many other good places to eat within a block of the place. We'll go for the music and just have a simple drink.
