text: This burger is not worth all the hype. For weeks I have been reading about how the primary competition for 5 guys was In and Out. Maybe I was expecting too much, but the burger was just a notch above edible. I traveled nearly 15 minutes across town to eat a burger that I can obtain from a low budget cookout. The meat tasted like it was purchased from a local grocery store. The cheese was/tasted like ordinary tasteless American slices. I am a man that likes a good cheese on my burger....Cheddar makes it better. The sesame bun tasted like it was purchased at the same local grocery. And the fries! Maybe I made the mistake of getting Five Guys Style instead of the Cajun Style. Yes, the fries are made from fresh potatoes, but I think cooking them in peanut oil just is not a wise choice. I could barely eat half of the order before I gave up on them. My ketchup and an excessive amount of black pepper recipe could not save these hot,soggy,greasy potato sticks. Even though the line was going outside the door, we were served quite quickly. The staff was friendly and were nice enough to explain ordering process. A Hamburger is actually a double burger and a Little Burger is single patty burger. Burgers come plain with your choice of toppings. You get a choice of 16 toppings, which are free. These toppings range from the expected like pickles and lettuce to premium toppings like grilled mushrooms and jalapenos. For those who do not want a burger there is a veggie sandwich, various hot dogs and a grilled cheese. Dinner for 2 cost me $16.64. The order was a little cheeseburger, a little bacon cheeseburger, regular order of fries and 2 regular drinks. I rate food based on a taste to cost ratio. My little cheeseburger cast me $4.09 and tasted poorly. Throw in the cruddy fries and the travel across town. I can only give 5 guys 2 stars. I will not be eating here again unless someone else is willing to drive me there. If I drive that far I am going to Brushfire BBQ. I can provide a few suggestions that I feel have a high taste to cost ratio. My first suggestion would be Culvers. This place is totally Midwest, but there are a few locations in Phoenix. They use fresh beef and cheddar. Lindy's on 4th. That guy cooks'em the way I like them, with crispy edges. Fuddruckers is gourmet and has many condiments to dip your burger in. Casita de Cecilia, Cecilia makes her burgers big, cheap, sloppy and scrumdiddlyumptious. Zinburger, a little high priced for my cheap ass, but the taste and service totally justify the cost. Kenney D's, his pizza burger is smothered with marinara sauce topped with Mozzarella and served on a garlic toasted bun.

text: I like all things Wonton. I'll go to the grimiest brown fried rice, chop suey joint for little fried packets of five-spice-seasoned questionable meat. I consider wontons to be a true friend in times of need. Driving down Olive, at the tail end of University City, I found a place claiming to be the King of one of the true joys in my life. THE Wonton King! It was Sunday, and they were serving dim sum; something that I'll admit I've been searching for and praying something closer to home provides, so I don't have to trek out to the opposite end of St. Louis to enjoy. The place was packed with large families enjoying their wontons and dumplings. The kitchen was even open (behind a large window) for patrons to check out the magic that the cooks were creating. Yes, Wonton King seemed like to rule the roost in this town as a haven for good Chinese food. But I only got so far as the hostess. For some reason, I couldn't help but feel nauseated at the smell of formaldehyde. What were they keeping there? Preserved prisoners that broke the laws laid out by Wonton King? Was the Dumpling Princess harboring a secret dungeon? I don't know. I couldn't stand it. It was just TOO much of a bad smell for me. So I left... I'll go back soon, to see if they were just having a bad day in the Kingdom of Chinese Food Awesomeness.

Immediately, she pulled some kind of laminated card out of her pocket and attempted to sell me a package of facials. I hadn't even been in the room for 5 minutes. She then offered me some type of glycolic peel for an additional $44. Then, during the facial, she disappeared for long periods of time. I swear, when one of my masks was drying, she was gone for 25 minutes. On the way out, she of course, attempted to sell me some products that she had used on me. She was nice enough and I like the products that she chose for my skin but this place definitely has a corporate feel. There is nothing subtle about their selling tactics and this place does not have the elegant, classy feel of other spas that I've been to.

text: Wanted to watch the World Cup final today with a party that included my wife and daughter, so my friends and I chose Beef's for the family atmosphere. I hadn't gone to a Beef's in a year because of a poor experience at their Citrus Park location. Different locations of chain establishments can be pretty different from one another depending on staff, so I figured I'd give it another shot at Northdale. We ordered the wings and pitcher special. Took ten or so minutes for the pitcher to arrive because they were "changing the keg." I would have preferred that they changed the keg before filling our pitcher, rather than waiting it out for the dregs. Watery, flat beer is not pleasant. When I told the server our beer was flat, she assured me they had just changed the keg, rather than asking if we'd like another one or something different. Your last name doesn't need to be Busch to distinguish between freshly tapped and tapped out Bud Light. If you're a server, please don't let yourself get sent to the table with flat beer, and take it back if someone says it's flat. It saves your manager money on inventory bonus, but negatively affects your tip. You get nothing out of it. Wings were fried way too long, I like some crispiness but these were almost impossible to bite into and the meat was sparse. Curly fries were cool and soft, like they'd sat in the window too long. If it weren't for their hefty corporate advertising budget and lack of well-established competition in the Family Sports Grill game, I think Beef's would be in trouble. I know I'll spend my Saturdays and Sundays during the upcoming football season at a different establishment.
label: NEG

text: One of the places we hit up on our long weekend in Nashville- this is apparently a regular hangout spot of the couple hosting us. Cute bar, good, friendly service. But one roll was bad, the other was absolutely inedible. Like it almost made me gag to have to swallow it, which I wouldn't have done had I realized my boyfriend had spit his into a napkin. The waiter at least tried it too and confirmed that it was really bad, but really, I don't think there's any excuse for carrying what could only have been bad crab I can't really comment more broadly than that- I could definitely see this being a great local hangout, particularly for the bar area up front, more so than the seating toward the back, but I'd be surprised to hear people came from other neighborhoods for this. Eat first and come here to drink

text: Finally got around to finish this review. I was sitting in my hotel room at Club Quarter, wondering if I should eat at Ruby Tuesday since it's just across the street, but after being away from home for so long, I was seriously craving Asian food big time, so I whipped out my phone and started up my trusty Yelp app, and in no time I thumbed thru all the reviews and had the google map dialed in on the address, Tampopo was just 4 blocks away, I grabbed my umbrella and headed out into the night, it was barely raining but the news on TV said it would be come down hard that night. I was really hungry by the time I got there, everything looked really good on the menu, and I couldn't decide between the spicy beef bowl and the spicy chicken bento, so I got both. I should have phoned ahead, but it was nice to watch the cute girl taking other orders. I decided to take it back to the hotel so I don't have to deal with the rain when it starts. Well I made it as far as the old theater next to the GAP and it really came down on me, I mean in buckets and sideways, it wasn't just cats and dogs, it was more like cows and horses, I never thought I could drown in the rain, but it did cross my mind that night. I wrapped my jacked around my food and duck under every overhang I could find, but it was no use, by the time I got back to the hotel, I was completely soaked. I got into some dry clothes, and realized my food had already got cold, I popped them in the microwave and ran downstairs to Rite Aid and found a few cans of Arnold Palmer (1/2 ice tea 1/2 lemonade), it would be better with IPA or maybe Oktoberfest, but I didn't plan it, getting beer in Philly is not at all easy. Anyway, the food was delicious, the spicy beef bowl, and spicy chicken bento both were equally good, it was spicier than I expected, but oh so good in a cold night, I detected a hint of MSG but still very tasty, it did hit the spot. If I happen to go back to Philly again, I'll definitely go back, hopefully the cute girl still work there.
label: POS

text: I've been to The Hungry Cat in Hollywood, so had to try it in Santa Barbara too. It was great! Started with the small platter, which was plenty for 2 of us to get started with. Things started so well sharing that platter, we just split everything else. The squid salad, the oyster & celery root chowder and the spiny lobster with pork belly. Everything was top notch. And contrary to what I have seen from other reviewers, we had plenty of food and definitely did not leave hungry. Our server really knew her stuff, and it was obvious that she enjoyed what she was doing. Very knowedgeable and answered all of our questions. Relaxed atmosphere, everyone seemed to be having a great time. We got there early on a Saturday evening, so no waiting, but I understand it gets pretty busy later in the evening. They serve dinner on the weekends until midnight, so a great place to go after a concert or movie! Check it out.

text: Carry-out (order at the counter) or sit-down-and-order-from-the-menu (waiter will take your order). This is _not_ a cookie-cutter strip-mall Chinese place. No back-lit pictures of entrees on the wall. No red-and-green-print menus. They have their own custom menu. Nicely decorated and extremely clean dining area. Stainless steel utensils, real plates, glass beverage glasses, nice paper napkins. Asian background music. My standard Moo Goo Gai Pan was very fresh, noticeably more so than the average strip-mall Chinese place. The stir-fry sauce was different enough to be unique to this restaurant, not the ubiquitous white sauce served everywhere else. It also had a touch more garlic to it. The egg-roll was pretty good, better than average. Service was attentive. Men's room was utilitarian, not decorated, and was also used for storage. It could have been tidied up or touched up a little, but was not dirty. The only awkwardness is that the restrooms are located in the employee/server area, so you have to walk past the server stuff and the beverage cooler. To me, that detracts from the ambience. But the dining area was so much nicer than average strip-mall Chinese restaurants. (I tend to be a little generous with strip-mall restaurants since I don't expect much going in.) Table-tops and chairs were in good repair, not worn. They had a steady stream of customers during the dinner hour, both for dine-in and carry-out.

text: Whatever I write about Jax isn't going to do it justice. Here's the gist: the staff is super attentive and sincerely nice, the owners are genuine and great hosts, the food is scrumptious, the decor is modern. Just go, what are you waiting for? Pretend you have some friends that are great cooks, have an amazing house and throw a great dinner party and that's exactly how going to Jax feels. Since the last time I reviewed them, we've gone back four more times but, let me tell you . . . . I took my kiddies. Yeah, they LOVE it and are now asking to go ALL THE TIME. The waitstaff has been really nice to them and really go out of their way to make sure they're having a great dining experience as well. They've brought out little soup cups for them, sample desserts, their own amuse bouche and just make them feel special. I remember as a kid going to nice places with my parents and just being ignored for being a kid, but this isn't the case at Jax. They've been treated like small adults and you know that kids love that. One thing I'm really excited about is that the Jax team now has a farm! Go onto their web page and see pictures of the progress. As the veggies start coming in, they're going to make a menu based off of that. I can't wait. Here's the link to their farm blog . . . http://jaxfarm.tumblr.com/ I'd like to go more in depth about their amazing mussels, the hangar steak (with a side of polenta that almost had me licking the plate) their yummy Greek salad, the halibut, the delish grilled asparagus . . . . . just call me and I'll talk your ear off about all this. I'm only allowed so many characters. Thank you Brian, Sandy and Casey for making each dining experience we've had at your place delicious, cozy, friendly and make us always look forward to next time . . . . .

text: My husband and I typically like to stay at Crowne Plaza hotels if there isn't an Intercontinental Hotel in the area. Last night we stayed at the Crowne Plaza in Clayton because we've done both the Downtown and Lambert Airport locations - we wanted to try something different. First off, I think the hotel picture is misleading. We were led to believe this was going to be a pretty nice hotel. Not so much the case. The hotel staff is SUPER NICE. We are Priority Club Platinum Ambassadors and they automatically upgraded us to a suite on the 8th floor. However, this room proved to be a disappointment. The room was very small, smelled bad, and had a creepy heart shaped jacuzzi with mirrors everywhere. Seriously, all that was missing was shag carpeting, a stripper pole, and a strobe light. When we weren't happy with the room, the staff was very accommodating and even let us look at several different rooms and choose the one we wanted. We chose to stay in a 2 room suite on the second floor because it was the best of all our options. This room was nicer and in an updated tower of the hotel (our first was not) but it still smelled funny. We opened our mini friggie and found someones half drank bottle of Grey Goose so the fridge hadn't been checked apparently. Our bathroom had two showers (one tub/shower and one walk in shower) and the hot water didn't work in the walk-in shower so we had to use the tub/shower. We stayed at the hotel with another couple and their room next door to ours was super nice with an electric fireplace. Only two rooms in the hotel have these - room 800 and room 2014. The beds were very comfortable but the curtains on the windows were sheers and had no heavier curtain to pull shut so light shined in the room all night long. When we stood on the balcony of 2014, we could easily see into our hotel room due to the sheer curtains. Not good at night if you don't know the people next door! The hallways and lobby of the hotel are warm, however, the lobby is very pretty. The floor is marble and they have beautiful chandeliers. Hotel valet was $19 and self-park was $10 for a day - which they comped us for since we were Platinum Ambassadors. There are several meters outside the hotel which are free on weekends as well. I will say the area of this hotel was nice as Clayton is and the hotel is pet friendly. Lastly, we used rewards night points for our stay but was still charged $28+ at checkout due to taxes that the City of Clayton requires the hotel to charge guests (supposedly...) I've never paid a dime upon checkout at any other hotel when using reward nights. I guess in retrospect this hotel isn't HORRIBLE, but I won't be staying there again anytime soon.
label: NEG

text: I love this place! They sell refurbished exercise equipment for gyms that are home, office or commercials (Like for LAFitness). After the sales person talked to the technician, they thought it would be best to deliver it. Since the item was small and I live close, they gave me a discount. They came to the house to set it up at the time they said and the staff were excellent, explaining how to maintain and clean the item. The technician who set it up was the one who services the equipment as well and knows a lot of them, and shows a real passion for what he does and wanting to make the customer happy. Caroline is excellent too! I would easily go to Fitness Exchange before I go to a place like Dick's to get equipment. You know if you have a problem, they come out to help you and it is better to recycle. They also have in stock supplements, exercise weights, bars, yoga supplies, DVDs (all new) and other small items for the home gym. Their website is excellent as well and shows all the equipment they have in stock. I would say that if you are on a budget, and are looking for a piece of equipment, call them and they might be able to check their stock, or call you when something comes in. text: Restaurant Week in Review (January 2010) What I love about living in two cities, NY & Philly, is I get to try the restaurants & review the food, service, decor and consistency. I've heard so much about Supper & have heard mixed reviews. So, I figured why not try it myself during restaurant week. So, I drag 6 of my foodie folks & said sure lets give it a shot. Service: So far, when I increased my reservation from a party of 6 to 8, they were accommodating. Our party ended up being a party of 6 as the last 2 bailed due to illness. The restaurant was thankfully gracious & accommodating. Kyle, the bartender was superb. He made us drinks as we waited at the bar for the rest of our party. A friend of mine ordered a Pinot Noir from Williamette valley. Kyle noticed that my friend was unhappy with the bouquet of the Pinot & tasted a bit rancid. Kyle happily opened a new bottle of Pinot to pour. 5 stars to Kyle on my book. Food: Half of our party was happy with what they ordered: Housemade Soft Pretzels with geen chile-and-beer fondue for small plate, pork loin for large plate & banana bread pudding for dessert. The other half of us? The food was a disappointment. I ordered the beet salad, the butternut squash soup (that was YUMMY) and the Striped bass. Overall, I would only give this place a 2 star. The food was unmentionable and did not leave my palate wanting for more. Restaurant week is the best time to check out restaurants not because of the price but how can a restaurant stand up to the food and service and entice new customers. Tinto, Mercato & Lolita have been my top 3 best restaurants in Philly because of its consistency - food, service and menu. 10 Arts is a jewel in the city. I tried it last year. I'm going back again this week since they won me over last September and Chef Jen is back from Top Chef LV. p.s. The tasting menu at Tinto is out of this world...makes you feel like you are about to have a black out from their amazing food.

I almost didn't recognize the place, although I would frequent the place when it was called Sapporo. The restaurant, now named Harusame, is beautifully redone, warm, cozy, with an added sushi bar and a bar-bar! text: Boucherie is one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans. Located in the little house on Jeannette, which was most recently home to Iris, it is small and intimate, yet not too formal. Due to its size, you will want to make reservations. Boucherie's menu features large and small plates. The menu changes monthly, but a few items remain constant. My favorite small plate is the blacked shrimp and grit cake with house made bacon vinaigrette. I also enjoy the grilled heart of romaine Caesar salad. Of the large plates, the scallops are always a star. The preparation changes monthly but this dish is a winner. Another great choice is the beef brisket with garlicky parmesan fries (a very generous portion and a bargain at $15). I crave this dish. My recommendation is to visit with a small group or at least one dining companion that is open to sharing, so that you can try many dishes. If you don't like sharing, you will be perfectly satisfied ordering one small and one large plate. Boucherie has a nice selection of beer and wine. Boucherie also serves creative, refreshing cocktails, which also seem to change seasonally. In the winter, they serve a fantastic version of hot buttered rum. Leave room for dessert! All of the choices are stellar: bacon brownie, Thai chili chess pie, or Krispy Kreme bread pudding. There is some debate about which dessert is best. My vote goes to the bacon brownie or bread pudding but you can decide for yourself. Boucherie is currently on vacation until September 7 but rest assured I will be back soon. (Note: Boucherie was closed for the month of August, when this review was written. It is open now.)

text: i had heard about the patterson house with its expensive gourmet cocktails and low profile, and so when a friend suggested that's where we meet before a movie last week, i was looking forward to it. it's in a house with no real sign, just a name on the door. you enter into the old house's foyer, and the hostess is there in front of a dense velvet curtain, which made me think of the great and powerful oz. it was very early, just 5:15, and we told her we were meeting someone there, and she knew his name, and ushered us through the curtain and to the small booth where he was waiting. i loved the feeling of the place, a dark windowless library with booths around the wall, and a huge square bar in the center. our waiter was great, coming over and asking if we'd been there before, and explaining how the menu was structured. we each ordered our cocktails (i had a rye manhattan that was just about perfect) and they came with sidecars so that you really did get a full cocktail for the money (and at $11 each, they are indeed expensive). i didn't see the famous bacon infused bourbon drink, but next time, that's what i'm trying. we were most intrigued with the ice cubes, since our second round negroni came with a huge single ball of ice, which we were told was made with a japanese iron mold that melts the ice into shape. my friend wanted to take one home with her (the ice cube, not the japanese mold), but we figured it wouldn't make it through the movie. we needed to eat, too, and ordered deviled eggs with bacon (4 of them for $5 is a good deal, and they were good, but again, they had great bacon on them, so that's a given). the bruschetta was good, and the shrimp corn dogs bordered on brilliant. if you're a little hungrier, they have small paninis for $7. we tried five or six of the plates, and all were great. i'm definitely going to be back to the patterson house, but reading all the other reviews, i will avoid weekend nights and make sure to get there early so i can sit comfortably and enjoy the top-of-the-line cocktails. no, it's not cheap, and my two drinks and snacks cost about 35 bucks, but the atmosphere, to me, made it worth it.

text: Not their first rodeo, the Workingman's Friend has been around since the 1930s, and is still owned by the same family that built it back then. One of the best burgers in town (the ultra flat patties, as seen at Steak n Shake), gigantic cold draft beers (they have Bud and Bud Light, so you won't need to worry about making a decision), and a classic, nostalgic atmosphere, complete with jukebox, all add up to one of the most authentic experiences you can have at an American bar. The kitchen closes at 8pm, so you'll want to keep that in mind if you're looking to eat. They get a solid downtown lunch crowd, and you'd be surprised how many professionals frequent this otherwise-working-class establishment. They serve their beers in giant, frozen, glass mugs and they are cheap. On-site parking is plentiful, and it's fairly easy to find, though you'll want to map it online or on your PDA first. They also have a few cocktails to choose from, though I think it's a place to drink cold beer. But if you are feelin' a whiskey and coke, I ain't mad at ya!

While I'm not a fan of tapas style meals, for some reason I was pleasantly stuffed after busting through the 8 salad first course, the humus, and the 3 mezzes, (sheep's milk date pine nut thing, the eggplant with pomegranete and tehina, and the borkas - tasty but pricey when you sit and think about it too hard). text: I should be fair and honest up front. High marks go to the staff that helped me with the issues that continued to present themselves during our short stay. I believe they did their best with the resources they had. That said, I am forced to suggest that you avoid this hotel for one huge reason - amazingly filthy floors in the rooms. I can honestly say they were so dirty I felt that there might be a health risk. More below... I choose to book this hotel based on high reviews on Trip Advisor. Since we were travelling with our 11 month old so, when booking I requested three things that were needed: a fridge, a tub and a king bed. We booked an executive room and these items were confirmed in my reservation. Upon check-in I immediately noticed that we only had a shower stall, so I reported that and we were moved to a new room. Not on the executive floor (where the executive lounge/workspace was), but a suitable room. Only a mild inconvenience and short disturbance. Once in the new room, we discovered a toilet that sounded like a jumbo jet's engine when flushed. We were off to dinner so I reported that at the front desk and they said they would have someone look at it while we were out. Upon our return at about 10pm, I checked in with the desk about the toilet. They called and spoke to the repairman who said that it was broken but they did not have the part necessary to fix it. They asked if I wanted to moved again, but they could not find a suitable room while I was waiting. It was already past my son's bedtime and we needed to give him a bath and get him down, so I said I would call them shortly from the room and in the meantime, I asked that they try and figure something out. Once back in the room, my wife found the tub to be dirty (pubic hairs from a prior guest). Our frustration level was rising, but we had to get our son to sleep, so she washed the tub herself and I knew I would mention it when I called down. When my wife picked up our son for his bath, we found his hands and feet to be black. We considered the day, where we had been, where we might have put him down, etc. and were confused. Then we considered the room. I grabbed a white wash cloth from the bathroom and a simple, light swipe across the floor revealed it to be filthy. A black streak was on the cloth. I checked multiple places in the room and found the same condition. Finally, I called the front desk. At this point, I explained, we had been given the wrong room and a new room with a broken toilet, a dirty bathtub and a floor so dirty we could not bring ourselves to take our socks off, much less put our son on the floor. My room was comped at that point, without hesitation I must add, and I was offered another room. My concern now, however, was that no one knew anything about a carpet cleaning schedule - I wanted to avoid the same issue in a new room or just leave that night. It was suggested that a go into the other rooms with the person in charge of housekeeping and choose my room. She escorted me into three different rooms, all of which I found to have dirty carpets as well (I used the same cloth test in each room). It was after 11pm and I knew we would not complete our 3 night stay at this hotel, but did not wish to uproot my now-sleeping family. When morning came, we packed up and left this hotel. I must again say that the staff was very helpful and understanding. In fact, a few offered that they were as disgusted as I was. Of the number of people that helped me, thank you to Tiffany and Theresa (I might be confusing this as actually being one person - whomever seemed in charge behind the desk that night) and the rest of the desk staff, and Bertha, the housekeeper. However, no amount of customer service can clean a carpet or get my to put my son on the floor of that hotel ever again. I should add that we wondered how often this floor condition might be the case in other hotels and we just never noticed. Well, our trip included two more hotels, neither of which had this issue at all.

text: House of Jin (HOJ) is a real gem which seems a bit out of place in Germantown. I lived around the corner for a few years, and even though I have since moved a few miles away, I still go back to HOJ once in a while because it has left a lasting impression on me. It rivals a lot of the upscale downtown Asian eateries in a lot of ways. Food - Solid B+. Not every dish on the menu will knock your socks off, but for the most part, they are above average, and sometimes everything is just amazing and you forget you aren't on restaurant row. I fell in love with Phoenix rolls at HOJ, and while occasionally I'll find good ones elsewhere, HOJ makes them just right for my tastes. I think the presentation of the dishes is one of the things that elevates the dining experience beyond what one might expect. Service - Always attentive. This is one of those places where you are always compelled to tip well. If you ever have a meal that doesn't meet your expectations, you can't say it is because the waitstaff didn't try hard enough. Sometimes it can be a bit much when the restaurant is relatively empty and the servers are watching your every move, but if you become a regular, they are like family to you, and you don't feel like you are under the microscope all the time. Ambience - Surprisingly OK. Located on the south end of Chelten Ave, the exterior fits in pretty well with the surroundings. That is to say, while it's not run-down, it's nothing to write home about, and whitebread suburbanite metrophobes might have some anxiety as they pull into the parking lot. Once inside, the lighting and decor are very inviting, regardless of whether you are the only patron or if it's a full house. Overall, I guess you could say I have a soft spot for House of Jin. It's not perfect, and sometimes I feel as if they are trying too hard, but if you are in the area I say give it a shot--I bet you will be pleasantly surprised. I have had to do some convincing to get friends and family from the 'burbs to give HOJ a chance, and I have no regrets whatsoever.

text: Sushi Time is a great choice for all you can eat sushi in the Sparks area. The sushi chefs, waiters and waitresses, and owner are all very friendly. The fish is fresh, there's a decent variety of rolls, and the price is about middle of the road for all you can eat. If you want a sushi place where you'll feel welcome and everybody knows your name, Sushi time is the place to go. The owner is extremely friendly and will actually sit down and talk to you to see how you're doing, especially if you're a regular. The same can also be said about the waiters and waitresses. The sushi chefs all have their own personalities and quirks but all friendly. Fresh fish is a necessity when it comes to sushi, and Sushi Time delivers with some of the freshest fish around. The nigiri is pretty standard fare as far as sushi places go, but you'll find some nice things like surf clam that not all the local sushi restaurants have and some of the best mussels in town. Their regular menu for hand and long rolls is also fairly pedestrian, but where Sushi Time shines is in their chef's specials menu. The chef's specials menu eclipses the regular menu many times over in terms of variety. On the specials menu, there's something for everyone. You run the gamut of fried rolls, raw rolls, and sashimi. It's not every sushi restaurant in the Reno-Sparks area that you can get that. Along with the good comes the bad. With the economy the way it is, everyone is hurting. Sushi Time is no different and they have started to noticeably increase the amount of rice used in nigiri, hand rolls, and long rolls. There lacks consistency amongst the chefs in sushi preparation. As far as the standard menu goes, everything is about the same from chef to chef, but ever since the chef's specials menu was introduced about a year or so ago, the same item on that menu varies wildly from chef to chef. It wouldn't be so bad if it was just each chef adding an extra bit of personal flair to the sushi, but sometimes the chefs are caught unaware of what the roll is. The chefs should get together and have a meeting on the preparation of all the rolls on the chef's specials menu to really bring it together. It would seem like there's a lot of bad things to say about Sushi Time, but I'm just being extremely nitpicky. It's a fine restaurant that has fantastic sushi and makes you feel welcome. I've been a customer since the place opened and go nearly every week, and I haven't been disappointed yet. What have you got to lose? Give them a try!

Lovin' caters to the crowd who wants home style goodness loading down their stomachs with heavy duty burgers, sandwiches, dinners, and sides. That's not to say you can't get light food here, but they really shine with the mock meats. On top of all of that the decor is cozy. So many people are turned off by the vegetarian/vegan lifestyle by having to go to some co-op restaurant and eating next to kids with dreads down to their knees, lip rings, and a "insert political statement here" shirt. The beauty part of Lovin' is that all kinds of people meet to eat here. Yes there are the above mentioned types who dine there, but more often than not it's people who are just popping in on their lunch hour. Professionals, retirees, college students, and people with serious health restrictions all come to Lovin' for some lovin'. Peg (the owner) has done more for the cause of vegetarianism/veganism in Tucson than any amount of sign waving and slogan shouting could do. I highly recommend checking this place out and look out for franchises to open in the future. Is it the best food you will ever eat? Simply, no. Is it the best meat substitution you will ever eat? We don't know too many people in Tampa, and weren't sure about hiring a complete stranger to come into our home and care for our pets, but because we would be gone for so long, we weren't left with a lot of options. I am SO glad I took the chance and hired them! Veronica came to our apartment prior to our trip, and met with us and the cats. She seemed very nice and I immediately felt at ease with the situation. Once we had left, she sent us a text message after every visit, reassuring us that all was well at home. It really couldn't have worked out better...I had so much other stress involved with a wedding, that it was nice not to have to worry about what was going on at home. We will definitely use their services in the future. Seriously, if you are looking around for a pet sitting service, please consider Tailored Pet Sitting. I know how risky it seems having someone you don't know enter your home and look after your beloved pet, but believe me, they will gain your trust, and you will not be sorry! I joined Yelp just for the sole purpose of leaving them a great review, if that gives you any indication of how pleased we were with their services. Thank you, Veronica!!

As we circled around the different food vendors, I kept passing by the nondescript Basic 4 Vegetarian Snack stand. It looked so unassuming, kind of sparse, and the nice ladies were walking back and forth albeit not taking orders because there weren't many customers to serve. My sister settled for some Cajun food and I grabbed a veggie chili cheeseburger. Oh my. I stuffed my face. Because this is the best fake-burger I ever had!!! It was a little steep for a "chili burger," (around $6-$7), but it was huge. And delicious. Two co-occurring adjectives that supersede price. text: This is an amazing dessert place but a word of advice if you're going to sit outside: spray Deet or some other bug spray. We sat in a dark corner table on the patio and I had about 23+ mosquito bites on my legs the next day. Some of them could have been from elsewhere, but I definitely felt the nasty critters on me the whole night and now have polka dot legs to prove it. Anyway, moving on to the good stuff. Their ice-cream martinis are da bomb. Yeah, I'm bringing back 2003. DA. BOMB. Gooey, vodka-y goodness. The Bailey's is decadent deliciousness and my special, tiramisu, tasted JUST like a liquid tiramisu. Not as enthralled by the Eve's Apple, but that's more because apple desserts don't really do it for me. My friend and I are obsessed with Port Salut cheese, so she caved and ordered a cheese plate. Lots of great accompaniments, definitely not enough cheese. They gave such a thin slice I wondered if they were being cheap. So, I probably would have given this place 3, 3.5 stars for the bugs, the slow service, the slightly underwhelming dessert list (thought it'd be more unique), and the way too-little amount of cheese, but a few things kicked it up to 4. First, the ice-cream martinis: no complaints. Second, the atmosphere. It's the perfect place for a date, a girls night out, a family reunion, etc. The interior is all dark, candlelit, red-hued Moulin Rouge-esque loveliness complete with real red roses at the tables. The exterior (keeping in mind the bugs) is open and cheery with lots of strung lights. Wish we we had a unique place like this in Boston (and Finale definitely doesn't count!).

text: Pub and Kitchen, I can finally cross you off my list of new places to eat at. I can now add you to the list of disappointing spots that I'm unlikely to ever visit again. My sister, Laura, was visiting this weekend and we went out for dinner. I gave her a few places to pick from, and I was happy when she chose Pub and Kitchen. It's a swanky little spot at 20th and Lombard. They don't take reservations, so we had to wait around at the bar until a seat opened outside and we could enjoy the beautiful weather. The tap list here isn't great; they have English beers on to go with the pub feeling, but I'd rather just have some stuff that is better and reasonably priced. I drank Thomas Hooker IPA, which was good and is actually pretty rare to see on tap. The service here was poor. We waited too long at the bar for drinks and our table service was slow as well. The worst part is that all of the servers are dressed like the clients, making it difficult to flag down anyone to help you. The atmosphere here is kind of annoying. It's darker, more crowded, and louder than it should be. If I wanted that, I go to any number of bars that I like better. The one good thing is the outdoor seating, because there isn't much car traffic passing by to annoy you as you eat. The bar has a few TVs, but they're all on the same spot. I wouldn't recommend this place if you're actually trying to watch anything, but if you want a baseball game on in the background, you'll probably be in luck. The one saving grace here could be the food. I had read great things about the Windsor burger before coming, and was excited to eat it. My medium rare burger was properly cooked, and came out with cheddar and bacon. Nothing I ate seemed flavorful enough; everything was lacking. The entire meal was forgettable. Pub and Kitchen also overlooked the importance of good bread on a burger. The portions here are pretty good, and the table next to us had the cheese platter and oysters which looked like decent appetizers. They also looked like you could get better elsewhere. Bottom Line: Meh.
label: NEG

text: Fast food serves two purposes in my life. The first is for ridicule & scorn. The ungodly portions, non-existent nutritional value and overall harm it does to our society are just a few of the reasons I loathe these zits on the culinary ass of America. Hypocritically enough, the second is income. My main client at work is McDonalds. If you've heard any McD's radio in St. Louis, I wrote it. So, there's one reason my invitation to heaven will get lost in the mail. A few times a year, the urge strikes and I must be reminded why I hate it so much. Last night was one of those times. It was about 11pm, my gut was groanin' & the debit card machine was busted at McDonalds. I pulled into Jack in the Box to see what all the fuss was about. Holy shit people. This was the slowest, most obnoxious, goopiest, limp-fried experience of my life. It took roughly eight hours to make it through the drive-thru. So much for the fast. The headset chick was snippy to the woman in front of me. After repeating her order wrong three times, the headset chick finally got it right but shoved a giant, steaming pile of Sarcasm through the speaker. The actual "food" part was a pretty sad experience. There's got to be an incredible demand for cholesterol & saturated fat because every sandwich on the burger side had at least two patties, two pieces of cheese and two strips of bacon. I found the only single burger on the menu. Here's a question, do they really need to put a whole tub of mayo on the burgers? Skip the trip to Costco & just get your mayo for the year at the drive-thru. Isn't it a cardial sin to serve limp dick fries at a fast food establishment? I believe Jesus said to Ronald himself, "Always serve crispy fries, my clown son." If so, then Jack & I will be side by side in hell for the rest of eternity. But what do you expect for $4.38 at 11pm? If Whole Foods was open, I would've gladly driven over to Brentwood and crawled into their salad bar. Let the routine repeat iself. It'll be six - eight months before the urge strikes again and I'll have forgotten about how bad this place was. "It won't be so bad", I'll reassure myself. "What other choice do I have?" I'll ask. Future Mike, It will be that bad and you do have a choice - go home and rummage through the composter. See you in February.
label: NEG

text: I am pretty sure a guy took me here on a date once....it was funny because he said "well I looked at your facebook and I discovered you liked sushi so...." little did he know I am a sushi maniac?!?!?! text: Personally, I hate when restaurants pick too many kinds of food to "specialize" in. Invariably, you end up with a ton of mediocre food, instead of a smaller number of well-made dishes. Pan-Asian? Just think of how many countries and cuisines that encompasses. So yeah, Zoe is a nice restaurant, pretty plating, flavor combinations that sound interesting on paper, but the actual dishes pale in comparison to what you would get at a restaurant that actually served Thia, or Indian, or whatever kind of food. I had the wok-seared salt shrimp with mango yogurt sauce. Sounds good, right? The waiter warned me that the shrimp were meant to be eaten with the shells still on. Ok, no problem. I could do without the little legs and things, but whatever, I'm adventurous. Except that the flavors of the cooking couldn't penetrate the shells, so the outsides tasted great, and the insides were totally bland and pointless. One of my companions had the curried chicken, and it was completely nondescript. I think it was supposed to be a Thai-style curry, but it was so generic, they only way you could tell was from the peanut sauce. text: We recently stayed here over a holiday weekend. Admittedly, it was not our first choice but after seeing the ridiculous prices at the downtown hotel locations, we figured we'd give this hotel a try. I've stayed in boutique hotels in the past and have really enjoyed them. Well, Hotel Indigo certainly did not disappoint. We were able to get rooms for almost $100 less than what the others were charging. Sure, we were not in the downtown area, but we'd already been there and done that on previous trips so this location in the Central West End was fine. Another great feature was that they have FREE parking & it's also walking distance to nearest Metro station which we used to get to the Edward Jones Dome. The hotel is small and there is not much of a lobby to speak of. As others have mentioned, the bar & café area were a little deserted. However, we didn't come on vacay to hang out in the hotel, so as long as the bed was comfortable and the bathroom was clean, that is all that mattered. We were greeted by friendly staff and check-in was quick and smooth and we got a very clean and modern room. The walls were brightly painted and the décor was in good taste. The bed was really comfortable and the linens were impeccably clean. I really liked that the room had wood flooring - seemed much cleaner than the shady carpet you can find in some hotels. Also, there was a comfortable chair with a large ottoman as well as a roomy desk with a very ergonomic chair. Free wireless Internet too! The gym was decent - it had several pieces of equipment and treadmills that had TVs and it was well stocked with clean towels. There is also a nice outdoor patio in the back of the hotel with large tables and chairs. However, no one was out there on the nights we peeked out there. I think it would help if the hotel had some good lighting out there, even some plants, etc. to make it more inviting. It has potential! The main issue I had with Hotel Indigo, as with most people on here, was the tiny bathroom. You'll have to schedule who gets to use the sink at a certain hour in the morning to get ready because 2 people in the bathroom is not possible. Also, it was a little annoying that the bathroom fan (which was really loud) came on every time the bathroom light was turned on; it'd be nice to have a separate switch for this. And, you'll have to get creative to shave your legs in the tiny shower stall with nowhere to place your feet. I perfected my standing-on-one-foot balancing act while on this trip. What stops me from giving this place a 5-star rating is the small bathroom but it certainly is not a deal breaker by any means. The location is really great. You are steps from the gorgeous Cathedral Basilica, Forest Park, as well as all of the cute clothing boutiques, restaurants, and cool bars lining Euclid Avenue. Also, the price and the room as a whole definitely outweigh the cons of the bathroom. I am hoping this place makes it (seemed a little empty for a holiday weekend) because I'd love to come back here on our next visit to STL.

text: [This review covers both Pat's and Geno's, so it's posted at both pages.] So for some reason, my crazy friend, Elliott, and his friend, Bill, decided to drive from Richmond, VA to my house (oh, probably about 5 hours) Saturday morning to go into Philadelphia for cheesesteaks. Why? To put the ages-old debate between Pat's King of Steaks and Geno's Steaks to rest once and for all... Not that the debate will ever really die... We ended up hitting Pat's first, then trekking all over the city, only to return to Geno's before heading home. Gotta work off the calories, yanno! In the end we all came to pretty much the same conclusion. Overall Pat's really is the King of Steaks. Geno's decor was overwhelming and gaudy. We did not find the giant picture of a cheesesteak surrounded by flashing neon lights on the roof to be particularly endearing and certainly did not add to the flavor of the sandwiches. The bright neon orange slathered all over every possible paintable surface did not help, either. I greatly preferred and appreciated the understated and unassuming simplicity of the decor (or lack thereof) that we found at Pat's. They still had what looked like the original Pepsi sign with their name. We were also taunted by a 10 year old walking by with a Geno's cup while we were minding our own business, sitting on the curb eating our steaks. None of us appreciated the blatant politics of Geno's either. For those unaware of the controversy, a few years ago Geno's was sued for having a sign on their window that said "This is America, Speak English when ordering!!"... While I acknowledge their right to have whatever signs broadcasting whatever politics to which they ascribe, I find the hypocrisy of their Italian heritage coupled with their obvious prejudices to be quite distasteful. On to the actual food. The rolls from both place were exactly the same. More bread than meat - first bite: all bread. The onions at Pat's were actually fried, with that caramelized color and flavor I like in my onions (when on a cheesesteak, that is). Geno's onions seemed to have been lightly fried, more from incidental contact. They were still so crunchy that they were almost fresh. Not that I mind fresh onions, but fried onions aren't supposed to have that fresh-onion zing. They're supposed to be fried. The cheese. I could barely taste the cheese at Geno's. I opted for provolone, while my companions opted for the orange cheese-snot product called Cheez-Whiz. Pat's was generous with their provolone and the steak was hot enough to actually melt it before I was able to sink my teeth into it. Initially my companions did complain about the Whiz oozing out of the sandwich and onto the paper, but after eating at Geno's they realized that having enough Whiz to *taste*, much less have ooze out of the sandwich was a blessing, not a curse. Finally, the steak. This is the one point that we did have to give to Geno's. Pat's steak was shredded, more or less, which is really the way every cheesesteak I've had is. I have no complaints at all about shredded steak, however Geno's steak was sliced, so it actually maintained the classic "steak" texture, more reminiscent of roast beef than typical cheesesteak. This is really more about the style of cheesesteak than the quality. Though Geno's sliced style was a bit tastier, it wasn't what I think of when I think of a true Philly Cheesesteak. All in all I prefer the cheesesteak experience I found at Pat's King of Steaks. The fries were delicious (though I didn't try the fries at Geno's, I suspect they're about the same), the line moved faster, the onions weren't overwhelming, but just added to the sandwich, the cheese was tastier and meltier, and the whole experienced oozed real, authentic Philadelphia culture. If you want a taste of what Philadelphia really is all about, I'd recommend Pat's King of Steaks.

My lovely date and I had the arroncini which were undistinguished and bathed in a seriously pedestrian tomato sauce. Certainly nothing that would impress you at a run of the mill chain much less a Steven Starr, much hyped, pizzeria. The seafood salad was good enough but given the proximity of the italian market, nothing I can't buy and have at home with zero preparation (ok ok, so I overstate the case...I'd have to cut olives and boil potatoes. sheesh). But on to the main event...why we were there...the pizza. We went for the egg/truffle amazing sounding 'za. It wasn't. The toppings had way too much liquied leaving a soggy crust that provided no contrast to an undercooked egg. It was way oversalted. And frankly if you can't get a wow with fallback ingredients like truffles...maybe you should quit while you are behind. I did see some tasty looking other options - pepperoni, pistachio/red onion, but the crust itself was the real problem here. Obviously it is not easy to do what the few great places do (Lombardi's anyone?) or more would, but I had hoped that the backing of a perfectionist like Starr would have yielded better results. Guess I'll hop a bus to NYC when I want pizza that is up to snuff. Screw it. I'll fly to Rome.
label: NEG

text: I used to drink the kool-aid too. Ikea used to be God's gift to man. The other day I found myself unplugged from the Matrix. I went there with my roommate to pick up a few items. A shelf she wanted was "located" in a bin that didn't exist. After waiting in a long line, they finally provided her with a slip that would allow for her to pay for it up front and then pick it up at the place near the exit. Well, we had to wait in a line where there was a real register operator because of her purchase order. There was only one line. The person in front of us also had a purchase order, but the machine that processes it was broken. We waited about 15 minutes just to get up to being checked out. Then, as you could imagine, my roommate encountered a similar problem -- add another 10 minutes onto my time in line. (While all of this was going on, a second line was finally opened. But, they took everyone from the BACK of our line and they could only pay with credit cards -- no cash. Good job Ikea.) Now it came my turn. I had a very large shelf for myself in my cart and when I went to present it to the cashier, it was discovered that there was no bar code. I worked in retail for over five years, and whenever that happened at one of my jobs, it was my responsibility to get on the phone and have another employee come and get a new one for the customer or just look it up. Instead, the cashier informed me that I should go get another one myself! It gets worse.... Then, she reminded me that I had to GET BACK IN LINE. That's right, the same line that I just wasted over 25 minutes of my life in. I asked to speak to a manager at this point. Instead of calling one over, she pointed to a desk where I could find one myself. Guess what? That desk had another huge line at it. So, I nixed the manager and decided to just get the heck out of this hell hole. I retrieved a shelf with a bar code and dutifully waited in line again. FINALLY, I was able to check out and I joined my roommate in the waiting area. She was STILL waiting for her number to be called even though there was only ONE other customer that was being waited on. At this point, I went up to a desk and got very firm with them, insisting upon speaking to a manager. Can you imagine, they actually LAUGHED AT ME when I explained the problem?!?!?! I finally managed to get a manager and he very slowly corrected the problem and got my roommate her shelf. I understand that Ikea is low priced and low priced for a reason. But, come on people. This is a little too much. I'd rather pay 10 more dollars at target in order to avoid another headache like this. It took us over 45 minutes to exit Ikea after we began our stay in line. That is NEVER acceptable for a retail outlet. Stop drinking the kool-aid people!

text: This place is one of the cheapest vets (compared to Penn Vet and the other clinic in Center City) you can go to and it's very accessible from center city. I took both my kittens here when I first adopted them and the receptionist is super nice. They also try to fit you in as soon as possible but I've always had to wait at least 20 minutes each time I've gone with an appointment. They will accommodate you if you have an emergency, however. The doctor here is very nice but she doesn't seem to be very thorough when there is a slightly more complicated problem (when I ask her a lot of questions, the answers get more vague and uncertain). They also don't work every day for the same hours so you have to make an appointment to know what hours they'll be there. There are always other people waiting in the waiting room so at least you have company. The doctor provided us with plenty of prescription-only Hill's wet food that is very high in calories for our dying 4-month old kitten that we adopted at 1.5 lbs. Unfortunately (read my review on Rittenhouse Pet Supply), after he recovered from his Upper respiratory infection and gained 4 pounds, we got him neutered (not at Cat Vet) and he came back with Ringworm (hair loss and scabbing on his nose and near his ears). The doctor predicted it was ringworm so she took a skin culture to make sure, which costs a lot and the test, some medication and the visit cost over $200. (There are discounts for bringing more than 1 cat in and if it is a subsequent visit, and I feel like they provide discounted fees for students...not much though.) I don't know why the doctor provided us with a shampoo to use 3x a week over the course of 2 months (cats DETEST water and will often claw their way out of the tub to get away) and failed to tell us that there were pill alternatives, so we tried the shampoo and an ointment, all of which were very difficult to use (if you have cats, you should know what I mean). We ended up buying the pills which actually can be grounded up into a liquid form for even easier application and they had to be shipped to us, all for $90 for 2 cats. There was enough medicine for probably 5 cats so we were kinda pissed. Overall, a very frustrating and expensive experience. Cat Vet provides in-home care for cats with very serious problems like kidney failure. They also do neuterings and spayings. The assistant is very nice but I don't completely trust her or the doctor's judgment because I didn't feel like I got great care or answers for my cats' ailments or my questions. As long as my pets stay relatively healthy though, this place is fine. I got Frontline or the equivalent from Cat Vet and they seem to have lots of other types of supplies on hand. The rooms and the whole place in general are pretty dingy though.
label: NEG

text: Island Way Grill is so heavily promoted on a variety of Clearwater Beach and Florida tourism websites, in hotel tourist magazines, in airline magazines, and a variety of online reviews, but I was SHOCKED to find that no one had yet reviewed it here. So here goes.... Summary: Dinner for 6 on post-Christmas Eve (12.26) was a visual and culinary delight but a service NIGHTMARE. An excellent wine list (when you can find one they ACTUALLY have), delicious and fresh sushi, and a broad menu of pacific rim and carribbean island selections may allow you to forgive the unprofessional and uninformed wait staff. Detail: This well-designed restaurant, located in a prime location on the causeway leading to Clearwater Beach, offers a variety of steak, seafood and even sushi to satisfy nearly every family members appetite. The restaurant is large and very attractive. It has an open kitchen area and sushi bar located just past the main entrance, plus several beautiful dining areas which seat over 300. Island Way also features a large outdoor dining area overlooking the harbor, with waterfront bar. You can even arrive via boat, with docking slips to accommodate even large (40') boats. Arriving just before 8:00pm for our reservation Saturday night in our 20' powerboat, we were only 1 of 2 boats to take advantage of docking slips. However, that was not an indicator for the attendance at the restaurant. The place was packed! We felt that 8pm was a reasonable time to dine, but apparently the peak seating is between 6 and 7:30pm. 8:00pm seemed to be the last seating of the night. After first being seating in the back corner of their "harbor" room, we waited 20 minutes, never being asked once for a drink, offered water, or bread. At that point I returned to the hostess and asked to be reseated in the main dining room, where a few tables had now opened up. We shuffled over to our new seats, and after about 5 minutes, our server, Linda, apologized for our wait and told us that she would return in a few minutes to take our drink order. 15 minutes later... and now 45 minutes after we first arrived, we finally received our drinks. Island Way was featuring a "Wine Deals" page on their menu, with the intent of clearing out their wine cellar. As a fan of Zinfandels, I selected a mid-range bottle. Unfortunately, when Linda returned with our first (and only) round of drinks, she informed me that the particular wine was not available. As my family placed their dinner orders, I selected another Zin and my dinner order as well. Alas, Zin was not meant to be for me. Linda returned again to inform me that no Zinfandels were available from the Wine Deals menu. Unfortunately, she had failed to find an available alternative, leaving me to once again scour the 300+ bottle list for another selection. I chose a Malbec, an Argentinean cousin to the Bordeaux. Island Way promotes itself as a great steak, seafood and sushi restaurant and our table ordered each of their specialties. Our appetizer plate featured a selection of various sushi, including a dragon roll, spicy tuna roll and a firecracker roll. All of them were delicious. All of our dinner selections were quite good and dessert also met with our liking.

I would call them sort of "rockstar cool" brands. They have also like Triple Five Soul, etc. They do carry some of the more common boutique brands too, though most of the stuff looks very unique for Nashville. The small two floor store was very stylishly designed by the owner personally. The owner himself can often be seen working in the store personally. The store is tucked in a small but fashionable area called Elliston Place which is on the other side of Vanderbilt from Hillsboro Village, another street with a few boutique stores. Elliston Place is sometimes called Nashville's "Rock Block" because there are several live music bars nearby. Down the street there is a day spa, a couple of cool restaurants, and Nashville's only privately owned 24/hr cafe called Cafe Coco (on a side street) that is popular with the Vanderbilt students and young club crowd (on weekends).

text: I was having dinner with a "foodie" friend who wanted to try out SLeeK because of the Keller name attached to it. To be honest, I don't know Hubert Keller from Colonel Sanders but I imagine he must have a TV show or something. Either way, knowing that it was a steakhouse in a casino, I had an idea of what the atmosphere would be like and, sadly, I was not disappointed. Though I said that I am not a foodie I would have to admit to being somewhat of a restaurant snob. I like small, local, places with charm. I like places that are St. Louis owned. In short, I had no business being at SLeeK. But I digress. To SLeeK's credit, the food was good. I had a steak with asparagus and green beans and the strawberry souffle for dinner. Though the steak was slightly overcooked (I guess medium is a moving target), it was one of the best I have had in St. Louis. The souffle was excellent and I think the bread alone would be worth the trip. Now, if only the wait staff could live up to the quality of the food. As other reviewers have noted, the waiters try to upsell you on everything. No, I don't think you have to spend $60+ on a bottle of wine to get something that is drinkable and for what it's worth, if you really think 2 different Chiantis are "no good," don't put them on the wine list. What's worse is that it was like this for everything from sauces to dessert and when we turned something down, our waiter seemed to be perturbed. I get it, it's a casino so you're more worried about getting every last dollar from the out of towners rather than making repeat customers but please, Chef Keller, this is your brand. Perhaps this explains why the place was pretty empty on a Saturday night which could be bad for long term solvency but good for getting a table without a reservation. Price-wise, SLeeK is not too bad if you can manage to refuse the onslaught of upsells. It is probably on par with other upscale places in St. Louis (Niche, Sidney St., etc.) but in the end this is a place where you come for the food and leave because of the experience. The fact that it is owned by an out of town chef and located in a casino also makes you think of where you are putting your money. text: SAY CHEEEEESE!!! This is a case of rounding up from 3.5 to 4 stars. Most of them are college girls calculated to guarantee male patrons will drool at the sight of them in miniskirts, and so they skate by giving somewhat dubious customer service. Servers run the gamut from poor to excellent. While not each and every one of them are beauty kings and queens, I get the impression that Melting Pot values a server's attractiveness more than any other attribute and this is a grave error because servers here spend a fair amount of time at your table preparing your fondue. It's much more important that they simply be well-groomed and in possession of a pleasing personality since they kind of live at your table. After the 4th time I came here, and the 2nd time in a row I was stuck with a cranky, bimbo server who failed to bring more bread, or to accommodate not overly complex requests of any sort, or to give us timely service, or to give us even friendly service, I went on the Melting Pot's website and complained. Within a couple of days I received an email from the restaurant manager asking for my mailing address so that she could send me a freebie cheese fondue! Very cool. I love quick service based on the assumption that "the customer is always right" because 90% of the time, the customer is right. Melting Pot is quite expensive for what it is, but I understand that new locations cost 2 million dollars or more to get up and running. I was quite impressed by the owner who has gone through extensive training by the Melting Pot chain, and owns several of their restaurants in Western States. Parking is great, and that's a big plus since women may wish to wear high heels when dining here. The cheese and desert fondues are excellent. The salads are pricey, but very good. I recommend skipping the meat fondues as they take forever to cook and are messy. Besides, in this low light, it's hard to tell whether your chicken is cooked through or not. If you like the food, join their club because you get a coupon for a free desert fondue. Sometimes they run specials and will email out coupons for those too.

text: I have finally experienced the awesomeness that is Xochitl. Reluctantly, after several seasons of passing up on Restaurant Week, I decided to give the promotion another shot. Xochitl has made me a believer again. My friend and I arrived slightly early for our 7 p.m. resie but we were escorted to a table immediately. Our water glasses were filled and bread was dropped off with two buttery spreads. Our server, whose name escapes me, was wonderful throughout the experience. When she asked to take our drink order and I handed over the recipe for a "Skinnygirl Margarita," she didn't bat an eye although she did let me know that their regular margaritas are made only with tequila, fresh lime juice and a little bit of simple syrup. No sour mix, no triple sec, no hidden agendas; just honest ingredients, served over ice, with a rim of salt. I ended up taking her word for it. (For the record, one Skinnygirl plus two positively delicious Xochitl margs equals three sheets to the wind, minus any trace of a stomachache, which I almost always get when I drink margaritas anywhere else. Hallelujah!) The food was glorious. For our first course, we both chose the tortilla soup. Large bowls containing cubes of cheese, slices of avocado, tortilla strips and dried peppers were presented to both of us. The broth was poured on top, tableside. I really enjoyed this dish, although my friend and I agreed that the dried peppers had a curious taste. She didn't like them, I was intrigued by them. Next, we both ordered the octopus, mackerel and shrimp ceviche trio. Each was served atop a little fried tortilla round. I have been daydreaming about the octopus ceviche since I awoke this morning. It was easily the most tender, well flavored octopus I have had (sorry, Mr. Garces). For my entrée, I chose the squid hot pot, which was another win. When the lid was removed from the pot, tender rings of squid in a spicy tomato sauce appeared before us. I have to say, the dramatic presentations really made the dining experience special. The woman seated next to me ordered a stuffed pepper that was so beautiful it could have easily been pictured in a food magazine. Meanwhile, at our table, my friend had food envy as she was experiencing mixed feelings about her skirt steak (which I thought was good, although it was served lukewarm). For dessert, my friend had the churros, which came with three dipping sauces. One of my favorite things in life is the right to choose several condiments to go with a meal and this presentation was right up my alley. Fortunately, I had my own dessert to tackle; an appropriately sized mini chocolate soufflé with a mini scoop of cajeta ice cream alongside. Perfection. Our experience last night wasn't just great by Restaurant Week standards; it was great by any night's standards. What a truly fantastic meal. When our bill was dropped, along with a plate of mini biscotti (delish, by the way), we were also each given a $10 card to use any time before November 31. My dining companion and I are already discussing what we will order on our return visit!

text: This restaurant is located inside the Inn at Chester Springs. First off it's a restaurant within a hotel/motel, which already puts it at a serious disadvantage. For starters they had mixed greens salad which was fresh and delicious, a mozzarella salad, breads and chilled shrimp. The chilled shrimp where the medium-small size and they had a really off/chlorine taste to them. Fortunately I only took a few of the shrimp. For entrees they had a cook to order station with choice of pasta, toppings and sauces. They also had a chicken dish, tilapia in a butter cream sauce and prime rib. The sides were mashed potatoes, squash and a few other typical sides. The pasta was so-so. The chicken was the same. The big stars of the night were the tilapia, the prime rib and the mashed potatoes as all were delicious. My wife even commented that the tilapia and the mashed potatoes were amazing. The desserts were in a word, horrible. It was painfully obvious from just looking at them that they were the mass manufactured type (you know, the kind that taste like Little Debbie) and not at all fresh. We sampled a few between my wife and I but were disappointed by it all. The service was half decent and friendly, though not exceptional. This is a fairly benign place that I think wishes it was more than it is but just doesn't have the tools to quite get there. text: I was in Indy on business. Staying downtown, I noticed at least three breweries in easy walking distance - Alcatraz, Ram (right across the street) and Rock Bottom. I generally stay away from Rock Bottom, and when I did some research I found that Ram was more of a chain than Alcatraz, which only has one sister restaurant in California. So I figured that Alcatraz would have better beer and food, even though it looks a little cheesier from the outside, with the corny "best beer behind bars" tagline. Well, I don't know how the fare is at Ram, but the beer and food at Alcatraz were decidedly mediocre. The best beer was their Searchlight. While it was light, it was considerably more flavorful than most American light beer. After that, I would put their American stout (can't recall the name), which was more hoppy than an Irish stout, but that's why they call it American. The pale ale was harsh with little of that delicious citrus hop aroma that's so good in Cali pale ales. The "alt beer" was totally mislabeled. If anything it was actually a Stuck beer, that is a strong alt beer. The syrupy notes and overhopping may have been equally excessive, but it did not add up to a balanced beer. The American wheat was alright, and my problems with it (fizzy, thin body, lack of banana-clove aromas) are more a complaint against the style - the German-style wheat beers are much more interesting than most American-style ones. And the Rock Bock was bland, with a syrupy body standing in for the grainy malt flavors that abound in a good bock; it was also, to my taste, underhopped. Now for the fish tacos. Bland chunks of fish with neither interesting coating or a grilled flavor, without enough cabbage to add solid texture to the taco. And the rice - it looked and tasted like it came from a can. Salty, vaguely tomatoey, and very institutional. Hot sauce saved it. The staff, on the other hand, were great, and the bartender who served me deserves kudos from the management for being as enthusiastic as he was for food and drink that are so underpar.

The left side of the restaurant has a neighborhood bar feel and lots of regulars to keep it filled. They serve decent burgers and pub grub. and they have a decent patio out front. But, as a Greek restaurant, they fail. The hummus is some of the worst I've had, the tzatziki is also weak and bland. The dolmades taste like they come from a can, the spinach rice is overpowering, and the spanikopita and cheese pies are not fresh. The filo is chewy and tastes like it is made days ahead and nuked prior to serving. The Mediterranean mixed veggies were pure mush. So, all things considered, I don't understand why they are priced higher than most of the Greek restaurants in the area. The right side of the restaurant is completely odd and dated. First, you have to trek past the open station where they dump all of the food and dirty dishes in order to get to your table. They built a wooden room within a room that has lattice rafters up by the ceiling and it is ladened with dated would accents throughout. This "room within a room" wastes a ton of space in the restaurant and it is butt ugly. The light fixtures are big, obtrusive monsters from the '70's and I honestly think they haven't been cleaned since they were installed. Most of the bulbs are burnt out. Look up when you are eating and notice the splattered food and cobwebs in the pendant lights that hang over your table. Lovely. In addition, the grime is all over the wails, the artwork by the table and the condiments and table signs that sit on your table. It's a sticky, grimy, mess. The last time I was there, it took forever to get our food and while we were waiting, they stacked all of the chairs on the tables around us. How rude.
label: NEG

text: Toscana catered my wedding last weekend and they were absolutely brilliant. Three things stand out - first, Erica at Toscana is fantastic to work with, she was responsive to every question we had in planning the event and was incredibly attentive to every single detail in setting up and planning the reception. We had a difficult reception site logistically (at the deleware museum of natural history); there wasn't much time to set up and the set-up itself was quite complicated - yet everything was set up in plenty of time and looked fantastic. Second, the servers were also super helpful and took extra care to make sure the bridal party was well fed - which was greatly appreciated. Third - saving the best for last - the food was INCREDIBLE (particularly the homemade pastas and desserts) - the wedding was beautiful, the reception was fun, but in the end it was the food that people couldn't stop talking about. Many thanks to Erica and all the wonderful people at Toscana - it was a fabulous reception - couldn't be more pleased we choose them to cater it!

text: In my experience, there are not many quality restaurants to choose from in St. Albert. Luisaâs is located right in the heart of downtown, and itâs a tiny space with romantic lighting, paintings, Italian music and plenty of smaller tables for intimate meals. The food here is wonderful. You just know by the smells emanating from the restaurant. I start with red wine and their bruschetta, which is overflowing with fresh garden tomatoes, garlic, Parmesan and fresh olive oil. Sometimes I come here just for this appetizer and a coffee. If youâre having a main dish, anything with their signature tomato sauce is a safe bet. You wonât be disappointed. Prices are reasonable, and service is friendly. It has the feel of a small neighbourhood restaurant in the heart of Italy.

text: You will be disappointed. The menu items look pretty interesting and mouth watering, but they just don't deliver. We started out with the Mushroom Shrimp Dumplings - they were edible, but nothing special. I went on to have the Red Curry Shrimp as an entree. I'm not sure if this was my fault, but when i ordered, I asked of they could make a mild version of the dish. Our waitress, who was nice enough and chipper said she would check. Next time I saw her, she was serving me the dish, so I assumed my request was granted. Upon the first bite, my mouth was on fire. I know, curry is usually spicy, but I have had mild versions before. I also know that I am such a wuss when it comes to spicy food. Anyway, I had to send it back. I ordered the scallops and they were overcooked and bland. What a bummer. text: When most people think of pawn shops, they often think of skeezy, backwards places of business where they're liable to get ripped off or only find junk. Berry's seems to defy all of the stereotypes of pawn shops--it hardly even struck me as a pawn place at all. Berry's is a lot larger and more open than most pawn shops. Toward the back is a very large display case with a surprisingly large selection of cheap DVDs. They also carry dozens of rifles, shotguns and mounted deer heads. Several employees and a couple of security guys seem to be in there at all times, keeping riffraff at bay and and making sure everybody can find what they need. Berry's is especially known for its jewelry. At the front of the store, there are dozens of display cases with countless necklaces, bracelets, rings and watches of all shapes, sizes and prices. It's set up more like a Kay's or Jared than a pawn shop, and there's always an employee there to show you items. What I particularly liked about Berry's was their selection of musical instruments. Along an entire wall of the shop, there are dozens of guitars and basses (mostly brands like Ibenez, Alverez and Squire). They also carry a handful of percussion items, especially snare drums, and their selection of amps and cabinets is pretty varied. I must say, I was far more impressed with Berry"s than I expected to be.

text: The Dotty's chain isn't exactly a casino. Nor is it a restaurant. It's hard to even define it as a bar. It occupies a strange neither-region that all the other touch, but do not occupy. Imagine for a moment that your grandmother decided to open a casino in her living-room. But rather than re-design the room, she left everything as-is, and just brought in gaming video machines. But in order to bring in customers, she puts a counter at the kitchen, sells cigarettes and booze, and hires some of the most surly cashiers on the planet. That's what this place is. The customers tend to be mostly housewives who want to do a little gambling before or after picking up groceries, senior-citizen who prefer the more casual atmosphere, gamblers who can't afford other casinos (or just don't want to make the trip to downtown), gambling addicts who haven't realized they have a problem, and gamblers who've burnt their bridges elsewhere. In all of these categories, everyone smokes. I don't understand why they advertise this, as it's only food-service that the no-smoking rule applies to, but they tout all over how "smoker-friendly" they are. It's definitely not a place to go, if you're looking for a typical casino experience. As a matter of fact, unless you live within three miles of one, and fit in one of the previously described categories, there's really no reason to go.
label: NEG

text: First off, I would have given this place a 2 or a 3 but they get 1 star for their rude, unhelpful staff (sorry, were we not hipster enough for you?) and fairly dirty interior.
