Foodwise, three of us (all vegans) tried out Gianna's and we all thought it was only "okay". We ordered: - Chicken Run (vegan chicken salad sandwich) - Buffalo Freebird (vegan chicken with vegan cheese and buffalo sauce) - GG Special (vegan cheesesteak) - vegan cheesy krabby fries The Chicken Run and Buffalo Freebird were total disappointments. The "chicken" used was soggy, unseasoned TVP crumbles mixed with vegan mayo for the Chicken Run and a mediocre buffalo sauce for the Buffalo Freebird. I think the Chicken Run had a piece of lettuce in it but that's it for vegetables and no additional seasonings. The GG Special was okay but kind of boring after a few bites. The only thing that was really good was the fries, but frankly, I can get better fries and less attitude elsewhere. Should have known not even to bother after the whole vegan cheese controversy awhile back as well as rumours of their staff knowingly serving meat to vegans. text: The Pageant is a great place to go see a show. Now, with Mississippi Nights closed it is basically the only place that I'll see a show if a band or comedian comes through that I like. Between there is the pit, the place right next to the stage where you can stand, dance, and do what you please, just so long as it doesn't get you kicked out of the show for doing something utterly ridiculous. Each time I've seen a concert or comedy show at the Pageant I have always enjoyed myself, even before I was old enough to sit in the seating area. Of course when I turned the magical age I was able to stand up in the area where all the cool kids go to go. The best thing about sitting up there is the face you get a better view of the show without as much obstruction from crazy tall people standing in front of you. The Pageant is a great place to see a show. Some of the best that I've seen there are The Flaming Lips, The Killers, and The Strokes. There isn't a bad seat in the house and you can always get close enough to the band to actually see them.

text: When I go looking for a little dose of sun therapy, I tend to have low expectations. Honestly, put me in a warm bed and let me sleep for a bit, that's all I ask. I decided to visit the downtown Planet Beach before going away on a trip to mexico, and after my trip, I definitely didn't go back. I went during wintertime and the salon was absolutely filthy - the front area was totally muddy and disgusting - yet they ask you to remove your shoes. And what? Mop the floor with your stocking feet? I found this to be a problem EVERY time I visited - maybe they should invest in a door mat or an employee who can tell mud from linoleum. The pricing is a little higher than most salons and my biggest issue with them is that they don't offer minute packages - they offer session packages, or monthly packages - and it's pretty pricey for someone who isn't going to be hopping in the UV rays consistently. For a "chain" salon, the quality of the beds was sub-par (albiet better than Fabutan) but the cleanliness of the beds and the rooms was questionable. Each time I went in, there was always garbage or leftover lotion packets on the floor. The beds didn't always seem to be wiped fully (I always gave them a swipe with the provided towel before I dove in). The employees at this location aren't very engaging or seemingly knowledgable, and judging from the general cleanliness of the salon itself, not very observant (or else very apathetic). I was never asked if I had lotion or goggles with me (which in my opinion, should be mandatory for each tanner). However, I was always so busy trying to manuever around the mud monsoon in the front room, maybe they were too afraid to ask me. I don't really blame them.

text: Jackson's is another popular restaurant in the Hillsboro Village neighborhood, but not one of my personal favorites. They're very small and because of this theres almost always a wait for a table. It's hard to walk throughout the restaurant because the tables are placed so close together that free space is severely limited. I always end up never wanting to go to the restroom when I'm there just so I don't have to deal with the claustrophobic walk. Their menu features mostly lighter fare like sandwiches and paninis but they do offer some pasta dishes and other entrees. There's a distinct West coast flavor to their food, don't come here looking for comfort food items. The food is pretty good, but nothing too outstanding. Their portions are on the small side and the prices are pretty high for a sandwich. They serve brunch on Sundays, but its generally too crowded for me. They've got a full bar that'll accommodate most of your beverage needs but their drink specials aren't really exciting. The atmosphere is very laid back, and is enhanced by the artwork from local artists thats hanging on the walls. They have a small patio at the front of the building facing the street that can be nice, but 21st Avenue is generally so busy that the noise often detracts from the experience. They have a very small parking lot, so you're generally going to have to find a spot somewhere on the street. Not the best Hillsboro Village has to offer, I don't find myself coming here too often, but overall it's not a bad choice for your meal.
label: NEG

text: I'm not giving this place another cent, friends going there or not. I'll overlook that my last roll would fall apart upon picking it up, which I wouldn't even expect with a sushi guy at Albertsons, much less a legit sushi joint. Two general things to point out to management. If someone hates their job and doesn't want to work there, then get someone who would actually want to work there. Because it's quite obvious, and the bad vibes rub off directly to the customers in the form of poor service. And it's not like these are isolated incidents where it can be chalked up to having a bad day. The service hadn't affected me in my original review, but now it has. It's among the worst in the valley for sushi, or anything in general for that matter. The service at Superb Sushi was bad since I got literally no service, but that was for a one-time thing and haven't returned since. But Sakura has been chronically bad. I'm amazed they get away with it. My friends seem to be getting annoyed with it finally. Also, as the employees aren't Japanese, why put someone on the phones who not only speaks poor English but also has trouble understanding the Japanese-language food items being offered there? Good luck with trying to place a phone order. I'm already annoyed with the near-complete dearth of Japanese involvement with the Japanese restaurants here, primarily because I think we're being denied many a Japanese-style offering due to lack of cultural culinary knowledge from the people working at them. But this is another excuse to add to my reasoning. Having only a very rudimentary understanding of English is forgivable and happens all the time at Asian restaurants. But don't have them working the phones, and in my case have them figure out what the menu items actually say on the menu without it being like pulling teeth. You won't find this kind of discrepancy anywhere else around here save for Japanese restaurants.

text: This restaurant could get 4-5 stars for atmosphere, depending on where you sit, and what you like. Nothing particularly special. 6 of us ate there on a Monday night (which could be part of the problem). There was only one other table of 2 all night (in what is a huge restaurant). That's with 4 bottles of wine, one pre-dinner drink at the bar, 4 appetizers, and 3 deserts... honestly, while I'm happy to pay that for a good meal, this place is not worth the money.

text: After all the hype and all of Oprah's talk about the power of a good bra, I decided to give intimacy a go....I was at the mall late on a Friday night and popped in to see if they could help me out....or help me up rather. A little back story (or shall I say boob story)....I had a wonderful bra fitting experience at Bloomingdales last year where I ended up finding out that I was a lot bigger in size...and that size is not that easy to find...I also happened to be losing a lot of weight quickly and didn't want to invest in a good bra since I was shrinking...I ended up going to Cacique, Lane Bryant's lingerie brand for my over the shoulder bolder holders. They were ok in fit but great for the wallet. Eventually I ended up between two sizes and found myself in a muffin top sort of situation. At the same time, my weight plateaued, so I decided it was time to get a proper bra... Thus, I went to intimacy...they happened to be able to fit me in, but they do suggest making appointments prior. Just so you know, they do not really have bras in the front of the store, but they do have a lot of panties, pj's and other fluffy things. I met with my bra fitter in the back and while the dressing room was small, she quickly (and loudly) went into her spiel about their process and I soon began to feel like I was buying a car rather than buying a bra... She brought one bra in for me to try on after eying me up...and while it was a pretty color, it looked and felt like a 1960's version of a bra (torpedoes are not sexy)...this was also the cheapest bra I tried on, at $80. I asked for more samples and she brought in a handful, which she helped me try on. If you are not into being seen topless by a stranger, then this experience is not for you. I liked two of the bras she brought. One, a cute ivory and purple number that was $140 and one, a simple black lace that was $160. I opted for the cheaper one. Before you go judging me for dropping $140 on a bra, please know that most bras in my size are often made by Delta Burke (I wish I was joking) and cute is never an option... During my entire experience, they tried to up sell me..."here, try on this robe" and "this tank top is perfect for everyone"...every step of the way, they show you more and more products... Please note that they make you sign a part of your receipt that guarantees that you will not be able to get your money back. You can exchange products, but once you hand over your cash, there is NOTHING you can do to get it back. I liked the bra, so I went for it. On the second day of wearing my new bra, I began to feel a sharp pain digging into my chest plate. I looked down and in my cleavage was the metal wire sticking out. I was pissed because I just bought the Cadillac of bras and it was turning out to be more of a Pinto. I was also stuck at work and gave my cube mates the pleasure of continually watching me shove my hand down my shirt to push the metal back in. I went back to intimacy and talked to the manager. I was irked that their product was bogus. She claimed it was a dropped stitch. Whatever, I wanted my money back since I had no faith in any of their high end undergarment's. She apologized, but said there was nothing they could do about getting me my money back. I could buy a new bra (I didn't have the time for another 30 minute fitting) or they could mail me a new one of the same size and design. I opted for the latter option, but left feeling like I was had. They did nothing about my painful (literally) experience. This is supposed to be a high end boutique, but I have had better experiences elsewhere. Two weeks later, my bra came in the mail. It may sound crazy, but I feel like it fits different than the one I fell in love with at the store. I give up. I do believe in the power of a good bra and yes, when Oprah speaks about lady lumps, I take it as gospel, but I will never give intimacy my money again. If Nordstrom's is good enough for Oprah, it is good enough for me!

text: Stopped here for a late-night drink and dessert, hoping for a casual, date-friendly place for a sweet nightcap. I wont say we didn't get that, but we certainly weren't impressed and certain elements (like the price) were actually quite off-putting. The decor was kind of like a slightly moodier Starbucks: one is greeted by churning vats of (fake?) chocolate and the carefully organized gift shop by the door, a bad, vaguely chocolate-related mural took up one corner, fake quotes about the ego-maniacal Brenner covered the other walls. It wasn't oppressive, but it was certainly trying too hard. We were led to a nice little two-top pointing out on open window and our order was quickly taken. Very quickly our cocktails (good booze, well-mixed, but not worth 10 bucks a pop) were brought out and, soon after, our chocolate fondue. We opted for the Trio: a molten toffee caramel and any two chocolate fondues (milk, dark, white) served with strawberries, bananas, banana bread, marshmallows, and little grill to roast them. The chocolate was far too sweet for my taste: the white had a lovely cocoa butter flavor, but the dark wasn't that dark and the caramel had a very bland flavor. All of them hurt my teeth, their saccharine flavors overpowering the already sweet accoutrement. Those too were disappointing: the fruit was okay (I would have liked to see local strawberries, but it might be a little early for those) but the marshmallows tasted like your standard Jet-Puffed (what self-respecting confectioner doesn't make their own marshmallows?) and the banana bread was room temperature. at best, and uninspired. All the same, I would have been much happier with less, and more savory fondues with more, and more thoughtful choices to dip. I know there are entire worlds of chocolate connoisseurship, but the quality of the sweets at Max Brenner didn't even stand up to an ignoramus like me. Naked Chocolate Cafe holds its position as my favorite late-night sweet spot in the city: cheaper, better, and its Rittenhouse location couldn't be closer. 4/5 for service, a "meh" for the cocktails, but thumbs down for everything else.

text: Has anyone ever heard of Charley's Grilled Subs before? Not me, but he sure is looking good! Come, stop shopping, savor our wonderful grilled subs and sit down for awhile! Okay Charley, it does smell good. Have you ever wanted to roam a restaurant or eatery and check out what everyone else was eating before making up your mind? Have you? Be honest! Everything looked so good that was passing by in front of my face and every menu item causes your glands to salivate! I knew the rolls were going to be good just by the fresh and crusty look of them. They have turkey, pepperoni, ham and they are piled high so your jaw gets a work out. They have veggie sandwiches, buffalo style chicken or teriyaki. I love Charley's, the bread is awesome and the sandwich was wonderful. They do not have to call my name anymore, because I will be calling theirs every time I step foot in the mall, I was very impressed! Hey I now have an agenda to try them all. Hey Charley, I'm here! http://www.charleys.com/menu/

text: Me momsie and I just did a craftie weekend in Tucson and this was one of our first stops. We didn't know much about this place -- it is about a year old, we've heard? -- and my mom sent me out of the car to go in and stake out the place before we decided to unload the bambinos. It didn't take me long to decide she needed to come inside, too. Laraine, who works there, is brash and fun and quickly told us they were the "best knitting store in Tucson". When we told her of our plans for the weekend, she told us we would go to the other ones but we would find "we're the best". Skeptical though I was at first, she just may be right. Their stock is of the highest quality compared to other stores in Tucson. Kiwi is pretty close up there, but Purls has too much crap yarn, and Tucson Yarn only carries the best. I wasn't sure of the vibe when I walked in because Laraine is so over-the-top. I asked if they carried Misti Alpaca Super Chunky (I'm short a skein for a project - I ask wherever I go...sigh...) and got a quick, brusque "never heard of it". Fine, there are TONS of yarns out there, I don't expect you to know every single one... If you go on Tucson Yarn's website (as I did today) it will warn you: "Make no mistake about it. Laraine is NOT a Knit Doctor - not even a Knit Paramedic. Laraine is a relatively new knitter who will be happy to show you around the shop, ring up a sale, register you for a class or wind your yarn." Okay, I get it now. Anyway, they have lots of Cascade, gorgeous Sublime yarns and patterns, Berroco, some Rowan, lots of Debbie Bliss... all great stuff. The ironic thing is I DIDN'T BUY ANY YARN!!! I bought a pattern book and a needle I needed, but Laraine was RIGHT - I should have gone there last - I didn't want to blow my wad at the very first stop of my weekend! I have that problem when I go to a really nice store with a superior inventory - I want EVERYTHING and so I can't pick ONE THING. Boohoo. But I will definitely be back. Gorgeous products. Beautifully laid out and very shopable - a help with yarn stores. Trying to be helpful even if they may not know the answer. Keep up the good work, Tucson Yarn! You are worth the drive!

text: I was vacationing in Santa Barbara with my mother for my birthday and I wanted to have seafood for dinner, so we cruised around by foot near the waterfront, hoping to find a good seafood place to eat. We crossed paths with FisHouse and thought we might as well give it a try. When we entered the restaurant, we were quickly and kindly seated by the host. The atmosphere is "casual/formal", I would say. I wouldn't feel weird coming in with a pair of jeans but I also wouldn't feel overdressed coming in with a skirt. Natural lighting flowed into the restaurant, so it wasn't a dim place. Once we were seated, the waiter came, introduced himself, asked us what we'd like to drink, came back with some bread, and served us our drinks (he was attentive throughout the meal). We decided not to order any appetizers because we didn't want to get too full. When it was time to order, I ordered penne with salmon and vodka sauce and my mother ordered a type of seafood soup, both of which came in less than twenty minutes. This was the first time I've ever eaten pasta with vodka sauce, and I was quite pleased. The pasta wasn't swimming in too much sauce, but it wasn't dry and it wasn't too rich, either. The salmon was sliced into bite-size chunks, and there was an adequate amount (not just a small sprinkling of salmon meat). The peas added a lovely bit of color to the pasta and the dish was presented nicely in a bowl/plate hybrid, which made it easier to eat (I didn't have to worry about my sauce escaping the plate). The portion was good and I ended up taking some of the leftovers with me. I can't say much about the seafood soup my mother ordered, but she said it was delicious, so I'll take her word for it (she's an excellent cook, so I trust her). Since it was my birthday, my mother requested for a dessert at the end of our meal and sure enough, our waiter arrived with a mocha ice cream cake slice (not too big, not too small) drizzled with chocolate fudge, topped with strawberry slices, sprinkled with thinly sliced almonds and garnished with mint. It was delicious, simple, and the right amount I needed after a filling plate of pasta with cream sauce. When we got the check, we were curious to see if the waiter charged us for the dessert and it turned out that he didn't. The cost of our meal was decent overall. For me, it wasn't bad for a first experience, which was great for a birthday meal!

text: Bobbie's has been around since the 'fifties, when there was still a drive-in movie theater on Charlotte Pike. They are fresh cut, real potatoes and they taste like it, served in little white paper bags spotted with fry grease. You should also try the sweet potato fries, served with a sour cream sauce. Bobbie's has a great, but not cheap, burger, and they serve two different kinds of veggie burgers. As legendary in these parts as the fries are the milkshakes. You could give yourself a headache calculating the permutations of possible combinations of flavors. My personal favorite is banana with bananas and pineapple.

I stuck with a classic chicken enchilada and my sweetie got a combo fajita. The fajita came out on a regular plate..no sizzling griddle, nothing! The beef, chicken and shrimp looked shriveled and dry, it was so disgusting! To top it off, it wasn't even hot!!! But of course, he ate it, I was so mad at him for that. Mine? Well, the chicken enchilada was the most disgusting thing I've ever tasted. The chicken inside was like boiled? Who does that? The corn tortilla it was wrapped in was so drenched in oil it was not edible. The sauce? That was the kicker! It was like someone opened up a can of Hunts tomato paste and dumped it on there. DISGUSTING! I call over the waitress and explain my disappointment. She brings us our bill. She tried to charge me for something that was not even eaten! I was like, excuse me? I told her that I would not be paying for the enchiladas. She goes back to the kitchen and a man (who I could not see) was arguing with her behind the wall telling her to make me pay for it! text: I'd never actually been to a Sonic before but I had always wondered about them. So it was perfect when they built one very close by! For a few weeks, the place was so packed that we didn't even try to go. Incredible lines! We went the other night though and things have calmed down to the point where we could just drive right in. What makes this place unique is the "drive-in" setting. You pull into a parking space and right there you have a full menu. When you know what you want, you press the button and tell the attendant your order. You then pay by card right there and soon enough your food is brought right out to you. That's pretty much all there is to it. Kinda neat I thought, I dug the 50's vibe. So we've established that the experience itself is kinda cool, but how is the food? I ordered a hamburger and large fries, my wife got a cheeseburger, regular fries, and a milkshake, and our daughter got the chicken strips, tater tots, and a chocolate milk. This was a comfort food meal because we are all recovering from colds! Our meal was delivered to the car pretty quick. I was kinda bummed to see that they sent me two cheeseburgers instead of hamburgers. This always happens to me, its some sort of kink in the universe that I have come to accept. Let's rate the food: Hamburger, Chicken Strips, and Cheeseburger: Good overall. No better than what you'd get at Wendy's, Burger King, or McDonalds though. One of my hamburger buns was actually a little stale, kinda hard. They were kind of sloppily put together too, I've seen better hamburgers "built" in similar fast food places. The chicken strips looked good, my daughter liked them. Fries and Tater Tots: The fries were decent, but Burger King and McDonalds easily bests them. Their "large" fry is really not all that large actually, kind of surprising in this day and age of "value meals". The tater tots were absolutely atrocious though. They had obviously been made about 3 weeks earlier and were left to sit under a light bulb before being served to us. I'd be embarrassed to send something like that out. And Sonic is batting 1.000 because both the fries and tater tots were lukewarm at best. Chocolate Milkshake: Unfortunately, the "chocolate" milkshake was not as rich as what you might have gotten back in the "drive-in" days. This is your basic vanilla ice cream mixed with chocolate syrup to create a very "vanilla" chocolate milkshake, if you will. Boooring. It all amounts to a rather stale experience that the cool 50's drive-in concept just couldn't save. Perhaps if the place had been swamped I could understand, but there is no reason for our food to have been sloppy, lukewarm, and just plain unsatisfying. What this comes down to is that if you need the campy drive-in experience and don't mind throwing your diet away on mediocre food, then you should go here. Me? If I'm doing a burger and fries (which is very rarely) I'm going to get it from a place that at least serves me fresh and hot food. You can easily top the food with a trip to Wendy's, BK, or McDonalds. Or if you really want to do it in style, go to Five Guys Burger and Fries.

Of course my friend really didn't see my problem with this, but even she admitted that hardly any of the dudes were even worth looking at. At one point, we were surrounded at the bar by about 15 doucheholes, dressed in golf attire and wearing one golf glove. For real? My other major problem was how unbearably loud the music was. Someone came up with what they thought was a very clever idea: let's pick random 10 minute movie clips, play them so effin loud that you can't hear the person next to you and at the end of the clip, morph it into a song that no one in their right mind wants to hear. Repeat with more shit songs and there you have it. Brilliant, huh? Apparently, Maloney's is also known for having shitty bartenders and high prices. I can confirm this. Although, we only had beer and were not graced with having a simple mixed drink screwed up, their attentiveness sucked big time. They do have a lot of beer taps but with Fat Tire or Guinness being the exceptions, it's all big beer crap (Bud, Coors, Miller, etc.). Despite all this, I don't want my only experience in Tucson to be a poor memory of Maloney's. At some point, I'd like to go back just to see if maybe we hit it up on an off-night (Saturday). Somehow, I doubt it. EDIT: After submitting my review, my friend informed me that her credit card was overcharged by nearly $20. And I cannot help but to think, after our experience, that this is something that commonly happens at Maloney's. My only question is, how many people catch it? I will not be returning here again!

text: I am going to go against the grain a bit here, but Five Guys is not that great. I think that the reason that Five Guys is so popular has more to do with lowered expectations than actual quality. Let me explain. I think over the past few decades we have been exposed to enough terrible hamburgers and fries from fast food establishments and lousy restaurants that our expectations of a good burger have been lowered so far that a passable hamburger seems amazing in comparison. That is exactly what Five Guys has, a passable burger. The fries are good and of course they are fresh, but aren't fries supposed to be fresh. I suppose this is why the "craft" burger has taken off all over the city and across the country. When people forget that a product is supposed to be good you can get away with charging a premium for anything that is above average. That get's me to my other point. After all is said and done, with fries and a drink, Five Guys is a $10 meal. There are dozens of places in Nashville that have excellent burgers for around $10. Hell I rarely walk out of Gabby's for more than $8 and that is a far superior product in every way. Most of the sports bar's and pubs in the area have Burgers for less than $10 so I don't really get it. Overall, I think that Five Guys is okay, but they are not particularly special or particulary a good value. Long live the era of low expectations.

text: Because of some... shall we say... ISSUES I had with David's Bridal, I decided to take my wedding gown elsewhere to be altered. I called Fashion Stitch on the recommendation of my cousin, and was able to make an appointment for a fitting that worked with my schedule. Had it not been for the all-knowing powers of Garmin, I would have passed right by the place. Fashion stitch is a tiny house on a busy road with a little sign. They must get their business by word of mouth (and now word of Yelp) recommendations, because I doubt anyone would just notice it was there and stop in. I entered the small, crowded front room and was immediately directed to a back room. There were many dresses hanging along one wall, a mirror on another wall, and a wedding gown draped for steaming in front of the window. It was a little awkward because there was no designated "changing room," but the owner did close the door to the room, so I had privacy while donning my gown. My dress didn't need many alterations, but the ones it did need weren't cake. The original design included straps that I chose not to use, and they were attached in between the top layer of the dress and the lining. Since I bought the floor sample, the dress also needed a new zipper (someone or several someones obviously too large for this dress tried it on at some point and the zipper was pulled away from the fabric), a hem, and of course a bustle. The seamstress (I feel bad- I really wish I knew her name) quickly went to work on pinning the hem and the bustle and noted on my charge slip the other alterations to be made. At this point, I said goodbye to my gown and hoped for the best. When I went back for my second fitting, I was completely pleased with how my dress had turned out. In addition to replacing the zipper completely, the seamstress had added several hooks and loops so that the outer decorative buttons would lay flat to conceal it. The straps were removed with such precision that you couldn't even tell they were there to start with. Of course, the hem was even, and she used buttons that matched those already on my dress to create the bustle. In addition to alterations, Fashion Stitch also creates garments from scratch. I will definitely go back here if I am ever in need of either service again.

text: Do you like chicken? Do you like fried chicken? Do you like fresh fried chicken? If you answered yes to the last three questions, Hodak's is the place for you. Hodak's is great. My friends, coworkers and I all enjoy eating that this fine South St. Louis City eatery. I must say, however, that although I love Hodak's, it isn't the most flavorful chicken I have had. In fact, I would almost argue that little to no seasoning is added to the chicken or breading. What draws me to Hodak's is how fresh the chicken is. Because this restaurant does so much business they are constantly frying up chicken. I have yet to have chicken that wasn't scalding hot when I ordered it. Dinners are cheap. The golden fried chicken dinner is just $6.75 and comes with two sides. Don't try and order chicken by the piece, 'cause they won't let you. Other dinners and specials include cod or catfish, Chicken Parmesan, a whole wing dinner. I have even heard of the toothpick which is a hot dog wrapped in bacon and deep friend. Sides include mashed potatoes, fries, onion rings, vegetables, and mac & cheese on occasion. My usual order? I get the five wing chicken plate ($6.50) with mashed potatoes, brown gravy and french fries. I know what you are thinking... 'What's with all the potatoes?' Simply put, I love dipping my fries in the gravy. I rarely eat the potatoes which I think are instant. There is a non-smoking section located in the upstairs section of the restaurant. Think you'll avoid the line by sitting in the smoking section in the bar? I would advise against it as you'll be asked to get up and stand in line. Fresh. Clean. Cheap. Yep, Hodak's is a wonderful place.

text: We were in Nashville for work and had one night to try a really good place to eat. We were greeted by the hostess who was extremely knowledgeable and spent time not only seating us at an excellent table, but took the time to review the menu with us, giving us line-by-line recommendations about their food. After a few minutes, our server, Scott, came over and assisted us with starters. Scott was extremely helpful and was quite knowledgeable about wine and food pairings; making recommendations that would later turn out to be on-the-money. The food was incredible. We started with sharing both a salad flyte and a soup flyte and both were excellent. Te remainder of the courses - the eggplant meatballs for my wife and the Australian filet for me - were likewise excellent. The steak rivaled the best filets I've ever had...on par with Ruths Chris, Morton's, the Compass Rose in Singapore, the Yokohama Sheraton, etc... The pairings recommended by Scott for our meals were right on, and really made it extremely enjoyable. Overall, this was an excellent restaurant, one that I will recommend to friends and one that I will definitely visit again the next time I'm in Nashville. I would have no problem taking any of my bosses here, or for that matter, if I were single, taking a date here to make a great first impression. My wife and I enjoyed it as a memorable evening away from the kids...making all the more worthwhile. Being a regular traveller, I have eaten in dozens fine establishments in 26 different countries throughout Asia, the Americas and Europe. I am also a regular at our own fine establishments here in Virginia. Flyte ranks in the top three or four restaurants I've ever had the pleasure of dining in. I would most highly recommend Flyte to friends, family, and co-workers. Most importantly, it's a staple on my map for my next visit to Nashville! - Dave, Chesapeake, VA

text: I saw an ad in the Metro about this place and the ONLY reason I was tempted in trying it was because the ad said they had "kati rolls....like the one in New York." Now that got me all excited, wow actually having the New York kati rolls here in Philly! Well it did not really go that way. My first mistake was making an assumption, never assume. The kati rolls in New York is a whole different experience and I think this place is trying to mimic NY but it failed especially in taste. The concept behind this spot I think is Indian fast food. Ambience/Atmosphere: The place seems brand new and the inside is clean and there was nothing really that bothered me. Unlike most indian places that cramped or stuffy with stale air this place was open and clean. The decor is very simple. Parking: Street parking, again located down town so you have to hunt around. Oh yeah...good luck finding this place, there is no sign on the building stating it's "Bombay Express." I just got lucky and saw the chalkboard on the sidewalk when driving by. Maybe because it's new and they are waiting on doing that part? Menu/Pricing: The menu is relatively simple, you will see a bunch of "traditional" Indian appetizers. There are samosas, chaat and lassis etc. I was "going" to try the lassi but decided against it because it was already premade and stored in the fridge (nothing wrong with that but I am picky). The prices are I think a little more on the higher side, I mean in New York the prices are a little cheaper. I paid $4.95 for each Kati roll and tried the chicken and paneer. -Food: Honestly I was really disappointed. Maybe I am expecting too much from indian restaurants or even simple dishes such as this. First the "pratha-bread" that is rolled was poorly cooked, sticky and by this I mean when the dough is not cooked well the edges are sticky. The paneer was "ok," I am not a big fan of carrots in my paneer roll or bell peppers in the chicken roll. text: Out of all the Chinese restaurants in Philly, this one undoubtedly has the worst standards of service. Despite a practically empty restaurant, we waited about twenty minutes for our steak, which came without the appetiser or soup. The steak was in a thick syrupy sauce, which somewhat masked the unfresh ingredients. We were ignored by the servers until they noticed we had finished our steak and rice. A server then plopped down a plate of oranges, which apparently was our 'dessert.' We asked for our appetiser and soup, which was met with a rude glance and grunts (our server communicated with us in largely unintelligible grunts despite attempts to communicate in both English and Mandarin). Some time later, he brought us a glass bowl of sweet-and-sour soup. I went to the front to get a copy of the lunch menu, and after showing this to our server and after more passive-aggressiveness, he got us a single spring roll, which can be best described as mush wrapped in hard crust. We didn't have any choice in any of this. We were also completely ignored by the dim sum carts, which moved a total of two feet the entire time we were there. text: I have been in this area for a very long time and I can tell you, this diner has CHANGED for the worse since the original owners retired. May still be family running it but they obviously missed something. First of all, the Dining Car is VERY expensive for a diner. Its the most expensive one in the neighborhood that I've experienced. Next, they don't even take credit cards. They do have an ATM where the surcharge is a nice extra fee. Next, the service there is slow. Doesn't matter when you go, what time of day it is SLOW. If you get something to drink, really nurse it since you don't know when your waiter/waitress are going to come back to check on you. They are pleasant enough to you. The food itself.. eh. I have had better. Its a bit lack-luster and you are left feeling like they got a good deal of money for the bit that they offered you. I don't feel its worth the cost. I have personally had food poisoning from this place at least five times. The reason so many times it happened was because the first 3 I thought it was something I had eaten before or after dining here. The last two times I ordered different things, thinking maybe something just didn't agree with me. I have several local friends who have all told me that they have gotten sick from eating here too. The bathroom sinks don't always work in this place either. Lots of times I have found them without soap, would tell the waitress and the response would be "Oh I know." and nothing would be done. After that happened the first time, I started bringing hand sanitizer with me. It makes you wonder how often the employees are really able to wash their hands. However, with all that said, this is one of the FEW places that is open late in the area. The service, while it is slow, is friendly and welcoming. The Bakery is very good and I recommend their cinnamon rolls, along with their goodies. The service in the bakery is like night and DAY compared to the diner itself. Wonderful service, great baked goods. I really recommend checking out the bakery and forgetting the diner.

text: Beautiful park -- I can't believe it's owned by the *county* because it has the facilities of maybe even a national park! Even the park ranger at the visitor's center was extremely helpful and friendly, reaching out to us even though we weren't looking for one-on-one help (at first). Having been recently ranked as the #1 beach in the continental US, a huge stretch of pristine white sand beach makes up Fort De Soto Park. You can rent bicycles and go up and down the several-mile road that goes the length of the island (which is full of lush vegetation but you don't really see all that much of the beach). You can rent kayaks if you come early enough and paddle through the marsh that is on the marsh side. You can also do some really excellent shelling. It's a very wide beach, and there are tons of little tidal pools of sunwarmed water where you can find lots of huge, intact shells. Every time we found one (since we didn't want to take many home), we'd plant it for someone else to find and then watch. For some reason, it was really funny to us to watch people get all excited when they "found" their new prize. Heheh :). The marsh side is also neat to explore on foot. Completely different vegetation, including cattails. The mud around the water had some life forms that I couldn't even identify (some sort of jelly fish?). The mud was super warm and squishy; I almost expected it to bubble and make those glub-glub sounds. There were tons of herons, pelicans, cranes... pretty neat. There's excellent bathroom facilities, rinse-off showers, and tons of picnic areas with bbq grills. I definitely want to go back there when it's warm enough to swim. It really is lovely. I also want to take the snorkeling excursion to a sunken fort that is on a key nearby. There are informational brochures with ferry information at the visitor's center. You can also rent jet skis at a place close to the toll bridge (which is less than a dollar to cross - crazy).

We used up the focaccia before all of the sauce was gone, so I used the bread from the bread basket to sop up the last bit left on the plate. I couldn't resist. Next we split a Capri Salad which was several different types of locally grown heirloom tomatoes and mozzarella made in-house, topped with a smattering of crispy fried onions. A very nice, light dish for our hot summer evenings. For entrees, my friend ordered the Chicken Milanese and I ordered the Bistecca. The chicken was served with a lemon sauce on polenta, and was bursting with flavor. The polenta was so creamy and delicious! The Bistecca had so many incredible flavors and textures-- the steaks were topped with fresh corn, tomatoes, breadcrumbs, mushrooms and served over pototoes. It was an explosion in my mouth-a little crunch, a little creamy, a little acid, a little sweet....delish!

It was dressed lightly with a tahini type dressing and came with a small additional side of tahini and one of sumac powder (kind of a tangy lemony spice). The falafels were a little doughy and not crispy which is my preference. The serving size was generous for the price. I think a yogurt based dressing would have been lighter and tastier than the pasty tahini. The koobedeh came on a very generous pile of rice, and came with two large grilled jalapenos and one whole grilled roma tomato. The koobedeh was spongey, oily, and bland. The rice was flavorful though. It also came with 3 large slices of "naan". This was not the wonderfully blistery chewy naan I've come to expect, but basic flatbread that I suspect was not housemade. The rice pudding was a gelatinous sweet mass sprinkled with cinnamon and slivered almonds. But it wasn't until i was in Redding Terminal and saw the sign for Hopes that i remembered the greatness. I convinced the bf to get some and i was instantly transported back to the memories of Hopes. They just melted in my mouth. The snickerdoodles had perfect flavor and i will even say they were better than mine! Even the bf was impressed. However, he didn't stop talking about it all weekend. So his birthday was approaching and decided to get him a dozen. I had a hard time chosing only six types from all their options and it sucks that you can't have more than six types in a dozen. I had them shipped to my house since i didn't know the ability of recieving packages at the bf's office. Well the people at Hope's called me to confirm that was really where i wanted the packages delivered. I thought that was really going the extra mile The cookies were delivered within 48 hours, It was awesome I just wish there was a way to pick the delivery date so i didn't have them two days early Still they are the best cookies... ever
label: POS

text: These people replaced the Florida Orange Growers wine outlet (wines made from non-grapes) with a more traditional wine outlet (wines about $20/bottle). They provide a wine tasting bar, also sell beers, hot sauces related products. They have placed adirondack chairs on the sidewalk and sell sixes of craft beer by the bucket. I rated them lower for a couple reasons. I think they're catering too hard to public drinking rather than fine wine tasting. They very rarely offer help/welcome the customer. The chips and hot sauces that are out for tasting look dingy/dirty. They "knock" the former wine store (and fruit wines) which I loved. I do love the $5-$6 dipped caramel & nutty apples they sell near the back.
label: NEG

text: After making a trip to Whole Foods and other stores around, I decided to go to a place that I had looked up to possibly grab lunch with a friend. I wanted something with like a Panera feel but also somewhere I have never been. After reading Andrew M's review though I was a bit skeptical. We decided to go and it was around 2 o'clock (the middle of the day) and they were cleaning up everything... I thought this was a bit odd as the door says they dont close until 9pm but just thought whatever. When we ordered our panini and our wrap... it tool almost 20 minutes for us to get our food... This was a bit riduculous as my friend and I were the only ones in the entire place. I am assuming this was due to the cleaning of all of the grills... which I am still unsure of why it was done in the first place. I am also assuming that they have a large lunch rush because at 2 there still looked like the tables had not been cleaned since noon when their lunch crowd had left..Along with the door and windows having finger prints all over them. The decor in the cafe was great. I really loved the mint green, yellow, and oranges. This gave a great feel for the neighborhood... if you dont look at the windows of course. My sandwich was ok...I got the Napa Vally Panini and I am still unsure today if I liked it or not. Overall I would say this is an OK place but I would much rather go to the Bread Co. or even Subway.
label: NEG

text: Don't go there! Super slow service, horribly over salted chips. My fish tacos were dripping with water-apparently they were poorly defrosted and even more poorly cooked. The server suggested next time I request additional tortillas to mop up the moisture! Once upon a time it was fun, go to Nicos for better food and service!
label: NEG

text: I ate at Crabby Bill's many years ago when we went to visit some family. Finally made it back. They all warned me that it wasn't the same as I remembered when I went there the first time. I remembered a nice cozy atmosphere, fresh sea food, and a fun courteous wait staff. It was none of these anymore. Now its a loud, raucous, annoying place to eat. You leave still hungry with a much lighter wallet. My sister-in-law got the "all-you-can-eat" crab. Don't order this unless you aren't very hungry or you have a few hours to kill. They wont cook you next plate until you've finished you previous one. So once your ready for another one you have to sit there with nothing to eat for ten or more minutes till they bring out your next batch. By that time everyone else is done with their meal and ready to go. The wait staff aren't rude, they are just blah. The girl waiting our table had no business waiting tables, at least not without much more training. Their bartender is hit and miss. My first pina colada was great, my second one tasted horrible and was nothing but marble sized chunks of ice. I hate to see icons of an area do this to themselves. It has become completely commercialized. Sad to say but Crabby Bill's is just not good any more. Oh they'll survive off tourists lured in by nostalgia (and the open air bar they've added) but it will be a disappointment for most.
label: NEG

text: India Garden is, indeed, worth the rave reviews that it's gotten. I lean towards Broad Ripple in the great downtown/Broad Ripple divide. The newer, larger downtown location certainly is more swanky, while Broad Ripple is a bit more cozy. Unfortunately, I am one of those diners who tends to latch on to one delicious thing and order it over and over again. I always feel a twinge of guilt about this, but it's just hard to say no to something I cherish as deeply as Chicken Shahi Korma. For that reason, I love to come to the lunch buffet, since I can try plenty of new things and still stuff face with Chicken Shahi Korma. All the same, I really prefer to come here for dinner, if only for the mouth-watering fresh naan (try the cheese variety). Also, I swear that they have different, more interesting music playing at night--well, in addition to the standard daytime CD, that is. I know every single one of those songs by heart now. That's not to say that I don't love them, because I do. But change is also welcome sometimes.
label: POS

If you go for the fries, I suggest a side of gravy for dipping. Some people like the gravy on top but then the fries start floating.

text: All Dressed Up and Going Nowhere-- Caitlin said all that needs to be said, but I'll reiterate for good measure. The huge plus for Pink Rose is its atmosphere. It's a very cute and charming place and guys, if you're out on a date who happens to be real drunk, she might be so inebriated as to allow the cuteness of the establishment to blind her to the fact that, deep down inside, the food and service kind of suck. Every time I've been there they've messed something up with my order. You'd think that the slow pace they're moving at would ensure accuracy. And, incidentally, the food isn't even that good. The last time I went I had French toast and a lemonade. The French toast was OK, but nowhere near the hype indicated by the badjillion awards adorned on their walls. The lemonade, however, was a disgrace. As I eagerly anticipated what this "cute" pastry shop would produce, I was horrified to see a bottle of Snapple being brought out to me. Snapple??!?!?!?!? Are you serious? I was expecting fresh squeezed at the most, Nantucket Nectars at the worst. But....SNAPPLE?!?!?! That's sugar water! The "best stuff on Earth" is, in fact, made out of High Fructose Corn Syrup which, by the way, is not an "all natural" ingredient. Shame on you Pink Rose.
label: NEG

text: I have been to hell ... its name is Bird's Nest of Beijing. My boyfriend and I are foodies and love to eat all sorts of ethnic cuisine. That being said, this has to be the worst restaurant we've ever been to in Edmonton, period. I would take McDonald's over this place in a heartbeat. The food was ATROCIOUS. We ordered fried rice, a sweet and sour bok choy dish and some cashew chicken. The fried rice tasted like it had been deep-fried in ham fat. It was overpoweringly salty and terrible. The bok choy was overcooked, limp, and all you could taste was vinegar and brown sugar. It was disgusting. The cashew chicken was not awful, but gristly in places and not very flavourful. For this, I paid almost $40. It was a complete ripoff. The food was SO bad. There are much better Chinese restaurants in town, such as Buddy Wonton, so don't bother with this place! Save your money!!

text: While I probably wouldn't choose this place as a dinner destination, I did have lunch here at least once every two to three weeks when I worked nearby. The food is definitely a big step up from your standard take-out places. It's got more of a P.F. Chang's vibe to it (meaning, stir-fried white meat chicken rather than random chicken pieces that are battered and deep fried to disguise their true identity). I always alternated between the cashew chicken and the garlic chicken (not recommended if you plan on getting up close and personal with anyone for the rest of the day). The Thai stuff I've tried is pretty good as well; particularly the chicken satay with peanut sauce and cucumber salad. Bonus, you have the option of white or brown rice with your meal!

text: Today was my first visit, and boy have I been missing out! There are so many positive things about Sugar Philly Truck: First, the dessert is amazing. I had the molten chocolate cake, which was fresh out of the oven. It was warm, moist and had the perfect amount of chocolate (not too heavy). The sauce was vanilla-y goodness, but the cake would have been plenty moist without the sauce, which is really impressive. Second, I love that they make the dessert right there in the truck. In my experience, dessert items from trucks are often made elsewhere and then sold from the truck. Not the case here! When I asked for a recommendation, the guy working there (unfortunately I didn't catch his name) pointed me to the molten cake because it had just been made. Talk about freshness! Third, the guy working there was so nice and friendly. I could tell he was really passionate about his desserts and sharing them with customers. Plus, he also just seems like a fun guy to be around. And finally, I adore the design of the truck - it's impossible to look at and not be happy. Plus, it's eco-friendly! It runs on natural gas and the utensils they use are made of cornstarch. A happy, eco-friendly truck, quality desserts AND great, friendly service? What a gem!
label: POS

text: Just when I thought the jinx was over, I ended up at this place. This place was recommended to me by two Mexican Americans. One guy went so far as to say they have "tacos better than Mexico." I have been skeptical of Mexican food since I got to Indy, and this visit didn't do anything to change it. I will say this place has more of an authentic selection than your typical Mexican chain restaurant. They had menudo, pozole, a variety of tacos (al pastor, lengua, cabeza, tripe, etc...), then even had aguas refrescas. Let it be said though just because a place is authentic, doesn't mean they are good. I thought about getting a variety of tacos, but I really felt like a burrito al pastor, so I rocked one out. The wifey got a "colorado" burrito with asada. To say this place was disappointing would be an understatement. My burrito was more rice than meat, and by the end of it, that's all I was eating. My wife's burrito was more beans and rice than asada. Heck, even the horchata wasn't up to bar. I think I've had better instant stuff than what they were serving. Overall- $7 for a rice burrito? No thanks. My disdain for Mexican food in Indy continues. Movie Star Rating- the chihuahua from "Beverly Hills Chihuahua"

The pit bosses were all around nice and the dealers were fun and entertaining. Overall, this is up there with Mandalay Bay for the top places to stay and gamble. text: I have no fault with Cafe Cioccolato. None whatsoever. And you shouldn't either. Cafe Cioccolato is a delightful chocolate shop in the Paul Brown building across from the Old Post Office downtown. The ambiance hits you with coziness as soon as you enter, and you're immediately greeted very warmly by David, the owner. I typically stop in for a hot chocolate, as the cafe is on my way home from the 8th & Pine Metrolink station. Once you taste this hot chocolate, Swiss Miss just won't cut it for you anymore. It's real hot chocolate -- honest to goodness chocolate that just happens to be in liquid form. You can get milk or dark hot chocolate. David will put cream or spices into it if you'd like, but I prefer my milk hot chocolate plain. It's so creamy and rich, and it makes "hot chocolate" from other places taste awful in comparison (those are usually just a bit of chocolate powder and water, anyway). There are also a number of coffees available, but because I don't drink coffee, I can't speak for those. To go with my hot chocolate, I usually pick out a few candies from the long cases. The chocolates here are so delectable -- so many flavors and fillings to choose from! I have a fondness for caramel, and Cafe Cioccolato has plenty of varieties, from liquidy caramel fillings to thicker fillings mixed with other flavors. I'm also a fan of the fruit fillings -- there are some raspberry varieties everyone must try, and the strawberry balsamic also is a favorite. If you're confused or hesitant about any of the items, David will explain what's inside, what the chocolates taste like, where they came from, etc. You're not going to find that kind of info on a Hershey bag at Schnucks. I brought home a box of many chocolates over the holidays, and my parents were ecstatic. These are far better than the Whitman's Sampler boxes that usually get passed around our family. Beyond the chocolate, there's also plenty of art to look at, and if you're not in a rush like I always seem to be, you can lounge on the cushy sofas and chairs and enjoy your treats. I'm so glad Cafe Cioccolato opened downtown. It's probably not the best thing for my waistline, but the confections inside definitely make my chocolate heart flutter.
label: POS

text: Without a doubt Nashville's best brewery. Whatever flavor of beer you like, they have something for you. it has been an interesting progression to watch the Yazoo taproom grow from their humble beginnings at Marathon Village to the widely popular establishment that now exists in the Gulch. I have to admit that I stopped going for a while towards the end of their stint at Marathon Village because it was just simply too much hassle... I love a fresh Yazoo straight off the tap as much as the next guy but it was just too much towards the end. I'm happy to report that that the new location is much more adept at handling a large crowd. The lines move more quickly and the location has much more room to handle the increased popularity. The outdoor patio is an added bonus during warmer weather and has a decent view of the downtown skyline. On to the important stuff, the beer. If you love dark beer, the onward stout is an incredible dark beer with lovely hints of espresso flavor. Want something that will split your head open with bitterness? Try any of the iterations of hop project. Want a nice refreshing wheat beer? Try the hefewiezen with its thirst quenching hints of banana and clove. If you don't fancy any of those try the Dos Perros which is a nice malty Vienna style beer similar to Negra Modello or Dos Equis Amber. As if that wasn't enough there is still the classic Yazoo Pale Ale which has just enough bitter hops to prime your taste buds but not too much to prevent you from tasting anything for the rest of the day. If you have never been, definitely start off with the sampler. You'll get to try all their current beers on tap plus you will get a discount on your favorite to take home in a growler. Once you have had a chance to work up a case a of the munchies be sure to check out the bread and cheese plates from local farms. text: I came across Play-a-Round Golf one night while eating dinner with Kristine and my dad at Cheeburger Cheeburger (also worth checking out!). It seemed like a novel concept, and it happened to be their grand opening. They let us play around (hardy har har) and I had a great time. Kristine got me a gift card as a present which I finally got to use about a month ago on a rainy Friday night. They accept tee times, although you don't need them and can just walk in. There are 3 sections of booths, allowing for private parties and public walk-ons. They charge you by the hour, no matter how many people are in the party. A full round will take about an hour per person. The goods: -It's great for winter, rainy or night time golfing in a climate controlled place. -Their systems gives you swing stats such as club head speed, launch angle and so forth (which means nothing to an amateur like me, but it's still cool to see for every swing) -You can set up a profile that will email you stats and such each time you go in -You can play a variety of courses around the world, and even some that don't really exist. They even have a simulation for the infamous 18 holes (http://www.infamousgolfholes.com/) The bad: -While it's fun, it's no substitute for the real thing. Every lie is perfect, and there are no hills that can be simulated. -Putting is not really realistic. Sure, you can get used to it on their system, and they are set up to give you gimmes inside 5 feet. But it certainly won't count for practice when it comes to the real deal. -Just like driving range mats, the tees are interchangeable but limited to the few heights they have in stock. This makes it very difficult to find that right tee for you...plus would probably get tiresome if you have a group that wants different height tees. -Exercise. Normally most people like golf for the walking and being outdoors. This place is mainly for people to practice your swing and have a little fun while doing it. Sure, you are getting a little exercise swinging the club. But it doesn't match walking a course. Overall, it's a great time and I will certainly be going back with a few golfing buddies. For those that want to know, I played Pebble Beach and shot a 90...and I'm certain that's what I would have if I played it in real life :)

text: Yes, it's a chain, but oh how I love me some Penn Station. I'd marry the fries if it were legal. And, you know, not weird and stuff. The fries are made from actual potatoes, and if you're curious, you can watch them spin-peel and slice the taters into fries. Add those to the oil, and bam! Real-fry heaven. Sometimes my body does yell at me to eat some veggies, though, so I either order the artichoke sandwich or make up my own. My weirdo dream sandwich includes artichokes, mushrooms, saurkraut, two types of cheese, lettuce, green peppers, tons of onions and some oil and vinegar. The folks at Penn Station never blink an eye when I order this, which I totally appreciate. For the record, I'm a skinny girl, but I can eat. When I do two buckets of fries, I'll only supplement that with a cookie. When I order a sandwich, it's either a small or medium, and I'll still order fries. My friends usually are filled by just a sandwich, but not me. In fact, I ate TWO large orders of fries AND a sandwich the other day. The Hampton Avenue Penn Station particularly is great. The workers there are friendly and quick, and they always manage to make my sandwiches really cheesy, even though I don't request it and even though I don't pay extra for it. "Cute girl favor" for me? Maybe. But seeing as how most of the sandwich makers here are girls and not boys, I wouldn't count on it. I think they've just finally realized that people like cheese on their sandwiches, especially vegetarian sandwiches. As others have mentioned, the lemonade at Penn Station is really, really good. I've found myself watering it down just a touch lately, though. Oh, and you'd probably guess this, but Penn Station is smoke free. Rock on. I give four stars instead of five for the following reasons: * The lemonade is behind the counter, and I feel really awkward waiting to ask someone to give me a refill. * They don't have to-go cups for water. I love the lemonade, but I only get it on rare occasions now; I generally drink water at all meals. More than half of my Penn Station orders are take-out, with me eating in the car on the way to wherever. However, the folks at most of the area Penn Stations look at you like you're crazy when you ask for a to-go cup for water. They usually hand you one of those tiny plastic cups, which are fine for dining in, but they don't fit into cup holders and lids don't fit them. text: I went to Cebu for dinner around 9:30pm on a Thursday. The interior was nicely appointed but dark, cavernous, and largely absent of customers except a couple of fellow diners and a few people sitting at the bar. I had the duck pancit, a dessert that amounted to banana lumpia, and a glass of wine. It was fine-- not ambrosial, but fine. What was not fine was some of the service. When I arrived, the hostess made a big production of pointing out how wonderful it was that I was dining out alone. As a frequent solo diner I must say that this did not help me feel at ease. The next part requires some explanation-- I have short hair and an androgynous appearance, especially when seen from the back. One of the managers (?) "excuse me sir"-ed me from the back, and then fell all over himself apologizing to me from the front when he decided I was female. I said it was fine, several times, and he groveled /more/, several times. I guess i could have gotten a free drink out of it if I'd wanted, but it was just very awkward and embarassing. By the time I finished with the bill I couldn't wait to escape. I don't have terribly high standards for restaurant service-- even benign neglect is all right so long as I am not in a hurry. The waiter who did my meal service did a perfectly good job, but the hostess and manager made me feel scrutinized and uncomfortable. Unfortunately, the food and ambience weren't good enough to make up for it.

text: I really didn't want to give this place one star. I tried to think of reasons to give it even a paltry 2 stars. But I can't. I can't recommend this place to anyone. It failed in nearly every way that a restaurant can. Let me break this down for you. It serves cafeteria-type food to elderly people in a strange atmosphere with a slow, overworked, and absent-minded waitstaff. Let me start out by saying this restaurant wasn't my choice. The only thing I knew about it was that it was a German restaurant in Dutchtown. I don't mean to be overly snobbish (only a little), but when was the last time someone had a really good meal in a German restaurant? Do nice German restaurants even exist? And moreover, what even constitutes German food anymore? America already stole sausages and hamburgers for themselves, so what's the difference between eating at a German place and a baseball game? In the case of the Feasting Fox, I'd rather be at the game. You'd pay about the same, get your food faster, have a better atmosphere, and at least have the chance of seeing someone under the age of 60. Ok, about that atmosphere. This place is kinda like if your grandma had a huge old house and converted it into a restaurant. No, not your cool grandma (the one that owns Winslow's Home), the grandma that never threw anything out and bought everything cheaply. The one that collects weird knickknacks of foxes and old faded landscape paintings. The one that mis-matches china, glasses, and silverware (There were 5 people at my table. There were 4 different types of glasses for soft drinks, and everyone had a different type of plate. I'm not entirely sure this was intentional). You know you're not exactly experiencing fine dining when people are wheeling in oxygen tanks behind them. No offense to all the oxy-tankers out there, but they're not known for their discriminating taste. In short, this place was old. Sometimes it was hard to tell which was older, the restaurant or the patrons, and I'm pretty sure the restaurant is over 100 years old. So anyway, the menu is pretty standard. Chicken, steak, german sausage, salad, and umm...that might be it. We got an appetizer of parmasan cheese puffs, which consisted of cheese whiz on melba toast. It may be the single most offensive dish served to me in quite some time. Seriously, even when I was in college I could whip up better stuff than this. I deliberately tried to find something on the menu that I'm sure they couldn't screw up, because at this point the fear of the restaurant gods had been stricken in me. I chose the herb chicken. It's pretty hard to screw up chicken, I thought. Especially compared to steak or sausage. The waitress said I got the last chicken of the day. I looked at my watch. It was 5:30. I'm assuming they're not expecting any late night diners since their clientele has to hit the sack in time to get up for the Denny's early bird special at 5AM. In retrospect, I wish they had been out of it because I would have gotten a second chance. I got a soup with it, and the waitress said the soup of the day was vegetable. Sounds good, a hard soup to screw up. Here's the problem. The soup of the day wasn't vegetable, it was irish barley, and it was brought to us anyway without asking if it was ok. And, surprise! It tasted like it was from a can. But hey, canned food was better than what awaited me. After about 45 minutes (and several ignored requests to refill our glasses), my entree arrived. The chicken was huge, a full half-chicken. I guess they made up for in volume what lacked in taste, because this thing was bad. It had been badly overcooked and dried out. The skin tasted like paper and peeled off in one long pull. The problem was that all the herbs were in the skin, so I was left with a huge skinless, dry, flavorless chicken. And I had no idea what to do with it. So I boxed it up and took it home, where it still sits in my fridge. At least the mashed potatoes and vegetables that came with it (probably from a mix) were decent. The desserts were alright, but it's kinda hard to screw up dessert, even if you try. Anyone can make a cake or a pie from a mix. Heck, the people at my work do it all the time. Oh, and we ordered ice cream to go with our strudel, which of course never arrived. At least at work people bring in a dipper so you can get your own ice cream if you want it. So when it was all said and done, our simple dinner turned into a 2 hour extravaganza of crap. The food sucked, the atmosphere sucked, and the service sucked. The stuff that tasted the best either was out of a can or made from a mix. There's a reason why people pay more than $10 for an entree, and that's so that they can eat real food that's prepared well. I'm not quite sure how this place has stayed in business for 100 years, but God help us if it manages to drag along for another 100. Time to put the Feasting Fox out to pasture.

text: After a happy hour last night, six of us headed to Roxanne in Clayton. It had been several years since my last visit, but I remembered a large menu, packed restaurant/bar, and well-cooked food. That is not what we experienced last night. We walked in around 9pm and the place was near empty. A DJ was setting up in the hostess area, and we were quickly seated to a table. Drink service was quick, but when asked about house wines, our waitress admitted that she had no idea how they tasted. Maybe beer would have been a safer choice. The menu consisted of appetizers, salads, sandwiches, and some entrees. Not much variety here. The burgers were well received, as was the macaroni and cheese. My sister and I split a house salad, which was decent, and a ham and smoked gouda toasted sandwich. The cheese on our "toasted" sandwich was not even melted, and our seasoned fries were limp. Taste was decent, but given the fact that we were some of the only diners there, I was expecting better. The DJ started blasting music around 9:30pm, which made conversation at our table difficult...it seemed that he could have turned the volume down, since: 1) we were some of the only people there 2) there is no room to dance 3) there was no one attempting to dance. Overall, I was very disappointed, and do not plan to go back unless I hear in the local foodie news that drastic changes have been made.

Nevertheless, there's nothing particularly special about their food...the pizza is uber greasy, and often requires half a roll of paper-towels to blot it to an acceptable eating level. The Peddler's Deluxe breakfast sandwich (egg, bacon, mushrooms, green peppers, onions, cheese) is a steal at $4.50, but can sometimes lead to very unpleasant bathroom trips. The same goes for the Peddler Fries -- what tastes like an orgasm when I put it into my mouth (mozzarella, cheddar, ranch dressing and bacon....oh yesss!) sometimes leaves me feeling a bit queasy 20 minutes later. To sum it up: PP is greasy, cheap food -- but not for the faint of heart. If you're in the neighborhood, stop on by (or get it delivered!); otherwise, don't bother.

text: I have mixed feelings giving the Brew Brothers only two stars, but based off of my last experience, I feel this is appropriate. Their beer is some of the best! I love their beer. The atmosphere is great! The food is pretty good as well. The reason I'm giving them two stars however is the service was HORRIBLE!! The last time I went to Brew Brothers, I drove up from the Sacramento area. I was hungry and looking forward to some micro-brews. The host outside told us that they stopped serving dinner at 8:30PM!! (WTF??!!??) Who's ever heard of a restaurant (especially in a casino town) stop serving dinner at 8:30?? (Contrary to what it said online BTW) I would expect this from a Carrows in Sun City, AZ but not from a Brew Pub in Reno! This wasn't even what made me the maddest. We decided to get some beers anyway and trek out later for some food. We took a seat and about four waiters/waitresses looked at us, then IGNORED us! Finally, I tracked down a waiter and asked him if we could get some service. The waiter looked at me very confused and almost scared. "Uhhh...what do you want?" he said very hesitantly. I looked at him bewildered....."well, are you still serving food?" The waiter quickly snapped "NO!" I then looked at him and pressed further....."well then...if you're not serving food...then what else could I possibly want?" "Uhhh....drinks?" the waiter slowly replied. At that point I walked out very disgusted. I'm very happy to say, that I found a great alternative brew pub in downtown Reno called the Silver Peaks Taproom. (Thanks to the front desk manager at Harrahs for pointing it out to me!) Even though,they don't brew their beer on-site (they brew it down the street), their micro-brews were much better, they served dinner until 11:00PM, and the service was PHENOMENAL!!! (FYI to the moron waiter who didn't want to help us....I tipped the young lady at Silver Peaks $30 on a bill that came up to only $50!! That's what good service does for me!)

This is one landmark restaurant that lives up to the hype and must be experienced. text: Whenever anyone asks me what I like better, Pat's or Geno's, I always answer, "Philip's of course." I love this place. There are a number of great reasons this is the best steak spot in town. But let's just talk about the steak. Some places like to chop the meat like crazy when it's on the grill, giving it an almost ground meat consistency. Most pizza places do this, and so does Jim's and Dallesandro's. Geno's and Pat's, and Tony Luke, and Steve's Princess Steaks, all leave the steak unchopped, which is better. But Philip lands right in the middle, he chops it a couple times. And there is plenty of meat, without it being ridiculous. The meat is fresh cut every morning. Philip himself told me that he does it most of the time. And due to the fact that it's kinda out of the way, there's never a long line and they make your steak to order. It's not sitting on a pile or in a warmer like the busy places at cheese steak corner. And Philip's will accommodate any special order. My friend likes his steak with sauce, and he likes it cooked with the sauce on the grill, and he likes a lightly sauteed hoagie onion, not the chopped onions, and they'll do that for him, no problem. try asking somebody at Pat's or geno's or jim's to do that. you'll get stabbed, or at least glared at and told to move to the back of the line. Anyway, this place is the best. So if you're in your car trying to park at pat's and geno's, just keep driving and go up to broad street, make a left, and then make a right at passyunk. it's about 5 min's down the road. the extra time you spend in your car will be handed back to you in spades when you can just walk right up to the counter and get your delicious steak right away. All without freezing your ass in line, and trying not to get in a fight with one of the hundreds of drunk douchebags around you. No excuses, Philip's is open all night, too.

text: I went to Casablanca with a large group of friends for dinner last night. One of my girlfriends wanted to get everyone together for a big Valentine's Day celebration, and Casablanca seemed like the perfect place to do it -- communal eating, plenty of seating for groups, and reasonable prices. I'll start this review off by saying that if I had written it at the start of the meal, I would have given them 4 stars... but by the time we left, I was ready to give them 1. I'll explain: The good: Casablanca is a really, really cool space. Outside it looks like it used to be some giant carpet superstore or something. But when you walk in, you feel like you're in a completely different world -- tapestries on the walls, tented ceilings, Moroccan music on the sound system... Plus the entire restaurant is a network of low sofas and cushions around small tables, accented with metallic embroidered pillows. Even though there are hundreds of people around you (again, the place is enormous), you feel like you're alone with your dining mates. Food is delivered on large plates that are meant for sharing, and people with giant baskets full of bread come around periodically so that you take take more pita wedges with which to scoop up your food (there are no utensils). At the start of the meal you're given a towel for your lap, and a giant urn of rose water is brought to the table and poured over your hands to wash them. Nice touch. The food is really good, especially for the price. For about $26pp we got the 7-course dinner: 1. 3 different cold marinated salads (eggplant, carrot, cucumber)... 2. phyllo dough stuffed with chicken and egg and sprinkled with powdered sugar... 3. chicken (we got the spicy version, don't be scared, it's not scary spicy)... 4. roast lamb (very tender, but if you're looking for "volume" get the beef choice instead as they only serve a few slices of lamb as opposed to several skewers of beef)... 5. couscous with chicken and chickpeas... 6. bowl of fruit (and it's literally a bowl of unpeeled fruit, the oranges still had stickers on them)... 7. baklava. now, #7 is where i get into the bad part of the review. there was no 7th course. let me back up -- when we went to Casablanca for dinner, we knew that it would be a long meal. (If you're thinking "let's eat here before we see a movie", don't. You won't make the movie. This is meant to be a long, leisurely experience.) We expected about a 3-hour meal, based on some of the party's previous experiences. However, our experience was DOUBLE that -- we arrived at 6:30pm, and didn't leave until 12:30 in the morning! 6 hours! At first, everything was great -- attentive service, a new course came out every 30-45 minutes... then after a couple of hours, everything started to break down. Bar service stopped completely, we didn't see our bar waiter (separate from the food service) for several hours. No joke. Then the food started taking longer and longer to arrive. Now, we understand that a restaurant's going to be busy on Valentine's Day, and the place was pretty much full... However, from what I could tell the slowdown wasn't due to the size of the crowd, it was the size of the staff -- halfway through the evening, all the servers we'd seen buzzing around earlier were nowhere to be seen. I'm not sure if they sent people home halfway through the shift on a packed holiday night, but we don't know where everyone went! By midnight, we were exhausted and just wanted our final course (the baklava) so we could all head home. One of the servers finally came around with our check, and when we asked about the baklava, we were told they were out. We had been waiting almost an hour for that final course, and no-one told us! Grrrrrrrrrrr!!!!! That really left a bad taste in our mouths -- 6 hours in the restaurant, and then no final course. And they hadn't even offered us a substitution, or taken a few dollars off of each person's charges to compensate. When one of our party spoke to one of the managers to complain, the manager was very apologetic and asked what he could do to make us happy, which was certainly nice. But the bottom line is, if you offer a fixed price meal and one course isn't going to come, you should proactively make it up to the customer instead of them having to ask. Bottom line: do NOT come here on a busy day like Valentine's Day! Try it on a regular night when they can handle the workload.

text: Considering eating here? Here's what you could do instead. Imagine that a camera's pointed straight at you. Then, say this aloud: "I just ate at Dolce, and I've just been Punk'd!"
