It does help when one can't get in / reservations at one specific place, of course. Come to think of it - that's probably another way of applying the "keep them around" principle that most casinos use around their gaming halls. There we were, at the Dolce entrance, speculating if all the rumors about its reputation and its cuisine were worth the 30-minute wait that we were quoted by the affable faces at the front desk. Someone opted out, and the three of us were ushered into a corner of the inner dining hall that a cozy table. A table that was probably best fit for two...if they were dating. Considering that we just skipped a 30-minute wait and that we were hungry, we figured we'd stick it out and picked up the menu for a quick selection. The "Appetizers you must have" section seemed interesting, and the "mixed calamari" was our first order. It claimed to be a mix of calamari, shrimp and zucchini. Turned out that the calamari was a much more mixed that we'd like it to be. Turned out that the entire plate of "mixed calamari" had one slice of calamari, one little shrimp, and a whole lot of greasy zucchini. Those numbers, and the greasiness; aren't an exaggeration. The house wine was surprisingly nice, but nothing that we'd consider buying on the way out or the sort. After the disastrous zucchini, er, calamari appetizer; we moved on to our main course. I opted for the filet mignon; and a Caesar salad on the recommendation of the server. That was strike two. They messed up the salad. The salad. To most people, that would be hard to do; unless the refrigerator had gone bad and their produce guy had a bone to pick with them. But, the fine folk in the Dolce kitchen seemed to pull off this feat with a great amount of (dis)grace. This was the worst Caesar salad I've ever had in my life. Ever. Ever. Ever. Bar none. Including the ones that I had on long-haul flights. The filet mignon and the wine were probably the saving grace of the meal for me. Nothing I'd go back for, though. Our server was polite, but his suggestions were obviously far from ideal; or even good. He also didn't have the, er, foresight; to get the "mixed calamari" appetizer off our bill in spite of us having run up a fair three figures between the three of us by the end of dinner. Well, that was the food and the service. I guess ambience is a factor as well, so here goes... For all the visions that the name "Dolce" conjures up, this isn't necessarily a place that I would recommend for a date, a business meeting, or an evening with friends. It's got a dungeon-y atmosphere that isn't exactly elegant or reminiscent of a castle or even a wine cellar. Neither does it exude the contemporary chic of an upscale nightclub that's frequented by the Ashton Kutcher set. The tables are a tad too close together, seating seems inadequate, and the noise level is somewhere between a Chili's and a sports bar. We didn't stick around for the dessert menu, but it was unlikely that a dessert would necessarily change my mind about the restaurant, after this experience.

text: Do you own any old hi-fi equipment? Is it broken? Are you sad because you can't find parts or people to repair it? It's o.k., Hi Tech Repair can take care of it for you. There's been a resurgence lately in vinyl records. Record companies are reissuing old albums on vinyl and many new bands are choosing to release their albums on vinyl with free digital downloads. I have seen a few places selling new turntables, but they tend to be expensive and are stand alone units. I much prefer my old console turntable from the early '80s, but when I inherited it, the turntable was wobbling and the auto side-change feature didn't work. I asked around town and was directed to Hi Tech repair, who fixed it perfectly, quickly, and for a reasonable price. The inside of this place is quite a trip. The walls are piled high with old audio and visual equipment of every kind. You wonder how they could find anything in there, but they manage to do it. They have some hard to find parts, including needles for record players. I'm not sure of all of their services, but I think knowing about this place would be handy for most music listeners and musicians.

I had the Victor Burger which was excellent - especially the fries. Looks like a nice place for dinner or drinks since the bar is large with numerous flat screens scattered about. text: Outstanding. Go there. Period. 5-stars is rare for me... you have to earn it. I'm a foodie and Amada may be one of the best restaurants that I have been to. Amada's execution is spot-on, the food quality is evident and uncompromising, the atmosphere is fun and sophisticated without being over-the-top, and the drinks were fantastic. Out of all of our meals from a week in NYC, Philly and DC this was the best (almost tied with Peasant in NYC) and any return to Philadelphia would have to include this one. I have great memories of this restaurant despite the fact that I was getting a fever in the process. The tapas of goat cheese and basalmic-marinated strawberries was refreshing. The garlic shrimp was very good, not great. The one tapas we almost didn't order of seasonal mushrooms from the grill was outstanding in it's simplicity (olive oil and lemon) and was devoured. We ordered too much food which did include the Valencia Pallea - which is the best (and authentic?) rendition of that dish we've ever had. The problem is that we were stuffed by the time we got it (takes 45 minutes to prepare). Next visit would be a few less tapas (thats going to be hard to do) and get the Pallea again. It was amazing.

The pool is set up for exercise use...nice big lanes for swimming....bring your googles if you are a crooked swimmer like me or you will be constantly bumping into the lane dividers. Facility includes a childrens level shallow pool for instructional use and offers many swimming classes for all ages, in addition to summer camps, diving classes in the diving pool and exercise classes....i.e. water aerobics. With your paid recreation fee you also receive use of a locker and access to towels so you do not have to bring your own. Locker rooms are clean and feel safe and secure. Plenty of outlets for hairdryers. Parking is easy and physically butted right up next to the natatorium so there is no need to walk outside with wet hair to find your car. text: A while ago, we decided to go to Amada practically on a whim. Being responsible adults, we called ahead and asked for a reservation. Apparently it takes at least 3 weeks to get reservations to Amada at a normal hour (between 6:30pm and 9pm)... So we waited 3 weeks and gradually I managed to built my expectation to a point where they were not even through the roof, but in some distant universe... Watching Chef Garces on the Next Iron Chef, did not help with the anticipation and growing expectations at all... Finally the day has come and we went to Amada. I was deadly afraid, as I know myself - if I have high expectations it's almost impossible to meet them, 'specially if I was building'em up for 3 weeks. Once we entered, the place was nice - well decorated and totally inviting. As we were a little early, we set at the bar and had a drink. The drinks were good and the scent of cured meats was almost intoxicating. Few minutes later we got seated and ordered $55 Chef Selection of tapas. It was a feast. I don't know how anyone can actually finish the entire thing. Almost everything we got was amazing and somehow managed to exceed my expectations. Tuna salad with was really good, though if you don't like mayo, it might not be for you.. Cheese platter was out of this world, especially (I believe) Cabrales with a dip that sort of reminded of Nutella, but obviously was not. The sardines were okay, rather the fish was really good, but I was not a big fan of the sauce or whatever they were served in. Salad with asparagus, favas, avocado was amazing. Personally, I think there should be just a bit more cheese, as once you put the cheese with the greens, it made it taste THAT much better... but it was still great.. Spanish Flatbread with shortribs, horseradish and bacon left me speechless... Lamb chops were really, really good... Wild mushrooms were even better... I can go on and on with each specific dish, but I guess it would be easier to say that with each bite there was an explosion of taste and apparently I have taste buds that I was never aware of, probably in places that should not even have taste buds and each one of these newly found taste buds was totally enjoying the bacchanalia of superior taste...

text: The food--regular pub food---was ordinary, and the service somewhat indifferent, though that got better as the meal went on...until I tipped over my coffee. But that's a story for later. I ordered the mussels (our server said they were really good), and I did get a giant order for $12--something like two pounds' worth. But they were very dry, despite the marinara sauce, which (I suspect) was just a can of diced tomatoes warmed and dumped into the bowl. No flavor or spices to the sauce, such that the mussels were something to be dragged out of their shells and consumed because I needed to eat something, rather than treats I looked forward to. My companion had the French onion soup (which was good) and a burger (not so good). Dessert (key lime pie, $6 I think) was good, not great. When I accidentally spilled my coffee at the end of the meal, our server brought a rag so that I could clean up the table, bench, and floor. Uh...oh-kay... I'm fine with informality, and the spill was absolutely my fault, but I was sort of surprised, especially since the restaurant was nearly empty (it was mid-afternoon), and my companion was an elderly lady. We weren't rowdy young-uns. I also would have liked a refill of coffee (hey, it was decaf!), but no such luck. She must have thought I was too jittery to handle another. Anyway, when we left the place we looked at each other and said, "I don't think we'll be coming back. Ordinary." We agreed that it was not terrible--that award goes to Halligan's Pub in Flourtown--but it wasn't worth going back to. The revamped Broad Axe Tavern is a far better bet, with better food and a warmer ambience. (Speaking of which, consider bringing a jacket...Magerk's is a cavernous stone place that's pretty cold inside.)

text: Okay, we're going to practice some visualization. I want you to close your eyes. Go ahead...yes, even you there in the back. Now, I want you to imagine a happy place. You in the back, I said happy PLACE - no hand motions associated with the happy place please. Clearly some of you are having a problem with the happy place concept. You need some more structure? Fine, I can do that. Eyes still closed everyone. So we're going to imagine a relaxing, low-key spot. Maybe near water. Water always seems so relaxing, doesn't it? That's good. Add a little sound now - water lapping, maybe a boat bell in the distance, a touch of bird call...who's snoring? Could someone please poke the guy in the back row for me? Thanks. Maybe we need to liven up the happy place a bit. Give it a bit more structure. Let's transfer this to a marina or boat dock. And I want you all to imagine a beat up looking shack on the water edge, built right onto the dock. Now if we're in a happy place and we're on the water and it's a lovely warm climate then we can't possibly go inside the shack, can we? That would have to be the kitchen or something. So keep imagining - let's put a big deck around the side of the shack, right out over the water. And maybe a nice long bar under a shady awning. Casual seating, grungily comfortable plastic-covered menus, plentiful cheap beer and wine, yummy fish tacos, docking facilities for boats...and a pool table. Right out there on the dock, under the sky. Now that's a happy place. You may all open your eyes now. Any questions? Yes, you in the back row? Restrooms...No, I don't think I remembered to put restrooms in. Do I need to think of everything? Fine, we'll put restrooms across the lot by the boat storage. Class dismissed.

text: I love Mediterranean food. It speaks to me. And when I'm not on the East Side to dine at my preferred Greek restaurant (Chicago Style Gyros), Istanbul is a pretty damn fine replacement. While they specialize in all the delicious items you'd expect at a place called Istanbul (hummus, gyros, falafel, et cetera), they also allegedly make a very tasty burger. Istanbul is just a short walk from Phonoluxe Records and one of my favorite Mexican joints in town, La Hacienda. Nolensville Road is a bit overwhelming, since it is packed with countless foreign food joints, and it's difficult to tell what's good and what isn't. Istanbul is genuinely tasty and authentic but relatively cheap. Just the other day, I got their gyro plate, which included lots and lots of lamb with long-grain rice, tabbouleh and pita. It was just over $7. There is plenty of room to dine inside Istanbul, and it makes for a good spot to have a casual, quick lunch. They are located next door to a funeral home, and those guys are very strict about parking. You'll need to park around back to avoid getting towed. The staff at Istanbul is pretty nice, but you might feel a bit ignored from time to time. They have a habit of speaking to one another in their native tongue at great length while you're trying to place your order. No big deal, though...it's just part of their charm.

Then tend to tone the curry down for Americans, so you may want to tell your waitress that you want yours hot or perhaps even extra, extra hot. The staff is very friendly and quite competent, though some have a slight problem understanding the U.S. dialect of English. text: Charter sucks. Period. I ordered Charter internet and cable television for one reason: AT&T Uverse is not yet available in my neighborhood. Having heard customer service horror stories from every former Charter customer I know, I didn't have great expectations...but I still prefer cable over dish so I thought I'd give it a go. The order: The man on the phone was polite. He asked me if I'd had Charter service at my previous address. I told him I'd been a Comcast customer; he told me he also uses Comcast. Red flag? The cost was also alarming. Charter quoted me twice what I had been paying for Comcast! Yikes! The installation: I was given a 9-11 am window. I had a family party to attend out-of-town, so I was really hoping for 9. Ha. The technician arrived at 10:56 am, just as I was about to walk out the door. Not his fault. I'm sure he had other appointments prior to mine, whatevs. He was incredibly friendly and efficient. If I were basing this review on his performance alone, this would be a 5 star review. Thanks Eran, for being the best part of my Charter experience. My cable and internet were up and running within an hour and I was on my way to the farm. The Moxi: I hate this fucking box. First of all, it's huge. It looks like it walked right out of 1984. The remote is crappy, the device is slow to respond, the guide is all kinds of fucked up, and don't even get me started on the "on demand" feature. I've read mixed reviews about this giant, energy sucking DVR. My decision is firm. I hate it. The first Moxi complaint: When I called Charter to tell them how illegible I find the guide and how I refuse to pay for something this cumbersome, the woman I spoke with told me I could either: 1) set-up an appointment with a technician who would bring another DVR, but I could not specify which DVR I wanted so he might walk through the door with another Moxi or 2) take the giant DVR to Town and Country, wait in line for days with the hundreds of people who show-up to pay their bills in person, try to trade my Moxi for a Motorola, and then come home and hook it up myself. Are you kidding me, Charter?! Just in case you forgot, you're in the business of customer service. Neither of those options would serve me. I explained to the woman that I didn't like either option and that I would most likely cancel my Charter service. She had nothing else to offer. The second Moxi complaint: When I don't like the answer I get from one representative at a large corporation like Charter, my plan of action is to call and speak with another rep. So after my second attempt at Moxi-ing ended in frustration, I called Charter. This woman was much more polite. I explained my situation, my hatred for the Moxi, and my desire to leave Charter for Dish Network or Direct TV if I couldn't have a Motorola DVR brought to my house and hooked up. She understood. She made an appointment for me for the next day between 1 and 5 pm. She specified on the order that I was to receive the Motorola HD DVR. The second appointment: So I got home from work at 12:55 pm excited for my new DVR. 2:30 came around and I was getting antsy. 3 pm and I decided to walk the dogs in the park across the street, that way when Charter showed up I'd be able to see the van and meet the tech at the door. We played in the park for about 30 mn. No Charter. Came home, did dishes and a little paperwork, threw in a load of laundry. No Charter. It was now 5:20 pm so I decided to give them a call. When I reached a representative, she asked if I could hold while she looked into the matter. 10 mn later she informed me that no one would be coming. WTF? I waited around for 4 hours for a service appointment that was canceled without so much as a phone call! Her excuse: "They are out of those DVRs. All they have are Moxis." She had absolutely no explanation or apology for why I wasn't called. The call was dropped. I waited for 5 mn, thinking surely she'd call back seeing our matter had not been resolved and she had my account information in front of her. Another confrontation: So she didn't call back! I called Charter. I explained I'd just been disconnected while discussing a no call/no show service appointment. The rep asked me if I'd like to be reconnected to the woman who was previously "helping" me. Hell no! I'd stick with this new gal. Again I had to explain my hatred for Moxi, my request for a new box, blah blah blah....She told me she could order a Motorola. That's hilarious, considering the previous rep told me that there were no Motorola DVRs. Only Moxis. I love how consistent Charter is. Anywho, she promised to call me within 48 hours to let me know the status of my DVR. And what about my wasted day? Was I offered a credit for my time or the cable I'm not using as a result of my building hatred for this Moxi? Of course not, because that would be good customer service. To be continued in 48 hrs...

For between $35-$45 per head, you can have an effortless clambake in your own home, including a choice of soup, fresh corn, red potatoes, chicken, sausage, 1/2 dozen mussels, 1/2 dozen clams, and a choice of seafood (lobster, king crab, snow crab or shrimp). text: Before I share my review, I will preface it.... As one who has first started out practicing hot yoga years ago, enjoyed it for a while , and then converted (finally!) to the traditional hatha yoga, yin and kundalini, I was/am seeking a yoga class that fills my spirit and body and allows me to leave class feeling both relaxed, yet strong and full of positive energy. That said, as I just relocated back to Indiana and am on a budget as I try to find a good 'yoga fit', I signed up for their monthly intro deal thinking Wow, The Yoga Center of Indiana must be a good spot! Desperate for yoga, I forced myself to go back what?, only 4 times in the month, noting I normally do yoga every other day. Why didn't I go more? What did I find at this Yoga Center of Indiana? Well, let me share my experience from today which was a last, and final, fresh in my mind example of what this place is like. Again, noting that to me the whole point and intention of yoga is to be the connection of mind and body centered from within that feeds positive energy and healing in a welcoming community (I don't mean utopia, but at least a bit friendly!) that fosters peace within and with the world. First, I chose to go mid-morning thinking the early, evening and noon classes I tried prior were packed so this might be better. Right? No, absolutely wrong. I walked in to a literally jam packed area that smelled of hot sweat and cheap swiffer cleaner. As I was 2 steps in, I was held up b/c it was so packed with hot bodies coming out and eager humans in line there was no spot to take off a coat let alone change. Sidenote - Oh, yes, note there is 1 restroom for classes of 50 or 60 and NO Showers - at a HOT YOGA Place! Crazy.... Anyway, I digress. After battling generally unfriendly folks so I could simply take off my coat, slip off shoes and get in line for the class, it was about 10 minutes of stuffy shoulder to shoulder mayhem. (Note mayhem does not = yoga). Most places both in the US and abroad where I have done yoga have a calm, clean, welcoming space. Not here noting not one person ever welcomed me or engaged in a chat despite my genuine effort. Ah, finally, I am ready and in line to enter the freshly swiffered hot sweat scent room. There were already 5 people smashed in per row where arms were bumping and the instructer asked us to make room for another - note, it is great to make room, but this resulted in the inability to literally move your arms to any thing resembling a swan dive or movement to the side (yet the wonderful gal all dolled up in jewelry next to me enjoyed reaching onto my body and dripping sweat without a flinch during this horrible experience - note, foreshadowing). As class begins there is loud music revved up from Madonna and I try desperately to breathe deeply and say 'Okay, remember this is not yoga, this is like just a cheesey aerobics class'. So, it begins.... an instructor yelling/speaking loudly constantly coupled with sweaty, and many overly thin and overly tanned women in my view (and a few men) led through an hour of 'yoga poses' without any focus on alignment or form or what the benefit of the poses are (i.e. making space, releasing tension, detoxification of the internal organs, etc..). Watching some nearby folks, I can only imagine the injuries they will have due to the lack of instruction and no focus or teaching on the safe way to do poses or to modify. The tone is one of 'oh, yeah, you can modify if you aren't strong enough!'. And, I believe a few instructors literally said 'this yoga doesn't worry about alignment!' and I thought you must be joking. As the class went on I kept trying desperately trying to focus on my breath and my internal strength as I had over the last 2 years growing my 'real yoga' practice. But, I could not during any of my few visits to this place, move beyond the loud music, loud instructor and smell of vanity as though most people were there to lose weight (although almost everyone appeared to be on the edge of unhealthy thin). As a result, I actually had to leave early as the sweaty women to each side of me had their feet literally under my body on my mat and dripping arms over me. Despite my buddha belly breathing and my prayers to the gods above to let go, I had to get out of that room! Yes, hot yoga is great to detoxify and sweat it out, but even compared to my other hot yoga experiences, this was pretty bad. To me, yoga is not about weight loss although when done regularly and with a 'yogi health diet' it builds fascinating strength and natural return to ideal body weight. That said, I found this place very disappointing, unfriendly, unsanitary and overall not for me. Disclaimer: For those who are not seeking an authentic mind/body workout/connection or proper alignment and want to jam out in a competitive fashion while sweating to tunes, this might be for you. Seems to be popular here with some though as they are growing.

Definitely, a tourist spot. You wait in a long line to have someone snap at you. Granted their menu is small, but not everyone knows the lingo. Sort of reminded me of the soup man from "Seinfeld". Then there's a matter of finding a place to sit and enjoy your bread, I mean cheese steak. It was fun to stand on X street and wander how cars would get through when the two lines from the competing stores merged. Don't forget they don't take plastic, but conveniently located on either street are fee charging atms. Next time, I'm taking the cousin's advice (which I received after this disappointment), and going to Jim's...aka home of the heavyweight. After Geno's, not gonna be too hard to beat.
label: NEG

text: The grounds look great on picture but living here is a different story. The walls are VERY poorly insulated; I can hear the conversations of my neighbors next door and those below me. Our electricity bill has been as high as $350 (we never turned the heat higher than 73 even on the coldest days, 65 during the day). Neighbors have reported bills as high as $650 for units larger than two bedrooms. This has been attributed to the poor insulation which allows the heat to escape. Personally, I believe it is the outside billing company (Nationwide Energy Partners) charges ridulously high amounts for distribution and generation. This company installs meters for each unit and electronically reads them from Columbus, OH but our utilities are provided locally. Their website states that they help recover development costs for real estate developers. Basically, Dobson Mills has found a way to charge you an addition $100-200 each month for living here. In addition, the security is poor, the craftsmanship lacks quality and the maintenence department takes weeks to follow up on order requests.

text: A few months ago, I was kicking around the idea of purchasing a new piece of furniture for my bedroom, a lingerie dresser, to be exact. Fast forward to last weekend; my mom asked if I was free to shop around on Sunday afternoon in search of my birthday gift - a lingerie dresser. Yeeeeaaaaayyyy!!! We went straight to Howard Hill, the wood furniture warehouse I had always seen without really seeing while driving by hundreds of times on Route 130. We were welcomed immediately by a friendly employee who showed us the wares. The store was chock-full of beautiful creations ranging from desks to vanity tables to toys to water bowl holders for dogs. Most items come unfinished but there were several finished pieces available as well, although the markups were considerable. Within minutes, we selected our favorite option but decided to shop around, for comparison's sake. I'm actually embarrassed to admit the other place we went; the items were so sub par with respect to their quality that it would be like comparing apples to... crab apples. We returned to Howard Hill a few days later and were welcomed back by another gentleman from our first visit. In ten minutes, the stain and top coat were selected and everything was paid for and loaded into the vehicle. The dresser has been stained and is awaiting a coat of protective finish. It's a beautiful piece of furniture that was made all the more special because of the hard work my mom put into preparing it for me. I'll cherish it for years to come!

text: I got a Groupon for this bakery and decided to try it out. I'm a total sugar and chocolate addict and always looking for a great bakery, something other than the thousand Italian bakeries that seem to abound in the Philly area. I bought 4 items on my first trip (and all within the limits of my $10 Groupon!) I got a specialty pastry called a "marjolaine," a chocolate/chocolate cupcake, a hazelnut cake slice, and a complimentary double chocolate brownie-cookie drop with vanilla glaze (because I actually came a little under the $10 and they wanted to make up for it.) Very friendly service from the one woman I dealt with on a Thursday afternoon. I ate the cookie first. Very "meh." It was dry except for the embedded chocolate chips. You can make much better at home using the Baker's Chocolate Drops recipe found on the back of their unsweetened baking chocolate, very easy to do, just add a generic confectioners glaze. Next I tried their specialty marjolaine, priced at $4.99, so I expected it to be good. This is a four layer hazelnut meringue filled with hazelnut and chocolate cream, a bit of jam, and covered with a chocolate glaze. Again, I was underwhelmed and had a hard time pinpointing why. Ultimately, I found it to be too rich and too sweet (half a slice made me sick to my stomach) but without a whole lot of actual flavor. The chocolate glaze quality was pretty good though. Next I tried the cupcake. And I found myself asking, what do the following have in common: 1. Sahara 2. Mohave 3. Death Valley 4. This cupcake You guessed it - dry dry dry! And the frosting was airy nothingness. I threw part of it away. Why do people bother to make cupcakes that aren't moist yumminess? If you want cupcakes, go to Brown Betty. End of story. Finally, the hazelnut cake square. Again, a lot of airy sweet nothingness, very unsatisfying. (In fact, the bakery box, when it held just the cupcake and cake square, weighed almost nothing. The marjolaine was the only hefty pastry.) This place reminds me of many of the local Italian bakeries, because their cakes tend to be a lot of airy sweetness as well. I was hoping for something different given the "Swiss" designation. No such luck. I won't be coming back.
label: NEG

text: Under New management again. The Explorers Den (Since 1956) has had a revolvement of various proprieters. Their advertising and signage all bear the bright GoExplorers logo. They continue to accept gold card (student debit) and credit cards. My first call went to voicemail that did not contain the restaurant-typical hours of operation, address or any please hold spiel. So I almost was prepared to give up but my stomach begged me to put another call through in ten minutes. Second time around they did pick up. Now, when I arrived I found that they don't seem equipped to handle multiple orders. There were 4 open tickets at once that whole time during that half hour and orders kept getting crossed. Rather than read the tickets, the guys behind the line continuously kept asking for clarifications on the orders. Multiple hands were getting in the way of each other instead of expediting orders. Several customers were visibly annoyed by the long wait. In the end, it was worth the angst. They gave me the best cheesesteak I had in quite some time! VIP card allows you to buy 9 and get 1 free. text: Okay, so it's a chain store. But I've been to enough Ulta locations to know what separates one from another: the staff. Maybe the few times I've been here just all happen to coincide with an 'off' day for the employees, but it seems like there's only ever one person here at any given time who actually cares about not completely alienating potential customers. The last time I visited this location, I went with the intention of getting my eyebrows waxed. The seemingly lone salon employee said that she was busy with another client and wouldn't be able to assist me for at least 20 minutes. Okay, that's totally understandable. The (suspiciously empty) salon apparently had just one person staffing it, as it WAS in the late afternoon. Imagine my surprise when I watched her leave the salon immediately after telling me she was busy. Imagine my further surprise when, upon exiting the store a few minutes later, I saw the same employee smoking and chatting away outside, looking like she had no intention of doing her job any time soon. The few minutes I spent browsing the store were quiet minutes, as not one store employee seemed interested in helping me find this item or notifying me of whatever current sale was going on. I spent one college summer working at another Ulta location and, let me tell you, we were told that satisfactory customer service was our top priority. In that regard, this location brings the fail quite spectacularly, as well-stocked as it may be. In short, head to the Marlton Ulta if you can. text: I went here with my in-laws for Father's day (our treat). It's obviously a dress up occasion and has a warm, dim, nice interior. My only thing would be that it was actually quite noisy when we were there and there weren't that many tables full. The salad was delicious. I had a wedge salad that was crisp and refreshing. Now I'm craving one, great! My husband had corn chowder soup that was delicious and creamy. They give you amazing rosemary bread with two types of butter. I believe one was a rosemary one and the other a cheese one. They were both very good. One was just a bit creamier than the other so I favored it! The sides come family style. They do warn you about that when you order, but I was the only one who hadn't been there, so the rest of the party knew that already. We ordered Flemings potatoes...which are amazingly delicious au gratin type potatoes. They were so good I had to stop myself from inhaling them. We also got the chipotle mac and cheese. It was creamy and delicious (I'm using that word too much, I know), with a slight kick. My mother-in-law ordered a plain baked potato for my sister-in-law (she's only 4) and the thing was a monster! They don't have a kids menu, but they will tell you that they have some things that are kid friendly, like chicken strips. They also brought out a small plate of cheese and apples for my sister-in-law to eat while we were eating our salads. As a born and raised Kansas City girl, I ordered a steak. It was a 6 oz sirloin and I ordered it medium. It came out perfectly cooked and juicy and delicious. text: Came on a Friday afternoon and arrived just before the lunch hour bustle. We were greeted warmly and seated quickly. The lunch menu is broken down into anti pastas, soups and salads, sandwiches, flat bread pizza, deep dish pizzas and some heavier entrees. On the back is an extensive list of cheese and charcuterie broken down by regions. After we place our orders I take a glimpse around the restaurant. Like the menu, it seems very simplistic and sparse but there are all sorts of small accents. The while tile and pine wood gives a fresh clean look to the interior. There are lots of smaller tables in the center of the room and larger ones for communal dining. On one side there's a conveniently placed wine store (Garces Trading Co. is BYOB) with an decent selection. Why hasn't any other restaurateur thought of this? On the other side is a cheese, charcuterie and take out counter serving many of the lunch items. Everyone behind the counter was very friendly and helpful. By the register is a selection of desserts that looked delicious. All this before the entrees arrive! I got the duck salad per the serves suggestions and it was darn good. It was probably 60% duck confit and 40% salad though, and therefore heavier than I was expecting. The salad was crisp and properly dressed in mustard vinaigrette. Hooray for lightly dressed salads not drowning in a sea of oil! The confit had moist and tender shredded duck and some fingerling potatoes and roasted peppers. Delicious and not too greasy. The poached egg was a little on the raw-er side and resembled soft boiled eggs, which I love. The whites were just barely set and a little gelatinous and the yolk was runny but definitely cooked. Yum! The flatbread pizza verde was light and fresh. It came with spinach, ricotta, green asparagus, arugula and fava beans all perfectly cooked. It's large enough to share with a salad on the side to round it all out. The insalata simplice was a misstep. It came with exactly two slices of the red grapefruit and perhaps a very small handful of the marcona almonds, and a tiny bit of shaved red onion. Yes, this was very simple (read: sparse) salad. It might make a good side salad. I'm dying to go back and try their cheeses, charcuterie, desserts and come by for breakfast or dinner as well. The restaurant reminds me of the combination Italian restaurant and gourmet shop Bottega Louie in LA. But Garces has actually accomplished this tricky combination with flair, whereas BL fails spectacularly.

text: NOTE: We only had the ramen, we did not try the sushi or the Koren food, which everyone seems to like. We will give this place one more try for those items but for now, this is my review on just the ramen. Ordered: Seafood Ramen $9.50 / Tonkatsu Ramen (Pork Cutlet) $7.95 Being someone who adores ramen, especially Tonkatsu Ramen, I was so excited to finally come here that it makes me cry hot tears of disappointment to have to give this establishment a low star rating. Simply put, it was terrible. Worse than terrible. More like never-ever-come-back-for-the-ramen horrendous. We were seated right away by a rather dour gentlemen who just pointed to our seats and grunted and went back to watching a little TV he had by his podium. Not an auspicious start. There was a couple at the sushi boat area (I'm bummed to read that the floating sushi is just for show!) and there was another couple on the other side of the restaurant. Other than that, it was really empty for a Friday night. Which makes me wonder why we had to wait so long for our order to be taken. Then we waited a long time for our two bowls of soup. All told we were there nearly an hour before the food came. Not cool. When the soup came I was starving and it looked great. I have uploaded photos to show how beautiful the ramen was. We squealed with delight over the unique wooden spoons and the lovely amount of seafood and pork. Then we took our first excited bite. Which became a very disappointed and rather difficult swallow. Perhaps I'm spoiled from having eaten at the best ramen places that Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Sacramento, San Francisco, Portland and Seattle have to offer. All I know is when I go to those other restaurants, the ramen, tho unique to each establishment and thus differing in depth and flavor, always tastes fantastic. This ramen did not. The broth was exceptionally bland and flavorless. The noodles were inedible. The seafood varied between mushy and rubbery, and tasted so "fishy" that it simply could not be eaten. The pork was so nasty and tough we could not even attempt to gnaw through it. It, too, had an "off" flavor. Maybe from the "off" broth. Thus, after waiting an hour to eat, a few minutes after reviving our meal we sadly pushed away our still-full bowls, asked for the bill, paid it and left our food sitting on the table, mostly uneaten. Now, remember how I said we were really hungry? Well, dining elsewhere that night was not an option because here is the kicker. Within a very short time of leaving the restaurant, both myself and my dinner companion became violently ill. I'll spare you the gory details, but suffice it to say thankfully our hotel was close by. Something was seriously not right about that ramen. I'm not going to give this place 1 star, because I did not try any other food items; perhaps the sushi is great, or perhaps the Koren food is as wonderful as I hear it is. So I'll give it two stars, that second star being one of hope. We will come back and try some of the other items yelped as being good and we'll do an update on this review. But I can confidently say that I will never, ever again make an attempt to eat the ramen here. And if I do try something else...well, let's just say I'll make sure I get a hotel really close by. Just in case.
label: NEG

Somehow the City Hall station always smells of something and is really dirty. The Metro lines at DC are the cream of the train lines that I've ridden on. Clean trains, very clean stations, and friendly workers. Reliability: As far as SEPTA reliability, I"ve had fairly good luck with the Orange/Broad St. Line. However when I've switched over to go to West Philly, then the trouble starts. The trains that I've taken to West Philly may or may not be on time and may or may not have room. Not to mention there isn't enough seating for the masses that accumulate when the trains aren't on time. Service: Hands down, SEPTA workers have to be the surliest, most customer unfriendly of all the mass transit workers I've encountered. I've worked in service industry positions before so I know how people can be idiots, but still, there is a level of uncaring and downright hostility that exudes from the majority of the ticket takers I've encountered here. So far for me its been a mixed bag. I get to where I want to go, but I do feel like I need to take a shower after riding on some of the train lines. Not to mention having to swallow some anger after being treated like crap from ticket people.

text: I'm going to start this off by saying that I'm not even going to talk about the InBev stuff...this is not the place to talk about that kind of thing. text: I would have given the country's first zoo five stars, if not for the hoard of baby strollers present on this stunning spring day. The zoo should have a maximum stroller count for entrance into the zoo, to keep the traffic down to just a feverish din. Of course, my wife and I brought our daughter, so we were certainly part of the problem. But, I guess, a crowded zoo is a vibrant, happy zoo....so why carp? 'Cuz I'm a curmudgeon, that's why. Apart from the Evenflow and Graco frenzy, the zoo was as impressive as ever. Most of the animals were enjoying the great weather (save for the Giant Rats, which don't come out until dark....damn them!) and the variety our zoo has is terrific. Baby lemurs hanging to their father's backs are worth the price of admission right there. But there's so much more. We even went on the swan paddle boats, which was great exercise until my wife got noivous and wanted out. Truth be told, I was rocking the boat back and forth like some dope from junior high. Can't take me anywhere. If you haven't been to the zoo lately, make a date. Weekday afternoons are probably the least crowded, with school buses driving away and the downtrodden still at their day jobs. Lemurs, elephant shrews, flamingos and cool new exhibits like Big Cat Falls and Squirrel Alley are just a few of the hundreds of reasons to see our animal friends. Better yet, get a yearly membership and enjoy the rides and parking for free. Worth it! ps---Squirrel Alley is not a real exhibit.

text: A great place for quality food, wine and beer. I was in the area a few weeks back and was delighted to discover this gem in the neighborhood thanks to some great Philly Yelpers. They did not steer me wrong at all. I love great and interesting food combinations and here you will be treated to plenty of them. I also love dining tapas style, sharing a variety of bites, it gives you a chance to sample a bit of everything. Thus Tria is ideal. We loved the roasted beets with feta. We are beet fans though, the roasting highlighted the sweetness and the feta was the perfect salty and sharp contrast to it. The figs with gorgonzola and prosciutto were indescribably good, I won't even try because it will not give them justice. The Italian meats platter was gobbled up, I am convinced there is no bad Italian meat to be found in Philly though the garlic oil, balsamic red peppers and bread added extra happiness here. I especially loved the bruschetta we got. Pistachio herbed ricotta with lavender honey. Like everything I had here, balanced flavor, crisp with soft, sweet with a bit of salty. Just really creative and delicious. I had a bit of the smoked salmon salad with citrus mascarpone and quite enjoyed the great flavors in it. Asparagus, capers, arugula all wrapped up in a delicious lemon pepper vinaigrette. I also swiped a bite of the smoked chicken sandwich, delightful with cheddar, tomato, piquillo pepper, and happy sigh inducing herbed truffle aioli. My pick was the smoked duck and spinach salad with cherries, pistachios, grana padano (yum) and a citrus mint vinaigrette. I am not normally a mint person but after a consult with the waiter and a little sample I was all over this dressing. Fresh and it matched perfectly with the ingredients. I did appreciate that they were willing to help me out if I was not a fan though. Even though I could not indulge in the great wine and beer, I had a lovely iced tea and enjoyed myself here a lot. So no worries if you are not a drinker. Fresh, innovative cuisine in a fun atmosphere with very friendly and knowledgable staff. Really not that spendy at all considering what great ingredients they use with such flair. Oh and I cannot even start to talk about the flourless chocolate espresso cake with hazelnuts and mascarpone. Madonn'.

Honestly, I vastly prefer the prepackaged sugar waffles that Whole Foods sells -- they remind me much more of the Lieges waffles that I actually ate in Belgium. However, even if I liked the waffles, I'd never go back to the Walnut St. Bonte because the customer service is so crappy. The two had struck up a conversation and by the time I arrived I felt like was in Han's pocket. We were intrigued by the Dry Hot Pot style with rabbit and were dissuaded by Han himself to sample the dish with another meat. If I weren't sold already on the simple decor and delicious scents in the air his recommendations sealed the deal. I would have eaten out of his palm. And then there were the dumplings in chili oil. Oh dear lord. I have gone back each time dreaming, salivating, having dirty thoughts about the satisfaction of Han's chili oil sauce. These dumplings make me want to write home to Mama. The flavor is full and well-developed. The heat of the chili pulses outward from my mouth into every pore and yet the food is delectable, not at all overpowered by the heat. Han and Eric (the other gentleman who I've had a chance to meet) are both wonderful. They are warm and welcoming, make genuine recommendations that show they have truly eaten everything on offer and have a keen eye for what makes each dish sing. I told my date tonight that if either of the aforementioned gentlemen suggested anything of the sort I'd have to run away with them. I love the food that much. text: Stanley is great. Opened by Scott Boswell ( chef of Stella!) after the hurricane, stanley is a great casual place to grab lunch or breakfast. Dont come here expecting a light healthy meal. Vegetarians might also have a hard time finding something to eat ( the only vegetarian option is the bananas foster french toast, not that they should be complaining!). When i asked for egg whites i got a weird look. But, its all worth it to taste the amazing creations chef boswell has come up with. Twists on casual favorites. The location is great too- perfect for people watching in jackson square.

text: Meh, I've had a better steak at Chili's. Service was good, the water was always kept to the rim, and removing my dishes from the table always happened in quick order. Now as for what I ordered... I had house salad with their citrus vinegarette. It was fantastic. However the tomato mush thing on the side was not touched at all by me. It wasn't all that good, and aesthetically unappealing. My main course was a buffalo steak with a blueberry compote. The steak a poor cut with a lot of fibers running through it, making a small section inedible. Add to that, blueberry compote? If I wanted to fruit my steak I would ask for it. To top a steak with a breakfast topping was lame. Cowboy Star in San Diego got the Buffalo steak right for me, not so much here. Overall it's not as renown as they make the steakhouse out to be, and if it was voted best steakhouse in Reno, the others much be really bad, as Charlie Palmers was only average.

text: If your getting an iceberg salad get your dressing on the side. Also, if your food is cold but the plate I warm - your waiter was slow and your plate was sitting a plate warmer for a long time. (such as Irish Cream) make sure you don't refrigerate them, as they will dry out, so store at room temp, or freeze for a later date. so many choices you will find it difficult to pick just one or two flavors.

text: I am the type of girl who enjoys eating her weight at a meal. I don't finish eating until I am full and satisfied. Mama's has let me down. I often CRAVE falafel, so on my way to the trolley one day I saw this place and thought "have to have it, now!" After the two people behind the counter finished their conversation about a party the night prior, the guy asked which size I wanted. "Large", I said, licking my lips in anticipation. Sadly, he handed me a palm sized, meagerly stuffed pita. I tried to ask if he gave me a small but he went back to talking to his coworker. I seriously almost cried, especially after I saw the small bar. The olives were old and gross and nothing fit into the extremely small containers they had. $7 for the falafel and a drink and I was still starving. I had to walk down to Gianna Jr's to satisfy the beast within. Sorry Mama's. Your falafel is good. But you're hoarding it. For now, I'll stick to the hummus and falafel I make. yummmm

text: This is a great 'just the basics' doggie daycare and boarding place. My dog, Maya, LOVES coming here. There are no couches or massages or tvs, but she could care less about that stuff anyway - she just wants to play. They're an indoor facility, but the dogs get regular bathroom breaks. During the day, the dogs have tons of space to run around together (there's a separate room for little dogs if they get a bit overwhelmed). At night, they have separate kennels, which are huge. It's totally clean and very affordable. It's run by a husband and wife team who are super nice. Also, it's located near the airport which is handy if you're a frequent flyer.
label: POS

text: Decent Korean BBQ for Nashville but horrible service. I've been to this restaurant twice now, each time receiving less-than-friendly service. To sit at the grill tables, you'll have to order a minimum of 2 meat items which is understandable. Two orders of meat will feed about 2-3 guests. A plate of Bulgogi and Kalbi will run about $20/plate while Samgyeopsal costs about $17/plate. Anybody that has eaten Korean BBQ at a more Asian populated city will know that's a bit pricier than normal. But since we're in Nashville with limited choices, this is decent. Seoul Garden uses hot coals instead of gas grills, so the servers will rush you to eat medium cooked meat to prevent too many grill plate changes. If you like the meat crispy and not chew a piece of undercooked Samgyeopsal, please be prepared to receive some "looks" from the servers. They serve about 6-8 Banchan dishes which the servers have turned their nose if you ask for refills. Please note that you'll have to specifically ask for how many orders of rice, they won't serve one per guest, unless you ask. Also, even if you order 5 orders of meat at the grill table, asking for a 3rd helping of lettuce will result in a charge. Final note, a 17% gratuity charge is automatically tacked on if you sit at the grill tables. If you're dying for the grill experience, give Seoul Garden a try. If you don't care for it much, there are a few local joints that will serve it to you ready to eat with a smile.
label: NEG

text: My two sons both study in New Orleans (one at Loyola University and the other at Tulane). On one of my first trips to visit them, they made a point of taking me to the Camellia Grill. Boy, am I glad that they did. What a great place! The burgers are fabulous, as are the enormous omelettes. It's fun to sit elbow to elbow at the counter and make new friends of strangers while taking in the floor show that the cooks provide. I wouldn't dream of visiting NO without at least one trip to the Camellia Grill.
label: POS

text: I came here mainly for the roti canai which I was craving and hadn't eaten for years. I'd been to the Penang's in Boston when I was in college several years ago and remembered it being decent food but nothing great. This visit fell short of my even already low expectations. The roti canai was fine and I gobbled it up. We also had the oyster omelette as an appetizer, and the ratio of egg to oyster was too high. For entrees, we shared the mango chicken, the fried squid, the malaysian buddhist, and the malaysian pork ribs. In Boston, the mango chicken was reliably tasty, but this time, the chicken was dry and stringy. The fried squid we sent back because we were sure they were old pieces of squid double fried in month old oil. It was that bad. The replacement was better, but still, the squid was too tough. The Malaysian buddhist was a vegetable dish that had a way cornstarchy, coagulated consistency, but otherwise the flavor was fine. The pork ribs in flavor and texture were good, but there wasn't much meat on the plate. Our waitress was great, however, and very helpful when we weren't happy with the squid. If I ever come back here, it will only be for the roti canai.
label: NEG

text: We actually just went for drinks, so I can't attest to the food, but it's an absolutely lovely shady spot that feels like you're entering some secret garden spot!

text: Out of all the bars on the strip, this is "it". And hell, it's no wonder why Nashville is dubbed Music City USA when even the bums outside are talented musicians/singer/songwriters (that's a totally different, yet funny story). Walking along the strip you'll hear one talented band after another, but Robert's is especially cool. text: One of my regular Sunday morning spots. The Soft Tacos are my favorite, fresh with a little bit of spice against the eggs. The French Toast is thick and tasty, pancakes are stacked high, and the omelets come mixed with great ingredients (my girlfriend is a big fan of the spinach and feta). The waitresses at the counter are friendly and remembered us after going in just for a couple of Sundays (always a big plus for me). Prices are reasonable, if not cheap. My only complaint, and it's a nature of the beast thing, is that they are always packed for breakfast. I mean, people sitting on the curb outside packed. As long as tables are moving along (we watched a guy slowly work through half an omelet over a half hour period after his friends had finish) the tables flip in a hurry, but don't expect to get seated right away. My suggestion would be to take a counter spot...more fun that way anyway. Great food, good service. It's unfortunate it's not bigger, because they could fill it up.

text: I've been taking out and occasionally eating in, at Jannie for several years now. I have to say its a really nice place outside of Chinatown. The decor and space is nice, the staff and service are great as well. I must admit in my 50+ trips to this restaurant, i've never tried their Chinese side at all, except once I had the hot and sour soup, but that was pretty good at that, with that classic tang that most places miss on. Their Japanese is nice though, fresh, cool, clean fish, always classic cut with a nice artistic flair. The sushi rice is quite good as well, all in all it's never let me down in all my trips here. I heard they deliver as well, but I live in the Port Richmond area and they won't come out that far.

text: Wow. Walking in. First impression. What a dump. Met friends here for dinner based on the recommendations of friends. Nice waterfront view but because of the low ceiling (all cheap drop ceiling tile), fairly dark paint colors, and orange lawn chairs, you get a feeling of being squished in versus enjoying the light airy feeling dining with a view of water should give. There is a lot of pride of being a mom and pop style restaurant which is rare in chain driven Tampa but the hallmark of Mom and Pop restaurants is inexpensive prices, delicious food, and family like atmosphere. No hits on any one. My husband and I enjoy good food and don't mind paying the prices that sometimes accompany it but the food was only so so. Nothing worth the 20 to 25 per entree cost. At those prices levels, there are similarly priced chains in International/Westshore Mall or boutique restaurants in South Tampa that cook food to blow you away. Everything just tasted like something you could find in the burbs or in Costco's frozen section. We enjoyed the music but in such tight quarters with hard tile floors to reverberate the sounds, it was almost too loud. Next time, we'll return to our preferred Harbour Island spot: Cafe DuFrain next door.

text: We went on NYE, which prob wasn't the best place to go (I prefer an urban nightclub myself) but nevertheless, it was an alright night. text: I am going to sound like a suck-up - but Couch Tomato is one of the best, if not THE best cafe outside of the city. C.T. is right off of Main St in Manayunk and specializes in specialty pizzas, wraps, and salads. The atmosphere inside is neat with stools, a bright red couch and tables. Add in some track lighting and you've got 'neat'. Usually when I goto a place like this I like to try their vegetarian entres because they are usually the most creative ones - not at CT. On my first visit with a friend from college we indulged on a Paco's Taco Pie. This pizza had meat, sour cream, tortilla chips, and some great cheeses. The 2nd time I visited with my parents we all went the salad route (which I recommend now) and got the 'Strawberry Fields Forever' salad which had greens, strawberries (duh), almonds, and coconut shavings. I know a lot of yelpers aren't the biggest Manayunk fans (not that I can blame them), but if you are outside the city swing a turn on that exit 338 and try Couch Tomato - you'll say, "Thanks Matt H."

Although not one of NO's "famed" restaurants, it's definitely worth an afternoon lunch (esp if staying in/near the quarter.)

text: I have a college professor to thank for turning me on to this radio station as I drug my unhappy butt into my 8am MWF class freshman year. Morning edition was always on the radio while we did our studio work, and while the lull of the voices and music made me want to go to sleep, the stories eventually got to me. This was real news that wasn't laced with celebrity news every other segment. I'm now addicted. I would much rather get my news from NPR than most television stations, where they let any idiot give an opinion. This American Life and Morning Edition are my absolute favorites, and I also enjoy the puzzle shows on Sunday mornings. I've also caught my beloved David Sedaris and Jack Handy on days when I was just flipping through my programmed stations, furthering my devotion. If no shows are playing, you're probably listening to classical music, and while this age of Britany Spears seems to continue to rage on, it's nice to catch some Beethoven sometimes. Just by listening to it on the way to work I can tell a difference in my demeanor than if I just turned on the local rock station. I probably owe my good blood pressure to NPR.

text: I normally do not write a review for this type of restaurants. However, I once wrote a review regarding Tuna Tartar at Cheese Cake Factory; so, I thought it is fair for me to write about Tuna Tartar served at this place. So, this review is strictly regarding Tuna Tartar. First of all, why they cannot use higher grade Tuna part as much as they are charging the price? ...means I thought it was over priced. Amount was not generous, rather small using really lean part of Tuna chunks only. However, it was mixed with minced Tuna meat with some oil - thought it was sesame oil and fish oil mixed, to make Tartar more like "Toro" type of feeling. IMHO, Tartar is much better if used with between chu-toro and O-toro with fine chopped blocks, not chunks. Served with baked chips...nice idea but I could not agree with. Besides, Miso paste on cucumber slices really killed flavor from Tuna if eaten together with Tartar - Miso and sesame oil do not get along in my mouth, unfortunately. BTW, they serve Sapporo Silver 22oz beer...was surprised see its price :(

text: I am definitely a fan. The view is great, the food is delicious and prices very fair for the area. All the fish dishes are good. I often get the Paella, filled with clams, mussels, shrimp and sausage. The service is mostly good but can be very slow during rush time.

text: This place is a real gem! Family run operation with Tony's brother in the back as the head chef! I had the angel hair pasta with scallops - the sauce was perfection and the pasta was cooked al dente. I was a little disappointed with the scallops as I was expecting thick hearty scallops that I'm used to in San Francisco, however St. Louis Scallops are a tad larger then a garbanzo bean. My husband had the chicken canneloni, again quite tasty. Everything there is made in house, which is why it tastes so fresh. Gian Tony's is a place i would expect to be in Little Italy out here, so bravo to you folks in St. Louis!!

text: I can't say anything about the treatment of employees, but I can say that they really helped me out when I needed it. text: Park Avenue Coffee Home of FIFTY-TWO flavors of Gooey Butter Cake! Gooey Butter Cake is a St. Louis staple, a classic right up there with toasted ravioli, Ted Drews, and Budweiser! Park Ave really steps it up a notch. I had never heard of flavored GBC, as far as I knew it only came in gooey butter flavor. I have only had 8 of the flavors they offer, but they wer all wonderfull. Even the Mint Chocolate Chip, which before I tried it gave me pause. So be adventurous! GBC is not the only thing they offer, oh no. This is a super cute coffee shop in super cute Lafayette Sq. Its sort of small, but it never seems over corwded. They have FREE Wi-fi and excellent coffee, roasted by the locally owned Chauvin Coffee. Tot top it off everyone there is very friendly. They have tasty spicy chai, a must in my book.

text: Wow. I can't even believe I'm only giving this place 4 stars. We went here for my birthday dinner last night. Since it's the top rated restaurant in Philly, I guess I had high expectations. And I just ate at Le Bec Fin a few weeks ago, so I have that fresh in my memory. The space is beautiful - The flower arrangements were to die for. It is very elegant, even if you still know you're in a hotel restaurant. Why can't hotel restaurants break free of that? The service was excellent. Not once did we want for anything. We did the 6 course chef's tasting with wine pairing, and the courses were brought out at a good (not rushed) pace, which actually allowed us to finish our wines for each. (I hate when I do a wine pairing and I have 3 partially drunk glasses of wine in front of me.) The wines with the pairing were very good - 2 California and 3 French. The Sommelier was very informative, obviously very excited about the wines, knew it all about the grape, region, etc. Hubby and I know a fair deal about wine and at first we thought he was talking down to us, but then realized that he was just giving us the whole scoop. The food. Maybe I'm just too hard to impress. Or maybe this particular menu wasn't my taste. But reading the descriptions on the menu, it certainly sounded like it was right up my alley. Not once when I took a bite was I "OMG this is AMAZING." That's kind of the reaction I'm looking for at a restaurant of this caliber. Actually I take that back - once I got that reaction. But only because the course included a hunk of fois gras, which I ate in one bite and since it was fois gras, was of course amazing. The food was very good, but in my opinion not the best in Philly by any stretch. Hubby loved it. But his palate doesn't crave the savory as much as mine. I have to say, I like Le Bec much better. There, every course elicited the response I was looking for. So I deducted 1 star because I wasn't wowed.
label: POS

text: We stayed there and the room was just okay but the TV didn't work and we couldn't get anyone to fix it and then we had to walk up a huge hill because we couldn't get a golf cart to pick us up. text: This is a great place to enjoy some excellent quality food and drinks with friends. The appetizers are amazing, as are the desserts. We got the cured pork tenderloin with raisins and cilantro (raisins gave it the perfect hint of sweetness), spicy tuna and chickpea stuffed peppers (soooo good!), white bean spread with baguette (creamy, flavorful spread on a warm, toasty baguette...need I say more?), and truffled egg toast (my favorite of the bunch). I had the smoked salmon sandwich with goat cheese, spinach, and brioche roll. It was the perfect blend of ingredients and brought out the flavor of the well-smoked nova lox. The roll was deliciously crispy, soft, and toasty simutaneously. I enjoyed a very smooth Pinot Noir, and capped off everything with the flourless chocolate cake. It was quite rich but incredible with hazelnut. I happen to love all things hazelnut and chocolate so I was in heaven. The service is very attentive and the prices are very good for the quality (~$5-8 for appetizers, $8-12 for wine, $9 for sandwich). This was my first time back here in over a year but I will be stopping in more often, for certain. The only downside is that it's so far away from where I live. Actually, that might not be a bad thing because then I would turn into a version of Augustus Gloop by devouring their desserts every chance I get...
label: POS

text: Tequila's is a beautiful place, but the food leaves a lot to be desired. I wanted to give three stars because one of my friends really did like her meal, and overall I had a really lovely evening - but when it comes down to my experience with the food, it really scored a 2 star rating by me. My tortilla soup had a strange taste, and the grouper I had was way too sweet as it was drenched in mango sauce. Their chocolate cake was super dry and their flan was oddly soggy. Our server, on the other hand, was great. I loved that he kept calling me and my friends "Senoritas" (until he broke, once, at the end, and called us "Ladies," ah well) though at first I thought it was a little too cheesy. He was very attentive, but sometimes in a way that made us feel too rushed. We were given very little time between courses, even though there were plenty of empty tables. Why the rush, fellas? And still with the speed of our meal, our plates seemed cold which was a huge disappointment. Worst of all, I feel tremendously full from a meal I neither finished nor thoroughly enjoyed. While I'm unlikely to return here for food, the ambiance was so lovely that I'd give the place another try for the fancy looking drinks I didn't get to try on this visit.

text: If you have lots of time to kill, OR simply want to have drinks/people watch in Spring Time this is your place. Ditto if you are a fan of small bones in your shredded chicken Quesadills. After we'd finally asked another waitress if we'd been forgotten, ours finally arrived and asked "Are you ready to order drinks and food now?" (as if we were the cause of delay... you know, by waiting 15 minutes politiely and quietly after having been seated). This place is lacking in good service, hot fresh (boneless!) food and pleasant attitude. This neighborhood needs some alternatives, but if Johnny Manana's is the only TexMex game in town- I definitely don't want to play. YUCK! Drive a bit further and perhaps go to Mi Puebla in Mt Airy. text: During a recent excursion to Chinatown, we found this place on yelp. As vegetarians, it looked pretty promising. And, my partner remembered going here over 10 yrs. ago when living in Philly. The concept of this place is really great. And we love how they serve brown rice. But, we think it could be done better. The lunch menu was reasonably priced, with interesting looking options. But, must say that it is weird that everything is referred to in meat terms, but none of it is meat. There just isn't a reason to call menu items at a VEGETARIAN restaurant "chicken," "beef" etc. And, a lot of it is just fried bean curd/tofu, which isn't very creative, and honestly isn't much better for you than meat (but I guess it depends on why one is a vegetarian). So, it sufficed for a cheap, non-meat meal. But, I can't say we'd hurry to go back.

text: If you are not absolutely certain you have picked out the perfect gift, think twice before buying a gift from Dandelion. IF YOU DO NOT RETURN AN ITEM WITHIN 14 DAYS, YOU GET NOTHING. No exchange, no store credit and certainly no refund. I have never encountered a store that was unwilling to at the very least provide store credit in a situation like the one I am about to describe. According to the store's return policy, I would have needed to return or exchange an item 3 days ago. Initially, I thought I would keep the necklace (purchased at their King of Prussia store) because I received it as a gift. When I realized it was a $75 necklace and decided to ask if I could exchange it for something a little more versatile, I was told I was out of luck. I contacted the corporate office, explained the situation and asked if there was any way they would make an exception and allow me to exchange the necklace as it was only 3 days past the deadline. I was not asking for money back. They refused. This is why I don't shop at smaller stores with such rigid policies. I understand that stores have a policy for a reason, but they can also go the extra mile if they choose to for a request that is not unreasonable. I appreciate the uniqueness of a smaller store or boutique, but not enough to put up with store policies that are this inflexible. Dandelion's return policy (taken from their website) is pasted below. The misspellings and poor sentence structure are theirs: Exchange at a store location 1) Make sure all merchandise brought in for exchange has its gift reciept; we will not be able to except any items for exchange with out this reciept. If items brought in with in 14 days, in good condition and have gift reciept then you can exchange for an item or receive a store credit.

text: valley green inn is blessed with a beautiful location but comes up a bit short on food and service. my girlfriend and i decided to ride our bikes up the river to vgi for lunch this saturday. and while the weather and the view from the porch were great, the lunch itself turned out to be merely mediocre. we ordered a course of soup and some sandwiches. the soup arrived in a timely manner, but my choice, the du-jour lentil soup, garnished with prosciutto and asiago, had a poor texture (gritty) and tasted heavily of bacon. what does it take to pass a soup through a chinois? our other soup was the everyday french onion which seemed to be topped, generously, with mozzarella cheese, but was otherwise good. if we were a bit underwhelmed by the soup, the sandwiches didn't improve on things. the individual elements of my girlfriend's grilled salmon club were fresh and tasty, but the sandwich was overloaded with, in her words, "blah bread." minus one slice of the chiabata, it was actually very nice, but as served, no. i really wanted to like the catfish po boy. it had a nice coleslaw topping and looked good on my plate. but again, the bread overwhelmed the fillings and to add to its troubled existence, the catfish itself was, well, a bit fishy and bland. i wasn't that impressed with their side of iceberg, red cabbage, and carrot salad. this is the kind of salad you get from a bag at the supermarket finally there were the yam fries. while they are tasty, the preparation and presentation on this offering is problematic. the fries are of a shoestring cut and served in a big bird's nest, which makes them almost impossible to pick up or eat without making a mess. and why they served them with ketchup is beyond either of us. we weren't up for dessert when our server returned. the service itself was good, but not very hospitable. plates were bused in a timely manner, but in a perfunctory fashion, and glasses were refilled with water, but not iced tea (nor was iced tea even offered again). a woman behind us complained about an undercooked piece of food to her server, who dismissively agreed to get the manager for her. the manager was civil, and certainly didn't contradict her in any way, but was not exceptionally gracious in hearing her complaint either. go if you're stuck in the park on a nice day. otherwise, skip it, or just go to the ice cream stand on the side of the building.

text: Wow, this place is absolutely adorable. Whoever decorated it- kudos. We were lured in by their gorgeous display of perfectly decorated cupcakes in beautiful glass cabinet, like little treasures. I got a cookies and cream cupcake, which set me back a somewhat shocking $4. I think that's the highest I've paid for a cupcake in the city- and it was only about half the size of the generous-portioned Brown Betty cupcakes for $3. The cupcake looked pretty basic, but maybe there was more to it, maybe some interesting flavor combinations like at Betty's Speakeasy... Now, keep in mind, it's RARE that I meet a cupcake that I don't like. I love 'em. Unfortunately my cupcake from Philly Cupcake was incredibly dry- like it was more than a few days old. The icing was basic buttercream icing with cookie crumbs in it, and the cake was just a regular chocolate. I kind of feel duped for paying $4 for something I could probably make better myself. My friend got their red velvet cupcake and it was the same. Totally dry and I couldn't really taste the cream cheese in the icing. Luckily hers was only $3, but that's still more than we should have paid for the quality. I will say, however that another friend of mine got the gluten-free Chocolate Coma or something and it was really yummy. The cake was moist and not too sugary sweet. The icing was really good (although again, nothing too special) and it was kind of dipped in chocolate to make a crispy chocolate shell on top. Maybe they should stick to denser flourless cakes for now. God, I want to love this place. It's so pretty, it's in a great location and everyone seemed really nice and helpful. But I've had cheaper, more complex flavors with more exotic ingredients at a number of other cupcake places in town. Their actual cupcakes better catch up to the adorable decor- cause I'd rather go to the ugliest storefront you got if they have an excellent cupcake. For now right I'll stick to gaze into their cute little window.
label: NEG

text: Warm, cute, cozy, hip, trendy, relaxed, friendly and unintimidating, Juju is the best. Oh, and by the way, it's eco-friendly, which helps to ease the pangs of guilt felt by suburbanites who undoubtedly contribute to the environmental crisis by burning a quarter tank of gas in traffic on the Schuykill Expressway just for a haircut, albeit an amazing one. text: Jeff (husband) and I have eaten at some of the best restaurants across the country, and Larry Dunning is hands down our favorite chef. text: I went to Cuba Libre for an event sponsored by my college for our Senior Week. For four years, I'd been hearing rumors about the world famous mojitos and salsa dancing, but never made it down to 2nd and Market until four days before I graduated. I wasn't disappointed. Cuba Libre's decor has a fantastic, weathered 1940s Havana vibe with its lazily whirring paddle fans, large potted palms and cracked plaster walls. The upstairs bar includes an iron balcony, which looks over the main dining area that is cleared out at night to become a makeshift dance floor as a live DJ spins Latin music. I normally don't dance - I'm a white girl from Connecticut, there's only so much I can do - but even I couldn't resist. Thank God it was a Thursday night and a partially closed event, because if there had been real salsa professionals there, I would have been against the wall like a seventh grader at a semi-formal. God bless the bartenders, because the mojito is one of the most labor-intensive drinks out there. I'm a bit of a mojito snob, but I wasn't disappointed - the classic mojito ($9) was delicious, but for a real treat, go for the pomegranate mojito ($11). Pricey, yes, but absolutely refreshing and delicious. I can't speak for the food, as we sampled one of the special events menus, but the passed hors d'oeuvres - I'm not a foodie, but I remember the empanadas, beef skewers, fried crab, and miniature mozzarella and spinach panini were all delicious and flavorful, and if they were any indication of the quality of Cuba Libre's regular dinner menu, then I might just have to move back to Philadelphia.

text: So. I'm not quite sure what a "utilitarian bar" exactly means but I can tell you that I like it. A lot. I was a little shocked by the locale but curious and thrilled that the East Side would home another independent biz. Fast forward to Tuesday evening, my friend let me know that she was at a "soft opening" and suggested that we have our planned "girls night" at No. 308 in lieu of our original plan to head to Holland House. Sure, why not? I knew that I was in for a treat as soon as I walked into the dark yet spunky retreat. The retro furniture and booths were perfectly appointed but not overly staged. Even the striped walls stood out yet didn't take away from the overall tone of the space. I absolutely loved the bar. The contrast of wood and metal pipes masterfully showcased character. Bottoms up! Our group nestled into a massive tufted booth and started ordering the "goods". The drink menu boasted imaginative cocktails with interesting names such as the "Writer's Block Shots" section ($5) that included the William Burroughs and Charles Bukowski! Smitten. I opted for a gin laced cocktail named the Suffering Bastard ($8) which nearly knocked me on my arse. Delish but potent! Our whole table enjoyed the libations and a few even ordered some food. The Sweet Potato Soup was on point and comforting! My friend knew the owners well and made the intro. I really enjoyed meeting Alexis and her staff. She proposed to the other owner in a Manhattan hotel room...guess what room number they were in? No. 308 Witty right? The owners and staff were casually dressed in tee shirts and jeans and was actually a refreshing contrast to what some may expect. It further drives the message home that this is going to be a fantastic destination place for some but still manage to be a cozy neighborhood bar for me. No. 308 is a real bargain due to crafty cocktails and interesting space. I am sure that I will be "checking in" a ton moving forward! TIP: The playlist was a fun mix of Johnny Cash, Top 40 R&B, and Indie Rock...gotta love it.

text: Oh... Oh my old... My grandfather is a stereotypical retired Floridian when it comes to dining out. His idea of a great meal is fettuccine at Carrabba's and a skirt steak from Outback Steakhouse. But he wants to impress us while we're visiting, so he takes us here. We walk in on a Wednesday evening - not a peak night for post-work dinner plans or a touristy day by any means - but nevertheless, I'm saddened as I walk in. "Is this place even open?" my dad asks. There are 200 tables and 5 are taken. Wtf is going on? Are we on a set from "Weekend at Bernie's?" or is this the restaurant from that famous scene in "Goodfellas?" Where's Scorsese? Where's he hiding? After we wander and find the hostess, we are seated right next to one of the 5 dinner parties eating here. Thanks for that. I order the ($26!) traditional paella. I'm expecting this to be great. The menu looks great, it boasts of awards and chefs that have helped craft the cuisine here. So I'm thinking maybe, just maybe, this isn't a tourist trap and the food may actually be authentic, who knows?! So all the food arrives, my grandfather's 1905 salad, my dad's pork chop dish and my paella. The word for the evening, as we are clicking our seatbelts as we drive off, after lying to the waitress about how good the food was: Bland. This place sucks. It honestly reminds me of a high class CoCo's Restaurant. Probably a great place to score some blow in 1983.
