Downtown Reno is pretty much gross anyway, and not someplace you want to be clicking along in your cute little heels. The back half of the bar is booth seating, where groups of younger (20--30) people gather to leer at each other. If I sound like I have a personal grudge against this place, well, I kind of do. It's tacky, run-down, and not even particularly clean. Sleazy, fat tourist guys are everywhere, making retarded small talk and flipping their stupid man-ponytails around over their "hip" bowling shirts, and the whole thing is so incredibly depressing that I never want to go there again. text: Whenever I move to a new area, job one (realistically job twenty or so, but that's not effective rhetoric) is hunting down a good place to pick up used vinyl. BWS eluded me for a few months, but upon discovering it I have fallen in love. Granted our courtship has been fast and capricious, as things tend to be at the beginning, but I imagine my feelings won't be changing any time soon. Not only does Beautiful World offer a considerably wider inventory than its closest analog in the area (the misleadingly titled Marvelous), loads of new material is constantly spilling in, and the staff are quite knowledgeable and are not pretentious, self-styled music elitists, a common shortcoming at such establishments. They also endorse reuse of the plastic bags they supply, which I like. Many may find the simple alphabetical organization under genre headings (as opposed to organization by band name) an inconvenience, but I think it only adds to your delight when you stumble unawares across, say, Mott the Hoople's "All the Young Dudes", as I did earlier this week while perusing the M's, rather than noticing a divider with the band's name and flipping right to it. I find the scavenger hunt format to be much more exciting. Some may agree. Beautiful World also has a modest but appreciable amount of new vinyl, both reissues and contemporary stuff, which is often an attractive alternative to CDs or mp3s because many bands these days include with their new releases on vinyl a code and instructions for downloading the entire album for free, if you consider having a digital copy necessary. I'm not really in the market for used CDs anymore, but a cursory survey suggests that their selection in this department is also respectable, if that's your thing. Also, if you come across any Flying Burrito Brothers in your browsing, please purchase it for me and I will reward you handsomely. Too long has that record evaded my best efforts to secure a copy.

text: Panting like John Belushi for Blues, I was for a patio with beer & lo! live blues! I heard good things about the restaurant that occupied this space prior...but it couldn't have been this good! Inventive use all around: front dining room is a tight squeeze but intimate, and, well, they're serving food so good there'll be wait, and, Indy, kind of really needs a tiny bistro where people are spilling over each other and people wait outside. Speaking of outside...front patio...back patio. Patio bar. When I see two bars so close to one another in one establishment, I get all fuzzy inside -- especially if one of them is a cabana style outdoors bar. Really...I could sit outside of that bar & feel like I'm in Cabo: outdoor bar, patio, music, people (not to mention that shimmery canal ;) !) Awnaw Claus's gone Northside of Indy, finally! I've seen some other Southside, downtown joints have Indy's Sausage King (Abe Froman's got nothin' on Claus!) and now, Flatwater brings him uptown with their "Best of the Wurst" plate of sliced sausage, brie, nuts & pears. It's distinct that Flatwater is local and supports all things local -- from Claus to Sun King beer. Stellar resiliency by the bartender to get a customer to try the Sun King, then said customer requests Miller Lite, and the Bartender then proceeds to really clarify what Sun King has to offer. Deal struck. Customer quaffs the Cream Ale! What a victorious bartender! The menu ranges from Walleye like your Uncle caught & served back in '87 to ribs to mediterranean chicken drenched in artichokes & kalamatas to pork tenderloin, pork medallions ("do I wear them around my neck?" "I will, doggonit.") pulled pork to shrimp tacos to a veggie french onion soup. Yes, a veggie french onion soup (that's the dream isn't it? at least it was for me when I was vegetarian). Okay it has cheese. But cheese is a fruit, right? The servers, cooks, owners, bartenders, are all together on something: they're good people. Really. Laid back and hospitable and on top of it. Speaking of the Top -- this is the top of the list of Indy's new eateries & imbiberies. Get it!

text: Well, you have to compare Feast to Cochon since they both focus on pork and meat products and well, Feast beats Cochon in terms of flavor. Placed right next to Rock n Sake on Fulton street - the interior of the restaurant keeps its warehouse interior but with lots of wood and dim lighting - with playing classical and french music in the background. The menu is divided into two - they have a "classics" section which are favorites from the other Feast restaurant and then they have rotating daily(or however fast they change it) menu as well. Note to everyone - I find that the entrees are what they are, but prepared differently than what you would expect. I started off with the classic pork rilette - which I'm always used to rilette being cold and pretty much in pate form - however it came out warm with a similiar texture to canned tuna - I was kind of disappointed with this one. My dining partner had the lentil soup which he liked a lot - but that was part of the revolving menu. I had the pan seared amberjack with haricot verts and bacon and sauteed spinach- the amberjack was seared very nicely and the vegetables were delicious. My friend had the pork belly pot pie - you would think the inside would be a thick stew but it was pork belly and veggies in broth - like I said, things are prepared differently here, but the flavors and ingredients work nicely. Service was great with enthusiastic servers - they have a pretty decent wine list but their cocktails are well made. I had a delicious Pimm's Cup. They also have happy hour from 5 - 630. Again, one of the newest restaurants in the city, has been open a couple of weeks as I write this. Check it out.

text: I visited to Jacque-Imo's years ago when I first arrived in New Orleans and I thought it was phenomenal. I've been several times in the years since and still loved the food. I visited recently with my husband and barely recognized the food. The decor is still the same, eclectic New Orleans kitsch, but the food has seriously devolved. What used to be good, innovative cuisine from a funky, authentic neighborhood joint is now mass-produced, mediocre fast food in a noisy, hostile dining room. It appeared from our seat near the kitchen that the kitchen is now merely an assembly line with no chef in sight. The salads were wilted and the fried oyster on top overly-greasy and luke-warm. Our entrees, which back in the day were phenomenal, were overcooked and extremely bland, and the Alligator Cheesecake I used to dream about was cold and gritty. The service? Awful. Our waitress was cold and abrupt and made us feel as though her main objective was to get us in and out so that she could flip our table. My husband is one of those guys who always has menu questions and he bit his tongue after she lost her cool when he had a question about the wine list. By the time our entrees arrived we had resigned ourselves to finishing as quickly as possible and getting the heck out of there with no plans to return. The above being said - the whole affair was extremely over-priced. The golden days of Jacque-Imo's are over and there are plenty of far better restaurants in the Jacque-Imo's price range.

We should have ordered the lamb, someone else had it served in the interim and it looked pretty delicious. Total was $70, Adolfo's takes cash only. text: I was so excited to see a new restaurant opening in the area, especially one that wasn't a chain, so when i heard that the Village Bistro had finally opened, I went about a week later (give them time to work out some of the kinks). It was by far one of the worst dining experiences I've had in many many years! I don't even know where to start... First, I think "Bistro" and I think warm and cozy, easy lighting, nice music, comfort food with a creative touch... there is nothing 'bistro' about this place. It's loud, lacking in color and personality, and the tables are tiny, uncomfortable, and crammed together. The menu is fairly large and comprehensive - I chose the Tilapia Mignonette and here's what their menu says: "pan fried tilapia topped with lemon, lime, shallots, and buttermilk carrot fries. served with coconut basmati rice" sounded promising. I also got the tomato bisque and fruit plate as my sides. My 4 year old ordered the chicken strips and fries. Our waiter was making a good effort but was either really new or really bad at his job. I tried to give him the benefit of the doubt but as the meal wore on, it got more and more difficult. Finally, our food came (with no silverware, of course) and when it was put in front of me, i think i actually gasped. I'm no food snob, I swear to you - i can eat fun carnival food and i can eat Michelin starred cuisine - but this was shocking! I've seen better at hospital cafeterias! And, as it turns out, I've TASTED better at hospital cafeterias!!! The tilapia had the texture and smell of canned tuna, the 'topped with lemon, lime, shallots" turned out to be light yellow water tasting faintly of lemon, the carrot fries were raw and so greasy that the batter oozing off of them (not to mention that there were only three tiny pieces), and the coconut basmati rice was undercooked institutional-looking long grain and wild rice with absolutely NO flavor - no coconut, no basmati and so underdone that i actually thought i cracked my tooth when i crunched on a wild rice grain. Finally, I just put my fork down in disgust. I couldn't manage any more than a few bites. My daughter's chicken strips were on the verge of being burned but salvageable. I cut them up and was happy to see that it was nice strips of real chicken. I took a fry as she ate a piece of chicken. We both looked at each other like all of the moisture had just been sucked out of our mouths. They were so dry and bland that i actually salted my 4 year old's food! I'm sure people were shocked to see a mom salt her toddler's food but seriously, that was they only way we could get any of it down! Then, my sides were brought. Oh boy, I had forgotten about those. The 'soup' looked ok but the fruit plate was pathetic. I'm not kidding - pathetic. On the 10" white plate, there were 3 or 4 thin slices of fresh apple that were browning already, 4 slices of orange that were so over ripe that they were mushy, and a small pile of canned pineapple sitting in the center. wow! Ok, skip that and on to the soup. Tomato Bisque. First of all, the owners and chef need to look up the definition of a bisque (smooth and velvet with cream). Let me tell you my version of how to make their "tomato bisque" - take a whole fresh tomato, drop it in boiling water for a minute to loosen the skin, take it out and peel the skin, put it in a bowl and mash the heck out of it with a potato masher, pour a little puddle of cream in the middle, and serve. Seriously?! It's kind of sad that that's the best thing we ate while we were there! I wanted so much to like this place - it's new, it's local - but I can not recommend this place and will NEVER go back!

text: If I had to pick a favourite Starbucks in Edmonton, I think this one would be it. The only way to describe this setting is that it is wonderful. This is what a coffee place should be. It's a very relaxing location that is conducive to having a relaxing chat with a friend or avoiding the stress of the office. It's not far from downtown either. I just wish it was closer to home for me. I will now judge every other Starbucks I go to by this one. Busyness - It's pretty steady. Obviously it's a popular coffee place in this older neighbourhood. I get the feeling I was lucky to get the biggest table in the place. Noisiness - Aside from the occasional blender, it's generally pretty quiet. The music is at an acceptable level and I'm tucked away at the back, so I miss much of the traffic. Ambience - I understand this is called High Street and it's a great area just a short distance from 124 St. Power - The booths don't seem to have power but the other tables look to have power available. You may have to stretch a cord in some areas. I don't know if the patios ever have power. Free wifi - Yes, free wifi is available and works well. Staff - They're friendly as always. I got my coffee quickly as I usually do. I almost always order coffee, unless I'm at a Starbucks in the evening when I order passion tea. If it's got an 'O' on the end of its name, I probably will never order it. Seating - It's not a big place, but it's laid out well and it has a lot of seats. The prep area doesn't take up half the floor space, like it seems to in some places. There are 24 seats with two of them being comfortable armchairs. Those seats also include three great little two-seat booths. With one large table to work at, you'll easily fit four people. The outdoor patio is huge (nine tables) and on a hot day it would be really nice to enjoy sitting out in the shade of the huge trees (elms?) lining 125 St. Security - Seems like a pretty good area, but I'd still lock up the laptop or bring it with me when heading to the washroom.

text: This is just our personal experience based on our circumstances. From talking with other parents, I know that others have had different experiences. We signed our son up for the older babies/young toddlers' swim class. We had done the low-key class at the YMCA previously. We went to the classes that were held in the swimming pool of a retirement home. The school is the exclusive user of this pool at night. The pool itself was very very busy. While the class was going on in one section of the pool there were numerous private lessons with older children and instructors going on, as well as their parents hanging out around the pool. This wouldn't be too bad, but I think that the siblings or kids waiting for their lessons that hang out around the pool ramp were the biggest problem. I'd be walking my son down and 7-year-olds would be doing headstands or swimming beside us. It made it harder to enter the pool. Secondly, the amount of noise in that small pool did not make for a calm, peaceful environment. Third, there were so many toys just floating around the pool. I don't know why there were so many toys there. The pool edges were covered in toys - many of them those that didn't seem to be "pool toys" like stuffed animals. Maybe other kids are okay with that much stimulation, but my kid isn't. The class itself (babies/parents) was pretty large for the space. The impact of this was both that one didn't get as much one-on-one interaction as perhaps you'd hope and that there wasn't a lot of room to move. The range of abilities and ages was pretty wide. There were 3-year-olds that were nearly swimming on their own in with not-yet-walking babies. I realize that this is more due to the scheduling than preference of the school (you can't force people to do a Wednesday or a Monday if they don't want to), but it was a bit tougher. My son was not doing well in the class and while Wendy gave helpful suggestions for getting him more comfortable in the water (and I totally trust her opinion on this), they didn't jive with our parenting philosophy. We aren't believers in letting our son (at that time he was about a year old) cry through something that he isn't enjoying. Wendy could have totally been right that letting him cry through it could have worked, but I wasn't okay with it. And finally, when it came time to renew, I felt a lot of personal pressure from Wendy via phone and email to continue with the class. It was not working for us because our son wasn't happy, and we were going to be traveling extensively during the next class period, so signing up to take only a portion of classes wouldn't work for us. We also were limited as to what classes we could take because we were commuting from 40 minutes away. Although I clearly presented these issues to Wendy, she kept pressuring me to sign him up again. (And I have heard from other parents about this pressure.) I know that this is her business, but the pressure left a bad taste in my mouth. Business-wise, Wendy's school is very organized. The billing, the sign-ups, the class schedules, the listings -- while few are electronic (although some are), all are done very professionally. She has a ton of staff, all easily recognizable in their uniforms, mostly polite high school and college students. You're not likely to encounter issues on that side of things. All-in-all, if you are interested in your child swimming seriously (swim team or whatever), Wendy's school is a GREAT choice for you. Her instruction is good, she runs her business professionally, and there are a lot of options as a kid grows. If you are more like us, looking for a fun activity for parent-baby bonding that also helps baby get more comfortable in the water, Wendy's class is probably not for you. We had a good experience at the YMCA with a more relaxed class.

text: So... my bf and I were sitting in the car one Saturday morning, tossing around breakfast/brunch ideas. Sabrina's?? Nah, too crowded. Honey's? Nah... too over-rated. Cafe Estelle? Nah, too expensive. IHOP? Nah, too dirty. Finally, I thought of the spot I pass by all the time on the way to my hair salon.... Urban Cafe. My bf agreed to give them a try. When we pulled up outside the place, I was kind of surprised to see that there were meters outside. Hey, I'm a Jersey girl! I haven't spent a lot of time in Germantown, so I thought meters were just a downtown thing, for the most part. LOL When we walked in, to our surprise, there was no host to greet us. One of the cooks in the kitchen told us we could either eat upstairs or downstairs. That was a relief to hear, because "downstairs" consisted of 3 already filled tables. We went upstairs, selected our table,and decided we were feeling Urban Cafe's vibe already. What a unique mix of people. Everyone from church-goers, to college kids, to families, artsy, geeky, white, black, old and young. It was modestly furnished, but comfortable, and it was warm and cozy on this 12 degree day. We decided we loved the menu choices... your typical breakfast choices, but you could also get fish, or turkey bacon or sausage, something my bf and I took note of immediately because we aren't pork eaters and very rarely eat beef. We both ordered the Rittenhouse Scramble: eggs, crabmeat, spinach, tomato and cheese. (Although OURS was MYSTERIOUSLY missing TOMATO! LOL) It came with your choice of two sides, so I got turkey sausage and potatos, and my bf got turkey sausage and grits. Our food was DELICIOUS!!!!! Best of all, we got REAL portions, not those mini-samplers you get at MOST of the popular brunch spots!! My bf also ordered a delicious hot apple cider, served with frothy whipped cream on top. I ordered a milk chai tea, which was good, but not half as EXCITING as my bf's cider. LOL When our drinks were delivered, I was immediately sorry I didn't get what he got!! Our waitress was cool. Bubbly personality, and right there with whatever we needed. I enjoyed Urban Cafe. I would suggest they play the music a little louder, as I'm NOT a fan of other people's conversations AT ALL!!!! LOL Go..... you'll be happy you did!

text: I really only wanted to use this site to extol praises upon positive experiences I've had however, this place has prompted me to forewarn you all before you are severely disappointed. As I usually stop in after I drop off movies at the TLA, I'm certainly not dressed to impress anyone in this shop, (not that I would anyway), so they tend to look at you like you are conveying a foul stench into their store by not looking like you could spend a million dollars. Now, as this IS a consignment shop (in case THEY forgot that) I'm obviously in the market to find good bargains on gently used items, which would insinuate that I am not in the market to spend a ton of money. So yes Attitude here is a must if you'd like to fill out an application. I bought a denim blazer that has a bustle added. A big bustle with sequins and lace and tulle that I absolutely adore. And I am more apt to support a local designer than anything else in this store. And so for that I have come back. Two weeks ago I was dropping off movies when I beheld in the window this absolutely amazing pink fur purse. I marched right in and was determined no matter the cost to but it as I was absolutely in love with it. I asked the girl how much it was ($89.00) and told the girl that I would take it. Right there, I offered to scoop it up no questions asked about it's designer or grumble over the price. The girl proceeds to tell me they can't just sell items from the window as they would have to change out the display too often. I was a bit taken aback by this as a sale is a sale is a sale. This is consigment, there won't be any in the back or any more coming in. So, at this point I'm like great so I'll just have to wait and then pray I get it when it comes out of the window? She's like oh no we keep a list and when we change the display we call the people on the list starting from #1 and offer them to come in and purchase the item. So of course I'm determined to have this purse so I ask to be put on the list thinking if I'm lucky I'm the 3rd or 4th person who wants it. No, the girl tells me I'm #1. I write down my name, my phone #, and the item that I want really really big so it can easily be seen. The girl puts a big #1 next to my name. I ask again if there's any way I can buy it now and she even looks briefly to see if she can replace it with anything but, no luck. I ask again it won't be sold to anyone else until I get called? I get a no way we do this all the time and everyone knows to use the list. Okay I think, just breathe the purse will still be mine. BOY WAS I WRONG!!!! Yesterday I am joyously returning movies to the TLA (love that place btw), and I decide to look longingly in the window at the future Ms. Kerry's purse. To my shock and dismay, it is not in the window. Not only that, there is nothing in it's place! As it is 11:45am they are not open yet for me to inquire as to where MY purse is in person. I go home, I stew until 12:05pm when I know they are open, I all ready know what they have done, and I am not happy about it. I call and the girl answers the phone and I say I was just up there and I noticed that the pink fur purse that I had put my name on the list for is missing out of the window is there a reason for that? Not only that but my name was #1 on the list for that item. She stammers and says oh well someone who works here who didn't know about the list sold it, I'm so sorry. Sorry, SORRY I say in disbelief? I ask what is the point of having a list if you're going to disregard it and sell it to someone else anyway? I ask why I was told that all the employees know about the list if you're telling me now someone doesn't? I'm fuming at this point but, I keep my cool and simply say well that's fine then you just lost a good customer, saved me some money, and I will be sure to tell all my friends how horrendous your store really is. So please if you go here don't ever expect to get an item in the window, don't ever expect to be treated with respect, and dear God don't ever ask to be put on the list! Hands down I will never walk into this store again!! BOYCOTT!!!

text: Peanut butter and jelly, milk and cookies, chips and salsa, fish and chips, gin and tonic, Spencer and Heidi: some things just go well together. Hard as they try, others do not. Sushi fused with Mexican sauces do not. Indeed, Sushi Saga is a fusion kind of place melding together Japanese with Mexican. The end result, in my humble opinion, does not provide for the best of both worlds. Allow me a bit of your precious time to elaborate. I like sushi. I like spicy sauces. I do not like spicy sauces drowning out sushi. Unless, perhaps, the sushi is of sub-par quality. Does this sum up the complete review of Sushi Saga? Partly. I cannot say with absolute certitude that the rather strong and spicy sauces they create is done intentionally to mask mediocre sushi. All I can attest to is that I did not particularly enjoy the sushi I had on this particular visit. On my most recent visit this evening (my last visit was literally years ago when I lived in the area), I ordered two mini rolls. One shrimp roll topped in a creamy/spicy shrimp sauce (Crazy Shrimp) and another with tuna roll topped with a ponzu sauce and green onions. There were a total of six pieces in each roll, and altogether each was moderately sized. Two mini rolls pretty much filled my tummy. I think if I separated the sauces from the sushi, each ingredient would tasted fine. Together, however, not so much. It didn't taste bad by any means. It may be that I am purist at heart, or stomach rather, when it comes to sushi. Honestly, this is really the only fusion sushi I've ever ate. Being a Saturday night, I can forgive an establishment for bad service. With that said, I forgive Sushi Saga's service. My poor friend arrived five minutes before I did. As I sat down next to him at the sushi bar (the place is fairly small and the bar accommodates 6 or 7), he quietly informed me that he thought that the staff there didn't like him. I asked why, and he replied that he never got a menu and that he sat himself at the bar. After a couple of minutes of my arrival, we got a menu. One set (with separate dinner and sushi menus) between the two us. After marking the sushi order list, I wasn't sure if I had to hand to the sushi chef, who looked busy and had gloves on, or give it to our server. Nearly five minutes elapsed when I flagged down our server to hand her our sushi order. Again, the place was close to capacity, so the spotty service wasn't a big deal for me. For some inexplicable reason, the signage out front is simply a question mark. Seriously. Perhaps it's because it's confounding why anyone would create sushi creations with a Mexican flair.

text: If someone were to ask me why Thai food in St. Louis was less-than-stellar, I would probably list the admiration of the King and I as exhibit A. The stir-fry dish I had here was oily to a fault, and the appetizers (crab rangoon, spring rolls) were mediocre. Forgettable food, service that wasn't endearing, and slightly overpriced. Now I'll list the more fundamental problems I have here that cause me to rate this 2.5 a 2 instead of a 3: -It's named after a Rogers and Hammerstein musical about an English governess who in real life fabricated large parts of her story. They're in Thailand for goodness sakes and there's singing and dancing. And they got a Russian-born actor to play the King. It couldn't be more fake if Jayson Blair wrote an article about Pam Anderson's upper half. As such, it is, to me, a lousy name that suggests the food is fake and caters to Westerners, which probably would be accurate, but I digress. -On the menu, you will find Thai Ravioli, Bangkok casserole, Thai Fajita, and something called Forrest Gump. I'm not making this up. But the owners did, because it's sure as heck not Thai. Maybe the casserole is, I honestly don't know, but if they're going for delicious fusion food, I think they could do better than throwing some meat and curry sauce in a cheap tortilla to attract people who really wanted Mexican but got drug to this place. -Despite boasting of Thai Fajitas on their recommended section (!), they have the audacity to boast of authenticity on numerous parts of their website. Call me what you will, but I'm sorry, if you offer Thai Fajitas and Thai Ravioli, I can't take you seriously. You're a half-step from offering curry burgers, sweet potato fries, and Thai custard milkshakes. Maybe I'm just a stickler, but I don't think you can't have your curry and eat it, too. If you're authentic, be authentic and get the Empress Chicken and the Forrest Gump off the menu. If you want to appeal middle-of-the-road Yankees and pseudo-cultured 20-year-olds who think Pad Thai is hardcore Bangkok cuisine and appreciate things like Thai Fajitas to introduce others to the Thai flavor palate, fine. Frankly, I'd rather have you refine that flavor palate and cut the oil out, but to each his own. I just don't think you can claim to be a true Thai restaurant with such blatant Americanization.

While I understand the connection between provel and St Louis pizza, and I'm OK with it on pizza, the FDA doesn't even legally allow it to be called cheese (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provel_cheese). And if your main ingredient in your cheese dishes isn't allowed to be called cheese, I don't think you should be allowed to be called an Italian restaurant. And you can't call a dish Chicken Parmesan if there's no Parmesan in it. Aside from just the issue of cheese, the overall quality just didn't seem to be there. The Pasta Con Broccoli that I ordered was just plain bland. In fact the provel based cream sauce tasted almost exactly like the Alfredo sauce from Chicago Uno. The marinara on my wife's ravioli was also pretty sad. Now, when my Mom makes sauce, she takes an entire weekend. A pot simmers on the stove for three days and two nights. I learned from my mother that good Italian cooking is essentially simple, but requires quality ingredients and takes time. Concetta's marinara tasted remarkably like tomato sauce out of a can, with some herbs in it. I didn't hate the place, and if you live in the neighborhood, and it's convenient, it's not the worst place to eat, buy my experience was no better than I've had at Olive Garden.

text: I hate to be that person. The person that gives a place one star. But our experience here was truly awful. We had reservations for New Year's Eve, but when we showed up Star Joey got all frantic and said "I told them not to make reservations for two people, you're going to have to wait by the bar." Mind you, the bar seats six people, and every stool was taken by people dining at the bar. We stood there for a few minutes, then he came back and took us to the first table in the room. The table was fine, except that it was directly in front of the one man band. The vibrations from his music almost made it hard to eat. So things started shaky, but we were happy to have a table. We waited about 5 minutes, then we were brought menus and the manager told us he would be right back. About 15 minutes passed and we still had no waiter, but finally one came along and gave us a wine list. We ordered a bottle of the Sterling Merlot and it was great. The rest of the meal went ok. I had the garlic fillet and it was excellent, and my husband had the cajun fillet, and it was also wonderful. Part of my husband's fillet was very undercooked, but aside from that, it was a perfect. I think the veggies that came with the steak may have been frozen though... ewe. We wanted to have one more glass of wine before leaving, so we asked the manager if we could have the merlot by the glass. That was when he said we'd have to check with the bartender and that he was sorry but we really needed to go to the bar because there was a couple that had been waiting for our table for an hour and a half. Normally, I would understand and be happy to go to the bar, but the six person bar was still completely full, now with even more people standing around it, so going to the bar wasn't really an option. He basically asked us to leave after we'd spent over $100 on steak and wine. I don't care if it's New Year's Eve and they over-booked, and are short chefs (the manager told us one of the chefs walked out that evening) you just don't ask your customers to leave! text: "Meh" is really the best word to describe this place. Actually, no, the best way to describe it would be to get all grandiose and let William Shakespeare do it. I think these lines from "Much Ado About Nothing" sum up my feelings pretty well: BENEDICK. "Why, i' faith, methinks she's too low for a high praise, too brown for a fair praise, and too little for a great praise; only this commendation I can afford her, that were she other than she is, she were unhandsome, and being no other but as she is, I do not like her." Old Pueblo Grill is not an awful place, by any stretch of the imagination. It just doesn't really have anything by which it can commend itself. Thus, I would classify it as both totally innocuous and thoroughly unremarkable. It is the go-to, post-work watering hole of choice for my coworkers, due to its proximity to our workplace, so we will often find ourselves there on a Friday afternoon (as we did today). That said, if there was something nearby with more character, better service, or a more interesting menu, we would likely go there in a heartbeat. The decor feels a bit like the southwestern Holiday Inn that time forgot. Whenever I sit down in there, I constantly have to remind myself that I'm not actually hanging out in a hotel lobby. The walls have the standard, yet muted "holy shit, the desert sunset threw up on me" look to them, and the bar looks like it was designed by someone who owned a lot of bolo ties. The service is generally OK. Most of the waitstaff seems pleasant enough, but they sometimes seem annoyed at the idea of having to wait on a group of more than four people. They also seem chronically overwhelmed, even when the place is basically empty (as it seems to be on many afternoons). As others have written, the food is standard southwestern-influenced American fare. Our group usually orders the appetizers when we go, which consist of things like "Rattlesnake Eggs" (bacon-wrapped, cheese-stuffed jalapenos), various enormous quesadillas, and fried calamari (which always smells like death and looks almost as bad). I have one coworker who swears by the jalapeno concoction, but it just looks like a fried heart attack to me. The rest of the lunch menu is an uninspired assortment of overpriced salads and wraps with cutesy southwestern names. The dinner menu is marginally more interesting and contains some semi-fresh takes on old standards, like steak and salmon. Generally, though, the dinner food is significantly overcooked, which may have something to do with average age of the dinner clientele. Most seem to be in their 60s and 70s. I'll say this about the food, I have never tasted anything that was out-and-out bad, per se, but I've also never had anything that made me say, "Great googly moogly, I simply must have that again." The salsa is harmless and fresh, if flavorless, the salads are a touch on the limp side, and the wraps are OK, but they're nothing you couldn't just make in five minutes at home. For what you get, the food prices are pretty whack. Salads are in the $10-$12 range, and I think there is one app. on the menu for under $10. And that's the lunch menu. Frankly, the dinner menu has 4-star prices for 2-star food. On the boozy side, alcohol prices are par for the course and are nothing to either cry bloody murder or write home about. While we're talking booze, the beer selection is fine, if a bit tepid in the inspiration department. At least they don't limit themselves to Bud Light and Banquet Beer. There's usually Kilt Lifter, Fat Tire, and a rotating microbrew on tap. Mixed drinks are also on the strong side, which is pretty nice. A well-liquor vodka martini ran me $4.50 and was sufficiently alcoholic to the point that the rattlesnake eggs started to look kind of tasty. It wasn't brilliantly mixed, but it was fine. Old Pueblo Grill is a mixed bag, indeed. Too low for a high praise, to high for a low praise, too middle-of-the-road to be considered interesting, too nontoxic to be considered Lucky Wishbone. If it were demolished tomorrow, I likely wouldn't miss it. At the same time, though, I wouldn't slip the wrecking crew a Benjamin to "speed up the job and put some stank on it." Take of that what you will.
label: NEG

text: Keep your expectations LOW if you decide to dine here. First of all, it's in a casino. With that in mind..... There was a bit of a wait to be seated, even though there were several spots open. The green tea was made from a bag of Bigelow. The seaweed salad was so-so but rather chewy. Nearly ALL of the roll offerings contain something fried, or the entire roll is fried. They douse every roll with copious amounts of sauces (probably to mask the low quality of the ingredients). Everything is made with way too much rice - rice that was undercooked and not properly prepared or seasoned. You must eat all of the rice if you are doing all-you-can-eat and your server will point this out to you if you try to leave any behind on your plate. The fish is NOT fresh high-quality sashimi grade one should expect from a sushi restaurant. The maguro/tuna was quite dry and tasteless, the hamachi/yellowtail lacked the usual flavor punch you get when it's truly fresh, same for the sake/salmon. The fire and ice hand roll (salmon and scallops) was the best offering IMO but again, not as fresh or flavorful as it should have been. The tobiko/fish roe was like eating large grains of dry fishy sand. The sushi chefs all appeared to be Mexican line cooks. This would not be a problem except that these so-called sushi chefs had absolutely no idea what omakaze meant. WTF??? That's like a chef in a steak house not knowing the difference between rare and medium. It may have been just as well considering nothing was of very high quality. The portions are generous, but what's the point if doesn't taste that great? All-you-can-eat is not a good value when the quality is sub-par. I'd much rather pay double and get the highest quality fresh fish that is prepared by skilled sushi chefs. Oh, and you cannot sit at the sushi bar unless you pay for the all-you-can-eat option. Definitely NOT a place for the true sushi connoissuer.

text: We came to VRC on a referral from our vet. Our American Bulldog needed knee surgery (two of them, actually). We'd gone through quite a process finding a good vet and getting the knee problem diagnosed. So I carefully researched my options, which included UPenn, a vet in Atlantic City and Redbank, NJ, and a practice in Langhorne. We chose VRC because they were willing to answer questions about pricing before we even came in for an evaluation. VRC performed all of the knee surgery options while other practices performed only some of the surgeries and others performed some at one location and some at another location. With VRC we were able to visit one facility, regardless of the surgery that was best for his condition. VRC was much cheaper than UPenn. This surprises no one, right? VRC was cheaper than the Langhorne practice that does dog knee surgery. Malvern is a lot closer than AC and Redbank. VRC is clean, well-managed, and professional. We were shown to appointment rooms quickly and our vet was on time. I can't give VRC five stars because there was a noticeable change in attitude and service after the surgery. One of the staff actually told me that she didn't have time to answer my two questions and only would answer the one that she thought was more important. We also sometimes had to wait a few days for someone to respond to our calls. I also feel liike an expensive surgery should include follow-up visits, especially since our visits were a couple x-rays and a few minutes with the vet. I agree with Martina M.'s review on this matter but like I said, Langhorne and UPenn are pricier! Our dog had a TPLO, an increasingly common surgery for dogs of all size. Our guy is a big boy and our vet recommended that the surgery be done by a board-certified surgeon (otherwise, she could have fixed it for less). If you have a large dog who needs a TPLO, you should go to VRC.

I then told them that I had received a phone call a day earlier from a girl saying the time had been moved. They said that's untrue as no one would ever do such a thing. I told them no, it had happened. The girl asked for who had called us. I said she never gave her name, just confirmed our treatments and gave us a new time slot. She proceeded to roll her eyes and said, "Fine. But your aromatherapy bath will be shortened." We were quickly ushered into a waiting room and my fiance whispered to me that this probably isn't going to work out. I said if I smile and treat them nicely, maybe it will. After we were ready, we were shown to the massage room. My fiance said his massage was fantastic...mine on the other hand was awful! They pressed way too hard, and when I said to lighten the pressure, they didn't! I asked multiple times, and it didn't happen. I brushed it off thinking I would feel better in the morning, like after having a deep-tissue massage (I didn't BTW, I had to make another massage appointment elsewhere just to recover from that one). After, we were shown to the aromatherapy bath. The girl curtly told us that 30min had to be shortened to 20 and then slammed the door behind her, not even telling us how to operate the bath. The bath was cold and not full, and by the time we figured out the controls, we only had 10 minutes, before we were curtly told our treatment was over and we had to get ready to leave. This was the worst part!! They have lockers at Perugia, and I locked all of my belongings and clothes in the locker, taking the key with me. Upon my return to the changeroom, I found out that someone had stolen my underwear!!! I searched for them in the locker room thinking I dropped them, and someone had thrown them out, but they were nowhere to be found! I didn't even bother to ask about it when we were leaving because I was too upset to care. Needless to say, I will never go back to Perugia, and I tell everyone I know never to go there either.

text: Reader's Digest version: good recipes, bad staff, so-so remodel. When Chilango's opened years ago, I went all the time. The food was delicious, healthy and affordable; the staff was friendly and efficient; the place was clean and well maintained. That was then. This is now. I don't know if the place changed hands or if the management has simply lost its way, but hell, meet handbasket. Mind you, the food is still delicious, and more inventive than ever. Compared to the original menu, the new menu places much less emphasis on "healthy" (adios, Power Burrito) and "affordable" (hola, $14 entrees). That's OK as long as things taste good, and they do. But everything else... what a mess. Today we ordered a shrimp and squash salad off the special board, and a burrito mojado. More on those in a moment. We had to search the restaurant extensively to find a clean table -- most had not been cleared and cleaned, even though the restaurant was deserted and it had been two hours since the end of the lunch rush. We did find a clean one eventually, but the dining room was buzzing with flies nonetheless. Yuck! More thoughtlessness: no opener on or near the cooler for your bottle of Jarritos or beer, and no paper towels in the bathroom. When the food arrived, there were no forks. When I went to get one from the counter, the fork container was empty. When I asked for one, the server said, "Oh, we don't have any. We ran out of forks hours ago." Mind you, we had just ordered, FROM THIS VERY PERSON, two dishes that cannot be eaten without forks (a salad, and a burrito half-submerged, submarine-like, in sauce). Maybe she should have told us then? And what kind of restaurant runs out of forks? After a moment, she muttered something about trying to find some, and disappeared. We waited a while, and finally I gave up and arose to go snake some forks from the restaurant next door. At that very moment, I saw our server return from the restaurant next door, and place forks in the container--without bringing us any. Grr. During the long forkless wait, I had drained my soda. Alas -- Chilango's no longer has self-serve soda for your refill convenience. M's shrimp and squash salad was missing the squash -- seems they forgot it. She reported that it was tasty nonetheless. My burrito mojado -- the restaurant's signature chicken axiote burrito, only served in a deep dish, drowned in mole sauce with a bit of cheese melted on top -- was delicious. So points for the food still. A good recipe competently prepared is still worth a lot. But EVERYTHING else about the place has gone to hell. It needs new management or new ownership, stat.

text: This is an attempt at fine dining on top of T. Hogan's Pub. Despite a cozy and nicely decorated dining room, complete with a fire place, the food still has a way to go. It needs to get better if there is hope of it surviving, especially in this location, on top of a noisy bar and across from the Wissahickon train station. On a recent weeknight, my dining companion and I were the only ones there. Our waiter, while very nice, was over-attentive (perhaps out of sheer boredom), asking us frequently if everything was "ok." Fried calamari were heavily fried and greasy, but tasty. Steak "medallions" tasted like a Lean Cuisine I could microwave. Lukewarm and lacking sophistication. They came with an avalanche of mashed potatoes. Way too big a portion, and the potatoes were too hard. Vegetables were decent. My dining companion seemed to enjoy the lamb, which came with the same side dishes. Bread pudding was "interesting," but I can't tell if that was a good thing or not. Rarely have I ordered bread pudding that was an actual "piece of bread." The reviews in the paper said it was good. It consisted of a large piece of challah bread, warm and soft, drowned in what seemed like a pool of butter. It tasted more like french toast than dessert. I asked the waiter what the sauce was made of, and he sheepishly said something about a rum "reduction," but I'm not even sure he knows. The prices here are fairly steep for such mediocre food, but there is potential for better. The one bathroom I saw was "iffy" and you had to pass by an open kitchen to get there. Once done, our waiter asked for our names and seemed genuinely thankful that someone had come by to eat. He said business had been "good" since a move from Germantown. He said the owner was sitting at the bar downstairs and would be sure to thank us on the way out. We never saw him. Either way, the food was forgettable and I probably wouldn't return, though I'm told the brunch is good. Roxborough desperately needs some good restaurants. I hope this one gets better with more time.

text: This place is the shizzz-it! I happened to be in Philly for work this week the same time one of my BFFs was also in town. I'd researched where to eat near my hotel prior to our meeting, and knew I wanted to try Tria. We all stopped in half frozen to death and were instantly greeted with a warm and friendly waitstaff. The temperature was turned up really high and we were nice and toasty in a matter of minutes. The menu was more wine and beer then the food (which was just fine by us) but the food they had was super yummy! My friends ordered a lot of different tapas to share. They loved them all. I got the roasted beet salad, with pecans, fresh goat cheese and arugula. Delicious!! I also ordered the truffled fontina egg toast (an app). Holy cow, super yummy! I would recommend it to anyone. We ended the meal with a chocolate, Allagash cherry bread pudding and a banana, goat cheese caramel panino. OMG, the banana panino was out of this world. It was fab-o and worth every minute of the cold we endured to get there. The meal was actually a lot less then I thought it was going to be (only $90 for 3 of us, and we each had 2 glasses of wine). Def a place to stop in for a drink or dinner!!

text: This place seems to be like a SuperCuts (aka Russian Roulette of haircuts). If you know someone who's good, it's totally worthwhile and an absolute deal. Otherwise, steer clear: I got my hair cut here a year ago. The woman did a wonderful job. She took her time and was very laid back about it all, and I felt it was as good as the cut I got at this fancy studio in San Francisco years previously, for a fraction of the price. It's hard to find people who will do a good job on Asian hair. So, naturally, when it came time for a trim, I decided to come back here. I forgot the woman's name, but I'd read reviews saying that everyone here is good, so I just took the first available stylist. I just got home. This is the single most god-awful hair cut I've ever gotten in my entire life. That includes the time I decided to cut my own hair for kicks in intermediate school, and the haircuts my mom used to give me as a child. I just asked for her to trim off ~2" to get rid of my split ends and to layer it a bit, and said I wanted to keep it as long as possible. Something like 3-6" later (depending on what part of my head you look at), I just told her to stop, and left. She cut haphazardly in full snips (better places cut it straight a little at a time and then feather it), and wasn't even checking if the left and right side were the same length as she went. I don't think she had a clue of what she was doing, and certainly had no idea what "layers" meant, other than "the hair should be different lengths". She kept saying "I add more layers" but really what she did was add more rat bites. Everything I asked her to fix became even more uneven. I was trying to grow out my hair for a special event, and now that's not going to be an option for me anymore, since I'll need to get a fairly short cut to even it out. I'm absolutely heartbroken.

text: The PSPCA now controls PACCA rather than PAWS. My husband and I had been fostering 3 PAWS kittens since they were a week old..many late nights feeding and taking care of them. They are now 12 weeks old and we took them to the Hunting Park location to get their final shots. We are adopting two and found a home for the other. Our usual Vet Tech, Julie, was there and she was great with the kittens as usual. Then we had the unfortunate experience of meeting with Jill, the adoptions advisor/counselor. If she is what the PSPCA considers to have proper social skills, then they are sorely mistaken. When we first fostered the kittens the adoption price was $40 for two kittens. When we went to fill out the adoption papers they were $75 each. This is a significant difference that threw us off guard. We asked about honoring the original contract and she said that the contract meant nothing. My husband asked if he could talk to someone about it and she gave an attitude very quickly. She told us just to hand our kittens over and leave them there until they figured everything out. What? Anyone who has ever loved an animal knows that they couldn't possible stand the thought of leaving their animals in a kill shelter. And with the tone she used it was a clear aggressive provocation to make us shut up about the issue. Then she raised her voice and said that they were trying to save animals lives as if to insinuate that we didn't care about animals. I think that was probably the worst part. Except for a puppy dying in one of the worker's arms and Jill saying "get used to it" when the girl was clearly upset. We decided to just take the kittens home and return the next week when the other adopter would be there and she made it clear that she didn't trust us and had to take my name down for fear we were going to flee with the kittens when we had documented every visit we'd had there. I offered my number too but she said she had it in the system. I would never discourage someone from adopting an animal from a shelter, but I would certainly think twice before coming here. We don't plan on ever adopting another animal from here and we will file a grievance with the SPCA and PACCA.
label: NEG

text: The wait at Stanley can be considerable, but the food is well worth the wait. I came for brunch and had Pecan Pie Ice Cream Malt, Egg Stanley, and Poor Boy Sliders. I would normally have a cocktail at brunch, but the shakes/malts looked far too tempting so I had to have one. I had a Pecan Pie Ice Cream Malt which was a pretty great way to start my meal. It was thick and had bits of malt. It could have been colder though as it got to room temperature much sooner then expected. Let's talk about the Eggs Stanley. It's essentially eggs benedict with fried oysters: english muffin, ham, fried oysters, poached eggs, and a hollandaise sauce. The oysters were crunchy and tender in the middle, eggs properly poached and the hollandaise was creamy. Decadent and rich I could only handle about 4 bites as there was other things to try. The Poor Boy Sliders consisted of a three mini sandwiches: fried oyster, korean BBQ and a club. Of the three the korean BBQ was the best. It was korean style beef with kimchee in french bread. Tangy, sweet and a little spicy it was a real winner. Sure a bit out of place in New Orleans but good food is good food. The fried oyster Poor Boy was pretty good as well with a slightly spicy remoulade sauce. The club was pretty basic and should be ignored when there are much better choices available. I read that others has poor service, but when I went it was pretty busy and I had good service. The only thing that was awkward was figuring out who exactly was my server. Once he introduced himself everything was peachy. I would certainly return to Stanley for another meal and if you haven't been I would certainly suggest stopping by.

text: I guess I spoke too soon with my original post. . . I went back to Grin to get a set of acrylic nails and was pretty disappointed. First, it took forever because apparently only one employee there could even do acrylics--you'd think they'd be more prepared on a Friday afternoon. I guess she was the only one who could do a number of services because she kept disappearing to help other clients, leaving me in the hands of someone else who was obviously just killing time so I didn't feel abandoned (she would file my nails but then the other woman would come back and re-do it anyway). I realized after I left that she didn't even make all the nails the same length and one is pretty crooked. Now, a week and a half out, one of the acrylics is lifting from my nail bed (near the cuticle). Plus I see gaps between my real nail and the acrylic tip on 4 fingers and I know that's not right. I'm pretty sure it took over 2 hours!!! I've only had acrylics once before, but the experience was nothing like this one. I also question the cleanliness at Grin. I didn't see any employees washing their hands, wearing gloves or masks, and I don't even want to think about the tools. . . I didn't see sterilization machines like I have at other nail places. I consider myself lucky that I didn't end up with an infection and I won't be going back. I've heard Diva Nails in Doylestown is much better. . .

text: my first visit to chapterhouse was for the unofficial yelp book club meeting last week. it will certainly not be my last! this is a great little spot whether you are looking for a quiet place to work on your laptop, read a book or simply sip a tasty beverage or snack on a delicious baked treat while admiring the unique artwork. it is also a good spot for groups, like ours, who likely made a lot more noise than most other patrons - sorry! the set-up is great as it is a large space with a few different sections, so i got the feeling noise didn't carry all that bad (or so i hoped!) if we didn't have our book to discuss, a group could pick up one of a number of board games on hand, along with a selection of books. i had read good things online about the nutella latte (nutella as a beverage? yes, please!), so i ordered one iced, and it did not disappoint. in fact, writing about it...i am craving one right now and wishing i didn't live in the burbs. they were out of yogurt - wah - so after deliberating for quite some time, i finally settled on a coffee cake, which i believe came from flying monkey patisserie? well, wherever it came from, it was heavenly - makes me kinda glad they were out of yogurt! in light of the recent thread chatter, it is worth noting that the barista was quite patient with me while i waffled on my food order. prices were reasonable, and my bill was under $10 so i politely paid with cash :)

text: Um, no plat recognition? No tv reception and upgrade to a room next to the ventilation for the restaurant? No DVD remote control? Call to ask for one and it never arrives? The inability of this hotel to staff the front desk when there are 10 people checking out? Mushy bananas and molding oranges in the fruit basket that serves as breakfast? text: Wonderful Mongolian Stir Fry. You pick out all the things you want in your bowl from a buffet bar. Chicken, beef, shrimp, fish. So many possible fresh veggies. You add in spices and sauces. text: Holy crap this place is delicious! I didn't expect much out of a TINY bar with only outdoor seating - probably because I'm from Chicago and not used to an only outdoor seating restaurant - but I was happily surprised. The Queso de Cabra was so amazing that if I wasn't out in public I would have licked the bowl. The Sangria was very good and, even thought I didn't have any, everyone I was with kept raving about the spicy pappas. (I can't remember the name.) When/if I go back to St. Petersburg, I am DEFINITELY coming here again.

text: ALWAYS LUCKY AT Café Luck. Made our reservation via Open Table 8:00. We arrived early so we headed to the bar. Martinis....Very large doubles for 11.00. It may have been a triple pour. Shaken ice cold with frosting. Our table was ready on time. This place has the feel of the south of France. If everybody spoke French you just could be on the Mediterranean. Domaine De Crista Grenache Cote du Rhone at 28.00. Seared Foie Gras with apricot & arugulla. Second course, Octopus braised with a vinaigrette radishes and grapefruit. Octopus I have cooked or had served to me was like eating the rubber steal belted tires off your car. This was remarkable very tender and I have to say the best I have ever had. Washed it down with the Mas de La Day Grenache/ Syrah from Provence 33.00 For the main course I had the duck again. It's my favorite confit style it falls off the bone. The most amazing however is the floating Island. I haven't figured it out....do they make them to order or are they pre-made? And if they are pre-made how do they keep them aloft. I used to make them in my restaurant by poaching lightly in a crème anglaise a la Escoffier. They would only stay afloat just long enough. I am going back again just to check this amazing light and fluffy olfactory sensation. Finished off with an Armangnac. The service was great too.

text: Why do I like this place? Well, the 'beans' are really yummy in a weird weird way. And they have mac 'n' cheese. And sometimes you just need something they have and nowhere else will sell it. text: Buca di Beppo is an Italian chain featuring the theme "your Italian family's basement get-together". I found the food tasty and is served in very large portions. text: Marina does an awesome job! Her Brazilians are sooo worth it. It's not as painful as other places. The liter sales here are pretty decent, & they have a great selection of shampoo, conditioner & other hair styling products. They also carry my fave brand, H20+. The staff are very helpful. I like the fact that this place is open 7 days a week.

text: Hey guys, did you know I'm near sighted? Yeah, I can't really see, especially at night. I realized this was going to be a major problem in a month when I have to drive to DC, so I called on Monday to make an appointment here because it's close to work and positively reviewed by another yelper. The doctor saw me the same day. He, along with the rest of the staff, was quick and efficient without rushing me. There were a ton of glasses to choose from, and the woman who helped me pick out a pair was great. She was really honest and helpful, making suggestions and giving me feedback as to what worked and what didn't. The whole visit took an hour, and when I came back today to pick up my glasses, I was in and out in less than 10 minutes. So now I've got really cute glasses, and I can actually see stuff! text: Amazing food, great entertainment and won me over with OVER 200 different beers. Wowza.

text: Simply put: This is a good place to enjoy high-quality Indian food. First, the room is comfortable. Cloth napkins and clean white tablecloths. Good lighting. It's never been crowded during my visits so it lacks the roar that characterizes a number of the nicer places to eat in Philly (I live in Seattle). Second, the wait staff is professional and attentive. They offered a complementary vegetarian soup appetizer and finished the meal with a complementary rice pudding. Both were excellent and unexpected. Third, the food is better than average. The salmon tandoori was tender and flavorful. The vegetable dishes are quite good, although portions are a bit small (still, more than enough to share). The rice is a cut above what you might find in downscale Indian places. At the same time, I didn't see anything on the menu that was unexpected - all the standards, and only the standards, are present. I've eaten here twice - once last August and then tonight (March). Both times the place was relatively empty, which is a shame because it warrants attention from anyone who enjoys Indian food.

text: This place isn't very good...it's like a copy of Macaroni Grille but fails in every way possible. I think of it more like Olive Garden...bland Italian food. text: The food made at Lovin' Spoonfuls is simply good. There is no amendment to that statement; no, "It's good for vegetarian food." The vegetarian restaurants of yore that I was thrilled with became wallflowers after finding Lovin' Spoonfuls. Lovin' Spoonfuls provides a full menu of absolutely delectable options with all vegan ingredients as well as a separate menu with the gluten free options. This is home-style food better than you can remember it ever being made; there are no lack-luster or disappointing options here. The serving staff are friendly and knowledgeable about their food offerings and Peg, the owner, is also very friendly and is usually around to assist. The service provided by the staff is very consistent. This restaurant is especially perfect if you are looking to order on your lunch break. I typically eat at Lovin' Spoonfuls for lunch and the longest I have had to wait for my meal is 15 minutes. The highlights from my personal ordering experience: Breakfast: Possibly the best french toast you will ever find, vegan or otherwise A good selection of delicious and hearty scrambles from the menu or made-to-order Lunch: Southern Fried BBQ Chicken Sandwich (usually the Friday afternoon special only, but it is the best) Club Sandwich BBQ Beef Sandwich Golden Chicken Nuggets Good to know for lunches: Lunch basket selections (mostly sandwiches) are served with Poore Brothers regular potato chips, a quarter of dill pickle, and a side of cole slaw, carrot salad, or potato salad. You can substitute a small green salad for the other three sides if you prefer and their made-in-house sesame dijon dressing is great. Lunches average around $6 to $8. Dinner: Country Fried Chicken Platter Dessert: I hardly ever make it to dessert, but they have a large selection of everything from cookies to very decadent cakes. They also make great shakes, some that are always on the menu and some that change daily/weekly. I usually saw there to be a gluten free dessert option in the dessert case as well. Some tidbits about the restaurant: Ordering style is at a counter but food is brought out to your table Patio seating is available The food is totally Vegan Seating for groups is available, but the restaurant probably seats about 60 only--if you have a group bigger than 6 you may want to call ahead, especially if it is for lunch. Please, do not miss out on trying Lovin' Spoonfuls!

text: Some of the worse fish taco's I've ever tasted in my life! text: Kopperman's stinks. I've been to 2 really bad Jewish delis in my life, and they're both in St. Louis. One is Billy Sherman's in Chesterfield, this is the other. text: I wanted to like it more than I did. text: Often before visiting restaurants, I like to browse the dinner and wine menu online to get a feel for what I may enjoy later that evening. While I was shocked by their general 500% markup (from retail) on wines, I expected to be thoroughly pleased by the food on the unique menu. The food was good, no doubt, but all things must be considered when giving a review - Value, Service, Decor/Comfort etc. The consensus of our party of 6 was that the appetizers far outshone the entrees. The specialty drinks were good but at half the cost of the liquor bottle, they should be phenomenal. The seating was very low, which became uncomfortable later in the evening as everyone started stretching their legs out into the middle of the seating area. The service was unobtrusive - no problem there - but any recommendation requests were always met with the most expensive option. I can forgive that, my taste is often bigger than my wallet. If you are looking for a nice dark place where you can impress your date with how much you are willing to spend, this is your place. By the look of the crowd in there on a Saturday night, those people are becoming few and far between.

text: Never. Again. I went to rumba recently and I promise you - never again. A friend of mine went on and on and on about how GREAT Rumba was - and he wanted us to go one night. So, my friend, myself and 2 others go to Rumba and are seated promptly. And, oddly enough, that is where the good service ended. We waited for - maybe 30 minutes - and still no one had stopped by our table. To make matters worse - it was SLOW in the restaurant. In fact, most of the servers were standing in a semi-circle about 20 feet from our table just yapping it up and laughing. Having a great time apparently while we hadn't had a single person even come over to our table to even get us a DRINK much less take our order. Finally - after sitting there for over 45 minutes - we got up and left. Then finally - as we were leaving with very disgusted looks on our faces the manager came over and asked how everything was for us. text: I first came across Chickies right after I got out of high school. I was working with my dad for the summer, and he got back from a morning meeting down at Methodist, and had some sandwiches with him that they had gotten catered from Chickie's. They were some of the best I'd ever had, but I always had trouble finding the place again, in those pre-yelp dark ages. That all changed when I moved into the city, and it turned out my favorite deli was now my neighbour. Chickie's is hands down my favorite thing about my neighbourhood. They have an incredible selection of sandwiches. Their "regular" hoagies are damn good, but they really excel with the specialty sandwiches. Normally I'm not big on the vegetarian options, but the veggie hoagie, with eggplant, rabe, roasted peppers and share provo is simpy awesome. I'm also a big fan of the Johnny Marz, with tuna and prosciutto, which sounds like a weird combination at first, but is great. The Chicken parm is good, but try the Chicken Fantasia, which adds roast eggplant, and prosciutto. The Chickies special is a perfect combo of Capicolla, Sopressata, and Prosciutto, with roasted peppers and sharp provo. They have some tasty antipasto options, and the obligatory rack of tastykakes and frito lay products. A big plus is they have Hank's sodas in addition to pepsi varieties, so I can satisfy my periodic Wishniak cravings. My only real negatives are that they only stay open until about 3 PM, and are closed on sundays. Even though I live very close, sometimes I don't get there for weeks at a time.

text: I went to this restaurant for the second time yesterday. My first visit was around a year ago. The first time I went the most memorable thing about the restaurant was the service. We were then ignored for close to 10 minutes before our waitress came to our table to take our drink orders. The wait was similar for her to come back to take our dinner order as well. This was early in the evening (around 5:30) and the restaurant was not particularly full, although there was a party of about 10 at another table. However, to the restaurant's credit they did recognize the poor service without our saying anything, and in an unsolicited offer gave us our choice of dessert for free. That was certainly a nice gesture. In terms of the food, I honestly don't remember much about the food that first time, either good or bad. All that said, we figured a year had passed and we would give the restaurant another shot yesterday (especially after I saw it received 4 and 5 star reviews exclusively on here). The service was better this time for sure, not great, but decidedly better. We were greeted pretty quickly at the door and had our drink orders taken immediately. We did have another unusually long wait before we were able to order. The waitress wasn't particularly friendly, but she was not rude either, so that was fine with me. In terms of the food, it was a tale of two dishes. I ordered the crab stuffed haddock. I thought it was delicious. The portion was generous (both of the haddock and amount of crab stuffing). The fish was cooked almost perfectly and was complemented really well by the blue crab. I also really enjoyed the sauce that the dish sat in. It was overall one of the better fish dishes I have had. My sides dishes were hushpuppies (which I really enjoyed) and garlic parsley potatoes (which were very bland and had no real hint of either garlic or parsley). Unfortunately, my wife's order of shrimp your way was not nearly on the same level. This is a half pound of shrimp, divided between hand battered, coconut, and "shrimp your way," for which she chose grilled- sautéed. The plate arrived with about 4 of each type of shrimp. She stated the hand-battered shrimp were fine. However, the coconut shrimp were clearly burned (to the point we were slightly surprised it was sent out) and the grilled-sautéed shrimp were overcooked and very rubbery and chewy. Overall on both visits the experience was disappointing, and I could not recommend it. The one dish was superb, but that unfortunately is not enough to overcome the glaring negatives experienced on both visits. *In a random side note, at this most recent visit to the restaurant Fred Robbins (of the St. Louis Rams) was dining there. I recognized him from his days at Wake Forest.

text: Philadelphia has a lot of gyms. Now more than ever there are new ones popping up ALL the time...there used to be a World Gym up on Sansom Street where now exists a bathhouse, and once upon a time, I worked there. This of course, meant that I also had a free membership AND since I was the opener on the weekends, I had a key and free reign to workout before or after hours. Still, I had a membership to 12th Street. WHY? Because it is THAT good. These days, one of the places I am employed offers a free membership to PSC Rodin. While this is a nice option to some stale periods in my workout life, I always end up back at my beloved Gayborhood haunt. I have also, in my poorer days, taken advantage of every free and trial membership in every gym in Philadelphia. And still, I remain here year after year. The Sporting Club, PSC, The Westin, Sweat...I will take my Gay Gym over these anyday. Why? Well, let me add up the elements here. 1. Cost. Their regularly running "specials" are low enough in price, and they offer different payment options for easier to hack dues. But their student discounts and special deals with local businesses are amazing. Their price among all gyms, up until recently, was THE LOWEST in the area. (then that $20 a month place opened up - but - no comparison there. 2: Amenities. The offerings here are awesome - Not that I take advantage of all the extras - like Basketball court, pool, dry/steam sauna, sundeck, TONS of classes at all different times (This has actually been steadily improving, too - more classes, different times and days...), A shake bar with many different protein powder options, as well as a bring your own powder option, which is only $2 to make a shake. You can heat up food in the micro, throw something in the fridge for a few hours (not storage, mind you - don't be a tool) Sit on the couches and watch the flat screen - It all feels like home to me. Maybe because I spend too much time there. 3. Maintenence of Facilities. You can actually SEE your membership dollars at work here. New equipment every seaason, speedy repairs on minor glitches, new snack/drink machines, and the cleanliness is unmatched. The only thing missing is the overbearing smell of bleach - because they use some really great solution of Fantastik for cleaning that I actually LIKE smelling... is that weird? I hope it's not weird... 4. Other members. So, I DID mention it's the gay gym, right? That being said, not ALL members are gay dudes. But the ratio is overwhelming and this, my friends, makes working out as a woman VERY VERY comfortable. One of the big issues being a young blonde is having to ignore stares and peacock behavior, and yes, even sometimes COMMENTS, from testosterone overflow. And it makes me want to turn inside out and run. Read: NOT MOTIVATIONAL. But the straight guys here are secure enough in themselves and insecure enough in avoiding the gay mojo that they stay to themselves. Which, really, is where they need to stay. 5. I COULD knock a star off for hours, but I won't. They are as good as any other gym in the city in that arena. Would I like extended hours on the weekends? Sure. But an 8 am opening ON Sat/Sun, and an 8 pm/7 pm closing time, respectively, is acceptable. They are 5:30 am til 11 most every other day (save Friday when they close at 10...Gotta get your party on earlier, right?) 6. Locker cost: Pretty cheap for a year or 6 months - of course the longer you rent one the cheaper, and I get to cram - I mean, store - half my life in one 12x12 cube. 7. Seven points? yes, we are up to 7 points here: The Camac Center in the back of the gym houses pretty much all you will ever need for your life. EVER. Massage, Hair salon, Esthetitian and laser skincare (you know - botox, bitches!), homeopathic services, a kids gym, and oh, who the hell knows what else is back there. Maybe Santaland and a lollipop tree. Next thing you know they will have housing available. 8. Last one - promise. Trainers - tons of them. Swim lessons. Boxing lessons. Freebies on a regular basis (once in awhile an announcement of "we have a few pairs of free theater tickets for this evening - first to come up to member services, gets 2 free tickets!" or free dinners/training sessions/guest passes with your membership, and promotions from local businesses stationed in the lobby. It's pretty great and ties you into a feeling of "community", which is probably the biggest draw for me at 12th Street Gym. I have tried to find better, my friends. I have been high and low - seen good things and bad things, even worked in places where I could have had it all. But I have been a member here for over 8 years. And I have no plans on changing that. Because really, gay gym boys are really really awesome eye candy. Just sayin'.

text: I had been spying this establishment for about two weeks trying to figure out if it was opening or had just closed and about two days after I came to the wrongful conclusion that it had recently closed I saw a sign up announcing their opening on the 19th of June. At best this is an unsuccessful attempt to create a good neighborhood French bakery, at worst a tourist trap for locals; in any case, there are better bakeries elsewhere in uptown New Orleans -- like the great new Maple Street Patisserie, which is everything that the Boulangerie pretends to be.

For starters, my friends and I tried two dishes: Yucca Fries and Empanadas. The "Aipim frito" is a fried yucca root or cassava. It's served with Parmesan cheese on top and a side of curry dipping sauce. Our waiter was happy to provide us with an extra dish of the sauce which went well with the perfectly crisped root wedges. There were a few different choices of empanadas, and I picked the "de camarao" which is filled with shrimp, onion and Brazil cream sauce (not sure exactly what that consists of). Topped with parsley and Parmesan and served with a side of tomato sauce, it was a delicious empanada. When ordering our main courses, we were given the option of a salad or soup. I couldn't pass the chance to try black bean and coconut soup, and I'm glad I tried it. The coconut flavor went beautifully with the pureed beans. I only wish they would have garnished it with some friend plantain chips or croutons. For my main course, I tried the "Bobo de camarao refogado" (or something like that). This dish consists of jumbo shrimp served in a spicy coconut cream sauce over rice. The sauce was very flavorful and I'd guess that it consisted of bell peppers, onions, garlic and cilantro or something along those lines. I was getting mildly irritated with my friend who enjoyed my dish more than his chicken dish, but the servings are so big that there is plenty to go around. If you manage to have room for dessert, you might want to try the "Paveé da nena", described on the menu as cookies dipped in amaretto liquor, layered with chocolate, egg custard cream, topped with chocolate sauce. I'd say it's similar to a tiramisu, but a Brazilian version. Four of us were able to share one big portion which was a nice way to end the meal. The only negative about the experience would be the painfully slow service by a waiter who had just started working there. I'm willing to overlook slow service, however I could understand others being annoyed by this. 4 stars...I'll be back for sure!

The you have to find a place to sit and wait for your food. This can range from not an issue to a disaster.
