text: I'm always ambivalent about coming here, for some reason. I've never really had a bad experience but I've been here MAYBE 4 times in the 2+ years they've been open. Weird, right? Well, this will definitely be changing soon. My friend and I ended up hear after a less-than-stellar attempt to go to my normal Center City staple and we're immediately convinced that we made the right choice. The menu, while it hasn't changed at all, always surprises me because I forget how good everything looks. It's your standard Americanized and yuppified Mexican fare, but which some good sandwiches thrown in for the mix. We ended up sharing a 1/2 order of the carnitas nachos with guacamole on top, I ordered the shrimp tacos, and she got the steak tacos. Holy moly, everything was delicioussss. I'm a die-hard chicken nachos from Cantina girl but these nachos definitely ousted them as my favorite nachos in the city. My shrimp tacos were divine and loaded as well - chili-glazed shrimp with some pico and guacamole with lime were really light and delicious. I didn't get a chance to friend the steak tacos but I'm sure they were awesome as well because we housed those tacos in minutes. It was kind of embarassing, to be perfectly honest. In terms of drinks, I think they are definitely trying to make the locus of their libations craft beer as opposed to margaritas and such. You can get pitchers of margaritas, and they do flavored ones as well, but I noticed that they conveniently don't advertise them. Good for them, because making margaritas is annoying as hell. They have a fair amount of craft beer as well so you'll never be lacking in selections. I'd prefer more variety because it seems like they stick with certain breweries but that's just me being picky. I do have a couple of qualms about this place though. First, they are way too over-priced. I'm probably spoiled by all the legit Mexican taquerias near my lovely South Philly home but paying $9 for TWO shrimp tacos when I can get 3 for cheaper anywhere else is stupid. Same thing goes with beer - it's insanely marked up. They sell a bottle of Franziskaner for $8.25 when my job sells the same bottle for $6. I mean, really? I know it's Center City but that's completely insane. Even Good Dog, which is right across the street, doesn't mark their beer up like that. Also - service is kind of hit or miss. Our waitress looked miserable the entire time but did manage to crack a few jokes here and there. She was probably just tired, poor thing, having to deal with the shitty Rittenhouse clientele. Other than that - I really like this place. I don't go out in Center City much because I'm a creature of habit but I'll definitely make my way back here soon.

text: Okay-- first thing to understand is that when you are only paying $68 a night, your expectations should not be very high. Second thing is that the first couple floors are "Residential" (week to month-long stays), and that's not exactly the best quality clientele for a hotel. Final thing is that a hotel is, at heart, merely a place for you sleep and bathe while you are in a place where you lack those things and need them so you can do whatever it is you are there for. That being said-- this hotel is conveniently located just off I-76 at City and Belmont Aves and has a mini-parking "garage" in the rear. Every room offers at least one bed, a working bathroom with a bathtub-shower, and TV with cable, including HBO. More importantly, you can stay for a week for the same price as two nights in just about any other hotel in Philly (besides the Blue moon, anyway). The staff is nice, if disinterested. I have used the North American for real reasons and party reasons in the past, and I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again (unless I get rich before the next time I or someone I know needs a spot to stay). However, some important caveats: 1. I don't recommend leaving anything very valuable (from watches to laptops) in the room. 2. I do recommend bringing your own sheets and towels (though purely for quality and not for cleanliness). 3. Be forewarned that your stay may include the pleasure of a vibrating bed from the thumping bass pounding upwards from the crazy foreign wedding taking place in the "ballroom" and restaurant on the ground floor. 4. Be forewarned that your next door neighbors might just be crackheads who decide to fight all night long (when they're not slamming their bed into the adjoining wall). 5. Remember that all through high school my friends and I partied here on occasional weekends, and that kids still do. 6. Remember that a functioning bathroom does NOT mean the shower faucets won't leak and that the toilet won't rock. 7. Remember that "smoking rooms" doesn't always just mean cigarettes. If any of the above sounds intolerable, than you, like the previous guest who stayed in the room I got the last time i was there, "should've stayed at the Hilton"... But, if pure utility and cheapness is your aim-- the North American is the spot for you...

text: In the past 6 years, Morimoto has always been a guilty indulgence-type restaurant for me & my friends. We have dined there several times before, to great satisfaction (except we discovered that their omakase menu never changes). These same friends drove up from Baltimore last night in the rainy, cold weather specifically so we could go eat at Morimoto. I made reservations for three people at the sushi bar at 9:15p. The hostess on the phone told me that there might be a "little" wait, but not more than 15-20min. Fine. Jump ahead to 8:45p - we arrive early, expecting to go up to the lounge for some drinks while we waited for our reservation. 9:15p comes, and we ask about our seats - we're told that it will be a little longer. Fine. Jump ahead to 10:00p - we ask a waitress to check on our table, as it's now been 45 min. since our reservation - she never comes back. We then ask a different server the same question - she comes back about 15 min. later to tell us that our seats still aren't available. At this point, one would think that the server/hostess would have the sense to at least offer us peanuts and the option maybe to sit at an actual table, if the sushi bar is over-crowded. Of the three hostesses hovering around the hostess stand, their combined brain cells could not come up with any alternative options or consolation items. We saw people in the lounge, who were seated well after us, being led to their tables/seats before us. After paying our $78 check (for 4 drinks) and being told several times that we would have to wait "a little longer," we finally decided to leave. The food is good at Morimoto, but there's no restaurant where the food is worth waiting over one hour, especially when you have a reservation. It was like a Seinfeld episode - what's the point of a reservation?! Word to the wise - if you want good sushi, there are better places than Morimoto; if you want good martinis/drinks, there are better places than Morimoto; if you want omakase, it's worth trying once at Morimoto, but you are a sucker if you get it again & again - the whole point of omakase is that the menu should be created on the day of w/ the freshest ingredients specific to that day - Morimoto's omakase is a cookie-cutter menu with slight variations (i.e.: maybe they give you hamachi instead of toro). On our way out, my friend complained one of the vapid, brainless hostesses, who did nothing but say "I'm sorry." Yes, you should be sorry - you just lost 3 customers!

After quite sometime (I am in the industry... I understand, shit happens) he came back and explained that the very last of the Grey Goose was used in my martini and asked if I would like another brand. Of course, I didn't care what liquor was used, but it dawned on me that the bartender was initially short on Grey Goose, and tried to cover it up with olive juice. Who does that? Appetizers and side salads were delicious. Entrees come out. I have pasta with blue cheese. It's rich and I love it. Boyfriend cuts in to his medium-rare steak to find it cooked medium- well. We share my pasta while waiting for the server to check up on us. He never returns. When we're done eating and drinks are empty, here resurfaces our lovely waiter. We tell him about the steak and he apologizes and takes it away. The rest of the story IS NOT A JOKE. This really happened. A minute later the chef comes out to our table, with the steak in a cardboard box, and asks us if we'd like to take the steak home. We tell him that we're not really interested in eating a medium-well done steak, and prefer it to be medium-rare to rare. It is at this point that he tell us that we are incorrect; the steak is medium-rare. Then he opens the box and shows us the steak, cut in half, grey in the middle. "See, it's definitely pink." We say not a word. We couldn't. We were so dumbfounded. I suppose, since we're in our mid-20's, he thought he could pull a fast one. Or, maybe he thought we would believe him.... or maybe he was high on crack. I'm not sure. I will never forget this experience. EVER. Seriously, who does this guy think he's dealing with? I'll go back someday, I suppose. But only if the chef is long gone. text: Founded by a grieving father who could not find his young daughters grave in a church graveyard in Old City, Laurel Hill is built on the site of the Laurel Hill Estate. It opened around 1840 and is recognized as one of the most beautiful, and inviting, cemetaries in the country. Members of every old and noteworthy Philadelphia family are buried here as well as forty Civil War generals and other notables. And though Paris' Cimetiere du Pere Lachaise may have Balzac and Jim Morrison, Philadelphia's Laurel Hill has Adrienne Balboa. Reason to go while you're still alive? There is no better spot, not even Rittenhouse Square to lunch on a beautiful sunny day than here. And it isn't being disrespectful, it is encouraged. The old and some magnificent gravestones, markers and family mausoleums make fascinating sight seeing and not at all macabre. Forget that you think that this recommendation may have been written by Crispin Glover or other slightly off center character, its a good tip.

text: If you're 20-something, live in Levittown or Langhorne or thereabouts, and you're too lazy to drive to Philly, then the Hulmeville is the place to be on a weekend night. In my case, I date a guy from Levittown, and he and his friends love this place. So I tagged along when he and I started dating, and the place really has grown on me over the past year. This place is historic, as well as fun. Located on Trenton Road in historic Hulmeville, PA, the Hulmeville Inn has been in business for over two hundred years. Originally, it was a hotel and stage coach stop for those traveling between Trenton and Philadelphia. There is still a hitching post and a stone step that was used to board the carriages located on the property. During Prohibition, the Inn operated as an ice cream parlor. Now it's a great place to grab a beer and watch some sports. I like this place because it's spacious (yet tough to get a table if you get there late on a weekend night), has pool tables, and has a pretty good beer selection for a place in the 'burbs. In fact, I can always count on them offering Dirty Hoes because they always have Hoegaarden and Framboise on tap (and I like Dirty Hoes... no, not that kind, the drink, silly!). They change their beer selection to keep things fresh every once in a while, so check out what they have on tap on their website before you go. They've also got bar food - fries and such. Their wings are pretty good. Usually, this place is pretty much a townie bar during the week, but it becomes 20-something central on the weekends, with a fun crowd and good juke box music. You can always find the random sketchy old dudes at the bar on the weekend, though, which reminds you that you're still near Levittown. They just add local flavor to the place and keep it from becoming too much of a hipster hang-out. The Hulmeville bartenders are always really nice, and the ID-checker guys at the front door get to know the regulars after a while. I like having people know me at businesses that I frequent. I just don't like getting hit on by the sketchy old dudes at the bar (some have said some really GROSS things to me while I tried to order a drink...). If you're a cute girl, be sure to order your beer at the other end of the bar from them. The prices are pretty reasonable, and you can also catch the Phillies game or whatever sports game on their really nice tv's. I also noticed that the owners constantly upgrade the place to keep it fresh. The decor has changed little by little since I started going there a year ago. Oh, and the pitchers have a compartment in the middle where the bartender puts some ice, so your beer stays cold until you finish the pitcher. That's always appreciated. They are open seven days a week from 11 a.m. until 2 a.m. My only complaint is that the Hulmeville is outside the Philly city limits, so the smoking ban is not in effect there. Thus, I've had difficulty breathing and leave smelling like an ash tray. Since the place isn't huge and it gets really crowded on the weekends, and since I don't think they have a state-of-the-art ventilation system, it gets WAY more smoky in there than your average bar that still allows smoking. In fact, it's so bad that I've been avoiding going there very often since the Philly bars went smoke-free. If the entire state ever institutes a ban, though, I'll be back in the Hulmeville at least once a week, like when I first started hanging there. In the meantime, I'll still go, just not as often as I'd like because I value my asthmatic lungs. If you can take the smoke, though, check it out. This place rocks.
label: POS

text: So, here is the next part of my terrible experience with Joey "knuckles"...First, I must add that he did not have me sign any paperwork, NOR did he check my ID!!!! He started drawing on me with sharpies...did not talk to me much, only said he wanted to add a planet and a comet...then he decided to turn my beams of light into this ugly, jagged "lightning" in white and green, against the black and purple background. Now...the background was supposed to be light, airy and inspired by "A Starry Night"! Instead, he covered ALL OF MY SKIN in black and purple and left no room to add brighter colors for stars, the planets looked like bad cartoons...as did the whole tattoo when he finished!!! The moon that i asked for looked like it had a skeleton face...there was no sun at all, and I never had the chance to speak up because he pretty much ignored me. I did not get the tat that I wanted at all. I am an artist, so I was incredibly disappointed...it lacked detail, the lines were very sloppy, and the shading very poorly done. And he left almost no room to improve it...and yet again I will state, HE COVERED ALL OF MY SKIN... I tried many times to initiate conversation, and it was like pulling teeth! The only thing he talked about was the drugs he'd tried!!! I dropped $500 plus tip for an awful tattoo, that is not removable, and not even close to what I described (many times!!!!) and even worse...I have had to spend even more money to get it to a point where I almost like the tattoo...but I had to have two sessions on top of the initial time...and this tattoo is still not to the point where I want it to be, even though I love the new artist, Tegan of Body Graphics/No Ka Oi Tiki Tattoo, who has worked on it...and will be working on it some more. Yes, it is improved now...no thanks to "Knuckles"...and this stands to be mentioned: he took an illegal shortcut by not taking my ID or having me fill out the usual paperwork. This artist has given me a terrible tattoo that I will have to drop even more money on, which I cannot afford. And his demeanor was arrogant, unprofessional and unfriendly! I live on a very very low, fixed income. I really cannot afford to have so many more sessions on this tat...and because of this, I will have to wait a very long time until I can get the next tats that I want. i will never go back to Eddie's or any of Eddie's Tattoo's affiliates because of this. I am in a state of grievance...because this tattoo covers my entire shoulder down almost all the way to my elbow...and most of it is black. I have gotten compliments on it AFTER my first session with Tegan, but it will never ever be what I wanted it to be, and it can never be erased. Please take a lesson for yourself out of my experience: research your artist well!! (Obviously, the hours of research I put in were not enough!!!!) Make sure that they come prepared with sketches like I was promised (if they come without, take a rain-check!!!), and do not let the artist tattoo you if they are have poor demeanor, are hungover, unprofessional (like mentioning drinking, drugging or admitting to being high while they are working on you!!!), and especially if they do not have you fill out the paperwork or they do not listen to your input. Unfortunately, I had to learn the hard way...however, I highly recommend No Ka Oi tiki Tattoo and their artists, especially Mony and Tegan (both are Body Graphics affiliates.) That's all for now--look for a review on No Ka oi Tiki Tattoo and their artists, Mony and Tegan...coming soon!!

text: I enjoy PHO the most when it comes to Vietnamese cuisine. I have mentioned my emotional attachment to pho in my previous review. I am picky when it comes to Asian cuisines but they got the right taste for my tastebuds. For example, they have fresh rolls( moo shoo is my fav), lotus root salad, and fried tofu. Don't over indulge in apps, leave room for savory entrees. For entree: lemongrass chicken (cliche), curry chicken(thai inspired),char broiled pork chop ( thin and perfectly done),shrimp sautee(just the right texture), rice flour crepe with pork slices ( this one is my fav also, just so fresh and light), panseared chicken w/ rice noodles ( lunch item more like it), special rice in hot pot ( MUST TRY) , it's like eating bib bim bap ( korean rice dish) but with different soy based taste. For beverage: vietnamese cafe,soy milk, or thai iced tea w milk. If you are a wild adventurous eater then try their authentic dishes. Sometimes, I like having tripe with pho, but it all depends on the pho broth! I didn't really think they had the best pho but they do very well without it. Bon Apetite.

text: I'd always wanted to try out boxing. I figured as an ex-competitive tennis player, I'd have some semblance of footwork and coordination that would transfer over to ass kicking. Right? Wrong. So wrong. But that's besides the point. I walked into here as it was the most prominent boxing gym chain in Tucson, where I was living temporarily for my job, and checked out my first free class that they offered to all prospective members. One of the trainers showed me some basic punches and proceeded to throw me into the Muay Thai boxing class. I'm not going to lie, it was a good time, and it was different than anything I'd been through before. Afterwards, I discussed membership fees with the guy at the front desk and was just about ready to walk out when he put on the hard sell and cut me such a huge bro deal that I just couldn't pass it up - $90 for five weeks (since I was moving away, he waived the initiation fee + some) and included the standard gloves, hand wraps and private session. Sweet! I scheduled my private session for exactly a week later with one of the house trainers. I showed up and the guy that was supposed to be training me was, by his body language, probably thinking, "I hate my life because I have to train dorks like this who will never last a second in a UFC match," meanwhilst hitting on every girl that walked by throughout that half hour, leaving me alone for minutes at a time to awkwardly practice the moves by myself. Awesome, it was like being in high school all over again! Fast forward to a couple weeks later. By this point I'd gone through a couple Muay Thai classes and was sort of getting the hang of things. I called in on one evening as I was driving home from work, and was told there was a grappling class in session for that evening during the hour I was planning on coming in. "Is that open to absolute beginners?" "Oh, most definitely!" I show up the class, and at the start of it everyone is doing crazy submission holds on one another with names I couldn't pronounce, which results in my body being contorted in ways I'd never dreamed of. I mention to the instructor that this is my first class. Halfway through the hour, he announces that for the remainder of the class we're going to straight wrestle one another, which leaves me with two options: a world of pain or watching from the sideline. I watch for a few minutes before opting for the latter, since these guys are all clearly current or ex-high school wrestlers that would probably break my spine before realizing I didn't have any idea what I was doing. I would rate it higher, but that one grappling class and personal training session definitely left a bad taste in my mouth, despite the other Muay Thai classes being okay. The location itself is also tiny, which leaves you feeling just a little walled in. Bottom line, if you're looking to check out a boxing gym in Tucson, I'd recommend the location on N. Stone instead. It's a different owner, and he's super friendly, and the facilities are much, much nicer and include a full weight room (although it's a little more expensive there) and plenty of UA students come out, so it's a better place to meet people.
label: NEG

Introducing another person into the process puts one more variable out of the owner's control in terms of controlling the atmosphere and experience. text: One of my friends decided that it would be a good idea to take me to yoga, so we went to the new Moksha Yoga on the southside. I obliged, not really knowing what to expect, seeing as I'm not at all flexible, and can't really tolerate heat that well. We got there a half an hour early before the class started and there was a line up outside the building (they lock the doors, as the yogi's keep their belongings lying around in the bathroom, and 'boot room'). Once we got in, we paid $20 for a beginner pass (unlimited yoga for a week) and got changed in the bathroom. We rented some yogitoes because we forgot our towels at home, and we stepped inside the 'oven' where we felt like Tater Pops. Okay, not really, but the heat was pretty intense, yet relaxing at the same time. Definitely not something most Edmontonians are used to. Our instructor Tod was great, super outgoing, and helpful. He took us through the poses one step at a time, and before we knew it, we were dripping wet! I found that flexability wasnt really an issue being in the heated room, having touched my toes with no problems. I have to admit, some times it got too much, so I laid down in childs pose, but Tod didnt have a problem with that. Overall it was a great experiance, and will definitely make it a bi-weekly thing :) Friendly staff, gorgeous interior. It's just got all the right stuff that make a great yoga studio :)

text: While doing some shopping in Maplewood, I got into the spirit of staying local and felt the urge to dine at Nosh. I was not disappointed! We walked in on a Friday night around 7pm and got a table right away. It filled up shortly thereafter, though I never saw a wait. This place is so cute! It's small but they have really cool small pieces of flair as the decor. The light fixtures, artwork, and bar area are nicely done. Not too much but enough to notice. We sat pretty close to the door and regretted it because it was a little colder than we preferred and also there was a piano playing there, so it was a bit loud. Not a big deal. The restaurant did get loud, but a lot of it was a group of people with "that girl" in it. Aka, the loudest, obnoxious, clap and scream at her own jokes type. Certainly not Nosh's fault. I've found one of my top 3 favorite cocktails here! Their list is very long and full of fruity stuff (and more). I ordered the hard blueberry lemonade. It was like candy! So fresh and refreshing, even in this weather. It had real, FRESH blueberries in it. I wanted more but I limited myself to one. It didn't taste like alcohol at all and I didn't care one bit! What other diners said is true, the food comes out REALLY slowly here. There is a blurb on their menu about making everything to order and taking time. Don't come here if you want it fast and ordering an appetizer is recommended if you are really hungry to start. The service was by no means inattentive. Our waiter (also the bartender) came by frequently. The manager came around to check on us too, and was very visible. I ordered the Orchard Melt and Butternut Squash Soup and my hubby ordered the Fried Egg BSRP with chips. Vegetarians, check out the menu because there are several vegetarian things, and gluten free or vegan meals are clearly marked. My sandwich was piled high with apples, maybe a little too many, but it was really nice flavors. The butternut squash soup was AMAZING. Nice and nutty and savory. Not really sweet like some soups with butternut squash tend to be. I felt satisfied after my meal but not like I had stuffed myself. My hubby liked his sandwich but wished he had gotten a salad or soup instead of chips because he has a hollow leg and needs a lot to eat! We will definitely be back!

text: The Jefferson National Expansion Memorial is located in St. Louis, Missouri, near the starting point of the Lewis and Clark Expedition. It was designated as a National Memorial by Executive Order 7523, on December 21, 1935, and is maintained by the National Park Service (NPS). The Gateway Arch is known as the "Gateway to the West". It was designed by Finnish-American architect Eero Saarinen and structural engineer Hannskarl Bandel in 1947 and built between 1963 and 1965. It stands 630 feet (192 m) tall and 630 feet (192 m) wide at its base. The legs are 54 feet (16.5 m) wide at the base, narrowing to 17 feet (5.2 m) at the arch. There is a unique tram system to carry passengers to the observation room at the top of the arch.

text: THE TAP ROOM IS BACK AND BETTER THAN EVER!! A few months ago, I wrote a scathing review of the SPTR, replacing my original shining review of this quaint neighborhood bar. I have been a loyal SPTR customer since 2006. I would frequent the Tap Room at least once-twice per week when the old chef was there. The original SPTR featured a delicious menu full of "bar food" that appealed to all walks of life -- both vegetarian and carnivore. The service was the best in town and the beer menu was incredible. The best part about the Tap Room is that it didn't cater to any one particular scene. As long as you liked beer, food, and good company you were welcome at the SPTR. Then something awful happened --- The SPTR hired a new chef that has delusions of grandeur and cooked like he was cooking for some hoity-toity five-star Center City eatery. Not to mention that he flipped the original menu upside down, adding too many meat-based dishes. The most appalling of this switch was that at one point, he added lion to the menu. LION. Why? Not only is this incredibly cruel but it's also incredibly ridiculous and unnecessary. The same time that this happened, the service got much worse. It got so bad that my friends --- also former fellow SPTR regulars --- and I boycotted the SPTR for almost a whole year. Only a few weekends ago, my friends and I were hanging out and looking for a place to drink, but we didn't want to go far from home. We decided to just suck it up and go to the SPTR. After all, we only wanted a beer or two. When we sat down at our table and the menu was presented, we noticed that the menu was yet again --- completely different and revised --- but in a GOOD WAY! Returned were the delicious staples that the SPTR was known and loved for and added were some new dishes, like the meatloaf and mac n' cheese that my husband ordered and was hands down the best meatloaf I have ever eaten. The staff was yet again happy to serve us, and they were as quick as lightning. THE SPTR IS BACK... AND SO IS MY FIVE-STAR RATING!!!

We never add salt to our meals when we go out, but everything we ordered we added salt & pepper to. Something I read in many other comments was that the silverware was cleared and then replaced. The only silverware that was replaced was my fork, which I purposely left on my appetizer plate. Our server did not replace any other silverware. Also, we were sitting at a four top, and the other place settings were not cleared away, even though there were only two of us. The bread was a disappointment, it had obviously been sitting for some time. And I was surprised/disappointed/appalled to receive bread sticks that I could have bought from the grocery store--still wrapped in the plastic and presented alongside the bread. My boyfriend had the ravioli, which was flavorless--and the ravioli themselves were flattened down with hardly any filling. I had the gnocchi with the Gorgonzola crema & walnuts. The gnocchi was quite doughy, too large of a portion size and my dish was flooded with the crema. The sauce was good, there was simply too much of it!! We also ordered a side of broccoli rabe, which is hard to screw up, but it was slightly tough. The broccoli rabe was the only thing that actually had flavor to it. The second side we ordered was the risotto cake--it was horrible. It was FRIED!!! When we tasted the risotto, all we tasted was cheese. It was overcooked, there was no nuttiness to the grains at all, it in fact tasted like long grain white rice! Overcooked and no flavor to it besides the cheese. I cannot believe they fried it. YUCK!! Wine selection was nothing special, mainly wines you see in the state stores and they up the price dramatically. You can get Luna di Luna for about $12 in the state stores and the price was $27 at Toscana. At least order good wines from a distributor that you don't see everyday! We ordered Robert Mondavi, because you can't go wrong with that! The waiter we had, Vic, was probably the best part of the meal. He seemed like he cared about his meal, gave us time to decide what we wanted for our entrees and did not rush us at the end of the meal. For dessert, we shared the creme brulee pie, good but it had to have been previously frozen & then microwaved, because half of it was warm & half was frozen! We were not offered coffee. Didn't want it anyway, but it still wasn't offered. At the end of the meal, another server/busser came over and cleared everything away...noisily. I might try Toscana 52 again, and if I do, I'd like to go during the dinner rush to see what the differences are at that time. I recommend spending your money elsewhere!!
label: NEG

text: At what should have been the end of a fairly long night, I realized that I left my credit card at Vango... Ugggh... And, like any other Manhattan I have ever had, it kicked my ass on the first swig... and the second... but by the third, it was going down smooth. text: I certainly adore this eatery. Allow me to employ my extensive research in the field to make a few recommendations for optimizing your Mama's experience: -Eat falafel. It's soft on the inside and crispy on the outside and rather delicately seasoned. -Most whole wheat pita is flat and tough and bitter, but not here. Go ahead and order it if you'd like to feel a little healthier by adding whole grains to your plateful of fried. -Don't skip the pickles at the salad bar. The olives are good too, but the pickles! -If you're the kind of person who never has enough tahini in your life, you can get an extra cup of it at the salad bar. -Add some fries if you're eating in; if you're picking up or getting delivery, skip 'em. If you happen to like your fries cold and extra soggy, strike that and reverse it. -Bring cash. Your ATM card will also suffice. -Don't even think about eating here on the Sabbath (even Friday afternoon is a roll of the dice) or on Jewish holidays. -If you want someone to bring your falafel to you, you'll want to call during an off-peak time. They don't have time for that stuff during the lunch rush. This last one is important. -Order hot sauce to liven things up, but unless you love the sensation of five-alarm fire in your mouth, ask them to take it easy. Otherwise, you're liable to end up with a few hot sauce-soaked bites at the end of your pita, and they will burn your face right off. I've warned you, now.

text: Fatty's is a great local sports bar in Wyndmoor. They have TV's squeezed into every corner place and even stuck a couple outside on the patio just for good measure. Like any good sports bar they have the NFL Sunday ticket. The staff are all die-hard Philly sports fans but they're still accommodating and friendly, as opposed to the Santa Booing, fight starting, retarded asshole Philly fans you can't avoid at most sports bars within spitting distance of the city line. So when this NY boy walks in with my Yankee hat or Giant jersey on to catch the game, I catch a ration of shit and hear the taunts from all of them, but it's all good natured. If you're an out of town fan Fatty's is a great place to go catch the game in an enjoyable fashion. On top of that Fatty's has a great selection of beers on tap including an ever rotating selection of micro-brews to try out. The prices are pretty reasonable making it a great place to go with the guys and throw back beers. The food at Fatty's is your standard pub menu but it is all pretty good. I'm especially fond of their cheese fries (especially when they have waffle fries in) and their cheesesteaks are pretty good too. My personal favorite of their sandwiches however is the Buffalo Chicken Cheesesteak, I have a tendency to get it more often than not and it's excellent. That leads me to Fatty's wings. In my opinion you just can't call yourself a sports bar and not have good Buffalo Wings. Fatty's doesn't disappoint. The wings at Fatty's are easily the best that I have found in the area. The wings are large and smothered in sauce. The "hot" sauce has a very good balance of flavor & heat which is what really sets them apart. To top it off they know to give a side of rich, chunky bleu cheese and celery. The last tip I can give about Fatty's Menu is to make sure you check the specials board on the rear wall of the pub. It's a whiteboard right between the kitchen window and the hallway to the bathrooms. See, Fatty's sometimes decides to pretend they're actually a restaurant, trapped in a pub's body. They use that little board to supplement their menu and they do it extremely well. In conclusion Fatty's is hands down the best Pub in the area and without a doubt my favorite pub around Philly.

I understand the need to garnish a dish to make it look fancier than your local Chinatown dish, but it just was not balance with this edible garnish/whatever it was. Salt and Pepper Style Shrimp How can you really go wrong with fried food?!?! This salt and pepper shrimp was pretty good, but all I could taste here was the five spice powder, too. The salad was really fresh and other than lettuce included tabouleh salad (not enough tabouleh in this salad for me, it was awfully heavy on the parsley), feta cheese, and Kalamata olives. text: We had Mother's Day brunch here, $85 per person. (On Mother's day, brunch is served all day, we had a reservation for dinnertime.) Three stars for the food , minus 1 star for the service. The good part: they had a lot of high-end dishes using a lot of expensive ingredients (lobster, caviar, etc.) So why such a low rating? After having the brunch buffet here, I became convinced that high-end food can't be served buffet style. There were dishes that I could tell would have been good had they been cooked to order and not sitting out. It's really disappointing to have overcooked pasta or a cold escargot tart. And remember, for $85 / person, you can have a tasting menu at many restaurants where food is cooked to order for you. Another thing we discovered was that there was too much to try and too much going on. We got lots of little tastings of everything , but never had time to savor it. Before our mouth could savor an item, we had switched to another. Having a prix-fixe meal of 5-6 courses is much better -- sure you don't get to try as much variety, but then you really get to savor the different flavors and textures that the chef is aiming for in a dish. You let a dish grow on you and understand the nuance of a dish. Instead this buffet brunch is like taking the top 40 pop songs and taking a sentence from each stanza and just playing them right after the other. It's a mad slapdash of really good things - but you don't really have time to savor and enjoy. Service: OK, this can't be too hard considering it's a buffet service. Yet our service was not good. We ordered sparkling water and had to wait a good 10 minutes (after we had already gotten our food). We ordered wine, and it also didn't come promptly. They took away my silverware but didn't replace it. A lot of things we seemed to have to ask for twice -- really, service should be a lot better than that. It wasn't rude or anything, just not top notch. And it seemed like they were really trying to rush us out of there. They kept pushing us to go to the next course. My boyfried and I like to use our expensive dinner dates as a time to talk and catch up on life , but instead it was like "go! speedracer go!'" to the next buffet table with these waiters. So we didn't get a nice elegant romantic dinner, we got a mad dash to try all these buffet tables.

text: Hotel Experience: October 10-25 to 10/30 2009 I truly enjoyed my stay at the The Renaissance Pere Marquette. My visit was during what many consider one of the more comfortable times of the year - October. The weather was perfect. Only steps from the famous Bourbon St., Pere Marquette is definitely an ideal choice for New Orleans accommodations. I will admit that I was a bit skeptical when my Garmin led me to this hidden gem on common street adjacent to a late night chicken shack. However, I must say that as I walked into the hotel lobby, I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is very modern, accentuated with velour couches and chairs in warm shades of blue, red, brown and white. Perfect lighting sets the mood as you leave the ever so busy Bourbon St crowd to seek refuge in your temporary home away from home. There are three laptop computers offering free Internet access near the Starbucks. The only downside is that the Starbucks seems to have very odd hours, so it was hit or miss if you wanted your daily white chocolate mocha. However, if you are a Marriott Elite Member you can always find fresh brewed Starbucks coffee in the Concierge Lounge. I was quite impressed with the small Concierge Lounge, it was quite intimate and always offered wonderful food and beverage selections. I was upgraded to a suite with an excellent view, so I LOVED my room as well. The bed was the signature Marriott brand, super comfortable and loaded with pillows. The bathroom was also nice and modern. There was no bathtub, but I'm not really a bathtub proponent in hotels anyway due to hygiene issues - so no complaints here. The fitness facility was also quite nice. Each cardio machine was equipped with individual televisions and there were ample weights and weight machines for strength training. I would definitely stay at the Renaissance Pere Marquette Hotel again, due to its close proximity to the French Quarter (true walking distance), modern hip atmosphere, customer service, and cleanliness.

text: I *heart* this hotel. I picked up a Travelzoo special (a $119 plus-tax room) and booked myself for a night at the Independent a couple days ago. I found out I had an extra night in Philadelphia earlier this week, and figured, why not? The price was solid, the neighborhood has lots to do within walking distance, and the hotel website showed photos of a charming, revitalized building. I'm so glad I chose this place to stay. It's rare that I get to stay in a non-chain hotel - I travel for business a lot, and only last night. I was in a Holiday Inn in the Atlanta suburbs. Ugh. Now, I'm sitting in a small, tasteful hotel room, with soft gold walls and rich-looking wood furniture. All the furniture (including the secretary-style desk) is either stained cherry or dark brown, the curtains are made of classically patterned raised damask, and the beautiful hardwood floors are perfectly restored. It's a classic room, with high ceilings and a bathroom complete with soft gold towels and robes. Oh, and did I mention the amenities? There's a fridge and microwave in here - hiding in a corner, of course. There's FREE WI-FI. There will be breakfast in the morning. The hotel also gives out passes to the 12th St Gym around the corner. Oh, and also: parking here is $15 at the lot a half block away. I've actually been spending most of today in my room catching up on work, so having a beautiful environment to work in has been a godsend. But twice today, I've ventured out: once to get caffeine at Brew-Ha-Ha, once to get a fresh load of fiction paperbacks at Borders by City Hall. And both times I've loved going outside to walk, because there are so many people enjoying themselves in this neighborhood! This whole area is full of twenty and thirty-somethings, all hanging out in bars and restaurants and generally having a fine time. I totally intend to stay here again the next time I come through Philadelphia. I would still gush about this hotel at a higher price point. It's just that nice a place to stay.
label: POS

The grits were lukewarm, lumpy, and had no flavor whatsoever. The biscuit was average. My wife ordered the grits with "debris" (ham) - and again, nothing special going on there. All in all a very disappointing experience and I would not recommend going back until the original owners come back, or until the current owners get a clue. One last thing: the price. text: I work in Donelson-Hermitage (which for some reason has an abundance of greek restaurants - I can think of 4 places that serve tabbouleh within 5 minutes of my office). I love greek food in general -- but this is the place I keep coming back to. It looks like nothing from the outside, and the interior decor is by no means luxe. The 'Italian Cuisine' part is pretty funny -- they even have pictures of spaghetti & meatballs up in the restaurant, but it's not on the menu. Only greek type items on the actual menu. The tabbouleh... that's why you come here. Unlike most places around town, their tabbouleh is so light. It's not wet or drippy -- it almost looks like plain, raw parsley with a good amount of bulgar mixed in. So it's not oily or watery in any way. I'm not sure if it's the bulgar, or what they've added to it, but it is ridiculously good. I quite often order a side of the tabbouleh and it eat it plain, sometimes adding some hot sauce to kick the flavor. But in and of itself, it is excellent. To me personally, the best tabbouleh I have ever had. Everything else seems good -- I have only tried the chicken, no beef/lamb. I typically get the greek salad (heavy on the tabbouleh), sometimes with chicken, sometimes not. The hummus (with oil & yes, more tabbouleh) is also good. Falafel was good, but nothing amazing. One of the things I enjoy most about this restaurant is the staff. The older guy who runs it seems grumpy most of the time, but he knows his stuff. Believe it's his wife running the cash register, she seems very nice. The hand-done chain stitched "GYROS" on their aprons is a thing of beauty. If you're nearby (or just on a really bad tabbouleh jones) give it a try.
label: POS

Second I chose the pimento cheese sandwich. As simple a classic as this is, it was so rich and decadent I almost didn't finish it. For dessert I had the goat cheese mousse. So creamy with just enough goat cheese flavor, not overpowering. All topped off with a bellini and I'm set for the day (or a nap). I can't wait for my next trip to NOLA so I can try their dinner menu!!

My wife, who has a cast iron stomach, and I both had severe indigestion for the rest of the afternoon. Required Zantac! text: I know this place is a bit pricey. But I fell in love with the place when I was in high school and I keep going back, because honestly, I just can't get all this stuff anywhere else in St. Louis....at least, not all in the same place. So if I am saving gas, then I guess that the store isn't all that expensive. This place has everything you could want for a "healthy" lifestyle. They have a huge array of veggie friendly snacks that I love to stock up on and leave in my car for the moments I am starving and stuck in 270 traffic. I also love, love LOVE the huge selection of natural soaps. I have a ton of random allergies and I have never had any problem with anything I have gotten in this store. And they all smell fabulous. They carry a huge array of local products as well. They carry everything from cashew butter (try it, it will kick any peanut butter's butt, I promise), to local honey (which is delicious) to a decent support of local artists through C.A.M.P. which was actually started by an employee of the store. I recently bought a cherry "jelly" (it may be more of a preserve, but you get what I mean, a fruit spread) here that my family went nuts over one Sunday morning when I made breakfast. These are the kinds of little jewels you will find in this store. Just expect to drop a pretty penny when you shop here, you can't get quality for cheap....apparently. (I suppose shopping at Wal-Mart could have taught me that lesson, though).

I had called ahead to tell them we had a vegetarian in the party, and he received an amazing plate of fried green tomatoes with green beans, some amazing peas and cheese...it was another eating highlight in this city for a guy who thought he might not have any. For us; the same again, almost all appetizers...the alligator and the plump wood fired oyster were my favorite this time...along with the cochon which were served with the best cracklin's I ever had. I need bowls of those, 3 were not enough...my mouth is watering now thinking of them. Our waiter was a bit boring, but it beats stuffy service and the other perkier folks on the floor kept coming up to our table to check on us anyway. Since we are beer drinkers, pitchers of NOLA Blonde Ale for $15 was more than reasonable, and kept the bill lower than any other fine restaurants I go to. Sticking with "If you can have only one nice meal while you are visiting New Orleans-give this one some serious thought"

text: Whole Foods is quickly becoming my favorite grocery store in the area, along with Trader Joe's. They have all sorts of great food that is organic and natural and whatever other hippy terms there are. What matters to me is that the products they sell are made with good ingredients instead of cheap junk. For example, it can be difficult to find soda made with actual sugar, let alone any decent selection to choose from, but Whole Foods has a bunch of different kinds (Boylan's is my favorite). Probably my favorite features of the store are the bakery and the deli. The bakery is packed with all kinds of delicious baked sweet things, exotic (to me) breads, and even a case with refrigerated items like cannoli or chocolate mousse. They also have larger items like cakes. I always pick up a few giant chunks of their delicious cornbread because I love it and I've found it quite difficult to find good cornbread in a store. I also recommend the peanut butter bars in the fridge case (I believe the label says "Vegan Peanut Butter Bar"). If you like peanut butter, give it a try. It's fantastic. The deli has the usual lot of deli fare such as potato salad and what have you, but my reason for visiting there is usually to get some of their tasty lunchmeat for making sandwiches. The meats I've tried so far have all been good. I do wish they had some type of sharp cheddar for sale, but the regular cheddar is pretty good anyway. They also have a meat department, and although I don't typically buy anything from there myself, it all looks good and I've been told that they have good stuff in that department. I wish I could say more about it, but I'm far too lazy to cook that sort of stuff myself. I think they have seafood and fish and stuff, too. There is a good selection of prepared foods such as sandwiches, sushi, and a salad bar. I'm not exactly a sushi connoisseur, but I enjoy eating it and the sushi they have here tastes great to me. Aside from that stuff, there's a fairly large produce section and the usual selection of standard grocery items. I'm able to get some things here that are otherwise somewhat difficult to find, such as grape jelly that doesn't contain high fructose corn syrup, so I'd say they have a good selection. I only have a few minor complaints about the store. First of all, I bought one of the vanilla cakes with buttercream icing and was disappointed by it. The icing wasn't very sweet and didn't taste much like buttercream icing to me. It's probably better for me because I won't be buying and eating a giant cake every week, but I don't know of any decent cake bakeries in the area so I was a bit sad that my hopes were dashed by this particular cake. I also don't like the way the parking lot is set up. The entrance funnels all the traffic right in front of the door where there are people walking all over the place. I always feel uneasy driving in the parking lot. Yes, these are the types of dumb things that bother me. Overall, I really like this store and am glad there's one in the area. It's nice to have a place to supplement Trader Joe's in the area of quality food made with non-disgusting ingredients.

text: Surly staff, sketchy location, mediocre hostel. I've stayed at Apple Hostel three times in the past few years*, and the staff seemed more unfriendly than most hostels I've stayed in. The day of my scheduled arrival, I emailed to tell them that I might be coming one day later than I said and to ask a question about parking. And they even charged me for the first day even though they couldn't find a bed for most of the rest of my reservation (just one of the remaining three days). P.S. text: Woodard's is a neighborhood gas and auto-service store that stays true to the customer and community focus that is missing from a lot of syndicated and franchised businesses. I had been looking for someone to service my car as it had been making terrible noises for the past two years and I couldn't find someone I trusted (I'm a law student who drove out from California). My classmate and friend took a look at it and diagnosed it as my power steering pump and belt. After taking it to Woodard's for an oil change, they diagnosed the same. They tightened the belt for me, free of charge, and filled me in on the rest of my car's issues (it's an ancient 94 mercury villagers with 200k+ miles). There was no hard or soft sell. He just told me what he thought the best course of action was for me (which didn't involve me paying him for anything more). It was slightly more expensive than your average oil change, being roughly $40, but for the service, competence and peace of mind by using someone you can trust, I'll take my car here for as long as I'm in Saint Louis.

text: Well, if it wasn't for Yelp (Carrie B, thanks!), I might have passed by this little gem of a store on 4th Avenue's East side. text: I am a stay-at-home Mom who doesn't have the time or the money to get the pedicures I once took for granted, so for a real treat (only my 3rd since having my toddler) I went to get a pedicure. I didn't go to my usual place (Signature Nails Spa) because I had noticed this new place, Illusions Nail Spa and thought I would try it out. I had seen an ad for them and thought they might be worth a try. What a mistake! First, the receptionist seemed loopy and out of it and couldn't understand that the woman who walked in right before me and I weren't together. Then, after wandering off, she pointed to two pedicure stations. After sitting in luke warm water (in which I felt something solid rolling around) for almost 20 minutes, a man finally came over. He never said hello or asked me any questions as to what I wanted-- I guess since the receptionist told him I said mani/pedi, he didn't feel the need to engage me. He was automatic in his motions, leaving me with a sub-par massage and sped through everything else-- especially the callous removal, which was my main reason to come in. I was finished several minutes before the woman beside me, who started at the exact same time. Then, we moved to the manicure. It was awful. Horrid massage, awful filing job-- there were hair left in my polish he didn't bother to remove. Now, less than 4 hours later, the gloppy polish he applied is already peeling off-- probably because of all the bubbles he left in it. I was asked to pay before my polish was applied-- due to smudges, so I tipped him my standard 20%. Boy, I wish I hadn't. Plus, there were strange signs all over the salon. Telling people payment was expected ASAP and no refunds would be given, in any circumstance. This is one reason I didn't even call back to complain-- it didn't seem like they would care! Also-- there were numerous signs asking patrons to not pay with a credit or check card unless necessary because it cost them fees. I'm all for helping a place out, but it was awkward and unprofessional to have these signs everywhere, and I certainly didn't have the $48 cash in my purse. All in all-- lackluster service, shoddy polishing job and not friendly customer service. I will not be going back to Illusions Nail Spa-- especially when it is supposed to be a treat and relaxing time for this stay-at-home Mom.
label: NEG

text: There are a few rules one should always follow: -Never get involved in a land war in Asia -Never eat Mexican food in Middle America. -Never eat Korean food in Nashville. I went in here with high expectations; my friend had come here before for sushi, so I expected that the Korean food would be even better as the place is *run by Koreans*. Alas, my hopes were dashed to the ground and stomped all over. The bulgogi was sweet. I know that it's supposed to be sweet - but it's not supposed to taste like sugar. The meat quality was poor; poorer than the quality that I got at rest stops in South Korea, and that's saying a lot. The kimchi.... Oh, what to say about the kimchi. It was pickled sweet, and it had LOTS of reddish sauce dumped all over it. The bean sprouts were good, but bland. The cucumbers were spicy, sweet, and bland. The broccoli was decent, but also bland. *sigh* My one foray into Japanese was the edamame and that was both overcooked on the outside (WAY too hot!) and undercooked on the inside. I was wondering if it had been freezer burnt, and then tried to be salvaged, it is was so bad. The service was pleasant enough, though our waiter was new and couldn't tell us much about some of the options. I'll never want to come back to this place, but if you do and want to try the Korean: on the way out, I saw the ethnic Koreans eating bibimbap & seafood soup. Presumably those are their specialties. I have no desire to ever come back and find out for sure.

text: My husband, toddler son, and I and another couple and their toddler boy went their for dinner and had the worst service ever! It started out okay--being seated right away, being served our drinks quickly as well. But it went downhill from there. About 5 minutes later the rest of the order was taken and at the same time, we asked for bread. About 20 minutes later we asked about the bread again since we hadn't received it yet. 5 minutes after that, the waiter finally came back to say that the bread was being prepared. 10 minutes after that...both of the boys were getting very restless and hungry. We asked the waiter about when the mac n cheese order would arrive...he ended up giving us a blank stare and "oops I forgot to place the order" look on his face. At about the same time, a table of 4 who came in about 15 minutes after we did were served their food. We finally walked over to where the manager was standing and complained. She didn't even come over to the table to apologize or offer to compensate us for the bad experience we were having with this meal. She just gave one of us two certificates for free meals. By this time the two boys were crying and wanting to leave. The food came out finally and we asked them to box it up for us. That's when we found out that they didn't even prepare all of our meals! text: I went to LCWR Salon and Spa with my BF for pedicures. Here are our experiences... Price: $50 for a basic pedicure Location: Convenient enough and with ample parking Decor: Sleek, modern, high-end The Good: 1. Calling to make the appointment was easy and the person who took our appointments was helpful. 2. My manicurist did a great job with my cuticles and polish application - which I am very picky about. 3. The manicurists were friendly. The Bad: 1. We were greeted at the front desk by the entrance, and was told to check in to another check in counter (for nails, I guess.) We were never asked if it was our first time and directions were never offered. 2. After we checked in for our pedi's, we noticed the strong chemical smell from artificial nails being worked on - I have experienced places where they have a separate area for artificial nails so clients will not have to inhale the fumes while getting natural nail services done. 3. The pedicure chairs were a bit stiff - which would have been easily fixed with a small pillow for lumbar support. 4. Both our manicurists were late. Nothing was offered to make us feel comfortable while waiting (i.e. water...) 5. The manicurists were all talking to each other, quite loudly actually. Sometimes to a point of yelling because they are telling stories amongst each other from different ends of the room. 6. When my BF asked to use the restroom before he got started, his manicurist actually asked him to turn on the water and fill up the pedicure tub himself when he gets back. Although he did it, I do not think it is his job to do so. 7. The place was not sanitary because: - They all dip their hands in the scrub container without using disposable sticks. This means that the container is contaminated because after scrubbing one leg, they dip their dirty hands in the contrainer again for use on your other leg (which happens over and over - do the math.) - Nail files and buffers are not new and have been used on other clients. 8. My BF's time was cut short. He was booked for an hour pedi and was done in 30 mins. He was really disappointed with the massage (which is what he looks forward to in getting pedis) as it felt rushed and the manicurist was done after a couple of strokes. 9. There doesn't seem to be a strict protocol (i.e. my BF got hot towels wrapped around his legs, and I didn't.) Summary: This is not a place to go to if you are looking for a relaxing manicure/pedicure. I would compare the atmosphere and experience to an asian nail salon, with the difference of higher prices, better decor and that they speak english. To be fair, I did get a good polish and the manicurists were nice. Hence, the 2 stars. Otherwise, I would have only given 1 star.

text: On a mission for an after-dinner chocolate fix, we remembered this place downtown. Located in the Paul Brown building on Olive, as soon as you enter you find a comfortable, cozy lounge with big chairs. The long case of seriously crafted chocolates and truffles await you towards the back of the space. We were greeted immediately by an employee (not the owner) who helped us understand the options and recommendations. You cannot find this variety of European-inspired confections in too many places. It is obvious the chocolatier takes time in the presentation. Very detailed pieces of chocolate that looked more like art than dessert. The spot also serves cakes, coffees, ice cream and other choices. We ordered a slice of dark-chocolate cake and then some variety truffles to go. We sat in the cozy chairs (only one other patron was there at 9pm on a Friday) and shared our cake, which came out with a scoop of cappuccino-sprinkled vanilla ice cream. It was a good end to a good evening. Don't ignore the St. Louis-inspired artwork and mural and the marble statues that blend Europe with our fair city. The space is a bit awkward, however. We couldn't figure out what Cafe Cioccolato was trying to be. Is it a storefront for selling fine chocolate? A lounge? A wine bar? The front lounge area is welcoming, but the stale area where the chocolate case is located only had one un-arranged table and low lighting. Directly opposite is a long, low counter top covered with wine bottles. Then it's just a dark, open space towards the back kitchen. We asked if they were still trying to set-up and the employee noted they 'add tables as needed for events' so we put together than the wine serving area must cater to parties and events, where the big void would be filled with high tables. Hey, A+ for diversity. The space would work great for events...but on a quiet weekend, it just felt vacant. Nevertheless...stop off and get a truffle or hot chocolate to go or relax in the comfy chairs. Now open late on weekends!
label: POS

text: Drove up to Reno for the weekend and decided to Yelp somewhere to eat for dinner. Came across Sushi Pier as it was one of the highest rated restaurants. We could've went to a casino buffet and had endless amounts of prime rib and crab legs but, I'm glad we went off the beaten path and tried out Sushi Pier. Sushi pier is located in a strip mall, somewhat hard to find but just look for the Costco as it's directly on the opposite end. Walking into the restaurant almost gave me a sense of clausterphobia, it's very intimate. We decided to do the all you can eat sushi at $17.95 pp. We were seated at the bar, seats #1 & #2, which you had to walk sideways to get to as it was narrow. We ordered sushi and I decided to try out their handrolls as I'd get my bang for the buck. I loved the Elvis handroll, which was "crystal shrimp" if you ever had walnut prawns, it's that, but using baby shrimp and no walnuts. It also had shreds of crab and sauce. Majorly, majorly delish! Also had to order CA roll just to determine the initial quality of the sushi. It was pretty good and they served up 8-pieces too! The sushi chef helping us (didn't catch his name, darn it!) was pretty cool and was on the ball making about making sure we were okay. (Note: He's a big polynesian guy - I think. Really nice guy.) Actually, everyone at the restaurant was really friendly and attentive too. There was one guy, not sure who he was, probably the manager/owner who came around while we were there and was checking in on all their customers. PROS: Pretty damn good sushi for Reno! NEGATIVES: Sushi offerings/creativity were good, could be better. However in their defense, if they served my "Livermore Roll" (see my review for Kawa Sushi- Livermore, CA) then I would've ran them out of business during this visit! LOL! OVERALL: The all you can eat deal is the way to go. I'll definitely consider eating there again the next time I'm in Reno and need to get my sushi fix on!

text: I had my heart set on a custom dress for my wedding. The perfect stitch seem to provide quality dresses at affordable prices. Sadly, my wedding dress ended up being my biggest regret. I contact TPS about five months prior to my wedding and asked if they could make a dress for me. I sent sketches and pictures of what I wanted and was told it wouldn't be a problem. At my first consultation my measurements were taken and Melissa also offered to make me a custom corset "with the same lace material as my dress" it was going to cost $125 but she promised it would be an heirloom. My wedding dress was suppose to be around $600 after two "consultations" I finally saw an outline of the dress (cotton mock, not the real thing) and realized it wasn't the right form. In order to change it to what I originally wanted she charged me an additional $250. I paid because it was a month away from the wedding and I was still hopeful that the dress would look beautiful. Two weeks before the wedding I still hadn't even tried on the actual dress. The day before the wedding I finally got to try on the dress but there were still alterations that needed to be made. That's right--I didn't get my wedding dress until the DAY of my wedding. She also had her assistant call to complain that I had "waited too long" to pay my final $125 (even though the dress wasn't even near finished). Melissa made snide comments at my mother because she didn't start to cry when I tried on the dress (probably b/c it looked BAD and my mom was pissed). Finally, on the day of my wedding I went to get my dress. I did a final fitting w/the corset she had made...the corset was too big. She tried to pin it up so that it would fit that day but it provided NO support. It was basically as if I was braless. And the promise that it would be the same lace as my dress was not true. She used completely different material. And to top it off, the "hooks" she used were just thread so no surprise it broke before I even got to the venue and was able to wear it, it was basically useless. The dress itself looked like cheap lace, it was rough and looked horrible. I was embarrassed to wear it but had no other options. It's taken me over a year to write this because it makes me sick to my stomach to think about how horrible I looked and felt. Additionally, Melissa was very condescending and unprofessional. If I could change anything about my wedding experience it would be the dress. Truly, I would have been happier finding a dress at any other store. AND this wasn't a "you get what you pay for situation"--I spent almost $1000 on this attire and that is poor quality that I received. Maybe you need to her friend to receive good service... PLEASE if you must have a custom gown--go somewhere else! And have an airtight contract of services and a plan B.

text: I travel to New Orleans often for business; I have been there twice since April and live in Seattle. I think part of the problem was the overly aggressive waitstaff; and their need to up-sell every item we ordered: "Maybe you would like two of those?" "You are only having sparkling water?" and on and on it went. Speaking of the sparkling water...three of us ordered. The wait staff brought a bottle poured the entire bottle into two glasses and then asked if we would like to order another one...even though obviously we needed more to fill a glass for myself. I quickly switched to New Orleans finest. We ordered our entrees. When a chef friend across from me pulled a piece of plastic out of his food and placed it on the edge of his plate. I quickly stopped eating my Rabbit & Dumplings (the same entree) It was full of bones already...and the plastic was the icing on the cake. When we pointed out the situation to our waiter he took the dish back to the kitchen where they removed the piece of plastic and brought the same plate back and proclaimed it to be nothing more than celery. They did not offer another option; they just brought the plate back. Thankfully they did end up comping one of our meals; but to inform a customer (who is a chef; and his table who was full of food marketers) that we were wrong and that it was celery and simply drop the plate back in front of the guest was unacceptable. A piece of PLASTIC is not a piece of celery. Cochon was a disaster...I am sticking with August.

text: My extended family has used Otto's as a convenient meeting place for big breakfasts for years. The breakfast menu is large, kid-friendly, the coffee keeps coming, and service is usually quite efficient and friendly. However, the place takes on an entirely different flavor for dinner. We went for dinner one rainy Friday night recently. Before we even walked through the second set of doors, we were assaulted by an overpowering smell of broiled fish and maple syrup. Fish should not smell that bad. It just shouldn't. I read somewhere that, given time, the nose accustoms itself to bad smells so you can stomach them. This did not happen for me, sadly. It seemed to emanate from the dark wooden paneling and bad paintings of bucolic farmhouses. Accompanying the stench and decor was the music. Dear god, the music. I think it was Home on the Range on an accordian. At that exact moment, my husband turned to me and said something like, "You know, we really need more fun in our lives. We're getting old." As I looked at the sea of gray-haired customers in sensible shoes and sweaters with dogs on them, I had a vision of our future and pretty much lost it. I giggled for about ten minutes. Ok..the food. That's what we're here to talk about. I had pretty much lost my appetite due to the fish smell, but I persevered and ordered a wiener schnitzel sandwich and a chocolate milkshake. Note the word "shake," because the waitress proudly presented me with a blended, foamy chocolate milk, clearly made with powdered chocolate and told me that she had never made a milkshake before. The sandwich was a pale, rather soggy slab of breaded veal on a dry piece of untoasted rye bread. That's it. Jeez, throw in some mustard or mayo...or even a tomato! The good-hearted waitress seemed genuinely befuddled when I told her I didn't want to wrap the sandwich to take home. As the accordian music turned from a gentle Home on the Range to a demented circus theme, my husband and I wound our way through the lederhosen and walkers to the fresh air of a busy 611. I had the stench of fish in my nose for an hour afterwards and just thinking about it now makes my stomach turn.
label: NEG

text: A new discovery in awesomeness for the Philadelphia summer nightlife scene; for just ten dollars a lawn ticket can be purchased to the Mann's Orchestral BYOB picnic jamboree. Apparently whenever the orchestra plays at the Mann you are allowed to bring in lawn chairs no bigger than 28", any food you feel inclined to eat, and any drink you might have a thirst for, alcohol included. We went to a performance of Tchaikovsky followed by a fireworks show last night and were quite pleased, all things considered. To begin I suppose I should describe the layout of the venue. The performance area is situated at the bottom of a bowl like hill, with an artfully constructed wooden building over and around three sides of the stage to funnel the sound outwards and up. Right against the dais is a large area of seats, and behind these seats is the main lawn seating area with the ideal concert real estate. This general admittance zone extends to the top of the hill where it is hemmed in by a tree line. If you stand on this main hill facing the stage, there is a large wing to the left with levels of extra lawn seating for bigger events, and then a fence to it's left . While this extra seating does not afford any real view of the concert, the view of the city skyline that can be seen from there is breathtakingly spectacular. If you were standing on this extra seating hill, at the top is a tented restaurant area. On the side of the tent farthest from the stage is another small patch of grass ringed on two sides by tent walls, and then on the third by a chain link fence with dumpsters beyond; This is where I was able to find open grass to sit, and the only view was of an abandoned factory. I know what you are thinking: "How can he give this place five stars when standing outside the property line would have let him hear more musical notes than where he sat?" (during the 1812 overture we listened to the dishwasher's clattering silverware in lieu of the cannons) The reason is because I arrived to an eight o'clock concert at 8:20 and understand I got what I deserve, so next time I will be much earlier. Plus, I can recognize greatness even when I prevent myself from experiencing it (the far corner was a big party anyway, so there was some consolation). P.S.- We may have been in the absolute worst possible seats on the grounds for the concert, but when the fireworks went off afterwords they were directly overhead. Suck on that, front row center. -Also, biting bugs were out in force.
label: POS

text: "You should have called ahead, as you probably know from being a vegetarian" Actually I think I should know what it is like to being a vegetarian as I have been one for 16 years ago this lent. Picture it, a temperate Monday at 12:30, the lunch room is half empty, the outside has a table open. We take it. The restaurant has come highly recommended to us for its oyster sandwich. I tell the waiter "I am not your target demographic" of his pig and fish full menu. "I am a vegetarian, what can you do for me" "Not really anything" said my waiter. "Usually the chef can make some alterations but not today, just too busy" He sends out the manager who tells me the same BS w/the money line "you should have called ahead, as you probably should know being a vegetarian" Yeah buddy, I've been a vegetarian for 15 plus years. I think I know how to live the lifestyle and calling ahead is not part of it. It is, in 2009, expecting that every menu has some type of vegetarian option so that people who rely on my for directions on great food in cities around the country don't end up feeling like assholes because they are eating and I am looking at a tiny plate of wilted greens and calling your salad lunch. "Lima Beans?" no cooked w/bacon, no exceptions "Double baked potatoes?" not them either so they brought me the salad and the side of mac n cheese. You would think they would have given me a larger portion of mac n cheese knowing that is all I would eat said my companion but ensuring I leave satiated was never their concern. Cochon convinced me that it is FAR easier to be a vegetarian in Buenos Aires than New Orleans

text: Friends of ours, who were veterans of this restaurant, took me and The Wife last Saturday, and I was not disappointed. We had the appetizer combo plate, and I was particularly fond of the pickle, served in the middle of the plate. It wasn't like an Indian pickle, which I find too harsh, but rather sweet. I also tried the Tom Yam soup, which was superb. The chunks of tomato were an incredible flavor combination with the broth. We all ordered separate entrees, and shared. Three out of four were great. Let's start with the disappointment - the basic Chicken Fried Rice that my wife ordered. It was quite bland. Didn't stop me from finishing it off her plate, though. The Malay Mee Goreng was fabulous, and ordered by my friend conveniently seated across from me. :) I had the Thai Curry Chicken, which had great flavor, but just as importantly, the sauce consistency was good, not greasy, which has been a problem with some recent Thai places I've visited. And finally, there was the Rasa Sayang Ginger beef, which was served like fajitas, sizzling on the way to the table. Drinkies? The beer options were limited, but at least they had a Singha for me. There were typical colorful martinis available, so my wife had something with blue curacao. Then the desserts. Leave some room. The fried ice cream was merely OK - it had quite a think crust, and it was served with a couple of chunks of fried banana. Fried banana was also available on its own. There was a coconut pudding, which was like a flan, kinda custardy, and a peanut pancake, which was very similar to a appetizer dish that I neglected to mention. We sat in the place long after we had paid the check, so perhaps we were the noise that the other reviewer objected to. OK, so it was a bawdy conversation. Its not like there were any kids around. Not much atmosphere to speak of, but that's not why we went. We were also given a $10 gift card for a future visit. A warning - we may not be going back, as many of the dishes are cooked with some kind of shrimp broth, which my wife is allergic to. It severely limited her options.

It's nice enough with it's intimate tables and even cozier low-floor-seating rooms, but that doesn't make up for the quality of the food. Okay, so it's not that bad, it's actually decent enough. But "edible" and "decent" -- is that what you would settle for? I should hope not. I know I can be a bit harsh, but hey baby, that's what I'm here for. The price at Yokozuna is average, just like their sushi. I have nothing else to say, besides that this place totally turned me off from tempura forever, which is a sad sad thing indeed. There was an unnecessary amount of flour and grease on the tempura, and I've never been able to stomach it again, even to this day. And I'm not being dramatic about this, I assure you.

The burritos and chimichanga are wonderful and the fajitas are delicious and sizzling hot. They have live music on Friday and Saturday night (a Harpist on Friday and Mariachi's on Saturday), which are always fun to listen to. My only complaint is that it gets extremely busy on weekend nights and holidays. On a couple of our weekend visits, they were woefully understaffed, which resulted in unacceptable wait times (even for a mom and pop, home cooked meal). That being said, we still frequent Carlota's and usually do takeout on the busy weekends.

Since I go so often, I always make it a point to try something new and "exotic", and whenever I ask about any of them, the servers know their stuff. I have never gotten something I haven't really enjoyed. Being that it is a Belgian bar, this is not a place for the lighthearted of beer drinkers. What it IS for everyone is amazing food. I've had a lot of their stuff, burgers, fries, what have you, and while all of them are delicious, NOTHING beats their mussels. They have a multitide of different types, from your standard mussels to the spicy thai mussels. It's a great place. Grab a chimay and some mussels - just don't forget the gum.

text: Best place to eat for breakfast! The service is okay, only b/c they get SUPER busy. But they do their best and they are pretty fast considering. Once you get there, walk in and on your left on a chair sits the sign in sheet. aka reservation sheet. Sign in and wait. Be patient, it's worth it.
