text: I love the new and improved Oyster House! So refreshing. As soon as you walk in you feel transported to a little seaside getaway - but the parking garage across the street quickly reminds you where are you are. Despite the view on Samson, it's the high ceilings, dark wood floors and paneling, cool marble bar and stark large white subway tiles that breathe room into this space. What a reno! I also love the contrast of the shabby-chic oyster plates hung up on the back walls of the dining room - Though I didn't venture too far in the back, it seems like the bathrooms (why downstairs?) are an afterthought. The narrow stairs only allow one person to go up and down and it's total traffic bottlenecking - Oyster House needs to rethink that space. Service is helpful (but our waiter was a bit absent-minded - sent us a pear martini with olives instead of a dirty martini with olives - blech!) and friendly -- but they do expect you to eat. Menu is all seafood all the time, with only a few salads and one or two sides that can feed your allergic-to-shellfish or fussy-eating friend. Nice menu offerings, with Oysters (duh) taking center stage. Entrées are a wee bit expensive ($28 for a lobster roll sandwich?) But with the $1 Oyster Happy hour special you can't go wrong. If you love a little entertainment with your grub, you can seat yourself in front of the raw bar guys and watch as they shuck your meal together. Drink and wine list is well-edited - They even offer up a nice twist on my favorite cocktail from home: The Ceasar. (it is a gagillion times better than the Blood Mary - trust me - see my recipe below**) I have yet to find a place ANYWHERE in Philadelphia that makes the original, but Oyster House gives it a whirl calling it the "Blonde Ceasar" made with Orange Heirloom tomato juice and clam juice - Don't knock it until you try it. It is served with a lavender scented green bean! Yum! **A true Canadian ceasar: - Rub rim of glass with a lime wedge and then rim glass in celery salt. - Add Ice, 2 ounces of Vodka, Mott's Clamato (This is important! You MUST use Clamato), sprinkle of celery salt, splash of Worcestershire sauce, splash of Tabasco sauce, squeeze juice of one lime wedge. -Stir well and add a small celery stalk for garnish

The service was spotty and overall it was a very disappointing experience, especially since we were celebrating my parents' big anniversary. I don't see how people think this place is good - unless they've never had the experience (and it's an experience, not just a meal) of dining at Bern's.

text: Izzo's is a no good substitute for Chipotle. Even though this place is only a block from my office, I doubt I'll be going back that often. I don't understand why it's so busy... I guess it's an easy lunch place, and that along with convenience is about all you need to entice people for lunch. Sigh... There were a few redeeming factors that usually get me to bump it up to 3 stars, but I'm not being that gracious today because Izzo's makes me miss Chipotle even more. Cons: 1-long lines and kind of a stressful experience ordering 2-pretty pricey for fast food lunch 3-they charged me for my "tortilla on the side" of my burrito bowl 4-food was meh. Three Pros, but not enough to be redeeming: 1-the roasted corn topping is actually corn that they roast there. I saw it on the grill and was impressed to know they use actually corn off the cob instead of some canned stuff. Still tho, they've got nothing on Chipotle's corn salsa. 2-the cilantro ranch dressing was the best part of the meal. that sauce is so good i dipped my "tortilla on the side" in it and ate most of it. I would go back in and pay for just their cilantro ranch. 3-different flavored tortillas. the spinach one was good. Would I ever go back here again? Probably, if I needed something and didn't want to think about it. Or if co-workers were planning to go. Would I enjoy it? Probably not. If you didn't already get the general theme, I'd rather hold out for Chipotle back home.

text: Their menu is mostly Chinese, with a few Thai items. I had the Chicken Pad Thai, and I was blown away. You can specify level of spicyness, and I had the mild. The flavors really came through, and the noodles were perfect. This was a different recipe than what I've had at any other Thai restaurant, and I loved it. Ambience is what is to be expected at a strip-mall walk-up. You can carry-out, or eat-in in the dining area. There was a steady stream of customers during the dinner hour. Owners are a handsome young-looking mom-and-pop Asian couple with three adorable little children, plus a teenager. The teen even helps out at the counter. Chopsticks, plastic utensils and soda are self-serve. Two separate restrooms for men and women. They are located on the South side of Indy, on South Emerson Avenue, about 2 blocks North of I-465, on the West side of the Street, in a little strip-mall building. I haven't tried the Chinese cuisine items, but for the Pad Thai, I'll have to say this is worth the trip. Ambience isn't going to impress the boss/wife/gf/inlaws, but the food definitely impresses. This is indeed a gem. They can also prepare large quantities for catering with advance notice. There is a different combo Chinese/Thai restaurant further South on Emerson, on the South side of I-465, so don't confuse the two. I liked this one much better.

text: 4.5 stars... Everything that a crab shack should be! On the water? Check. Cold Beer/drinks? Check Good food? Check Casual, fun atmosphere? Check Live music? Check I've been visiting my folks in Port Richey for 10 years and this is the first time we've been here and what a find! The place is literally a shack with trees growing out of the thatch roof and warped boards under your feet. There are parrots at the hostess stand, which by the way, is kind of hard to find from the parking lot we were starting from. You have to make your way through a maze of arcades and shops. You do have to wait to be seated, there is even a sign saying that if you are in a hurry this isn't the place for you. Food was mostly good to great. The crab cakes were wonderful, as were the grouper nuggets and gourmet fries which were basically potato wedges fried in a thick batter. My fish sandwich was HUGE and had so much fish it wouldn't stay on the bread! The onion rings were a bit bland and the calamari (which, oddly was only the body portion) were overcooked and a little tough. My table mates raved about their food also, which included a burger. The bad was pretty much all do to service: We were told a 20 minute wait and when we went to get a drink we saw plenty of open tables. The hostess said they were understaffed. The management should schedule better to avoid this. I can't imagine that in this economy they have trouble finding help. Also, food came out sporadically and some of it took a while. When one of our two apps arrived they brought out extra plates but there was only one set of plastic utensils. Another worker wasn't to be seen so we could ask for an extra set. Good thing I was sharing with my husband so we could share the fork. Be warned too that since the place is pretty much all outdoors there are lots of people smoking. Another cool thing about the place is that since it's on the river you can drive up in your boat and dock it right there while you eat. I can't wait to give that a try!
label: POS

text: Moe's is a lot like Chipotle -- you essentially pick a basic (burrito, taco, quesadilla, salad) & pick your fillings / toppings as you go down the line, then pay, grab some salsas & be seated & enjoy. All of the menu items at Moe's have strange names -- burritos include the "Homewrecker" & "Joey Bag of Donuts"; standing in line you hear people ask for a "J.C.", or "Joey Cocostan" quesedilla (meat, beans & cheese). On the tables they have those little triangular ad card things with a list of the "Top 10 Reasons You Know You Spend Too Much Time at Moe's", or something to that effect. One of them is "All your favorite foods are named after inside jokes." Oh, is that what they were supposed to be? I thought they were just idiotic phrases that someone thought would be catchy. I also think it a little ... pointless? that they have these special names for items that are *exactly* the same but for the fact that one lacks an ingredient & one has it. Better to have it Chipotle-style, in my opinion, & just go down the line & tell them what you want. Guacamole's extra? Fine, add it anyway. It's easier than calling out a different menu name. Maybe I feel like guac today & I don't tomorrow. That means I have to look at the menu again? Stupid. Chips & salsa do come with every meal, free (the salsas are at the salsa bar; you've got 5 selections & they're all fine but not exciting), & the portion sizes of the entrees are decent for what they charge. Overall Moe's is basically a step up from Taco Bell as far as Mexican fast food, with perhaps a little bit less variety. It generally leaves you wanting something -- flavor? originality? -- but otherwise satisfies.

text: I'm surprised that there are any good reviews here, much less a large amount of them. When none of the workers at a "Mexican" place have any discernable accent, it's a bad sign. I wouldn't be surprised to find thart Riendo is Mexican for Bell. After ordering at the counter, I went to the bucket of drinks to see the various Mexican soda options. Every bottle was warm. I asked for water, and the girl pointed me to an iceless pitcher and a styrofoam cup. The water was also warm. Nothing better than pouring your own warm drink. My chicken tacos came out, and in comparison, the water was actually warmer than the food. The salsa, however, is the hottest I've ever had. There's nothing wrong with heat if you can still taste the ingredients. All you can taste here, though, is heat. So instead I ordered a side of pico de gallo, which turned out to be about an ounce worth of pico. A 5-cent portion for $2. It didn't matter anyway since they never brought me any bloody chips! The chicken tacos would've been more aptly named "cilantro tacos." I couldn't even eat the tortilla shells since they had the texture of being microwaved 10x. They were as rubbery as...a big, thick piece of rubber (I'm at a loss for analogies, okay?!). The chicken was flavorless, bland and luke warm. I'm really digging deep for something positive to say about this place, and all I can come up with is: the girl at the register was pleasant. That's all I got. It's not enough to get me to come back. Nice knowin' you, Taco Riendo.

text: I had been working for the same restraunt for over 10 years. My coworkers were like my second family. They had seen me through graduation, engagement, marriage, baby shower, etc. When the restraunt suddenly closed down, without warning, it was like a death in the family. Tears were shed, alcohol passed lips, and many pondered about what was next. I was in my early 30s, a good 10 years older than the average restraunt worker. I had a young family that I rarely saw, my career during the day at the bakery was taking off, it was time to reevaluate things. While the money from serving/bartending was great, the idea of having nights free, of seeing my kids and wife more often, was alluring. Not to mention the easing up on my poor feet and lungs ( this was back when people were allowed to smoke indoors.) Yes! That's it! I'm out. No more doubles, no more late night closes, no more parties of 20, no more cleaning up cheerios on the floor, I'm out! This plan was feasible for about 2 days, until I ran out of cash. Its the golden goose of the biz., always having cash on hand. Suddenly, my George Costanza-like wallet wasn't bursting with small bills. I knew there were such things as ATMs but I didn't know how to use one and most certainly didn't know my PIN. This wasn't working. So I enjoyed my few nights of reading bedtime stories to my kids, and watching TV with my wife, and then set out to get another restraunt job. A brand spanking new place had opened up not 10 minutes from my house (great timing) called The Winners Circle. New Place, close proximity, sports bar, jackpot! I felt fate had stepped in and I decided to apply. I had tons of experience, knew sports, was reliable, personable, funny, I felt I was a shoo-in. Being older , I do have to prove that I'm not "that creepy guy" when I start at a new place. However it doesn't take me long to get accepted by the herd , with my fine cocktail of humor, immaturity, self depreciation and charm. So why did I feel like my interview there went so poorly? The hiring manager acted shady, and asked repeatedly if I had cooking experience. I'm " front of the house" all the way bro! I had my first taste of getting the brush-off and of course never got a call back. Of course, I landed on my feet and found another place, but it bugged me not to be accepted there. That is...until I went there shortly after it opened. The servers (dressed smartly in referee shirts) looked like a Maxim photo shoot. All female, all hot, and a marvel of marketing genius. I would have been the turd in the punchbowl. I laughed and ate my meal, harboring no ill will and understanding completely. Of course, the employee pool is always huge, when a restraunt first opens. They had the pick of the litter (apparently, I was the runt) and used it to their advantage. Now, when I come, it seems they are taking what they can get. Not a dig on the staff, but I see a more normal mix of employees. I like this place. Its awesome for sports watching. Ive seen some great games here and the place heightens the experience. Food is decent and their current menu is perfect sports food. Special props to their menu. Not necessarily the food but the names of the food. You can get The Rosenhouse...a customized wiener. The Krukker is a burger served on a glazed donut! All dishes have some connection to Philly sports, and as a homer, I appreciate it. All the talk recently of burger orgies have made me stop lamenting eating so many burgers lately and has let me embrace it. I got the Lefty Burger. Not only because I'm a Steve Carlton fan, but I'm also a fan of bleu cheese crumbles and caramelized onions. It was a damn fine burger. Not among the best but quite good. I also like that they sell an $8 large beer mug, which you get to keep, and bring back to be refilled for $4 or so. I have long since forgiven Winners Circle for snubbing me. Besides the fact that its a great place to watch sports and their food is good, I went on to better things and have met great people , who have since become another 2nd family. People like Aaron O. On second thought, screw you Winners circle.
label: POS

text: We wanted to try something new, in our area. So when I remembered Restaurant.com had a coupon for 333 Belrose I decided that's where we would eat. Then I checked YELP! And people had written good things. So off we went. I have to say nothing was overtly wrong with our experience, but we do not have to go back there again. Our waitress although extremely friendly was slow and did not return to the table after our food was served (by the wait staff) to see if everything was alright. In fact we were missing something from our order and when she finally did come by and we asked for it she got it right away. . And we are not very picky people. Yes really. We started off with Crispy Shrimp and Ginger Springrolls (you get 3 small rolls cut in half so you get 6 pieces) and it came with Asian Slaw. To tell you the truth I liked the slaw better than the springrolls. $11. Ahi Tuna Sashimi and Wakame Salad.- the tuna was very fresh. The Vietnamese clear dipping sauce had a slight citrus? flavor and seemed a little hmmmmm bland, so we used the sauce from the springrolls. This dish was a good value for your money. $13. The entrees start at $22 and go up to $28 from the menu. My husband had the Sage Cornbread Stuffed Rainbow Trout and it comes with green beans and "4" shrimp. This was the best thing about our meal. Very good. The stuffing gave the fish a lot of flavor and the mustard sauce drizzled over the fish just made it mouth watering to look at when it came to the table. Daughter had the Wild Caught Salmon with baby potatoes and substituted green beans for the braised red cabbage. This was also a very good dish. The salmon had a very nice marinade and the potatoes were very tasty. I had the Slow Braised Lamb Shank- substituting asparagus for the Brussel Sprouts. Sorry folks I don't do brussel sprouts. You get a very big shank bone. This was just an ok dish I am sorry to say. And I do like lamb shank. The garlic mashed potatoes were very good as was the asparagus. We had the individual carrot cake and the flourless chocolate cake for dessert. These WERE good. The carrot cake is basically a nice cupcake with sour cream topping and they drizzled caramel sauce around it, so the sweetness with the slightly salted sour cream top and the not so sweet carrot cake really was good. text: The Orpheum is still kind of that hole in the wall bar. Its not big, and you're not meant to sit around - its setup for dancing and rocking out to indie rock shows. Saturday is the most popular and highly regarded night with its $10 all you can drink 'sink or swim' special and indie rock music that DJs 'Rigg' and 'Noi' have titled 'Retro Red Square'. Don't come here expecting the trendiest music though or for them to even be able to play some of the most prevalent indie rock staples. While they will often update their set lists, it'll typically be months behind current trends. Also expect the indie music to share time with some crappy 80s rock and even crappier hip-hop/rap. Where the Orpheum has really begun to shine is its Monday nights which have about everything going for them minus the fact that they are... on monday nights. Mondays feature a $3 entry, 2for1 drinks all night long, and twice a month live DJs. The last Monday of every month features DJs spinning classic soul and is a blast. Also, one Monday of the month, is Vintage Vandals spinning 60s style garage rock including mod and mod-revival bands. Both these nights are a blast and sure to get your toes tap'n to a beat found nowhere else in Tampa. And then of course the shows, although less frequent since Crowbar exploded onto the scene. The Orpheum stills host a plethora of small time indie bands waiting to hit it big - usually with reasonable ticket prices in the $10 ballpark. The Orpheum doesn't have the best sound system for bands but it is setup so that you're right next to the stage and can really get to see the bands. Shows are interspersed throughout the week and can often occur before the later night dance activities which usually open their doors at 10:30. On most of these nights you can be guaranteed what my friend Rick has coined as the 'lightening round'. This is simply defined as the time after the bar has closed and all of its drunken patrons crowd out into the street outside of the Orpheum. People chit chat and arrange their late night hookups here and its usually good for a fight or two, at which point the police show up and tell everyone to go home. TIP: The public parking garage down the street usually stops staffing the garage after 4am on Saturday nights, so if you can wait it out by hanging around the lightening round or sleeping in your car till then, you avoid paying the $8 Saturday night fee. Monday nights has ample free parking around the Orpheum but sometimes homeless with light stick will try to charge you for parking. When paying for parking, always demand a receipt - if they cannot provide it, you do not have to pay.

text: So I bailed on work the other day, basically for lack of interest. I had slept horribly, had bad dreams, and I felt just yucky and tired. And HUNGRY! We also were trying to not spend too much dinero, so I suggested King Buffet. We both had lunch and sodas there, and with the nice tip we left, we got out of there spending like $22, which rocks. I mean, it's like $5 more than fast food. And way less nasty! So my favorite thing here is mos def the terriaki chicken sticks. I eat like, ten of them. That, and the sesame balls. Those things are freaking delish!!!! I also like that garlicy green bean dish, but I think they make it better at that other Chinese buffet on Plumb lane. When we go there, I eat like 2 plates full of those green beans. The selection here is kind of random and strange. They have super Asian seafood dishes, octopus and stuff that I won't eat because frankly I get a little scared about what that stuff might do inside my belly. Then they have Americanized Asian dishes like fried rice and egg rolls and sweet and sour chicken that mostly anyone will eat. And then they have french fries and chicken nuggets. Oh and they make these little sugar coated fried doughnut things. They are incredible! Seriously! Flakey and yummy and they melt in your mouth. The husband isn't much for sweets, but I practially mouth raped him with one of those fried doughnuts and next trip around the 'ffet, his plate was half filled with them. Their salad bar is also so random! It's like iceberg lettuce and nasty looking pasta salad, various canned fruit some of which I had no idea what it was but I still ate it, tapioca pudding and jello cubes. I did eat some pudding too, tapioca and banana mixed together. It was yummy. King Buffet is one of those places where you can't expect to want to eat EVERYTHING, and there will probably be some things that you shouldn't eat. But if you pick and choose you can fill up on delicious morsels of randomness. Oh and next time I need to go when I actually have money because I want to buy like 10 items from their display case. I want a lacy fan (for my daughters!) and a bamboo plant and some sparkley plastic jewelry. I love resturants that have gift shops and what not inside them!

text: Pretty good pizza, but not the best, and a better-than-average salad bar earn this four stars from me. This place opened about three months ago next to the new convenience store at Greg and McCarran in Sparks. The address is South Stanford Way, but don't be confused by that. It's on McCarran Boulevard. I went and got a salad bar and a 10-inch pizza. The salad bar stands out for having lots of fresh ingredients. The purple onions had obviously been freshly cut. The lettuce was fresh. And the bacon bits weren't that dried, processed Bacos-type stuff. You could tell they used to be bacon at one time. The good ingredients carried over to the pizza topping as well. I got The Coliseum Supreme and pretty much each topping was tasty. None of the flavorless processed food like you get in the chains. The sauce didn't seem distinctive. It wasn't good or bad. The pizza was a little too doughy. They may not have let it cook long enough. I'll ask for it crispy next time. The salad bar and the pizza came to $17. Not something I can do every day. But they offer all-you-can-eat pizza and salad bar for lunch for $7. That could be a screaming good deal. I'll have to try it. As a bonus, they have lots of nice HD TVs.

text: 7/22/07. It's a Sunday night and my last night visit at SB. I heard so many great reviews about Arigato that I just have to experience it myself. There was a crowd outside but we got sat right away because we wanted to be seated at the sushi bar. We sat right in front of a non-asian sushi chef. Great I though, we got freaking jip. O well. So we ordered several types of rolls. I don't quite remember all the names except for the arigato roll, and the yellow tail unigiri. As our non-asian sushi chef made our rolls, my mouth dropped with amazement. This guy is freaking good. He had fast hands and a very delicate way of using the knife. It was very entertaining. We end up having conversations with him and he was very funny and shy at the same time. We asked him for his name and he said Brian, hmmm I thought to myself that does not fit him..So the chef next to him said My name is Demitrio. I just started laughing. So our chef name was demitrio. We were laughing so much the sushi chef Brian joined in. It was great. The yellowtail was my favorite. It was buttery and it melt slowly in your mouth. My partner in crime wants sushi with spicy tuna but to our surprise they didn't have such a thing in the menu. So we asked our chef to make us something, and boy did he do such a great job. He sliced seared tuna as if it was tofu, he slapped the spicy tuna on the roll along with some veggies and sauces. The dish was created nicely, too good to be eaten. It was one of our favorite dishes. It is true, come to Arigato to try the different dishes don't get something regular like the dragon roll. WTH is that? You can get that anywhere. I've took pictures of the rolls, so feel free to check it out!! O, and I have a picture of our chefs. The meal with great conversation made our night special. Try to sit at the bar, all the chefs are really friendly and fun to talk to. This place is always crowded, but we came just in time to have two seats available at the bar. O, there was some downfall at the beginning such as our waitress. She spilled hot tea on my lap and she never came back to refill our drinks. It was horrible service on her part, but luckily for us our chef asked someone to refill our drinks. YEAH for demitrio. This place is a must try, it can get a lil pricey depending on your appetite. Overall if you come to SB to visit, its a must to go there. Seriously I can't wait till I visit again. Until next time Brian and Demitrio.

text: I live around the corner from this gem, and I have to say that this library is really an amazing space. Granted, the lighting is very poor inside and it's a hot spot for the homeless and mentally impaired. I say that in this instance, creepiness is directly proportional to character. I don't mind how dark it is because that's how it's always been. Sure, there are hundreds of thousands of books, newsreels, photographs, videos, and so on. There better be; this is the main branch. A friend of mine who works there told me that once someone lived on the 4th floor as a hideaway for a couple days before being discovered. The library's bathrooms have long functioned as bathing facilities for folks who might not have anywhere else to go. Supposedly there are attendants now since a poor little girl was attacked at the Independence Branch, but you definitely still want to keep your wits about you in the basement lavatories. Most of the librarians are charmingly librarianish. When I visit, I can usually spot at least two individuals who have been working here as long as I can remember. The folks who work the circulation desks in the Popular section, however, need to enroll in How to Be a Nice, Normal Human Being 101. And then 201 after that. Excellent physical features: the dinosaur prints leading to the children's section. The view on the 4th floor. The little insets next to the first flight of steps--these slanted surfaces have served my classmates well as slides during field trips, although I can't condone slamming one's feet into the wall at the bottom like we did... and totally f*cked up that one piece of wall on the left. That wasn't cool. Technological updates: no more paper cards in the back of books for loan :( Now they scan barcodes and give you a neat paper receipt, which you will inevitably lose within 24 hours of getting home. That's ok because you can access your library account ONLINE. Snazzy. They have also computerized the system for signing up for computer time. You get 60 minutes and after that, compy kicks you off. This saves the librarians from dealing with unstable individuals who in the past have not been pleased about having to get off compy, BUT it also means that you can only use compy for one 60 minute period per day. That kind of stinks, but you may be able to get more time if no one else has signed up for a time slot. Newest development: free wireless. Head to the social sci/edu/business sections on floor 2 for strongest signal. All in all, come visit! Where else can you read/surf the 'net/touch things all day without having to buy something or do some work?
label: POS

text: Recently, a friend and I decided to take a short hiatus from binge drinking. With Leila Cafe's strict "Don't BYOB" policy, it seemed like the perfect spot to nurture our newfound sobriety. You're basically on a first name basis with everyone after 5 minutes. We started off the meal with a hummus plate. The hummus was really flavorful and some of the best I've had in the city. It had a little bit too much salt, but oddly the hummus that came with our platters did not. My friend and I both had shawarma. I've had gyro and shawarma platters all over Philly but this was by far he best. The meat was really tender. Many times I find that the shaved lamb can be especially tough, which is why I usually lean toward souvlaki platters at other restaurants, but this was perfect. It came with a side of hummus, the traditional tomato/cucumber chutney and of course rice. Everything had a distinctive flavor which made it a pleasure to mix stuff together. We finished off the meal with a hookah of golden apple flavored tobacco. The location really lends itself to relax and people watch while you enjoy the hookah. You can focus on the hipsters at the Last Drop or the occasional freakshow that stumbles out of Dirty Frank's. We spent about an hour just hanging out and smoking, but they never tried to push us out. I live in the Washington Square West and this is a very welcomed addition to the neighborhood.

text: Well, I've ridden the system here for more than ten years, and I have to say, it's bad, but it's not quite horrible. The building here has a small museum, interesting for the kids. Mostly administrative and a few places to get coffee or sit down in. Yes, certain lines are overcrowded, it can be dangerous depending on which line you're on, there's always construction, and timing can be very horrendous. The regional rail lines usually have the best of it, with plenty of service, a mix of several trains and while sometimes delayed, most stations have the clocks up that tell you about how long you'll be waiting (or will announce delays). The trolley/subways are a bit dirty, although they did replace many of the cars on the blue line this decade, and it's a simple, relatively smooth system. The trolleys themselves are dangerous to pedestrians and other traffic, but all people need to be more aware of their surroundings, too. The bus system varies - Center City service is generally pretty smooth, but as you get outwards into the areas of the city beyond the little rectangle of Center City, the service drops downwards... suburbia is serviced by a few lines, like any other large metropolis, split into zones and while payment can be a bit confusing, it's not horrible. I still think the entire system could do without tokens, though. It's time to go the plastic card route of the MTA or almost any other system. They already do it for monthly passes. Stop taking money at all at the tellers and just adjust the machines to accept change. Make sure stops have a working method to enter the transport, too. And while the underground walking corridor is nice from 15th to 11th, clean it out frequently (power wash the corridor with a lot of water is my suggestion), and keep a patrol or two around each side, it scares some people (although you can just as easily walk above ground).
label: NEG

text: Located on Banks Street in Mid City (just a couple of blocks up from Jesuit High), you know Crescent Pie and Sausage is in the neighborhood as soon as you get out of the car. The smells from the grill hit your nose and draw you in like a siren's call. I'm not going to go into any more details on the food at Crescent Pie and Sausage, though. The service I received was so bad that talking about the food might convey the impression that it mitigates the way I was treated by the front-of-the-house staff. I arrived at Crescent Pie and Sausage about 1:15pm. They were pretty busy. I usually try to make my way to the bar when I'm a single; no need to take up a 2-top, and usually bartenders make for good conversation. Alas, the bar was full, so I stood, not sure if this was a wait-to-be-seated or a seat-yourself place. Crescent Pie and Sausage isn't very big, so it could go either way. There were two servers, one guy, one gal. They both kept walking past me, without as much as a 'hello.' Now, I know places get busy, but when you've got this big fat guy standing in your doorway, he's pretty hard not to notice. After the male server walked past me to check on the five-top on the patio, I figured maybe it's a seat-yourself place. I sat at a 2-top for a few minutes, watching the activity around me, trying to catch the eye of one or the other of the servers. I watched a guy come from out of the kitchen and bus the 4-top in front of me, I was wondering if I was invisible. The gal server actually bumped my knee as she passed between my table and the one to my left. She apologized politely, then proceeded to head to the bar, still not even noticing that I'm just sitting there. As the clock on my phone went from 1:29pm to 1:34pm, I was answering e-mails and such, still trying to catch the eye of someone on the staff. When the male server sat two people at the now-bussed 4-top and brought them menus, I asked him if he could bring me one as well. He said, "did someone seat you or did you seat yourself?" I replied that I waited at the door for a bit, then seated myself after he had passed by me on his way to the patio. He brought me a menu and cleared the table. When he came back to wipe the table off, I ordered a sandwich and an iced tea. By this point, I think they realized I wasn't a very happy camper, because after my Crescent Pie and Sausage sandwich came out, someone came from the back to ask if I was doing OK. I nodded and said I was allright. I finished the meal, and the female server brought me the check. I left $14 for a $11.50 tab, and one of my "mini-moo" @YatPundit cards. I probably wouldn't have written this Crescent Pie and Sausage article had it not been for the tweet I noticed at the coffee shop a bit later which said: "I had the *ahem* pleasure of serving @yatpundit at work today. I don't think he's ever been to a busy New Orleans restaurant." OK, ya know, I realize that a $2.50 tip isn't all that much, but it was only a $11.50 tab. Still, it's 20% of the bill, and that's the conventional wisdom for a lunch tip. Maybe this guy's a part-owner of the place or some such. I hope so, because then I'd feel no remorse about calling this behavior out in such a public place. Still, you don't treat people as poorly as Crescent Pie and Sausage did me, then insult them on Twitter after the meal. It'll be a while before I give Crescent Pie and Sausage another shot.
label: NEG

text: I moved downtown over a year ago, and I've been waiting anxiously for a full-service grocery store to open here. I'm happy to say that I'm thrilled with what we got. For this review, I won't take into account the demolition controversy and the small coffee shops and eateries that have closed because their business has been going to Culinaria instead. I'm strictly going to focus on what's in the store. I'm very pleased with Culinaria's stock. The produce is fresh, and there are enough varieties of staple garden goods to meet most people's needs. Moving to the frozen foods, Culinaria carries everything you'd expect -- pizzas, tv dinners, veggies, even those weird PB&J sandwiches without the crusts. Personally, I'm happy that they carry Kashi frozen meals at great prices. I do wish they'd carry Gardenburger varieties, though -- Morningstar doesn't do it for me. The refrigerated/dairy shelves meet my needs well enough. They don't carry my brand of yogurt (Dannon naturals), so I'll have to continue buying that at Dierberg's. There's plenty of shredded cheese and an ok selection of butter. Juices could be beefed up a bit more. Milk (white, chocolate, organic) is great, and there are plenty of dips and sour creams. Dry goods like rice, pasta, etc. are well priced and there are plenty of brands. I'm pleased with how many varieties of Nature's Valley granola bars Culinaria carries. Applesauce and apple juice often are on sale. As for the pet section, I wish Culinaria would carry more natural cat litters and foods. I'll still get most of my items at PetSmart. However, it's nice to have a store just a few blocks away where I can pick up litter or food if I haven't been to PS in a while. Moreover, even though it's not my preferred litter, Tidy Cats often is on sale at Culinaria for about $5 for the giant "Indoor Spaces" jug -- I definitely appreciate that. I haven't made much use yet of the health/medical or school supplies sections yet. I also can't speak about meat or seafood, as I don't eat those items. However, I do like the number of cheeses Culinaria has for the store's size. I also like the sandwiches I get from the deli. In the bakery, I ordered a cake for a coworker's birthday, and everyone in the office loved it. Even better, I walked in at 7 a.m. to pick it up on my way to the Metrolink station. For those doubters, yes, a scant few products have been marked up slightly to make up for this small store. However, most items are the same prices as "regular" Schnucks stores. Sales are frequent, and that's why Culinaria is my go-to store for salad items, Kashi frozen meals, frozen vegetables and granola bars. The checkout line is speedy, as it's set up like a banker's line. The cashiers are fast and friendly -- a bit chatty like cashiers at Trader Joe's. They encourage reusable bag use and don't bat an eye when I come in with three reusable bags and my shopping trolley. I love having a full-service grocery store just a few blocks away from my home and preferred Metrolink station!

text: Tavern on Broad is not in my regular rotation, though the location is convenient for the lunchtime and after-work crowds. Some folks might find the forty-odd televisions blaring sports and news entertaining, but for our small party just looking to drink and catch up, it was overwhelming; like crawling inside one of the giant screens from Blade Runner and trying to make small talk. We were the guests of a friend who had won a "free happy hour", but this translated roughly into the same happy hour specials that everyone else in the bar was already enjoying. They're not bad- half off most drinks and appetizers. The menu is already decently-priced for Center City, most sandwiches and sides coming in at $6-16. Their sliders were cute and nicely presented; the chicken sliders had a nice smoky taste, and the beef sliders with bacon and cheddar were hearty and not greasy. Their onion rings were a particular favorite- flaky and a little salty, not pre-frozen but batter-dipped and crisp, with a spicy chili-ranch dip on the side. Their mussels were tasty and abundant, with toasted bread and a white wine sauce. Nice! Unfortunately, after enjoying a pretty decent meal, we were informed that about half of the things we'd ordered were not half price after all. The waitress was quick to adjust the bill after we objected, but having to object because the "half-off" policy is clear as mud? Not fun. The beer list was decent, if not inspired, and most things were half-price. The mixed drinks, though, were ridiculous; beyond watered-down. Two different drinks arrived, both consisting more or less of unsweetened iced tea that had been allowed to glance longingly at a bottle of liquor before being brought out to us. We sent them back and got beer instead, but at check time again noticed that the returned drinks appeared on the bill. This time we shrugged and cut our losses, figuring we wouldn't be back. I have to give props to our waitress, who was polite, friendly, and quick to resolve issues. Overall, it's probably a nice spot to grab lunch with co-workers, but if you're looking to do some serious eating and drinking and talking with friends, this might not be the place.
label: NEG

text: There's something about coffee shops that are enticing and endearing. I don't NEED coffee, but I do enjoy a really good cup. They seem to be tough to come by unless you go to La Colombe or this place. The coffee is fresh and strong and served super-fast. The decor is cozy and dark with warm woods and earth tones (bull-shit, bull-shit) etc. A really comfortable place. Maybe too comfortable....and here's my rub against coffee shops. In other countries, most notably in Europe, people go to cafes to sip coffee, read the paper and talk with their friends. They spend hours and there's no rush. I love that. Here, with most coffee shops, there is also no rush....but everyone is WORKING. Good God people...please don't be attached to your computer, I-phone, I-pod 24/7. It depresses the hell out of me. I want to go to a coffee shop and feel the vibrancy of conversation and the pulse of the community. Today, at Chestnut Hill Coffee Company, everyone upstairs and downstairs, save for me and one elderly couple, were on their computers. Okay, it's cool to work in a coffee shop and be productive, but man, it bums me out. Technology was supposed to give us more free time; it's just forced us to be very very productive, every second of the day. Okay, rant over. Bottom line...go there for the great coffee and bring your own great conversation. Otherwise, you'll see me seething in the corner over my Hot Toddy.

text: I got a cat tattooed above my elbow by Neal about two years ago. It was small and relatively simple, and, at the time, I was glad he was the one to do it because he had a decent portfolio with a lot of small pieces featured. It must have been an off-day, though, because I am tremendously disappointed with the quality of the work done. The outline width throughout the piece is inconsistent, and the lines not crisp, but bleedy. Furthermore, one of the eyes is noticeably larger than the other. I understand that tattooing is not a precise operation and personal touch is something that I can appreciate in any commissioned work of art, but this was just poorly executed. The atmosphere of the shop was pleasant, the environment sanitary and the people friendly, but I can't overcome the dissatisfaction of my messy looking tattoo.

A carpet patterned after a 7-year-old's bedspread!) it is quite simply the ne plus ultra of casino tackiness/awesomeness. I love it, and my friends are rarely disappointed. To then take them to Oceano, with its funky sea decor and overwhelming blue hue would be the cherry on top of that sundae. Unfortunately, the fish entrees ain't that great (they were a bit dry and flavorless both times I've gone) so I can't see going back. text: I've lurked Yelp for awhile, but my experience tonight at Black Thorn has prompted me to finally write a review. I figured restaurant-goers would want to know about my abysmal encounter with one of the employees (possibly a shift manager, I'm not sure). I took my dad from out of town to the Black Thorn tonight. I just moved into the TGS neighborhood, the place is only a couple blocks from me, and had heard great things about their pizza. As everyone else said, the place is a gritty dive, and I enjoyed that aspect of it. The pizza itself, after waiting an hour and a half for it (which I didn't mind, we had a good time in the interim), tasted great. The problem was that it wasn't, after all that waiting, what we ordered. My dad had ordered a supreme; was very clear - "I want everything on it - no, not tomatoes, anchovies and artichokes, but everything else." When it came out, they called up "Mike F" (we even had our initial behind it, so it was very clearly meant for us) and it looked like sausage. I was wary, but having never had deep dish before, we thought maybe the rest of the ingredients were inside. Poked at it, took a few bites. Nope, definitely just sausage. Someone must have put the wrong order in. We weren't going to wait ANOTHER hour and a half for them to remake it, so we went ahead and ate it. It *was* delicious. But not what we ordered, or paid for. I took a piece up to the man behind the bar that took my order to make sure it was sausage and calmly explain what happened, and see if we could just get the extra $4 difference back. Our exchange went a little something like this: Him: "You ate it?! You ate someone else's pie!" Me: "It's under Mike F, you gave this to us. I didn't know if it was supreme in the deep dish." Him: "God damn it! What were you thinking?!" then screaming at the bar, pissed off: "Is there a Mike F at the bar? Because if so, this girl ate your pizza." The people at the bar looked shocked and embarassed for me; some nervously giggled, some gave me dirty looks. I was MORTIFIED. I said, "No, Mike F is us! And this is what you gave us!" He's pacing, mumbling things, yelling at the other employees about this awful travesty I committed, flailing his arms about and making a big scene, and told me: "You should have brought it back!" Me, raising my voice now: "I didn't want to wait another hour for you to cook another one!" Him, yelling back: "You wouldn't have had to...god damn it! Shit. YOU DON'T JUST EAT SOMEONE ELSE'S PIZZA!" I said, "You know what, forget it" and stormed off to my table while he's yelling at me to "come back and deal with this." I'm so shocked and appalled I'm in tears. I'm at my table shaking in anger. I've lost my appetite. Another employee who witnessed the exchange comes over and apologizes on his behalf, saying, "He gets like that" offered to buy us a beer or something, and then said she'd talk to him and see what she could do. Turned out that he wrote "sausage" on the order....but still charged us the extra $4 for a supreme. So HE made the exact mistake I suspected. It wasn't someone else's pizza, it was ours. HE fucked up, and I WOULD have had to wait another hour for the right one. Yet he assumed I was a selfish fuck-up and instigated a screaming match at the bar as he accused me of stealing someone else's pizza. He comes over a few minutes later (obviously because the girl went back and told him he's got damage control to do) and his "apology" was "Sorry for getting like that, but I'm really busy." Nice excuse (and they weren't even all that busy. The place was only half full on a Saturday night. Even then....there's no excuse!). He said he'd give us the $4 back. He also asked my dad how he paid for the pizza. "Oh, you paid cash? SWEET. Because if you paid by card it would have been this big pain in the ass to refund you the money on the card." Wow, how many excuses does this guy have? If we paid by card, would he have caused yet another dramatic shit storm over it? The girl comes back over to see what he did, and she says, "Uhhh he really should comp you the whole pizza. But I'm not the boss, he is." (My dad asked if he was the owner and she said no, so that's my thinking in that he's a shift manager) He comes back over a few minutes later and comps us the whole thing (again, I think he was nudged to do so). Just for that I will come back and purchase something as soon as have some savings. 29 Armstrong is not really packed with furniture - there are only several floor models just to give shoppers a general idea of what is in catalogs. On display, there are couches, armchairs, nightstands, shelving units and carpets. Everything is modern, trendy, and of best quality. Most of the furniture sold by 29 Armstong is made in Canada, constructed of solid wood and looks really sturdy. text: You have to go all the way past the strip of restaurants and bars and shops on South Grand and then a bit of a way to get to Mama Pho. It is a bit different than other places, hard to describe, I would say less spiced but stronger meatier flavor. There is still a hint of star anise and cloves, but it is more subtle. text: an open letter to the owners of the corner bar and grille: Dear Corner Bar and Grille Proprietor: Congratulations, it's finally been done. I've written reviews on over 130 restaurants, hotels, etc. in multiple states and many cities over the past year and I've never given any business one star. I've left restaurants before the food arrived because of service, been promised a suite and ended up in a closet in hotels and still have found some redeeming quality to give a location at least two stars. If you look at my reviews I think most objective observers would say I'm fair. First, I need to place much of the blame for visiting your location on myself. I did the proper due diligence and was given great info by NOLA yelpers, nevertheless I found myself with my friends half drunk on our first day in NOLA in Jackson Square and in serious need of sustanance quickly before one of us lost our balance. Oh yeah, let me also say I just called the rivers edge to ask them the location of your bar and also your restaurant, because I couldn't believe that anyone could give you more than one star and was confused when I read the other reviews. I spoke with someone a few minutes ago who did indeed confirm that this is the right corner bar that deserves my displeasure. We walk in and are greeted pretty angrily by an italian fella who without smiling says something to the effect before we even speak to him, you better be buying something and not coming to use the bathrooms. We let him know we are here to eat and drink and be marry and he can reserve his charm for another wary traveler. One other lovely aspect I find is that the ice appears grimy and dirty, needless to say I only have about one sip. We probably would have left then, but had already placed the order. Ron and Jason get the "philly cheese steaks" which have the similiar condition with respect to bun and veggies, but these are piled high with a grayish soft material that if I am to believe the waitress is meat of some kind. This provided more than a bit of a distraction for even the most hardcore and dedicated partier. In closing, thank you for giving me a reason to provide one star to a business and I hope you are forced to eat this food for the rest of your lives. P.S. one quick note of another sign of the apocolypse is that the next day we are walking by and there is actually a line outside to get into this place. Yes my friends we definitely need much more thinnning of the herd.

text: Some suburban shopping centers are chock full of C-list chains that boast dumb names and list franchising information as a featured link on their websites. Instead of headliners like Starbucks, you get It's a Grind! Coffeehouse. Instead of Jamba Juice, you get Blenders in the Grass. By my old workplace, you could find a Tacos del Mar, Great Wraps, and Pot Belly Deli in the same strip mall, all fighting for their share of the lazy and desperate lunchtime crowd. The food court area of the Goleta Marketplace fits right into this trap, so you might justifiably step into Gina's Pizza with some trepidation. But don't let the pictures of Italy and a bevy of healthy houseplants trick you into letting your guard down, man! This pizza is flat-out bad. It hurt my feelings. The crust is thick and hard, presumably pre-made off-site, and clearly inferior to if they had put the toppings onto French bread or a Boboli. The cheese is rubbery and not particularly flavorful, and though I'd like to provide an assessment of the sauce, there was not much sauce to speak of on my pie. Places you can find better pizza: *Any major or somewhat major city in the United States or Canada, except Pittsburgh *Bars *Stadiums and arenas *Little Caesar's at the Luxor Hotel and Casino *From those kids that sell mini frozen pizzas as a fundraiser for their t-ball team *Your microwave *Your friend's microwave *On English muffins *The Costco food court *Gina's Pizza if you're drunk Not to mention that the girl at the counter thought it would be okay to casually toss my receipt in my direction instead of handing it to me. I'm no Miss Manners, but that was bullshit. If they had some pizza worth eating, that would be one thing, but they don't have pizza that's worth eating. Honestly, if you live within 0.2 miles and you're desperate for somewhere to get a beer and watch a game, I understand. Otherwise, do yourself a service and pick up a DiGiorno.

They go through great trouble to clean that water before releasing it into public streams...and when it is released, it is water, and nothing else! So, it's perfectly fine to swim in, and you can even catch & eat fish from it. text: I too came here having read many positive reviews of this charming-looking restaurant, and the inconspicuous facade appealed to me. It was a Sunday night, for the tasting menu. As is common in my Philadelphian dining experiences, things started off alright: in this case, with imported butter that has been mentioned elsewhere. The bread was unremarkable. Next came a shrimp bisque that tasted good, but was oddly and inappropriately spicy, and reminiscent of premature acid reflux (the burn, not the flavor, which was good). Next, the small course for two of us was seared fois gras. I enjoyed this and it was executed well, but accompanied by a rather unripe and unflavorful pear, and spiced (perhaps pumpkin) bread that didn't help things much. The fois gras itself was also prone to connective tissue in it which made the texture imperfect. But it lacked the bloody undertones that fois gras sometimes has. The main course I chose was effectively bone marrow stuffing, as it was bread and vegetables chopped up and stuffed into a large bone. It was rich, and had an unpleasant background flavor which I guess I must attribute to the melted marrow... it was rather organ-like in flavor. To one side of this were small potatoes that really needed salt and a small salad that had far too much, so together that worked out well. Finally, dessert consisted of goat milk creme caramel and a chocolate trio, which was a sort of brownie with jam, ice cream and a mousse. The goat milk caramel was very plain, though the caramel was quite dark, successfully masking the rank flavor that goat milk usually possesses. However, the creme caramel itself was quite underwhelming: not particularly smooth or overcooked, it was very average. The chocolate trio was far below average, however, with the chocolate ice cream firmly at the top, followed by a very thick and grainy mousse and last an uncertain brownie (no one could tell what it was supposed to have tasted like, but surely not what it actually did..) with strawberry jam on top. It was our mistake not to have tried the sorbet, which was made elsewhere. All this was topped off by really, very hard and chewy coconut macaroons. Maybe to teethe. Anyhow, for $45 this might be worth it, but certain parts were just not enjoyable.

text: An absolutely beautiful three story mansion where respectable ladies and gentlemen used to meet in the parlor before sitting down to dine on a fabulous meal and to share an eloquent dining experience. This Victorian mansion was built in 1895 and restoration began in 2000, Bella Tori, which means beautiful tower, opened it's door in 2005. This massive mansion has sixteen gables and four fireplaces! Entering from the wrap around porch, I felt naked without my parasol, corset and full long dress, as you immediately feel transported back in time it reminds you to be a lady and what it was like to relax, Gone With The Wind immediately came to mind. I pictured proper gentlemen smoking cigars and drinking brandy from snifters in the library while women gossiped and sipped tea in the parlor. From the high vaulted ceilings, to the beautiful molding, heavy drapes which are pulled back to view the very large and long framed windows, sconces hang on the walls and beautiful fireplaces are ready to light for that romantic dinner for two. The plush carpets and stairways stay true to maintaining the original era of the mansion. We dined here for Easter brunch and had to change our reservation time They were fully booked for the hour that we chose to dine and we were asked if we minded sitting on the deck, it was a gorgeous sunny day and even though I need to experience the ambiance of dining in the library or the beautiful master bedroom, we decided this would be delightful and away from all the hustle and bustle that dining out today brings. There were only four tables with umbrellas to shelter out the sun and we had our pick of three as there was only one other couple there when we arrived. My own problem with this delightful setting was the omelet station was set up there and soon the traffic in and out the door began as the lines formed. It is unbelievable how folks will stand and glare at you and what you are eating, glaring back let them know they needed to revert their attention. Hubby and I both noticed how the eggs were not cracked to make the omelets and how the ingredients were not kept chilled or on ice. The dessert station was set up inside the deck doors and the chocolate was melting and when trying to slice a piece of cake it stuck to the spatula. There was no where to set your plate down so this all had to be done with one hand which turned your slice into a mess and left half in a glob sticking to the spatula. The large antipasto table held a spring leek and potato soup which was okay, I'm hoping it was the potatoes which made it the wonderful consistency it was because I detected a flour taste to the soup. The Caesar salad was crisp and the dressing was perfect. The table had a variety of cheeses, brie, camembert, bleu's, cheddars and pepper, the smoked whole whitefish was wonderful and I could have eaten the entire fish myself. Cold dressed noodles, a roasted vegetable salad was so good, cherry wood house smoked salmon which will bring me back to have more, fresh fruits, jumbo poached shrimp and Joanna crab claws. This is the first time I have had these crab claws which were fully cleaned of the outer shell and ready to eat and hubby and I are still talking about how awesome they were. This same table also had a nice assortment of homemade salads, bagels, crackers and muffins. Fresh carved pit ham and slow roasted stuffed leg of lamb, which was medium to medium well at best, was being served along with the omelets on deck. Inside the buffet tables held a multitude of chaffing dishes filled with delightful foods, braised short ribs which were very meaty, tender and moist, broiled New England cod soaking in a milk broth was tender and delicious, thick sliced bacon, sausage patties and turkey bacon. To accompany these meats and fish they had pasta with a marinara and homemade meatballs, thinly sliced potatoes layered thick which tasted like an amazing cross between an au gratin and scalloped potato dish, ginger glazed baby carrots, homemade cheese blintzes with homemade strawberry preserves which were beyond heaven and oh Bella, Bella, the eggs Bella will stay etched in my memory forever. Beautifully poached eggs served on a thin sliced Canadian bacon and a homemade hash brown patty makes me wish that you were open for breakfast everyday. They do not skimp on anything, detail is their middle name. I can not wait to return for a relaxing sit down dinner. Be sure to tour this gorgeous mansion, any employee is eager to answer questions. They are open Tuesday through Sunday for dinner from 5:00 until 9:00 and brunch on Sundays from 11:00 until 2:00. It's an affordable luxury!

text: I love this place. It's what the Loveless Cafe strives but fails to be. I visit both the Franklin location and the Leiper's Fork location regularly, and each offers its own charms. The Franklin location is more of a proper restaurant, still laid back but more spruced up. It has a bar and more of a funky decor. The waitstaff are AWESOME. Super sweet, friendly, and attentive. I've only been here for breakfast and lunch, although I do want to come by for the nighttime music performances and try dinner sometime too. Breakfast is my favorite here. I love omelettes, and Puckett's has one of the best veggie omelettes I've ever had, chock full of mushrooms, spinach, and cheese. They also have amongst the best biscuits I've tasted, and their giant cinnamon rolls are amazing. I'm actually not a fan of the buffet, and prefer to do one of the omelettes or an eggs/sausage/biscuit combo. As for lunch, they have hand-patted burgers cooked to order which are juicy, thick, and delicious. Way better than the burgers at Five Guys, which I find overrated. Their barbeque and chicken are great too, although not as distinctively fantastic as their burgers. Puckett's also has the best sweet potato fries I've ever tasted in my entire life--they are incredible! I also cannot rave enough about their cobblers and pies, especially their peach cobbler, which is spectacular. Great down-home food, awesome service, charming ambiance, what more can one ask for? There can be a bit of a long wait on Saturdays and Sundays for brunch but it's always been worth it for me. As for disgruntled vegetarians who can't stand to acknowledge the existence of meat...the menu is on the door. This is obviously not the place for you, it's a typical Southern meat-and-three place, though with a broader menu that most. You will smell meat if you go inside. Judging an entire restaurant's menu based on its veggie burger alone is a bit harsh, methinks.

It looked like the tire had been slashed between the treads. Apparently the folks at this shop sold me someone else's old dead tire, without even taking the time to check it or patch it. We ordered the pork half ribs and the seafood enchiladas with the cheese and salsa sauce as a n appetizer. Cheese and salsa dipping sauce: Not what I was expecting. The cheese tastes of a cheaper quality then Velveeta? Slightly sour, slightly plastic... if they change their cheese product-- great! Chips: A good standard chip however they need to make sure they don't mix the stale with the new-- we can taste the difference... The pork half rack: A thick well sauced slab of pork ribs served on crispy onions with a corn on the cob as well as black beans. I would recommend them to at least bake their ribs and then paint on the sauce in the last 10 minutes so it cooks and caramelizes-- this tasted as if it was spooned on after coming out of a hot water pan.... The corn? ugh-- old, very old. There were brown mushy kernels mixed in with the yellow-- and the corn cob was drying out-- when preparing to offer fresh corn, please ensure and keep your corn in a warm bath so it wont dry out... and check its age before you serve! The crispy onion strings: they came served under the huge slab of pork and when found, no longer were crispy but a mushy greasy memory of what could have been.. please serve those on the side so they can be experienced in their full glory... and a little salt would help too.... The black beans: black beans should be cooked with a few cloves of garlic and a lot of white onion and salted to perfection to truly bring out their flavor... these were just beans and water.... The seafood enchilada: After seeing the chef make them for Sam Shad , I thought they were going to be a spectacular cousin of what the chef used to make in Andeoti's of Harrah's. Wow, no way. barely any crab or lobster, the seafood is not fresh-- freshness is king for a good flavor to last the entire meal-- fresh garlic sautéed with the seafood in olive oil then mixed with the other ingredients would slap some life into this creation. The way he prepared it on TV was divine- his chefs need to be retrained and not skimp on the ingredients. Beans and rice were of course totally bland-- making a authentic Mex rice from a good chicken stock and the normal medley of ingredients will do wonders for your plates... and dont serve refried can beans--- make a good pot of pinto beans and they last for 5 days...... But then again folks I have worked and tasted the best food out there and also been served the absolute most authentic home cooked Mexican food and Mom will always do better then food commercialized.... I will not be coming back, because I have had and worked with better food then this....

text: The idea of snack bar is a brilliant one. It offers creative, competitively priced dishes to an eclectic center-city crowd. I have long been meaning to go, and last night I finally made it there. The restaurant itself complements the concept of the food. Small, edgy and different to almost anything in town. Its red walls and simple layout give it an endearing warmth. Our servers were helpful (if not a little forgetful) but perhaps less informed than in places like Tria. We started with the Poached Shrimp, Chicken Liver Pate, Caprese Salad, Foie Gras with Scallop and Potato Pierogies. The Shrimp and Liver were both great dishes. The shrimp combo was particularly well conceived as the melon and cucumber provided a refreshing taste. The caprese is fine but lacks creativity on a generally adventurous menu. The foie gras however was something of a disappointment. Served atop a heavily salted slice of toasted baguette, it had a weak flavor profile and texture. The scallop did nothing to complement the dish other than to provide an interesting visual but was in fact a delicious scallop, which should have stood alone in it own dish. The entrees on the table included lamb spareribs, red snapper, a stuffed chicken breast and a New York strip. Again, over seasoning was a big problem. It led me to believe that Snackbar is trying to hide lower quality ingredients behind a barrage of salt - and it fails. The spare ribs were small and greasy, and made it very obvious why I'd never seen lamb spareribs before. The snapper was decent but slightly overcooked and was definitely the most exciting plate on the table. The chicken breast is a well executed dish and was probably the winning plate, although with such interesting creations on the table, its lamentable that this is the case. Snackbar is on the right track. If they took more care in the crafting of their dishes to bring out the advertised flavors, and invested more in the quality of ingredients, it could be sublime.

text: Trust me, I know that Uhaul normally sucks if you are having a high stress/high volume move and need some dedicated customer service. Really, I know. I actually heart 2 of the staffers on 13th and Vine now, but they aren't exactly warm/relaxed/friendly upon first meeting them. They deal with lots of crap, and it probably takes a toll. So if you're a first timer, hit South Philly. - this location also has exponentially more of everything-boxes, dollies, trucks, storage units, staffers. More is good. - if you have any way to do your move on a weekday that isn't toward the beginning or end of the month, you should be ok as far as avoiding chaos & angry people at Uhaul. They have a peak period; avoid it. If you can't, I'd recommend *not using Uhaul at all* to save your sanity. I cannot explain how surprised I was to actually have a pleasant experience at Uhaul this time around, but it's pretty cool to be able to recommend them--especially since I hated the company before! I'm hesitant to give 4 stars because I know my experience is unusual, but maybe it's just all about avoiding the peak period & being positive with the staff to create good energy. text: This family run pizza joint reminds me of my childhood - you know, back in the 90's when your mom and dad would take the whole family out for pizza on a Friday night as a special treat. They have arcade games, little machines that dispense candy for a quarter, big screen televisions and the best pizza I've had in a long time. Oh, and they serve beer and wine ;) We ordered: 1) a hand tossed canadian bacon, pineapple and jalapeno pizza - yes, salty, sweet and spicy (my fav combination!). 2) a deep dish Gramboli's Special... pepperoni, sausage, green pepper and onions, yum :) and the all important 3) bread sticks with cheese sauce. All who know me, know that cheese sauce features high on my list of desirable foods. I can't pass it up on any menu offering. Pizza is an American favorite - it's hard to get it wrong. But Gramboli's pizza isn't just your typical pizza, their crust is freakin' fabulous. I'm not sure what they do to make it so dang good... the deep dish is well, deep. But also hearty, moist (without being doughy) and delicious. Deep dish is my husbands favorite... The hand tossed is super light (i.e. airy), flavorful and my favorite. The best part is their pizza sauce though... I'm not sure what they add to it, cinnamon? Who knows... but it beats the socks off the competition. We've tried to replicate it at home, but to no avail. All in all, get to Gramboli's and try their pizza. Whether you are a hand-tossed or deep dish type, you'll love it. And don't forget the breadsticks. They rock. Tip: Snag a coupon from their website before you go, and get the bread sticks for free.

text: My wife and I stopped there for an early dinner on 7/8/2010 after dropping my son off for his first quarter at AIPH. Not being a beer person like I am, she was a bit hesitant at going there. She ended up having a few glasses of wine from their short winelist, while I had a few of the Belgian specialty brews a Cantillion kriek and an oak aged sour Petrus both were quite good. The brew list is impressive, heavy on the Belgian styles (the main reason I wanted to try the place), but there are quite a few selections from other parts of the world (around 200 varieties overall). Overall the brew selection is slanted towards the higher alcohol styles. The food - We had the Charcouterie Platter as a starter. The rabbit terrine was wonderful as well as the grilled sausages and the mix of Belgian and English cheeses. The coarse mustard included on the platter was one of the best that we have ever had. She had a small pot of the Ghent style mussels (leeks, bleu cheese and bacon in a DuPont Saison) while I had the grilled duck salad. She said that the mussels were great (I can't eat them, as I sometimes become violently ill while eating mussels - something to do with whatever they were feeding on rather than the mussles themselves, so I avoid eating them altogether). I had a vew of the pomme frites that were served with the mussels, and was not impressed with them. The cut of the potatoes was all wrong, limp skinny shoestrings rather than thick cut & chunky, the included burbon mayo was quite good however. The duck salad included a perfectly cooked half breast, and a nice slice of fresh goat cheese but the mesclun green salad was rather average. The included spiced walnuts were good, but nothing to shout about. When I get back there again, I will probably just have a burger. Overall, I would give it a 6/5 (yes I know the scale only goes to 5 but the list was well above average) for the beer and a 3/5 for the food - call it a 4 overall.

text: Honestly, there's nothing much better during St. Louis summers than a free outdoor festival. And by golly, Schlafly is the local King of outdoor festivals! I've planned my share of outdoor festivals and attended quite a few as a vendor as well as a regular attendee, and I have to give Schlafly props for doing it right. They are organized, easy to work with and take care of both their attendees and their vendors. There's never a freak out moment from the organizers (and I love that "no one is going to die if X doesn't happen" mentality), they think of all of the necessary details (i.e., ice water available to all, plenty of clean port-o-potties, shaded tents) and their staff is well-trained to deal with crowded situations. Oh, and their events are fun! Sometimes I dread having to work a table at certain events, but never with Schlafly! This weekend's Pork Steak Championship was a good time! It was hot and sticky outside, but the staff made sure we all had plenty of water (and beer) and were entertained. I don't eat too often at The Bottleworks but I love the fact that a majority of their menu items are made from locally grown food. Last night I tried their pulled pork sandwich and it comes topped high with coleslaw. Normally I'm not a slaw lover, but this hit the spot after a long afternoon in the sun. And of course it goes well with a Summer Lager... Still haven't tried their beer in a can, but I'm sure that'll happen before the end of the weekend :) Great local company, fun festivals, accommodating staff. Love 'em!

text: The fact it is a workers collective of sorts, serves cheap drinks, and occasionally has good live music can't make up for what I felt was an overall pretentious vibe in this place. The first few times there I thought it was kinda cool, but then it felt downright cold. The bartender mentioned below seemed friendly enough but his girlfriend who often filled in for him was a rude snob and I wasn't too in love with the clientele either. It seemed like being a working-class guy who didn't like dressing like a slob and not being an artist or being in with the anarchist/gutterpunk West Philly clique that I wasn't welcome there. Although I'm sure I could easily discuss punk or anarchism with any of them, it's kinda hard to get into a discourse on who the best Black Flag singer was or the relative merits of Proudhon or Bakunin when the guy sitting next to you won't say more than two words to you because you're wearing a nicely-pressed collared shirt and a close-cropped haircut. Guess I didn't conform well enough to their brand of nonconformism. Or their brand of anarchism for that matter, where squatting in a building, being a vegan and having a huge collection of Crass 7 inches apparently constitute better credentials than years of union activism. Mostly I was disappointed. It could be a cool place if it weren't for the pretentiousness and clique mentality. Gimme the Dahlak bar any day of the week-- better mix of people and a friendlier environment. And no, I'm not that Omar, though I have heard of him. I'm the original Omar-- that guy is merely an ersatz Omar impostor.

text: I do not recommend them at all. I used the property services for several years for a rental property that I have owned for more than 10 years. I have rented the house out the entire time and have never had a problem with a tenant or house until Unique Property Services became involved. I frequently had to call for my statements and the rent check. The property management company sometime just "forgot" to send them to me. Once, they were three months behind; not the tenant but the property management company. The deposits are not direct deposits where you can easily track. They are hand deposits at various times of the month, without any reference to unique property services so if they don't deposit the full rent you can't tell who the deposit was from or why it is less than it should be. I don't know if it is true, but it seemed they rented to people they knew because when the tenants didn't pay on time they didn't seem concerned. Occasionally they did collect late fees. After hurricane damage I was charged for work that wasn't done or done correctly. I had to get involved to deal directly with the vendors and send someone else to the property to inspect the damage. I was charged for tree trimming and upon inspection the tree wasn't cut at all. When the tenants moved out their deposit was returned except for a $65 cleaning fee. Where can you get the house cleaned for $65? You can't. The house was very dirty, the oven and refrigerator was gross and the carpet was stained in several areas and dirty all over. At some point the tenant had a leak and cut a whole in the wall to fix it. This hole went all the way to the exterior of the house. The property management company should have inspected all of this and should have taken it out of the tenant's deposit. This was not a case of a bad tenant, that is why you take a deposit and the tenants deposit would have covered all of these items. Instead, I had to arrange and pay for everything. This is why I think they had an alliance to the tenant. Either way, the job I hired the property management company to do was not done and you should not trust your property to this compan

What more can I say than if you like visiting old historical sites this is a must see even if it can be a little disturbing or depressing at times. Fun times with crazy Quakers.

text: Ever found a gem that you don't want to share with the rest of the world? That would be UAL. OMG OMG OMG. The lack of selection doesn't bother me because the discounts are so steep. I could imagine coming in here and walking out with nothing. However, I could also walk out with some fabulous designer pieces that were 90% off. Define designer? Prada. Manolo Blanik. Dolce & Gabbana. The bargains are so amazing that I rather walk out empty handed 9 out of 10 times just for that one time that I walk out knowing that I just got an amazing deal. Call it beginner's luck but I scored BIG TIME.

text: A few years ago upon my first solo plane experience, I was rather anxious and worried about coordinating everything all on my own, getting to the airport and juggling all of my belongings. I couldn't seem to find anyone who could drop me off at the airport when I needed, so I decided to try Fly Away. Now I'm glad that I did, and I can't imagine doing it any other way. I'm a Fly Away regular and always depend on them to take care of me, making an anxious flyer relaxed and at ease. They make it all very simple with the check-in, baggage handling and drop off at the airport. Upon returning, I've never had to wait more than a few minutes to be picked up, and best of all my car is ready and waiting for me when I get back to the Fly Away office. A few times they've had bottled water waiting for me, too. The staff are all very nice. The drivers are always very friendly and courteous. The prices are also cheaper than what the airport charges for parking, and you get a more special treatment than any airport shuttle staff has ever given.

The interior is spacious and service is quick. No outdoor seating or patio, but overall a good lunch spot.
