text: My husband and I ate there couple days ago. We found their menu at the hotel we stayed at. We are usually hesitant to go to places which aspire to serve fine dining and charge almost $30 a plate because we almost always get disappointed but we decided to give it a shot. My husband has been in fine dining business for some time now and can distinguish between a restaurant that serves top quality food and a restaurant that aspires to be high quality, charges more for their plates but in actuality has a long way to go to be considered a fine dining place. We both ordered appetizers: shrimp that I have to admit was cooked perfectly and ceviche that unfortunately was tasteless and blunt. Duck and risotto Entree was served with a super sweat cherry sauce, sooo sweat that I had to eat it with an assistance of a glass of water. Poisun Entree was served with two potatoes and couple small carrots...do you call that fine dining? Would you charge $26 for that? Not to mention that chicken was raw inside and we were informed by the waitress that this is how it suppose to be served and that their chef calls that a tenderizing method....my husband has never heard about the method by the way. Overall I think that the restaurant would be doing much better if they stopped calling themselves "fine dining" and they started charging $15 a plate....The quality of food and the creativity of Enrees equalls not more then $15 a plate.
label: NEG

text: I went here with about 5 or 6 friends to celebrate. I was the only woman in our group and we still can't tell if they had a better time, or if I did. There was a $20 cover, but it was worth it. If you don't want a dance, you could probably get away with bringing $40-to cover entry, a few sodas (it's all nude, so no alcohol), and tips for the servers who get your drinks and bring it you. I'll tell you from personal experience that not every strip club in this area does that. I was pleasantly impressed with the set up. It's pretty spacious with comfortable chairs from the stage area on back. Although smoking is allowed indoors, the layout is such that it's not overwhelming, unless you walk into it, or are next to the person smoking. The dance area isn't bad, either. They're velvet-y booths that are tall enough, to offer you enough privacy that the person next to you can't peep at the dance you're getting. Their website has current dance prices, but keep in mind there's a $5 entry fee to the private area each time you go back there. There was a pretty good selection of girls, although I wouldn't have minded seeing some bigger butts. I'm not complaining about what they had, though. Kennedy and Princess were my group's favorites. They were quite live and I liked the way Princess moved. I spent entirely too much money there, but definitely plan on going back a few more times. I'd recommend it to anyone planning a birthday celebration or bachelor/bachelorette party, or someone just looking to unwind.
label: POS

text: This place is so close to my house I had high hopes that it would be awesome Mexican food, and I would never have to get on the highway again (for mexican food...) I was extremely disappointed. This place has changed owners a lot since I've lived in my house, about 5 years, and I was never interested because it was always a bar, and I was guessing there was no food. As soon as I saw the new name on the sign I wanted to try it! We walked in, there were 8 other people there at 6pm. The inside looks like a bar, there are a few Mexican decorations, a frame or two with the flag on them, but I did not feel like I was sitting in Mexico like with some other restaurants. I was very impressed with the menus, they were very well made and I did not see any typos. I think my boyfriend was trying to stay positive, the service was okay. I was also not a huge fan of the chips, and the food (both of our entrees) were way too salty. I got a chicken chimichanga and it was chicken and chimichanga. I'm used to onions and sometimes peppers maybe beans inside the chimi, I think lack of any other ingredients is what made the chicken super dry. I was looking to the sauce to make the chicken not so dry and that's when I was attacked with salt. I will probably try this place again, like I said it is sooooo close to my house, but not with high hopes.
label: NEG

text: Do yourself a favor. DO NOT LIVE HERE. The buildings are old, dusty & dingy. My wife & I have lived here 11 months & totally regret it. There's an outline of dirt & grime where our front door hits the door frame from all the dust that floats around the halls. We decided to go ahead & rent anyways because of location. We regret it. Maintenance is slow & horrid. We moved in with 2 ill-functioning drawers in the kitchen & missing screens on the windows. We noted them on our move-in checklist & still don't have them fixed. We can't open the windows at night, because bugs are attracted to our lights and fly in. The coating of our bathtub started chipping/coming up in October. You could see metal for about a 1.5 foot diameter circle. When I called that in, I got the run around for a few weeks finally being told that they have to followup with the subcontractor that did that work. It was fixed last month -- took 5 months to fix it. I guess if i liked calling them every 3 days, it may have gotten fixed sooner, but 3/4 of the time you call maintenance, you will get voice mail. And don't expect a call back. We have had 9 hot water shutoffs since we've been here. 9 out of 11 months seems like a lot to me & only half the time do they notify you. Sometimes it's with a sign on the elevator (I don't use the elevator every day) & sometimes they're kind enough to send an email, other times you just don't get water. We pay extra for 2 reserved parking garage spaces. The garage is poorly lit & leaks when it rains. On decent storms, it floods the staircase we use to get to our building. When we first got our spaces, I went back in to see if they could give us spaces closer to our building entrance (it take 7-8 minutes to get to our spots from our front door). I'm told they can't move us. Really? I see your Excel spreadsheet with my name & my parking number? You can't just copy & paste? Thanks. So, I haven't bothered to complain to them that when it rains, there is a leak of dirty, slimy water that comes down on my car. Thx. When we first checked in, we were told that the first thing we have to do is put our garage stickers on our cars. They also took our car models, makes and license plate numbers. We gave them 4 cars' information, because we borrow cars from family to move things. A month after we moved in, our cars were TOWED from our reserved parking spaces. Neither had their little stickers, but one car was on file. DON'T THEY KNOW WHOSE RESERVED SPOT IT IS? You really can't look up the parking space owner's name & call us? The doorman calls up when I have a package, but you don't think you should call me when you're TOWING two of my cars?!?! I see cars ILLEGALLY parked outside in the community EVERY night. I also notice that every once in a while they will get a notice on them stating they may get towed. Why didn't management have the same consideration for tenants that are paying extra for garage parking? Of course, when I complained, they said that I didn't have stickers on the cars. That's the system. Can I have more stickers? Of course not. I signed up for automatic rent payments every month. But, for the first 2 months, we were writing checks every month anyways, because we had no idea what our utility costs were. It's too confusing for them to combine our utility bill to our rent and garage bill and debit my checking account. So, I went in & told them I want to increase the amount that gets debited. Ok, fill out another application (now my third because when we first checked in they lost our first try at it). Anyways, for the next 3 months, we were getting DOUBLE debited: the original & the new amount. Finally got them to stop & told them to just start up the correct amount once our credit is done. Of course, that didn't happen. So, last month we got a notice saying that a court filing to try to evict us would be made if we don't pay our outstanding balance within 18 hours for the back rent that wasn't paid. Oh, it has to be certified check/money order (because we must be deadbeats). Last week, I locked myself out of my apt w/my car key instead of apt key. I remember that after a certain time you get charged for needing to get let into your place. So, when I go to the doorman, I tell him. "I locked myself out. Will I get charged to get let back in? If so, I'll just drive to my wife's work and get hers." The answer he gave me was "No". Great, let me in. Needless to say, I was in the office today writing them a $50 check. I sometimes use the shuttle that goes downtown. The routes have changed 3 times in the last 2 months, so I've missed return buses twice. I'm sorry I have more on my plate than wanting to remember that after 10pm on weekdays but 6pm on weekends, I can't lock myself out. And that this week but not next week, the bus comes back on Walnut not JFK. DO NOT LIVE HERE. I'm so glad to be moving out in 2 months. There are actually more complaints, but Yelp only gives 5000 characters.
label: NEG

text: We were interested to try a restaurant in Reno that wasn't a casino restaurant or a buffet, although there are some very good ones here. We love fine dining and wanted to do something special for my husband's birthday. We are so glad we did. First thing to be aware of is, the restaurant is not very visible from the street! It is set back from the street, up a short unmarked driveway. The only marked driveway you see is the one before it, for a place called Reflections - don't take that one, take the next driveway, go up an incline, and it leads to a small parking lot that is behind the restaurant. It is unassuming from the outside, and resembles a country house, but inside, the decor is clean, and cozy with dining areas in separate rooms. There is also patio seating. The service was professional and thorough. Our server, Tim, knew the menu well and explained the dishes in detail. For our appetizer, we ordered the Pimenton Spiced Duck Rillettes with a mango salsa, cilantro and soft blue corn tortilla triangles. The duck meat was deliciously spiced and served in a small dish, ready to be spread on a tortilla and topped with the mango salsa. What flavor! Our soup was a carrot-ginger puree with a yogurt swirl - it was so flavorful and perfectly balanced. You could taste the sweetness of the carrot, followed by the ginger spice. So good! My husband ordered the Pork Tenderloin, which was served with Tuscan Kale, Serrano Ham, and little Romesco pasta balls. The pork was moist and tender, with a wonderful pork flavor. It was the best pork tenderloin he's ever had, and that's saying alot! I had the Grilled Wild King Salmon, served on a mix of Elm Oyster mushrooms, white corn, summer squash and red and yellow cherry tomatoes. Those mushrooms had such a unique flavor and really sent the vegetables to a different level. The salmon was fresh and flavorful, and was so moist! The meat was soft and smooth on the tongue, not flaky or dry as can happen when salmon is overcooked. That was definitely the best salmon I've ever had! For dessert, he had the Poppyseed Angel Food Cake with Blackberry Curd & Creme Chantilly. Tim served it with a tall skinny candle in honor of my husband's birthday. My husband said that was the best creme he'd tasted besides his mom's. It was a delightful, light cake with a rich blackberry sauce with the creme for contrast. I had the Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Chocolate Ganache Torte with a Pecan Crust & Caramel Sauce. It was very chocolaty and rich, but not sugary sweet. It went well with the pecan crust, a nutty blend of pecans and butter. The cocktails were poured well and they have a nice variety of wine and after dinner drinks as well. GM Carol Wilson, stopped at our table to greet us and was very personable. We told her how much we enjoyed the meal and she seemed genuinely appreciative. We could taste the difference with the fresh and organic ingredients, along with the talent of Chef Natalie Sellers. Both of them have extensive fine dining experience from San Francisco and it shows here. We noticed that there were a number of regular customers. Even though we're not local, we're close enough to make the trip again soon and are definitely going to be coming back to try more of their items. We highly recommend you try this delightful restaurant!
label: POS

text: I'm a big fan of sushi and must say this place has the most fresh fish in town. Sagami offers authentic Japanese food (not a good place for fusion styled food). Their best dish has to be Chirashi for entree, and Hamachi Kama for the appetizer! oh yeah and it's BYOB!!!

text: As a Downtown Office Drone, I spend my fair share of time and lunch cash at Culinaria. I decided to hop across the street today to visit Jade for the first time...the lunch specials and promises of sushi lured me in... The dining area itself is nice enough, and I was promptly seated by a nice enough host, and was greeted (after some very visible 'Is she in your section or mine? Do I have to take a 1-Top?' discussion) by a nice enough server. He quickly took my order...and left. Five minutes later, I suggested that I may want something to drink. I ordered my food--a quick, cheap lunch special, a couple of rolls and miso soup. It was all just OK. Warm, way too big pieces, 'off' seaweed wrappers. The miso was...eh. It wasn't busy in the place, but the servers looked stressed out, anyway. My service was friendly, but forgetful. I have a feeling that this place may have gotten a better review from me had I experienced it in what I suspect to be its true calling: a bar/lounge, while drunk and looking for a late-night Cali Roll. Jade doesn't hold up well to the daylight, I guess. For the money, I suggest Wasabi on Washington Ave. instead.

text: Since Chipotle is relatively new to St. Louis, and since nearly everyone I know insists on comparing this place to Qdoba...I feel compelled to explain why Chipotle, in my very humble opinion, is better. First of all...their chips win, hands down. They are lime salted and just amazing. On the down side, they don't have nachos on their menu, but seriously, get a naked burrito and chips and bam...nachos... Ok...seriously, other than the chips, I don't see much of a difference. The food is fresh, it's not anything that will knock you off your feet or anything, but it's certainly tasty, and it's cheap for the amount of food you get, and it's certainly one of the better stuffed veggie burritos in town. If you want a real treat, and you like things spicy, get all the salsas, and the pico de gallo on your burrito...it will make it way over stuffed, and give it the flavor I always feel like my burritos are missing.

text: We had a simple order: 1 pint of beans and rice to go, side of chips and salsa. $27...doesn't that seem high? We asked for chips and salsa while we waited. text: Assi plaza has great produce and probably the freshest seafood. I am always amazed at the selection they have. Also best place to get kimchi. They have a few aisles of it. If you aren't from the area, I recommend you seek this out and go here.

text: I was this close to giving Pumpkin 5 stars because I've rarely experienced food that's tasted so exquisite. Pumpkin sets out to create a menu that highlights fresh, local and seasonal foods and I've never met an argument for using fresh, local and seasonal foods that has tasted better. I was here on a Thursday night with a group of 7 for our BYO-of-the-month club's April outing. We started with the octopus and the gnocchi as appetizers for the table - which were both heavenly, but the veggies that came tossed with the gnocchi were so, well, vibrant, if 'vibrant' can be a taste. I do not like cooked carrots, but the carrots in this dish tasted unlike any carrot I had previously had, as did all of the other veggies. What was most intriguing was the way all the components of the dish were so distinct, but perfectly enhanced each other at the same time. Looking for the same revelation with my entree, I ordered the chicken. I was not disappointed. This chicken was succulent, and I've never been able to use that word to describe chicken before. I also had a taste of my friend's scallops, which were delicate, yet meaty and perfectly cooked. Despite being a small BYO, Pumpkin accommodated our large group and a few others that evening quite easily, without making the dining room seem overly crowded. Pumpkin is a smidge on the pricey side and I found the desserts to be so-so, which prevented me from ramping this up to a 5 star review, but any place that can make me wax lyrical over a carrot has got to be tried.
label: POS

text: I'm currently staying at the Millennium in the South Tower. While I have not seen the North Tower, I can't imagine it'd be much more run down that the South seems to be. I am not at all impressed with the room. It's quite small and while I realize this is the "budget" side, I still expect it to be a little nicer, i.e. no stains on the carpet, no traces of peeling wallpaper, etc. The indoor pool is sort of a joke. It's a small wedge shaped pool that is 3' and 4' deep. The outdoor pool by the North Tower is considerably nicer though it was quite crowded with pool drinkers (AKA intoxicated people enjoying their beverages in the pool itself). The lobby is actually quite pretty with gorgeous views of the park and the Arch but that's about the only impressive thing I can say about it at this point. The staff was quite friendly and efficient. If you're going to a Cardinals game, Busch Stadium is only two blocks away so it's quite convenient for that purpose. It just doesn't seem worth the money though.
label: NEG

text: Dr. West and Dr. Giuliani truly love animals. I prefer Dr. West because he's slightly more friendly, though I've never been dissatisfied with Dr G either. He's very professional, but doesn't come across as all business. It's a small operation, with just two exam rooms, but you get personal attention; with sometimes fairly long visits, so you may have to wait while another pet gets the attention yours will as well. Very clean office, great staff and techs who are welcoming and helpful. Dr. West has always been honest with me in diagnosing problems, and in saying when it's not a job he can handle (like a complicated surgery, or a sonogram that they don't have the big equipment for). He sometimes comps certain things during a visit, like nail clipping, or tries to reduce your bill for you a bit. It's not cheap, but petcare never is--and this is *not* a country vet, so it's worth the cash--though still nowhere NEAR as expensive as going to Penn. One time, he diagnosed her cancer, and had a rotating surgeon come through one day and remove the tumor from her face--cancer free for 2.5 years! He helped us thru a gallbladder surgery performed at Metropolitan in Trouper back in July. Pets First keeps my old girl tickin; they have literally saved her life & I would recommend them to anyone.

Aggressive sales reps - would not honor my own corporate insurance which covers the auto rental insurance. They will take a huge chunk as a pre-authorization if you skip insurance. text: OK. I'm obviously missing something here, or else I haven't scrolled through the good reviews to get to the bad. The first time it was just blah (and expensive) and the second time it was hands down the worst restaurant experience I've ever had. There will not be a third time. The first I won't bore you with, but the second was surreal, so here you go. Went with a group from work for lunch, two of us are vegetarians and ordered the vegetarian lentil soup as there weren't many other options. The waiter was a pretentious fool, but that's another story. The food arrived along with a strong odor of bacon which everyone, including the vegetarians, enjoyed sniffing heartily (who can resist the smell of good bacon?). However, tasting baconn is a different story, and the lentil soup was steeped in a bacon taste. We tried to ignore it, thinking that maybe the scent of bacon from other's food was seeping into our taste buds or something, but the chunks of bacon that started to appear in the lentils was not to be ignored. Calling the waiter over, we inquired why there was bacon in the vegetarian lentil soup, and were told there was not. We pointed out the bacon and had a few friends eat the bacon at the table, thus proving it was bacon, yet the waiter still denied the presence of bacon in the soup. We asked the waiter to taste the bacon himself and he refused. We asked him to ask the chef if there was bacon in the soup, and he huffed away to the kitchen. In the meantime, we painstakingly separated all of the bacon from the lentils in two separate piles. There was a lot of bacon - glorious chunks of bacon. The waiter returned and said that the chef confirmed there was no bacon in the lentil soup. Now we had a PILE of proof on each of our plates, but he looked straight at it and said again that there was no bacon in the soup. We kept repeating "But it's right here! It came out of the soup!" And he had no response, and eventually backed away from the table and ignored us, leaving the bacon-piled inedible lentil soups on the table. About 15 minutes later, a brash woman marched up to the table and demanded to know "who had a problem". We were all like, "First of all, who are you?" and when she explained she was the manager, explained the problem. She repeated that there could not possibly be any bacon in the vegetarian lentil soup. Once again, we pointed at the bacon piles in the soup bowls, and it was as if....they weren't there. They were not addressed, she looked right through them and repeated like a mantra, "there is no bacon in the soup". At one point I said, (laughing at this point because it was so ridiculous) "I feel like I'm in crazy world! How can you say there is no bacon in the soup when you're LOOKING at it?" To this she said, "It must not be bacon." at which point we asked her to try it, and she refused. She gave us our check (the waiter never returned)... and charged us for the uneaten bacon lentil soups. It was insane, and for the first time in my life, I wholeheartedly agreed to leave a measly tip. My other revenge is this review.

Now I feel it has gotten even pricier and the staff at the register are more business like and less inclined to be interested in the art of true healing. I used to live in Ohio and could find my share of metaphysical oddities and good bookstores that just made you want to stay, gawk at the merchandise and really pore over a good occult book. This store is too commercial for my taste and the crystals are just your ordinary, run of the mill fare that makes for good gift giving but should not be taken seriously if you are a spiritual healer. The store left me feeling rather empty on this trip and the readers just appear to me to be a bit burnt out or jaded. I did opt for a reading with one of the older readers but it was such a cold read-- a generic read that it left me feeling unenlightened shall we say? The store is rather small and yes they do have quite the selection of teas but they have changed to plastic cups rather than china like they used to have so it just did not feel like the same indulgence or luxury from the past. I don't understand why they call this place Bottom of the tea cup since in the past it was the tradition in the 1930's to have your tea leaves read for you when you finished drinking your tea. Now it's tea in plastic cups without all the glamor and it really does not have the same vibe it had pre Katrina. I hate to write such a bad review but there is nothing out of the ordinary or special about being in the store in the Quarter.

My dad, little brother, and I were seated and waited for my mother and brother #2. While waiting we ordered drinks and looked over the menu. And there were 5 of us at the table, the least the waitress could have done was suggest we might want two. We gladly would have ordered two at once. When serving our appetizers our waitress carried out one of my BIGGEST restaurant pet peeves. I had not completely finished my lemonade, and at the price it was I was savoring it. It was hardly long enough into the meal for me to have finished a whole drink in the first place, and all she had to do as ask and I would have been fine telling her I was going to hang onto it for a while longer. Another thing I noticed within the first 15 minutes of being there was a man, who I am assuming was the floor manager (correct me if wrong) kept almost 'spying' on our table. It was a Friday night, so yes it was busy. But we had literally just sat down, if you were waiting for a table to open, it obviously wasn't going to be us. I'm sorry I cannot remember all the details, but I think it shows that the only things I can really remember were the bad things about this meal. Not only would we have gladly ordered more food, had our waitress been around more often, but we were so annoyed by the man constantly hoovering by our table watching us eat that we just wanted to get out of there. Osteria was a huge letdown and I don't think I will be going back anytime soon.

text: Sometimes I feel like Diogenes when it comes to venturing to Chinese restaurants in N.O. text: Beware of East Coast Super Subs. The moment your eyes touch down on the menu, a challenge is issued: 8" or 16"? What are you, some sort of sissy? Are you really going to be satisfied with just 8 inches of sandwich? C'mon, get the 16". You can handle it! If 16 inches of sandwich -- and not just sandwich, but meaty, cheesy, happiness-filled sandwich -- strikes you as completely ridiculous, then you're probably safe. But if you're an idiot / garbage disposal like me, it sounds just crazy enough to work. So 16 inches of Broad Street Bully it was: an overstuffed monstrosity of Philly steak, provolone, lettuce, tomato, fried onions, and hot peppers, the sort of thing you know you should eat alone so that no one will see the carnage unfolding between your hands and your throat. They handed me the bag containing what looked like two separate sandwiches -- only I knew that it was actually just one enormous awesome sandwich in disguise! Let me start by saying that this sandwich is utterly delicious. It's been said before, but the hot peppers totally make it. Well, the hot peppers and the fried onions. And the steak and cheese and...well okay, the point is: the ingredients here are all really good, and they work together fabulously. The difference in quality between one of these sandwiches and a Frankie's cheese steak is night and day (though Frankie's gets props for sticking with tradition and supplying me with Cheez Whiz). In fact, it was so good that I was finished with the first 8-inch half of the sandwich before I stopped to think about what was happening. My main thought was, "Oh man that was amazing. Thank god there's more." And then, nom nom nom nom... I ate the whole thing. I probably shouldn't have; I couldn't move for the rest of the day. But oh my gosh was it tasty. I would definitely recommend checking this place out. Just do yourself a favor: get the 8".

When I walked in, all the seats at the bar were taken except one, which was kindly offered to be by another patron, and another warmly introduced himself to me. So, points for a neighborhood, friendly feel On the other hand, I'm not sure how this kind of set up is going to work as a business. If the stools are actually occupied at the bar, it's unclear where a customer would go to get a drink. The bar would serve as a major choke-point, not allowing for the kind of traffic that a bar would need to succeed. The only way I can see this working is if they have 3 or 4 cocktail waitresses, who are floating around the rooms - which ideally would be crowded and a nightmare to navigate with a tray of drinks. Now, the other "review" does mention plans for a pool table and a backyard patio, neither of which would address the problems with getting drinks, but would round out the homey feel of the joint. Granted, in the second room on the right, there were counter tops sitting on the floor (I'd guess they're going to put little bar ledges around the walls), so it's obvious the place is being worked on. They just opened a week ago, so maybe some of this will improve given time, and they'll figure out how they'll do the volume to survive as a bar. All that being said, the place definitely has potential, if they can figure out how they're going to keep drinks in people's hands. I really would love to see the place make it, I'm just not super optimistic about it . . .

text: The place was good....until it attained celebrity status. Yep, to those who are not in the know, Guadalajara Grill was at another location literally just down the street. As mentioned by every single other review, the tableside salsa is great. Like your salsa super spicy with extra cilantro, the lady will make it for you. Like your salsa as mild as Jay Leno's humor, the lady will be happy to comply. You the get the idea. The food was, and still is, on the average to slightly above average range. My personal favorite in the area of Mexican cuisine is mole, and Guadalajara Grill does a decent job. One positive thing is that the place does not mess around with the drinks, especially the margaritas. I went to the old location many times since its inception. I even recall the German restaurant that came before it. Since it moved into its new digs, however, I have only been there twice. On my last visit, the place was jam packed; not just with any normal human beings, mind you, but with Greek-loads of sorority girls and fraternity boys. I normally have the patience of Job, but on this last trip, the service was appallingly slow. I would have enjoyed a hazing from the surrounding tables just to pass the time. In all fairness, however, the place was packed to capacity, and my party had over 10 people. Still you'd think that a larger operation would mean a larger kitchen and additional staff. Mmm hmmm.... My first experience at the new location was special. Well, it was special for purely external reasons: it was my birthday. The wait time for a party of 12 on a Friday night? An hour and a half at least. No skin of my back because I'm not above drinking at the bar. Yeah, the bar experience sucked. Sucked the life out me, that is. It took freakin' forever for the bartenders to even acknowledge our existence. While the fellows behind the bar were not of the surly sort, they certainly did not seem to understand the concept of tipping. After a while the staff approached one my friends and explained to her that there were a couple of tables available within the bar area, and she took it. In hindsight, it wasn't all that bad. It literally brought us together. Who knew that two booths normally meant for a total of eight people could accommodate 12 adults and one child? text: This bookstore really is amazing. I was in Olde City the other day and went to another used book store and nothing compares to this place. A House of Our Own is well organized, has a collection of both new books and used books. The interior of the store is beautiful and the collection has some amazing books. New books are on the first floor and used books are on the second floor. To follow up on what Viv C. said, this book store is not for the "regular consumer." For those people God created chain bookstores. For everyone else that is looking for inspiration or a copy of a classic that is actually a first edition or out of print, check this place out. What I found really great was the quality of the used books. Unlike many used bookstores, this place tries to avoid stocking "junk books" (e.g. Danielle Steele and her ilk) as well as all those self-help books. In addition, I didn't see many "how-to" books with really antiquated information (e.g. Windows 3.1 for Dummies). Their standards for what they shelve seems to be very high. Yes, books are grouped by academic subject matter then alphabetically by author. This is something to be excited about seeing as how most used bookstores are barely alphabetized! And the book store is on the UPENN campus, so wouldn't you expect this place would cater to its main consumer, the student? This place has been in business since 1971. When you walk through this old brownstone building, you'll truly be inspired and it will make you realize why the printed book probably will never be replaced by digital texts.

Noshville has great brunch cocktails, not just the usual bloody marys and mimosas. I had a "morning martini." i love their potato pancakes and the corn beef hash is a great greasy hangover cure. I always get my breakfast with a bagel, because they're very good here. For lunch, i like the reuben, and the matzo ball soup, even the small is absolutely huge and a great deal. I think there's been some issues at the Nashville locations with Noshville leaving the pickle spears on the table, but they do it in Frankln. They're great salt cured pickles. After trying them all, I think I could happily settle with the McDougal's sauce and the chipotle barbecue sauce. The fried chicken sandwich was crunchy and delicious. My one request is that they begin offering the chicken sandwich on that buttery, garlic toast... mmmm, that would be heaven. Everything about this place is homey and fun: wacky decorations, friendly service, FREE soft serve ice cream, and fried chicken. text: I heard about this place on roadfood.com. It got favorable reviews as being among the best sub place in Delaware. On my way home from a business trip I decided to stop in and check it out. I ordered a cheesesteak with fried onions and a store-roasted turkey sub with the works. The cheesesteak is comparable to the best you can get in the top-of-line Philly places. Only thing is they don't serve cheez whiz so if you are a fan of cheez whiz you won't get it here. The cheesesteak was very tasty. It had good fresh flavor.The onions were cooked perfectly and good quality provolone was used. The best part of the sub was the roll(which often separates a good cheesesteak from a great cheeseteak) Their roll was soft and just chewy enough. Great texture. It also was just crisp enough on the outside. This is among the best cheesesteaks I have tasted in the Delaware Valley that can come close to reputable Philly shops. The combination of flavors was good and it was not a greasy blob like you get at so many sub shops. Though Tony Luke's in Philly is still my overall favorite with just a bit better flavor and a better roll. The area where Casapulla's excels is in the store-roasted turkey sub. This was by far the best turkey sub I have ever had. The turkey was moist,flavorful,fresh and truly delicious. Combined with the awesome roll and fresh toppings, it was over the top. If you want to try the best turkey sub in the Delaware Valley this is the place to go for sure. They also put out a first-rate cheesesteak as well but their turkey sub is surely worth the detour.
label: POS

Red Bean! (Other note-worthy choices were peanut, green bean, and taro.) Like all good Chinatown eats, it's ridiculously inexpensive-- a very generous bowl cost $1.50. text: This place is one of the quickest places I've ever had experience at in terms of turning a car around. They recommend the correct tires and/or service and just get the job done. Earlier this year we had a blow-out and the guy from AAA said it was likely due to a bad valve. The tire was ruined, but thankfully my wife was only going 25 MPH at the time. We took the car back to RW and they sold us a new tire. Shame on us for not looking into the cause of the valve problem, but in retrospect I would have assumed they were also aware of the recall and would have made us aware or warned us. Yesterday another tire failure. Again - luckily only going 25 MPH. While changing the tire this time - noticed a cracked valve. The tire was not permanently damaged luckily. Learned about the valve recall after doing some research about what causes a valve failure. Took the car back to RW today. They replaced the valve and put the tire back on. They also replaced another faulty valve, but advised the 4th one is fine. Is it?! They confirmed that the manufacturer of the valve did recall them. Now it seems we have to chase the valve manufacturer for reimbursment for the first tire that went!

text: My feelings about this specific ES are quite mixed. I stay at an ES several times a year. This one is unique. First, the rooms are massive. The property was intended to be condos. You could literally fit 10 people (somewhat comfortably) with air mattresses or sleeping bags. Showers would be another story. The interiors are quite ugly and mismatched and the beds are average. Nice flat panel TVs (one in living area and one in bedroom). Bathroom is average. The tub/toilet/vanity area are combined. This lessens the convenience slightly--if more than one person is staying in the room. The free breakfast and "managers receptions" are much better than most ES. The breakfast has the standard "custom omelet" station but also waffles, really good coffee, biscuits and gravy, and much more that most ES don't have. On to the manager's reception--kickin! They have some premium labels and if you smile a little they'll give you a double - and it's free. Fairly standard staff. We asked for some non-feather pillows. It took more than 30 minutes. We called and the front desk acted slightly offended informing us that "we only have one housekeeper and we're doing our best". BIG POINTS OFF for parking that costs $7 a day. WHAT? And then Internet - $12.95 per 24-hours. I can't believe in this day and age wireless costs that much. Also, Tampa has plenty of space - why the cost for parking? It's not San Fran or DC. When I role all of this together and look at the rates compared to similar properties, you're getting ripped off at this ES. Stay elsewhere. If the rates were around 30% less and/or parking and wireless were free--three or maybe four stars.

You addressed me about it once, I acknowledged the message and stopped being tardy, now stop it. I would probably go back to these people for the simple fact that this is the closest physical therapy place to my house and when you're mobility impaired, that's freaking important. Just be careful and buyer beware. Like I said -- they're good at being personable, but never forget that all you represent to the company are dollar signs. Tucked in a quiet neighborhood, the place is trendy without trying to be so. The wait staff was informative, polite, and quick without being rushed. The bread was put in the oven for us as we arrived, and after our drinks came warm fresh bread accompanied our soups that were layered with an amazing orchestra of flavor. Upon the recommendation of our waiter, both my friend and I had the duck. I very rarely order this fowl when dining out as no one has quite mastered cooking this hard to make platter, but I soon was wondering if the chef could teach my (yes I am writing this) mother how to make it. It was a little pricey, but you definitely get, and then some, what you pay for.
label: POS

text: I went to St. Elmo's for a college graduation dinner for my aunt, and I must say that you don't always get what you pay for. I didn't try the "Signature" Steaks that everyone raves about, because I am not a huge steak fan. However, I did try other menu items such as they're Indiana Amish Chicken, and I wasn't too impressed. My chicken came out dry and cold, and I ended up sending it back. I did however vote to keep my Red-skin Mashed Potatoes which were very good.I knew St. Elmo's was expensive, but when you charge 7 bucks for a house salad, I think that is pushing it. I don't think I will ever return here, unless someone would like to treat me to dinner one day.

text: I went here ONCE and will never go back. I went with a friend and we both sat down, ready to get our nails done. The person who was doing my nails asked what I wanted and I explained that I wanted "thin white tips", which meant that she needed to put on clear tips and airbrush them white. Well, she put on white tips instead and I waited and waited for her to ensure that my tips were "thin," but this never happened. At the end she asked if I liked them and I told her they were not what I asked for. The manager (who was doing my friends nails and stopped many times to answer the phone and have long conversations) came over to look at my nails and said they looked nice and didn't know what my issues was. I explained to him that it was not what I asked for, and I either wanted a free service or I wanted her to fix them. He just kept saying "no, they look nice" I was really upset and told him I would never return and he just shrugged. The worst part was that I had to wait an extra half an hour for him to finish off my friends nails because he kept "taking breaks." Obviously, I would not return.

text: Over rated. That's really about it. The wine is OK, but it's nothing special. Their Meritage, is a bit expensive for fair wine. You can get a good Saint Estephe Bordeaux that blows the Meritage away for like 17 at any PA state store. The bottles are pretty though and I can see why people go there for the scenery, but I need more than just scenery. We have tried some of the other low key Bucks wineries and their varietals are about as good (as you are going to get from PA) as Crossing Vineyards. None that I recall make a Meritage so if that is what you are looking for, you are out of luck.but really, it's not that great. And their tasting are expensive for what you get. You drink wine to get drunk You drink good wine to get drunk pleasantly. You can go somewhere else to get good wine and save some loot as well. You can't even think of buying the wine as helping local merchants because most of their grapes actually come from Erie County. And for serving "ok" wine some that border on Vinegar, these people are snobby. Skip it, try somewhere else or just go to the state store and save your money, get a good French Bordeaux or a good Malbek for probably cheaper and less attitude than Crossings.
label: NEG

text: I lived in Indy for 18 years and can confirm that this is DEFINITELY the best pizza in town! They serve thin crust gourmet pizza with a variety of toppings, including some interesting choices such as snow crab, pea pods, capers, anchovies, prosciutto, and about eight types of cheese. There salads are great and they make some mean sandwiches (go for the Stromboli or Muffaletta). I worked in the kitchen here for a few years, so I have some fun facts that most people don't know: - Peyton Manning eats here regularly - The crust is homemade everyday (white and wheat) - The cheese is grated fresh everyday (fontina + mozzarella) - A TON of the ingredients are imported from Italy (olive oil, etc.) - The dining room of the original Bazbeaux Broadripple was a garage Anyways, even when I worked here six days a week, I never got tired of eating their pizza and garlic bread. You can't go wrong with the special, margarita, quattro, or chilope.

text: While we had heard great things about the place that used to be in this location, we discovered that the new place wasn't up to par. It started from the moment we were seated. When the beverage server came over she apologized again stating that they couldn't see the mess, at this point they should have just let it go and not made excuses for the mess. We ordered a vodka on the rocks and glass of wine and had to ask twice for the wine - in the meantime, our anti-pasta appetizer appears (still no wine). We picked the assorted meat platter with marinated mushrooms, peppers and olives. At a whopping $19 for the appetizer, we had four pieces of prosciutto, three paper thin pieces of salami and marinated mushrooms, etc that tasted like they poured a very cheap-sweet-bottled Italian dressing on them - we were not amused and while the meat was good (although minimal for the price) - marinade was terrible. After asking about various menu items we decided on the Ahi Tuna Ravioli - the waiter raved about the dish stating that the raviolis were wonderful and we would love the seared ahi on the side. text: My boyfriend took me here for our 1 year anniversary. We were both VERY impressed. He called ahead for reservations, and told them it was for our anniversary. When we got to our table, there was a single rose waiting for me. Very nice touch. The food was EXCELLENT. We ordered the "Big Night Out', which consisted of a cheese fondue appetizer, a salad, an entree, and a dessert. The cheese fondue was excellent. It came with a variety of things for dipping; bread, cheese, veggies -- you name it. It was absolutely delicious. The entree was just as good. It was a lot of fun cooking our own food, and everything was so perfect. The cuts of meat were amazing; everything was great. The dessert was good, as well. They brought us two chocolate covered strawberries with a candle in each (for our anniversary). How sweet! We also had the chocolate fondue, which came with pound cake, strawberries, marshmallows, rice krispy treats, etc. for dipping. SO good. I ordered the Yin Yang martini, and it was delicious. Actually, I ordered two. All in all, it was quite expensive, so this is definitely a "special occasion" type place, but you get your money's worth. The service is FANTASTIC, the food is plentiful (and GOOD!), and the ambiance is romantic. I love this place. Hands down, my favorite restaurant in St. Louis.

text: After experiencing Ivey Cakes in Franklin, and the Cupcake Collection in Germantown, HOW can Dulce compare to them? They simply do not! What a dissapointment compared to the others mentioned. We purchased six different cupcake flavors. Each cupcake tasted exactly the same. They all had the same icing (whipped topping) on them. text: The Decider is breaking his normal policy of sticking to reviews of restaurants in Los Angeles to provide a description of Tony Moran's in New Orleans. Ate here recently while in town on business (it was not my choice of restaurant) and really had no clue as to what I was in for because, alas, there was no prior review of Moran's on Yelp. So I'm hoping to make sure some other sucker doesn't get put in a similar spot in the future. Located on Bourbon Street in the heart of the French Quarter, Tony Moran's is a typical overpriced tourist trap of a restaurant that you should avoid at all costs. The cuisine is Italian, but aside from the general fact that you shouldn't come to Bourbon Street jonesing for Italian food, this place can't manage to plate a decent dish. We had some appetizer with fried disks of eggplant, which tasted of spoiled oil and spoiled breading. Just disgusting. They also use that COSTCO type shredded parmesan cheese that never really melts and is just undescribably lazy and nasty. Someone at the table ordered chicken parmesan and the nasty cheese was on top of that too. I tried to play it "safe" and ordered a linguine with shrimp, garlic and olive oil. The thing comes out swimming in oil. Nobody approaches the table to offer some fresh grated cheese or even some pepper. With entrees priced at the touristy $20-$35 bucks, you'd expect and deserve more. This place needs a major overhaul. On top of it all, the service was incredibly slow. You're better off just eating at the Hustler club across the street. At least the results will match the expectations. Given all that's happened in New Orleans in recent years, I really hate bagging on any business that's still open there and still trying to make a run at it. But that's still no excuse for being this lazy about one's menu and having a kitchen seeminly not try to be respectable. There's far too many better restaurants within a block of Tony Moran's to get away with such a mess here. So reluctantly, the Decider suggests going elsewhere for dinner...try the ACME Oyster House around the corner, it's much better.
label: NEG

text: Ok, so maybe it's just me...but Jose P.'s seems to be experiencing a major identity crisis. Seriously, what is up with this place? text: I have a soft spot for Greek things as well, which is why Kanella has made my s*** list. First off: overpriced. I ordered Ravioli, and i wasn't expecting to get a whole plateful. text: I recently went here with some friends on one of their parent's tab. It should first be made clear that if I had to pay myself this place would get a star less because the price they charge is ridiculous considering the experience you get. The food itself is pretty tasty, but the portions are not large enough to merit the prices that are charged. The salsa bar is robust and the chips are delectable; at any other place this alone would encourage me to give a higher score (though the fact that you have to pay for chips left me with a sour taste in my mouth). text: So many fetishes, so little time.... In the world of music, some of the more serious hobbyists (and music fetishists) prefer some older school approaches for another dimension of appreciation. Case in point, as old as vinyl records are, the serious music listener and collector will often debate that the warm and crisp analog sound of vinyl is more enjoyable than the sound off of digital plastic circles read by a laser. Some electronic keyboard musicians prefer the warm and toasty analog synthesizer "classical" sounds vs their modern all digital counterparts. e.g. Yamaha DX-7 (remember the 80s? Virtually every single band from that era you can think of has used it, including A-Ha's first album where I wouldn't be surprised if they used upwards of 10 simultaneously for some songs) or Moog keyboards (popularized arguably by Jan Hammer who shot to fame with the Miami Vice soundtrack). The Mini-Moog is still a very sought after toy trinket that can do some serious wonders. Ditto for the Fender Rhodes. And with music recording, there's the failed but once immensely popular format with professional recording artists, the Digital Audio Tape (DAT). http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Audio_Tape One of the greatest, yet most troublesome, and costly formats ever invented. Many of the more serious old school recording enthusiasts (professional and for home/studio use, and also in the field) used or still use DAT to some extent, even though technically the equipment has been discontinued for quite some time. I don't doubt that many recording studios have archives full of DAT tapes (e.g. KCRW's studio in Santa Monica). Although DAT is pure digital goodness, it's not just pricey, but the use of DAT tapes in machines wear out the heads of the players/recorders over time. Digital noise happens when the tapes are out of alignment, causing yucky shitty scratchy noises that hurt the ears (and if not, maybe your dog will bitch at you). DAT is way more finnicky than analog cassette tapes (which also go through wear and tear over time), and presents more problems than the average person's high maintenance signficant other or chihuahua poochie. Pro Digital Inc is probably the most well known amongst the DAT fetishists to still lend support to that community, by providing the technical know how to fix DAT machines (and also have the parts and skills at the same time). The brains behind Pro Digital Inc is Paul Plotnick who is well respected in his profession, and does the most solid work for maintenance and repair work. Got a DAT deck that won't play, FF or RWD or all, or it will play but without audio, or your deck's lid is busted so it won't accept tapes properly? No problem, there's always a solution (unless your deck is deemed totally FUBAR, in which case they may have some refurbished DAT equipment for sale). The only setback for most living out of state, is having to spend the time and $ to package the gear up safely and ship it over. The other great things are not just good work done, but generally the estimates given in terms of cost and turnaround time are VERY accurate. So keep PDI in mind if you've got a misbehaving DAT machine.

text: I have been coming here since early fall, and after a few months all I can say is that I really miss my studio back where I used to live. I have been to some pretty good classes here; for the most part, though, they range from mediocre to bad. Strangely, the most (consistently) terrible class I have been to here is taught by Bill Raup, the studio owner. In a 90-minute class, he forced us through all the major poses, from Sun Salutation A all the way to Half Pigeon, in the first 60 minutes. He spoke so quietly I could barely hear him, demonstrated nothing, and rushed us through -- no one was able to keep up, I looked. The final half-hour was spent on random poses that made no sense after what came before. I actually left early because instead of feeling calmed and energized, I was feeling tense and angry. Yoga is not about speeding through 75 poses and doing none of them mindfully. That is a recipe for injury. The other teachers here provide a better experience than this, but it is still not what I signed up for. They do little to correct people's poses, don't vary the flow at all, and do little to challenge intermediate yoga practitioners. They also don't suggest modifications when it is clear that you are struggling with a pose -- for instance, I can never do camel because it crunches my lower back every single time, yet not one teacher has ever said, "and if this pose hurts your lower back, try X." There is also absolutely no vibe to this studio. If you are looking for the sort of place where chummy regulars chat each other up before and after the class, this is not for you -- the anteroom is deserted before and after practice. The blah decor of the studio doesn't help this. Finally, despite being billed as Baptiste "hot" yoga, the temperature never really rises above 85 degrees F. What!? I rarely even break a sweat, which is sad, because that's what I'm paying for. In conclusion: poor pacing, sloppy teaching, low temperature, somewhat depressing vibe. And -- only 2 classes per day, both in the evening (huh?). I bet they could attract many more people in this student-heavy area if they offered classes throughout the day.

text: Call me crazy - as much as I love fine dining breakfast kitsch will always hold a special place in my heart (and belly.) Having dined at some of America's greats - Dottie's True Blue, Griddle Café, Bongo Room, Miss Shirley's, and Pamela's to name few - I knew that Carman's Country Kitchen was a must on my visit to Philadelphia. With lunch and dinner plans starring Marc Vetri and still sated from Modo Mio the previous evening I knew daytime snacking would be light and a solid breakfast would hold me the six hours to lunch - per usual I woke early and hit the ground running, arriving at the Country Kitchen before they even opened the doors. With the truck-table parked outside I took a seat on the hitch for only a moment before the front of house man would open the door and say "she ain't ready yet, but you can come in and take a seat and have some coffee or something." Making my way into the restaurant the server introduced himself by name and asked for mine - he'd call me Mike for the duration of my meal. Browsing around the small diner I have to admit the décor is not exactly G-Rated, but it certainly is hilarious - pigs and tea pots with enormous genitals, pictures from God knows where, and the famous "Put the C*nt back in Country" signage. Sipping my coffee - dark and solid, a bit acidic but not "bad," I chatted with the server about what I was doing in town, the restaurant, and Philly in general - he had a lot of suggestions for interesting things to see and do. Around 8am Carman herself would come in through the back door with an enormous grocery bag full of ingredients that she picked up on her way to work - things to "experiment with for next week's menu." Browsing the big board I made my selection (remember, only 4 mains and 4 sides are available) and Carman introduced herself and conversed boisterously from the back kitchen while preparing my food. Offered a selection of newspapers, magazines, and other assorted reading materials I browsed the sports section while we discussed the restaurant's history and other spots Carman recommended in the city. Never short on words or opinions Carman held up her end of the conversation admirably with lots of anecdote - for a solo diner who would spend the duration of his meal at Carman's as the only person in house it was actually very interesting. After 20 minutes and a couple cups of coffee my plate would arrive along with a dispenser of thick, rich, maple syrup. Entitled Buttermilk Pancakes with White Figs, Dark Chocolate, Ginger, Ground Almonds, and Anise I tasted a bite solo and then added syrup. At $14 and cash only for an Aunt Jemima based cake I have to admit the price seemed a bit steep for the portion size, but what was lacking in size was more than made up for by flavor. Impressively well balanced I was shocked by the sweetness of the figs and the manner in which they were balanced by the bitter dark chocolate and aromatic spices of the fresh ginger and Anise. Well cooked and fluffy the pancakes were stellar examples as well - whatever Carman is doing to the base mix I need to figure out. Finishing my pancakes and settling the tab I chatted with my hosts some more - parking cop lore, stories of the best places to go drinking in Philly, and her theory on why the Phillies were slumping all came to the table - I was also given a business card and told the menu would be changing the next day if I wanted to make a reservation because "it gets busy early on Saturdays." With food and service so impressive I have no doubt it should.

text: First of all, the name. Chew Man Chu? I mean, I get it, but... The picture on the door is Puyi, the last emperor of China, but now he is 'Chew Man Chu'? Anyway, on to the food... If you grew up eating South East Asian food, you might not enjoy this place. It is a fusion of Vietnamese, Thai, Malaysian and Chinese with lots of sugar added to suit American tastes. Everything is too sweet. Those used to American Chinese food may not notice it. At Chew Man Chu, they take sugar levels to an extreme, to the point of having homemade soy sauce on the table which is sweet rather than salty. I had the oxtail soup dumplings, fatty pork buns, salt and pepper shrimp and beef salad. The oxtail soup had some undertones of Chinese herbal soup, but was overpowered by sweetness which disguised the herbal taste. It was a bit strange. The fatty pork buns actually weren't so bad but the huge chunk of fat in the buns turned me off. I like pork fat in general, but it should be well balanced with the meat, not a big slab of fat. The pepper shrimp was okay and the beef salad had nice hints of basil but was, again, too sweet. At the end of the meal, I could feel my mouth coated with sugar like I just ate candy. Besides the food, everything else was fine. I like the deco and the waitstaff. The girl who served us was very nice so we didn't have the heart to tell her that the food is really not that great. Props for stocking Tiger Beer, the best SE Asian brew. The place filled up very fast, even for a week night. The tables are very close together and you can practically join in your neighbor's conversation. Needless to say, I will not be going back. For the price I paid I could have had 3 days of real Asian food from Chinatown. I was truly disappointed that the nice deco, ambiance, and interesting menu were all but a sugar coating.

text: I work at the zoo so I am a little biased toward it. Here's what you need to know coming in. One time visitors need to understand the following. Parking is 5 bucks. Admission is 12.50 Eat before you go. If you must spend money on ride tickets make sure to get the ticket bundles Get to any of the shows (Especially Dolphin) early as possible. Those things fill up quickly! Go on a mid-week day afternoon. Those usually are the best for no one being there. If you go in the summer, take the following - Sunscreen - Water Bottle - Some sort of Powerade or Gatorade, both help with hydration. - Umbrella (Because Mother nature hates us) Other things to remember, Going during Zoo Boo, or Kroger Christmas At The Zoo will yield HUGE crowds. So don't be suprised if you go and there are TONS of people there. Seriously. One last thing, The zoo is a big place, and it's very easy to lose your children. Please please please please please be mindful of where they are. They can get lost in a heart beat, if you do lose your child take 5 deep breaths and find someone who works there. text: Everything about Dante's is fresh & local - the food, the drinks, the staff and even the restaurant itself. So fresh & local we ate there twice - once for dinner & then for brunch on Sunday. The board at the front doesn't show the specials - just a long list of "What's Local". Repeatedly, the staff were overheard describing with pride where or how or why something was on the menu. They have a passion for what they do, and it shows. The menu changes every two weeks or so based on what's available, and creativity is everywhere on it. While the obligatory shrimp & grits were good, the lump crab salad with cucumber and cantaloupe on field greens exemplified this. The combination was so unusual I had to try it, and it more than just "worked". The lightly dressed & salty greens melded the other ingredients into something more that the sum of it's parts. Simple, creative, and delicious. My redfish on the half shell was cooked perfectly, topped with a crab & fresh chopped herb mixture. The topping complimented the fish, but was a little to leafy for me. Lots of crab & less herb would have still done the trick, but again it was simple and creative and tasty. My wife's eggplant napoleon was excellent, and frankly would also make a fantastic side dish. From what they told us, the chef is also doing double duty as pastry chef, which can be a real workload. He's pulling it off, because the fresh blueberry pie was the best I've ever had. If it's available, get it without hesitation. Yummy. Brunch was yummy, too. The place was full, with a short wait around noon, but they get the food out fast. My Debris & Eggs Benedict was another combination I'd never thought I'd try, and they were great. Blueberry pancakes didn't need syrup they were so tasty. Portions are small so don't hesitate to double up and try a few other items. Like the spoon bread. All in all, we really enjoyed Dante's. Right across from the stodgy Brigstens, they are vibrant, fun, and passionate about their focus on fresh & local food. Worth the trip uptown, we'll be back again. It seems like the kind of place that doesn't get old.
label: POS

text: Brew Your Own Beer has been on Darby Road ever since I can remember, at least ever since my friends and I were in middle school and asked John, the owner, if we could hang fliers in his window advertising that our awful band was playing an upcoming event. He obliged kindly without question. This shop has everything a beginner or expert brewer needs, and if you're looking for a little guidance to come up with ideas or recipes, John has a wealth of information about the art of homebrewing that he's more than happy to share. My brewing buddy and I often spend a little extra time chatting with John about some of our upcoming, harebrained concoctions, to which we are either met with a raised eyebrow or a confused cringe, but even if he disagrees, John is happy to lend moral support to some of the more adventurous brewers like us. I've been to other homebrew shops that have the ingredients you need, but haven't encountered a true shopkeeper anywhere outside this little store. John will give you advice if you ask for it, and give you cold, hard honesty when you have a bad idea and need it. We always make a point to share our final product with him to get his feedback but also because, hey, that's what homebrewing's all about. One can only hope that when John decides to retire, an equally passionate homebrewer will carry the torch.

text: Finally made it up to REI, mostly as a comparison to the local version--Summit Hut. It is everything that you would expect from the other reviews. I was impressed by the sheer size of the place. Two stories, with clothes on top and camping gear, bicycles, kayaks, ski gear, etc. all located downstairs. Really, basically everything you would need for most outdoor activities. One nice thing that I haven't heard much about it the $20 offer to "buy into the company". Basically, it is a membership card type scheme, where you get 10% of your purchase costs (excluding sale items) tallied into an account that you can access and apply to purchases whenever you see fit. The $20 is for a lifetime membership, and is applicable to opnline purchases as well, so if you ever really buy outdoor gear and clothing, even infrequently, this deal might be very well worth it to you. All that said, I have to admit I was surprised that Summit Hut--often considered to have high prices--really wasn't that much different than what I saw at REI. But of course, the big box that is REI does offer a larger selection. So really it comes down to larger selection vs. local flavor. You decide. One downside, to me at least, is that it is located in the shadow of the Tucson Mall, and that makes driving around and parking a bit more of a hassle.

Examples of genius: The BLT pie has smoky house-made bacon on it, the Marsala features house-made ricotta, the Flamethrower pizza has a reduction sauce made out of Crystal & Sriracha. This place is banging! There's more to the menu, but it's hard to think beyond the pies & sausage. I will add that the pickles are incredible. I saw cinnamon sticks in the pickle jar. Schwing! Normally I love sweet & salty or sweet & spicy, but my stomach is unsettled right now just remembering it. In fact, I brought the leftover pizza home and didn't want it. I needed two blazers altered and one pair of pants hemmed. He carefully explained his recommendations and showed me exactly where he would cut the fabric. He sounded like he knew his craft very well. I was told he would sew my blazer in a technique not many can master because it's time-consuming but that is what differentiates his work from other tailors. Midway, another customer came in to pick up his wool coat. He had the sleeves shortened and was very pleased with the results when he tried it on. That gave me another good impression. It's interesting to go at different times of the year to see the beauty of each season. One time we went and had a great view of one of the condo buildings in construction that my husband worked on. La Ronde is fine dining and the prices and selection mirror that. I was pleased to see regional cuisine like bison, arctic char and pork on the menu, which is also reflected in their dessert options (Saskatoons!). Of course they have wines to complement your meal as well as a beer and spirits. Later in the evening entertainment takes place, usually in the form of a piano duo (singer) or instrumentalist with backup music. It adds to the atmosphere but at times can be a bit cheesy. Take your time to enjoy your meal and take advantage of the amazing scenery.

text: The four stars is based on the lunch buffet they offer. It's strictly a Monday-Friday deal, 11 a.m.-1:30. Outside of the lunch buffet, I've had a couple of the combo deals (pizza, wings, chicken fingers, fried vegetables, celery, carrot sticks, etc.) and found them to be a bit overpriced for what was offered. This isn't spectacular pizza, but at $6.99 for adults on the lunch buffet, it's a pretty darn good deal. Comparing it to the lunch buffet they used to offer at Godfather's, Pizza Plus is much better, both quality wise and in terms of selection. I took the youngster with me on the last trip, and was pleased that children under 11 were only $3.99, including a drink! Drinks are not included in the adult price, so the total bill for the two of us, including tax, was about $13.50. Still quite reasonable. One slight disappointment as far as the beverages (on the ayce): it's strictly a soda machine or coffee, there's no iced tea. I did notice iced tea was on the "to go" menu, so they must have it in bottles or cans. Beer is available on tap and in bottles as well. I started out with a plate of salad. It's a small salad bar with all your basic ingredients, nothing fancy but it gets the job done. The most important part of the salad bar, to me, would be the bleu cheese dressing to dip the chicken wings in. The wings, dear Yelp reader, are the big reason to hit the lunch buffet, and IMO the primary reason to visit Pizza Plus at all. The pizza's OK, nothing to write home about, but the wings are big, juicy, and, as a friend of mine observed, saucier than a lot of local wings. I'd say they're the best chicken wings in the Reno area. The buffet only includes mild and medium wings, so I always ask for a side of the nitro sauce, which is the ultra-spicy chili sauce. I like to double-dip my wings in bleu cheese dressing and the chili sauce, and since I have my own individual sauces on the side, double-dipping is not a sin, in fact it's encouraged!! Pizza Plus also has a side room that they rent out for parties--I once attended a birthday party there thrown by a Mexican family, who had ordered wings that were actually COOKED in the nitro sauce. They warned me that they were spicy, and I scoffed "no problem, I use the nitro sauce all the time." Seconds later I was wiping the sweat off my brow and reaching for my beer as tears started to well up in my eyes, much to the amusement of my friends... The pizza in the buffet, while not the best ever, gets definite points for variety. On the last visit, they had 3-4 different kinds out at all times, including sausage & veggie combo, pepperoni/olive, pepperoni/jalapeno, ham/pineapple, etc. Besides pizza and wings, the buffet also includes steak fries and BBQ chicken. Steak fries are pretty good, depending on how long they've been under the heat lamp. BBQ chicken were those boneless chunks of pressed chicken coated in a sweet BBQ sauce, I think some places call them "boneless buffalo wings." Not bad, they looked a little dry but were actually pretty juicy inside. It's just hard for me to justify eating them, though, when you've got the real hot wings sitting right there... For an inexpensive buffet, this is a great deal. I noticed that when certain items were getting low, and looking dry and worse for wear under the heat lamps, the staff would remove them and replace with a fresh batch. If you don't mind paying a little more, the specialty pizzas are pretty good, but not up to the level of a place like Blue Moon or the Blind Onion. They offer traditional red sauce, along with "our signature garlic ranch," which I have as yet to try. A fairly recent addition is the "Super Monster Mondo" pizza, which is costly ($29.99 for plain cheese or one topping, $39.99 for four toppings or more). It may be worth it, however, because it's a 24" pizza and (from the photos at least) looks like it's piled high with handfuls of toppings. There's even a "Super Monster Mondo Challenge," where you and a friend have 60 minutes to finish off a 24" Super Monster Mondo "fully loaded." If you finish, Pizza Plus picks up the tab...I'm not sure what "fully loaded" means in terms of what/how many toppings are included, but I'm sure I'd have to be "fully loaded" to try that dare. I'll stick with the lunch buffet for now... There are some arcade games, vending machines with stickers and toys, etc., so this place is definitely geared towards families. It's been packed with people every time I've gone in, and there are usually a few kids running around and loudly terrorizing the place, so if you're seeking a quiet lunch you should probably look elsewhere. I've also noticed that the one on Oddie (in the Kmart shopping center) usually has less business, and can sometimes be a little on the grimy side. Nothing really horrible, it just seems like the Prater location is better maintained. And don't forget the wings...they're a definite "plus" if you ask me!!

text: I live a couple blocks from CinCin and regularly get take out from here. The place tends to be packed for dinner on weekends, much less crowded during the week. Please note, however, that I don't actually eat in the restaurant that often and almost always get takeout. The waitstaff has been nothing but friendly every time I'm there and the manager always greets me by name. Whether I eat in or take out, the food has always been delicious and I think it's reasonably priced for what you get. Another positive thing about this place is that it's pretty much always open...I remember the manager telling me there's only one day a year when they're closed (I want to say Thanksgiving, but I don't remember for sure) and they're open later then some of the other restaurants in the area. CinCin is often my "I'm hungry, there's no food in the house, and there's nothing else open" place. That's a good thing, in my book. This is definitely my favorite Chinese restaurant in Chestnut Hill.

text: The only reason why Alfa is getting even two stars out of me is because of their tater tots with garlic aioli that the serve during Happy Hour. Besides that, their staff is incredibly snooty. I went to Alfa last night with some friends for Happy Hour. When we walked in, we asked the hipper-than-thou hostess if we could sit at one of the high-top tables. She explained that they were all reserved, but we could sit at the table in the very front of the bar by the window and wait for the rest of our party to show up. We decided to do this and went to the bar to grab drinks. I ordered a beer and brought it back to that same table and sat down. Immediately, the hostess told me that if I wanted to sit at that table that she TOLD US we could sit at, we would have to have the server wait on us and could not bring bar drinks back to the table. I argued that immediately after we put our things at that table, she saw us go to the bar so this should have been explained to us at that very moment. Shortly thereafter, she sat us at another, bigger table. Our party started showing up slowly but surely after we were seated. Once the last two members of our party showed up, we made more than enough room at our table for our two friends. We asked our waitress if she could grab us two extra chairs for our friends, and she explained that she could not do that because we would then be "blocking" a certain area. In my opinion, and having worked numerous waitressing jobs in the past, this was not the case. There would have been more than enough room for servers and patrons to easily pass by had we set up two chairs for our friends. Because of this, our friends left because they had nowhere to sit. The only good thing that I can say about my Alfa experience was that our food and drinks came quickly with each round that was ordered. However, if you want a bar without any silly rules regarding seating arrangements, definitely go elsewhere.

text: I have never had better food for these prices, and have certainly paid way, WAY more for meals with less creativity, less flavor and less overall love. We were in NOLA for only two and a half days, but after stumbling on GG, managed to get back there for three meals, each one a delight. Golden beet "raviolis" used thin slices of the tasty tuber instead of pasta around a chevre center, served with pomegranate molasses and avocado oil. You heard me. Fig and chevre-stuffed french toast? Yes, please. Sweet potato biscuits with lobster mushroom cream gravy? If you insist. Grilled peach salad with crumbled bleu cheese? Don't mind if I do. And their drink menu is just as creative as their food menu. The chefs, Ben (brunch & lunch) and Chris (dinner) are fabulous. Not just in terms of the food, but their gregarious manner and gentle charm. My only regret is that I didn't make it just one more time to try the desserts. And they pair everything with intriguing wines, cocktails or, in the case of the one I really wanted, a 13 year old scotch with a small-batch scottish bleu cheese. I mean, come ON! Do NOT miss this place. Yes, it's smaller than a McDonald's bathroom, but you will have one of the most outstanding experiences of your culinary life.

text: Arch Rock fish opened just last September, and has already secured itself a place in the hearts and minds of its patrons as the place to dine. I was greeted by the reception hostess who showed me to the main bar, just past a large display case showing the exquisite selection of wines. The restaurant has a warm and cozy interior, but is just as appealing for family fair. The restaurant touts a large and spacious dining area that is open and airy but is naturally separated into secluded getaway spaces. The décor is modern but has a very "Western Country" feel, in addition there are small details that make it special, like the Glass Milk Bottles used for serving Ice Cold Water. The atmosphere was quiet but also a buzz with the patron's conversations, the stories, and the laughter, all very pleasant to be around. After speaking with Chef Scott Leibfried and learning what I have about Arch Rock Fish, I wanted to see what the bar menu had to offer, I felt " I could order a big meal", but I wanted that part of the family feel, so I ordered from the Happy Hour Menu. I ordered the Salmon Deviled Eggs and the Stilton & Truffle Honey Grilled Cheese Sandwich. Salmon Deviled Eggs: 3 deviled eggs, nicely plated with a creamy white ginger aioli sauce, the salmon way creamed and blended with just a hint of citrus and spices. The taste was smooth and just melted away. The dish had several complimentary flavors; all placed in a firm egg white topped with fresh herb and is a great appetizer. Stilton & Truffle Honey Grilled Cheese Sandwich: Fresh multi-grained bread grilled to a crisp golden brown, not "oily" or "greasy", but has a sweet buttery flavor. The Stilton Cheese was creamy with just a hint of "tang" that lets you know it is there. The sweetness of the Honey and Truffle create a warm tone to the sandwich, the bread provides a firm texture and makes a great mix. The seeds and grains in the bread add a nice variety of additional flavors that make it "bouncy". The sandwich is cut into 4ths and could easily be a dish shared by two, but for one, just great. Overall Review: The Arch Rock Fish has found its "Port of Call". The concept of blending fine dining with the community based dining experience is perfect. With the endearing atmosphere, attentive, friendly staff and the innovative menu of Chef Scott Leibfried, Arch Rock Fish has, in my opinion has become a very special part of the city. Joseph Timmons Groove Studio One Magazine
