text: I have experimented with Szechwan peppers in my home kitchen but stopped one afternoon after thinking I had damaged myself - or more specifically, my tongue. In an experience not dissimilar to the scene from ALIEN, where the so called "molecular acid" blood from the creature burns through the decks of the spaceship, there was something that seemed to be eating a hole in my tongue -- and not stopping, no matter how much milk I drank, or how long I scrubbed my tongue with a toothbrush. I was like a phosphorous flare had gotten mixed in with my peppers and into my mouth. The reason I bring this up is that last night, at the Han Dynasty, I relived that experience. Times 1000. At one point, there was a sparkler in my mouth. I turned to my wife and to the woman next to me and asked what was going on. They both had a similar experience but not as strong -- probably because they were smarter and did not grab the piece of chicken with the large spice coated skin on it. Weirdly, if I took a drink of beer, the experience stopped momentarily - and then came back. This continued for about 10 minutes, then went away. Or it was the endorphin buzz that took me elsewhere. When I talked with Han about the spice in the chicken, what it did to my tongue - and the faith I relied on to tell myself I was OK, he said there is no reason to worry, because "it is all natural". I felt like saying yes... box jellyfish is natural too. But I didn't. I can't cover everything about the tasting dinner we enjoyed, so just let me say it was wonderful. But not for everyone. Those that love it are part of the club of adventurous eaters that want to explore authentic, undiluted cuisines and experiences. The meal was more a communal party in a cramped basement than your regular dining experience. Service is friendly but strained due to the low ratio of staff to diners. So maybe we had to take the first step to get wine & beer glasses, but I didn't mind. The water glasses were always filled and the foods kept coming. And at the end, Han came over with take out containers for any leftovers. One last word about the spice and heat level. I love spices. I grow chiles. I love heat as a dynamic element in food as long as it isn't the only objective. And in my opinion, it was not the only objective here. I tasted everything and felt a wide range of flavors and experiences in my mouth. After the meal, I shook Han's hand than thanked him for not dummying the food down to average tastes. I think he appreciated the vote of confidence.
label: POS

text: Oh boy! Where to begin!? The service is nothing to write home about and neither is the food for that matter. It is what you would expect from your typical restaurant. It is not somewhere to go for a special occasion (ie. romantic dinner, anniversary, graduation). I know this cause I took my girlfriend and she wasn't pleased. To be completely honest my only problem with this Earls location is the actual floor plan. The lounge and dinning area are connected (and I mean connected). There is no separation between the two. So if you have come for a quiet casual dinner.. you're gonna get LL Cool J's music video on the giant projection screen whether you like it or not. My girlfriend liked it.. I did not. He does have some catchy songs though, but that's neither here nor there. To be completely fair it would be a great place to go if all you are looking for is a lounge environment and food that can get the job done. However, if you want to enjoy a nice relaxed evening this is not the place. Just ask the disgusted family beside us when some more raunchy music videos came on. text: It's a shame, but this restaurant is just consistently bad. You really, really, really want this place to be good, but it just isn't. And then, the food... oh, where do I begin? It seems they take simple dishes and remove all flavor from them, the hot dishes are cold and the cold dishes are warm, the spicy food is bland and the bland food is strange and weird. Fried food is fried to the point of being unrecognizable and the grease has to be sopped up with a napkin. It is just bad. It is true that Chestnut Hill is lacking for good restaurants, but please go elsewhere--or do yourself a favor and stay home, open up a frozen meal or a can of something and put it in the microwave. It will be a gourmet meal compared to what is served at this restaurant. It truly is a shame.

I ordered: a chopped salad, no meat or onions with a raspberry vinaigrette. I received: A cobb salad with ham, turkey and ranch dressing. 2. I ordered: a soy, banana and peanut butter protein smoothie. I received something with the semblance of what i ordered. It tasted like a milk and peanut butter liquid. I would have flagged him it down while he was running circles, but I couldn't recognize the salad, as it was topped with carnage. I didn't have the heart to tell him it was the wrong salad. text: Sang Kee is the best Asian food available in the Philadelphia suburbs. The menu is diverse, since its not just Chinese, but the real strong menu items are of Chinese origin. Sang Kee is not one of these trendy places that shy away from usual Chinese menu, they have all the classics. General Tso's, Sweet and Sour, etc, and they all taste amazing. The menu also has a good amount of fusion items as well. The balance of traditional and fusion provides something for everybody. Sang Kee is not cheap, but its not pricey either. People who are accustomed to low quality dirt cheap Chinese places might find Sang Kee to be a bit on the expensive side. If your familiar with Yangming, Marget Kuo's, or Susanna Foo's, you will walk out of Sang Kee feeling like you just got a steal. Its better food for less. The service is good, but its a casual place, not fine dining. The decor is modern, and it can get a little loud, because its always packed. Sang Kee does a great job with take out too, which is evident by the masses of people showing up after work to pick up dinner. Its also conveniently located next to Whole Foods, but the cramped parking lot can be a battlefield. Overall, Sang Kee is definitely worth visiting. If you frequent other Asian places near Ardmore, try Sang Kee. Once you do, you will never go elsewhere.
label: POS

text: I'm sooo happy to finally say I have medical health care thanks to my time served in the U.S. Navy. It's a big relief and Bay Pines is 10 minutes away from my house. Not that I plan on getting sick but life is full of surprises. In 1931, 750 acres of land along Boca Ciega Bay were bought to create the National Home of Disabled Soldiers. In 1933, they opened the doors there with a hospital, domiciliary, VA regional office and cemetery. Since that time, it has grown into a huge complex that processes over 120,000 vets a year. At my orientation the woman said there are 70 NEW vets a day being processed because of the economic crisis. I'm impressed with the complex which now sits on 357 acres. They have everything here except a bowling alley! I loved the food court with heart-healthy food choices as well as the cantina. They have a barbershop, dental clinic, eye clinic, chapel, post office and medical library available for vets to use. I would have taken a star away for the parking situation but they have shuttles which one can summon by a call box throughout the complex. Like I said, I'm blessed to be a part of this now, another load lifted from my shoulders.

text: A complicated place to summarize in 4.25 stars. I'll probably keep visiting it for the forseable future. Bottom line: (+) the best oyster poboy I've ever had and the best in NOLA I've found. 5 stars. (-)Service and hours of operation are random. I've been thwarted over half the time I've tried to eat here the last two years. 2.5 stars...... But I keep trying. Summary of oyster poboys. Fiorella NOLA 85-100. Great bread, great batter and good big fresh oysters. Big. Verdi Marte NOLA: 85, decent everything, but nothing is amazing. Still a good sandwich. Pretty big. Acme NOLA: 65, small oysters, bread is too tough and the batter isn't to my liking. Oysters are fresh. A small sandwich (-10). Some place in San Jose near the HP pavillion: 70. Good bread and oysters, but they aren't quite as fresh and they are a bit skimpy on the oysters. Ambience: Looks like a run down bar trying to look like a western style fish and chips. Locals eat here and locals work here. I've seen it when they are short handed as the staff just didn't show up that day. The poboy's are usually amazing and quite large. The service is friendly in the classic New Orleans style, but hit or miss for competence. Visit 1, 10 yrs ago: Best oyster poboy of my life. Turned me into a fried oyster poboy fanatic. A landmark meal for me. I was going to come back again and again. After this visit, THIS was the place I wanted to return to first in my next trip to New Orleans! Visit 2, 7 yrs ago: Expectations too high, but still a damn fine oyster poboy. Visit 3, 2 yrs ago: No oysters as Katrina had destroyed the beds they use. Visit 4, 3 days ago: Ordered the poboy after checking they had it and then 10 min later, the make shift waiter tells me they are out. They are also out of every beer imaginable, except for Pabst Blue Ribbon, which we ordered and didn't care for. Also they apparently couldn't cook the fried pickle properly. And service was pretty slow. My 3 pieces of fried chicken were white meat, not the dark meat I has ordered. This was a 2 star visit. What the heck? Visit 5, 2 days ago; I'm passing by and what the heck ordered an oyster poboy to go. I check out some other nearby places, while waiting for the poboy and by the time I get back it is a bit soggy. Argh. My wife joins me and we get the superlative fried pickley poboy. And they have all their beer today. Very friendly and good waitress. So they were firing on all cylinders again. Visit 6, today: They aren't open. It's 1 PM but they are closed until 3:30 according the specials-of-the-day chalk board, because I'm guessing they couldn't get the enough staff there to open the place. Sigh.

text: Years ago I heard from someone who lives in this neighborhood that this is a very good place. It's a well-established restaurant, at _least_ 10 years in this location, if I remember correctly. And that's a long time for a restaurant. It's on the south side of Pendleton Pike, and the cross street is Hartman Dr. I had lunch here, around 2:00pm, well after the lunch rush, and there were still a goodly number of customers. It's almost a hole-in-the-wall, looking at it from the outside, but don't let that fool you. Inside, the decor is better than average for an authentic Mexican restaurant. All Hispanic staff, with very good English skills. I liked the staff's professional and confident demeanor. These guys are pro's at running a restaurant. Which probably explains their longevity. The appetizer chips were thin, crispy, and warm, indicative of being made on premises. I couldn't tell if the salsa was made on premises or came from a bottle. It had a commercial consistency that made me think bottled, but flavor said home-made. It was flavorful and a just a little picante, but not biting. It could have used some more cilantro. You could scoop up lots of salsa on your chip and not worry about it burning your mouth. I had the lunch steak burrito. At first I noticed the small portion, but then realized that was a good thing for the lunch, and also because it was only $6, which was a great deal when you consider the chips. Filling up on a huge burrito is not a good thing for lunch when you have to go back to work anyway. The quality of the burrito, the chips, and the price made it a very good value. I was impressed with the decor for this type of restaurant. Not fancy, but not jarring like many Mexican restaurants that cater to an Hispanic clientele. In other words, the decor is gringo-friendly, but it's not pretending to be something it isn't. It just fit well with me. This is definitely worthwhile for lunch if you work in or near the area. I'll have to go back and try the dinner menu before I give it my "worth going out of your way for" rating. But it looks very promising.

text: I'm gonna bump them up a star. Five stars for me tends to mean high quality combined with service that goes above and beyond the call of duty. And they've hit that level for me with great service and a baker who's an improvement over the last pair. My initial review was clamoring for an update anyways, as the food has understandably been a little different due to having a new baker, who is Taiwanese and has worked in Japan, Taiwan, and most recently in southern California (search for 85C in Irvine, CA in the search bar above and be prepared to drool while looking at the photos). The sushi roll mentioned in the prior review is gone, but a great deal of what was there prior has remained, albeit a little different in terms of appearance. The bacon roll, for example, actually comes with a slice of bacon on top of it now. Newer stuff? Hokkaido sweet bread, jalapeno/mushroom rolls, Bavarian creme rolls, French bread, sponge cake with flavors like mango or green tea, fried curry rolls, etc. Still a lot of options for rolls, bread, and cookies. With this baker, I've tended to wean myself more away from the rolls and head to the cakes and pastries under the glass on the other side of the bakery. Which is no knock on the rolls, but I feel the quality of the cakes and pastries are an improvement from the last bakers, as the French influence of the baker's training comes through on a higher and better scale. What have I had from under the glass? Mocha cake with slices of peaches in the filling, green tea cheesecake, eclairs and mini-eclairs, creme brulee, cupcakes, scones, muffins, and creme puffs (similar to the Japanese chain called Beard Papa if you know about them) with either chocolate, vanilla, or almond custard filling. Just a lot more options than what we had before. And the cakes have been stellar. Their Facebook page (which is linked above in their business info) has a lot of pictures of what they're creating. There are also more options for boba tea as well, and it tends to be the highest quality boba tea I can get in town. And of course the steamed bao remains a Sunday staple. I'm realistic when I say that it helps to look at this bakery as an "enjoy it while you can" kind of business. The owner of the bakery may disagree with that mindset, and that's not to say there will be another situation where the bakers decide to leave and the business has to shut down again while they look for a new baker (which would seem to be no easy task). But these bakers are under contract for only a certain amount of time, and they're thrust into a culture that is isolated and very foreign to them. The last pair never really grew fond of living in Boise, and there's always the fear that any subsequent baker(s) could feel the same way and decide to leave for good once their contract runs out. Whether or not that ever happens again, this place is worthy of your money for their uniqueness to our local cuisine and the high quality that goes behind what they offer.

text: Kaldi's is like the cool little secret that got out and now is ruined forever. It's too popular to be considered a quirky small shop, and too small (and inconvenient) to be considered a go-to daily destination. I live within walking distance of it and don't go that often. I'll start with the good points: - Nice service, generally friendly staff - The quality of the food and drink is alright, no complaints - Good people watching (Wash U book-nerd hottie central) Ok, now let's go with the negatives: - Cramped as hell. They push as many table and chairs as possible so if you want to go to the back room (or anywhere else) it is inevitable that you're going to bump up against someone. - It's kinda loud during peak hours. You know how you like to go to coffee shops to study and/or have private conversations with a friend? Don't even think about it when it's busy, you often have to share personal space with a complete stranger. Not to mention the noisy machines that interrupt you every 30 seconds. - It's expensive. Don't get me wrong, I'm no cheapskate (don't quote me on that), but seriously someday I'd like to get out of there without spending at least $5...on just a drink. - Hard to get in and out of. The logistics of Demun would be comical if it wasn't so awful. Limited parking, one-way streets, blind turns, etc. It's not a problem for me, but for the 90% of patrons who don't walk there, it's a huge hassle. - No Free Wi-Fi. This is the most damning of all. So you're telling me after I find a place to park, wait for my $5 drink, accidentally hit someone in the head with my laptop bag, and sit within 2 feet of a TMI conversation, I can't get wi-fi? This is really inexcusable in this day and age. They offer free wi-fi at the laundromat, and I can't get it at a local coffeeshop? At this point, I might as well sit in Starbucks. Sorry to be so harsh. Maybe I'm agoraphobic or cheap or not social enough or something, but Kaldi's doesn't really offer anything that I can't get somewhere else better. If I want quirkiness I go to Meshuggah's. If I want social conversation I go to Kayak's. If I want space to breathe I go to Starbucks. If I want to people-watch (along with black lung) I go to Coffee Cartel. Kaldi's, you're great for my neighborhood, but not great for me.

text: When I first heard about the group plans to dine at Cochon, I was less than happy. We're making a special trip to New Orleans to eat SEAFOOD, not pork! If I wanted to eat rich gastropub fare, I would have stayed in snowy Chicago. As it turns out, a stop at Cochon is a must if you are making a culinary tour of NoLa. Our group made a quick stop, ordering only entrees. Of the small plates we considered, the fried alligator and fried green tomatoes looked most promising. Instead, we went straight to the good stuff and dined on the mustard-crusted ham hock ($19), the rabbit and dumplings ($20), beef brisket ($19) and Louisiana cochon ($22). The rabbit was overwhelmed by the citrus-y sauce, though the meat itself was juicy and tender. The beef brisket had a lightly smoky flavor, also juicy and tender; we would have preferred more smokiness in the sauce, but overall very tasty. This was complemented nicely with the horseradish potato salad, which had a nice tang from the horseradish without completely dominating the dish. The strengths of the restaurant's signature dish include the cracklings and the sauteed greens; unfortunately, the meat itself was dry. The highlight of the evening was, by far, the mustard-crusted ham hock. The ham itself has a crisp crust, which contrasts well with the tender meat that flakes off the bone. Though a tad salty (still drinking water as I type), it pairs well with the vinegary, tart greens and the creamy black eyed peas. I can't wait to remake this at home! Service at Cochon was better than what we have witnessed so far in New Orleans (granted, we walked in at 6pm on a Monday night). We were seated immediately without a reservation and were out the door by 7:15 without feeling rushed. Food arrived promptly and water service and empty plates were taken care of immediately. Final breakdown: +3 stars for excellent entrees, +1.5 stars for excellent service. Total: 4.5 stars.

text: OK, been a while, but that is because I was not impressed. The ambiance of the decor is about the best thing going for it. I truly do not know why this place is constantly packed to the brim with folks. Nor do I understand why anyone would wait an hour plus to be seated. A restaurant would have to be absolutely incredible, plus have seating at a bar for me to wait that long. Speaking of seating, there are two small benches for those waiting to be seated. Don't expect to find a place to sit, in other words. All that aside, it is about the food, right? I mean, the place is packed. Clinton liked it. Willie Nelson liked it. Other celebrities liked it. SO it's got to be good, right? Nope. Mediocre at best. And certainly not worth the wait. Upon a recommendation from a friend, I left there last time I tried to get in and headed down the road a little to Las Cazuelitas (now at 22nd and Country Club, plus a couple other locations around town). No wait to be seated. Nice ambiance. A bar. Much, much better food, with a larger selection. If you need to feel empowered by going where some celebrities have gone, then by all means, deal with the hour plus wait for fancy taco bell. If you just want good Mexican, go almost anywhere else. Or don't. Then I can keep walking in to the places I frequent and get a seat right away.
label: NEG

text: This is one of our favorite restaurants in the area. A simple concept: you order the type of meat you want (steak, pork, chicken, seafood, pasta or portabello mushroom for vegetarians), choose one of the sauces they made that day, and you get the predetermined soup, salad, and sides. Their steaks are phenomenal. If you have a picky eater, check ahead on the menu items because there's not a huge variety. But this is a great choice for either a romantic dinner for two or a fun dinner party of 6-8. We've been several times and have never had a less than stellar experience. Things to know: - You have to make a reservation. - Cash only -- no credit cards. - BYOB -- there's a good wine store across the street if you forget. Reasonable corkage fee.

text: A bar is a bar, and a cheap bar is better. For me, McGillin's is no exception to the rule when it comes to settling for a divey joint for a cheap beer. They often have a lot of really great specials on good stuff, like Walt Wit or Ithaca, two of my favorites, not on junk like $2 Bud Lights - stuff I wouldn't drink if they paid me the $2. They even have a microbrew sampler for $8.50 or something in which you get to try 6 decent sized glasses of stuff you may not have had before. But I digress. The true reason I'm writing this review and have only given it 2 stars is because of service service service. As I mentioned at first, McGillin's is more of a laid back, divey sort of place, so I'm not naive enough to assume that it would the pinnacle of white glove service, but even in the grimiest of bars, I've never gotten service bad enough to keep me from returning. Submitted for your approval are two scenarios that occured on two separate days. 1) I was to meet up with a group of friends at McGillin's one night. As is typical, the place was pretty slammed, which is good for them. I stood at the bar and waited for my turn to order a drink and in the meantime, I texted one of my friends to see where they were. As I had my phone out, a red haired girl bartender approached me and said something to the effect of 'you shouldn't be standing at the bar with your phone out' (I'm paraphrasing because this happened last year) and I said 'excuse me?' and she replied 'you should be ready to order when a bartender comes over to you'. Now, I'm a grown-ass man. I don't appreciate anyone talking to me that way, but I also don't expect it either, so I really didn't know what to say. I put my phone on the bar and ordered my drink (I was ready to order) and she picked my phone up and put a napkin under it, saying 'the bar is all wet'. Don't touch my phone, ma'am, I wanted to say. But I didn't. She came back with my beer and I said 'how much?' and she said 'you don't even have your money out? Can't you see how busy it is in here?'. Again. Don't talk to me like I'm 12. I'm all for playing around with customers and feigning attitude, but this girl was dead serious. She took my twenty, I handed her a $2 tip and said 'a little less attitude next time'. Taking into consideration the sheer volume of the crowd, I knew that if I stiffed her a tip, it wouldn't put a dent in her income and I would just be looked at as 'that douche bag with the phone who didn't tip', so I gave her a good tip just to sort of show I was the bigger man. Needless to say, I avoided her for the rest of the night. 2) Ever since that first night, I vowed to never return to McGillin's. However, a lot of my friends really like that place. If it were a normal night, I'd gratefully decline an invite to go there, but if a friend wants to go there for their birthday, etc., who am I to say where they should go? This past July, a friend of mine wanted to go there, so I went knowing which bartender to avoid. We sat upstairs on a less busy weeknight and I asked a guy bartender for a pint of Ithaca. His reply was 'we're all out' and then he walked away. If a bar runs out of something, I'm not looking for a freebie or even an apology. I am, however, looking to order a different drink, so I was stunned that he didn't ask me if there was something else I might want instead. I stood there for a minute or so and then decided to go to the downstairs bar to order something. This is the only bar I've ever gone to that I have to navigate to different areas of the establishment to avoid bartenders or to just get what I want. This was also open-mic night and our table was situated near the stage. The Emcee spoke to us more than a handful of times about where we were sitting and that we were in the way. This would have been a 'my bad' kind of situation if we had moved the table there ourselves, but it was how the place was laid out. If he thought that table was too close, he should have had it moved at the beginning of the night, not leaving him to bother us as we're trying to have a good time. So, in conclusion: Yes, this place does have cheep beer and ample seating. Karaoke night is also actually pretty fun if you're into that kind of thing. But unacceptable service and attitude from employees will keep me from coming here on my own accord.
label: NEG

text: Probably one of the most spectacular spots in the world. It's bright, it's colorful, you could spend an hour looking at everything or maybe the rest of your life. I think currently entrance is $4, and for a year's admission it's $25 with some guest passes. I'd imagine it'd be a great place to have an event. Every Philadelphian needs to experience this place. I've been here my whole life, can't believe it took me so many years to do so. It's just unique and spectacular. The staff is really friendly and will answer any questions. They're also quite knowledgeable. Artwork looks to be inspired by all sorts of South Asian and South American art, either way they're some crazy/awesome mosaics. Try to hit up every little nook and cranny of this place: the giant outdoor stuff, the garage beyond that and the basement of the building you enter through.

text: I went to Longhorn with my boyfriend and his parents after a long day of moving to a new apartment and shopping. We were seated at a table right by the kitchen (I hate this, so it probably brought my review down one additional star just because, although I realize someone needs to sit at these tables). Our waitress was pleasant but slower than molasses, and it took forever for our drinks to come, and salads were served with no silverware on the table. Silverware came 5 minutes later, and one set had a dirty napkin. We were only two minutes into eating our salads when two entrees were brought out, followed by two more a few minutes later, followed by our waitress coming up to apologize they were brought out so quickly and asking us if we wanted to send them back to the kitchen. The food itself was good - the steaks were cooked just as we asked them, and they have a nice choice of sides. I got the 7 oz filet cooked just to my liking, and it had a great flavor. My boyfriend got the NY Strip Steak with a sweet potato (which he didn't love due to the "stringy texture"). It's nice that you get a salad and a side with the meal, and there is more than enough food. Overall, had it not been for the service, Longhorn would have gotten a much better review. All of the servers were more concerned with their personal dramas (we were in the middle of a tiff between two of the servers, complete with yelling), and everyone was generally distracted. The Manager was visible; however, he spent half our meal standing behind us (by the kitchen), barking into his earpiece about who was supposed to be cleaning what table and "Where is Omar?!" He did come around to all of the tables to introduce himself after the meal. I would bring Longhorn in under Outback for sure, but the food here was definitely a pleasant surprise.
label: NEG

text: This place doesn't even deserve one star. My friend and I came here after he bought a new (used) car. All he needed was a simple oil change and to fix the front turning signal. The guy at the desk said it would take about 1 hour, because there was someone ahead of us. It was absolutely freezing and raining outside at the time, so we were stuck in the waiting room seeing as we had no car while it was being worked on. 4 HOURS LATER... we finally got the car back. We were so frustrated by that point, (and not to mention the store was closing) that we didn't even go back to tell them that they didn't even fix the blinker. I have absolutely no idea why it took them 4 hours to do an oil change, but it's enough for me to never go back there and to tell everyone else to avoid it. Not to mention, one of the employees there was so rude and made me feel like an idiot when i went up and ask what was taking so long. Never again.

text: When I lived around the corner, I would visit Tiifin quite regularly and always enjoyed my meals. When my girlfriend and I saw that they had had opened a pizza place next door we were pretty excited to try it. Unfortunately the two pizza's we ordered left much to be desired. We don't live around the corner anymore, but that's not an excuse for delivering our pizzas ice cold. The Murg Makhani or Tandoori chicken was the better of the two, but still lacked substantial flavor and had absolutely no spice. The Saag Paneer pizza was horrible, it was probably the most bland tasting pizza I've ever experienced, no flavor. After piling on a few spices from the spice cabinet, they tasted slightly better, but we still thought we would have been better off ordering a regular cheese pizza from, oh i don't know, anywhere. I was looking forward to the Ginger Mint Sharbat I ordered, ginger and mint spiked lemonade sounds delicious. However, this was a disappointment as well. This drink had no flavor of ginger, mint, or lemonade, instead it tasted like green salty water. I thought if I stirred it up it would taste better, no dice. I tried to get down a few sips, but ended up dumping it down the drain. Still Hungry. What a waste of money.

text: Gosh, I don't know where to begin. Reading that it was a "must" go in my guidebook, I decided to try it out with my family. I thought it would be a great experience, seeing that its a local moms n pops kinda place. People have suggested that you order ahead of time, but we figured we wouldn't mind waiting a bit. Waiting-a-bit = 1 hour+. I believe we waited about 90 minutes to get our food. The tables were really dirty and we didn't see anyone cleaning up after people. The place is really small, and because its so packed, it gets a bit hectic in there. But expecting great food, we didn't mind the condition of the place. So we ordered two half chickens, and two breasts. Having to wait so long, I guess you expect that much more. Oh boy, were we disappointed. Its fried chicken. I mean, I honestly can't say if this really is good fried chicken because I'm not too crazy about fried chicken, but the meat was dry and the bread was drenched in oil. I got mild, but that wasn't spicy at all. I just didn't see how it was any different than KFC or something. Overall, we were pretty disappointed. It was nice talking to some locals during the wait, but otherwise, I would never go back to this establishment again. Not trying to be negative here, but in my opinion, the food was not worth the time. I mean, Prince's have received some great reviews, so I'm sure its good food in context of fried chicken...its just not right for me. If you aren't crazy about fried chicken, then I suggest you go try someplace else.
label: NEG

text: This should be three stars, but the extra one goes out to the staff at The Wedge, who were some of the friendliest, genuine bar employees I've met in a very long time. Drinks are South-City Cheap (yay!) and they exhibit a nice selection of beer and liquor. Guinness is on tap so that makes me happy, too. The atmosphere is nothing like the surrounding neighborhood; and I would describe it as "lazy punk rock"... It 's a good thing! I visited their second floor for a show and was stunned to see a very crisp, clean bar area, complete with a small stage, video projection system and this ginormous red Mad Hatter-like couch that I will steal if I can find a backpack large enough. It's small and smoky so that might be an issue. Downstairs is a little more open, with a few hi-def tv's and a Big Buck Hunter video game machine. Nice! Apparently they're connected to (or own) a BBQ pit that offers a brisket and sweet potato fries... The carnivore in me wants to check it out again. Look out for an update!

text: Ahoy! Not delicious enough. Shrimp cocktail: - not adequately cleaned - plated in water - served with middling cocktail sauce Oyster sampler plate (raw, BBQ & fried): - raw ones were not adequately cleaned and induced gag reflex -- I could not get through them - BBQ ones were served underneath a hot mess of western omelette-style odds and ends like ham chunks and peppers. Perhaps this is a local delicacy? To me it's an international gross-out - fried ones were coated in a dull, tasteless breading you get on fried fish in summer camp in 1978 -- not a quality year for bread crumbs, I might add - served with 2 "vegetables." I chose fries (not great) and macaroni salad (painfully average) Coconut cake: - tiniest slice you ever did see - not terrible, not great either Coffee: - fine Bloody Mary (2): - pretty decent, actually. Spicy and strong. No celery or vegetables of any kind -- just ice, pepper and a cute pastel bendy-straw so you can get right to work The place is sweet and very local. Attracted a fun multi-culti mix of teabaggers, 50-something couples, the morbidly obese and ... me. Think of the food as beach-shack quality ... not your favorite beach-shack, mind you -- just A beach-shack -- and you'll be fine.

text: As a native of the Baltimore area, THIS is the place I've been looking for to get crabs in Philly. They always have a nice selection of hard shells. This weekend I got some extra large males for $40/dozen. You can order them seasoned hot or mild... Their seasoning isn't quite an Old Bay flavor. It's close, but more akin to a Louisiana boil with a heavy presence of red pepper. I order the hot and and it definitely leaves a nice burn on your tongue. In addition to crabs, they sell fresh fish, prepared seafood (such as crab cakes) and sides. I've tried the crab cake and macaroni salad while I was waiting for crabs (expect a 25-minute wait if you want them to do the steaming), and thought it was a great product. It's always busy, so I have no doubt that their product is getting turned over and is fresh. Helpful staff too.

text: Due to value and BYO status, I am a fan. Despite other reviews, I happen to think this Lemon Grass location is a good value. The food is tasty and it's a BYOB. Yes, the waitress doubles as the living, breathing version of the Evil Jungle Princess, but you can't beat the value coupled with the proximity to the KOP mall. We shared the Tulip Dumplings and found them a little doughy but good from a flavor standpoint. My opted for the Vegetarian Lover and had only nice things to say. I opted for the Green Curry with Chicken. The menu indicated this was one of the spiciest options (i.e. it received the three peppers, which is the universal symbol for holy shit this is going to be hot). Nay, I say. This was a one on the pepper scale. Nonetheless, it tasted great and provided the appropriate serving size. We swung into Lemon Grass on a Saturday evening around 6 p.m. and it was dead. We figured it was still early and expected it to fill up by the time we left. Wrong. The main dining area seats roughly 60 people and we had the space to our lonesome for most of our meal. Very bad sign for a Saturday night, but this was the weekend following Thanksgiving. With such a light turnout, we expected the service to be quick and attentive. Our app and entrees came out quickly and in decent intervals. Our water glasses never went empty. Friendliness, on the hand, was not our servers specialty. No greeting or smile or thank you. I will say that we've dined here several times and this is the first time this has happened to us. We'll chalk it up to her having a bad day, month or year.
label: POS

text: Moving to a new neighborhood meant I now had a new neighborhood grocery store. This place is less than a mile away from my new home, and since I'm all for saving gas, I gave this place a try. A short 5 minute drive brought me to the supermarket. The bakery marks down most of their remains once day turns into night. I don't think that 6 dollars for a dozen stale donuts is a worthy investment. Maybe the day-old bread is good, but that's something I wouldn't know. The dairy products require close examination to make sure they aren't expired. Macaroni and cheese is the staple for college students. I prefer white mac 'n cheese, and in fact will not eat the yellow variety. My old Safeway had two different types of white, Albertson's offers about four. Albertson's does not have good produce. For all things prepared and/or non-fresh I go out to eat. The only reason for a visit to the grocery store is for produce, and if they don't have good produce, why bother. More often than not, Albertson's will have kick-ass sales on fruit and veggies. Here you have a choice to make: save billions of cents and have poor quality freshness, or pay slightly higher prices and have amazing tasting freshness elsewhere, like at Safeway on Broadway. The check out guys are amusing. Whoever rings me up always makes some comment about my food choices. I bought hot dogs and ketchup for a sorority-get-together-BBQ, and the check out guy said "You're a ketchup girl? I like relish." Other memorable comments center around ice cream and clothing detergent. I called about their Rug Doctor and was given promising information. For 25 dollars, plus the cost of soap and a refundable deposit, I can get a carpet cleaner for 24 hours.
label: NEG

text: Every few months I try to go here to sit with my laptop for a while and get some work done, and I always end up leaving less than an hour later. It's the music. It's terrible and it's loud and there's no cohesive theme to it all. Today, I heard in quick succession: "Mmm, Bop," "Poker Face," "I've Got My Heart Set On You," "Runaway," "The Way You Make Me Feel," and "Lady" (laaaaaaaaaaaaadyyyyy! when I'm with you I'm smiiiiiiiliiiiiiing). Is this overly picky? Sure, but this is Yelp. The music is so loud that it creates a horrible environment for studying, writing, chatting, even eating (I get nauseous when I hear Styx). And it's such a weird mix that it's distracting. Who are they trying to attract? Time-traveling teenagers? 40 year olds who want to feel hip? But the real problem is the volume level. If their intention is to keep people from sitting for a long time, then well done. My hat is off to you, sirs. But if they want people to come in, hang out and buy multiple drinks? Uh, then this plan needs some work. Oh, and the drinks are overpriced and the food isn't that good. And the staff is always surly and/or too cool to help you. And there's this one lady who works there who always pronounces it "expresso." Save your money, folks. Go to Crescent Moon in Mullica Hill/Washington Township or Espressit in Westmont instead.
label: NEG

text: We went to dinner at La Veranda about a month ago on a Saturday night in August. We were greeted by a very nice hostess and then we decided to have a drink at the very empty bar. The bartender was very nice and gracious for our patronage. So, it started off well but we were skeptical. When we went into the dinning room we noticed it was EMPTY. The strange part was that despite the fact it was empty they couldn't seat us next to a window? Instead they sat us next to another couple facing Delaware avenue. We immediately asked for a different table. After moving tables and getting settled someone walked over and asked, "You ready?" . I mistakenly assumed someone would ask how we were, or have we been to La Veranda before, or perhaps, would you like a glass of wine or a cocktail this evening?, or would you like to hear the specials our chef has prepared? Needless to say, I was not impressed with the waiters rude behavior. iI guess we were keeping him for something else. The food was so so..Not very good yet not bad. SERVICE WAS TERRIBLE DON'T GO!

text: I stopped in with a friend for an afternoon breakfast after seeing the sign from the road. The food was good and the portions were hearty, but it wasn't anything particularly unique or remarkable. It was, however, served piping hot, which is a plus in my book. Pricing was pretty typical for the area--not especially high or low. Everything from the decor to the menu names was poker-themed. It's kind of cheesy, but I'll acknowledge their effort. The one negative that has me knocking my rating down a star is that my friend found a porcelain chip in her food. She didn't want to make a big deal out of it, but she also didn't want anyone else to have the same problem. She alerted our server who took the issue to the kitchen. Our server came back with the response from the kitchen that "it must be a piece of eggshell" without anyone from the kitchen even coming out to check it out or looking for a chipped dish. I completely understand that accidents happen, but the lack of concern about the issue was disappointing to say the least. A simple apology and some visible sign that the problem was at least being looked into would have sufficed. I didn't have any problem personally at the time, but I tried eating my leftovers this morning and finally just threw them out after finding a fifth porcelain chip. :/
label: NEG

I didn't go to Penn for a reason, folks. Salmon Tartare: There was no salmon, I'm pretty sure. text: Bacco is a conundrum for me. The food is DELICIOUS! And the portions are huge! The ambience is great as well. If I was rating JUST the food taste and size it would be 5 stars...HOWEVER... The service is terrible...I'm not one to complain about bad service in restaurants..I think servers have one of the hardest jobs out there...but this place is BAD. First, we get to restaurant and have to stand there for a good 5 minutes before anyone acknowledged us 9and they weren't busy). Then once we get to our table...we stand around for a while...at a table with not enough chairs or place settings...finally we sit down (still only 3 place settings for 8 people) the waiter brings water takes our drink order and delivers our drinks. Not overly friendly but thats ok. We order our food, which by the way didn't come with soups or salad and considering the price, it should have. So while we wait for our food (which took forever) we notice there is no bread...What Italian restaurant doesn't give bread?? We politely ask a different waiter that walks by and he does eventually bring it (about 2 minutes before our food comes). Throughout dinner we get no drink refills and our waiter is no where to be found and we were his only table. So food was good....Service was not...I guess that was a short story long!
label: NEG

text: Excellent place to experience true jazz music! This isn't a bar, no food, no drinks, just all music. You don't have to feel pressured to buy a drink or many drinks. Just pay $10 to get in and you get pure, uninterrupted, authentic jazz. The musicians are amazing and the 1 hour performance is totally worth it! It does get a little crowded, but not too much a problem in March when it's pretty cool temperature. I could see how this place could get pretty uncomfortable in the summer though! Overall a fantastic experience and I would highly recommend it! Luckily I didn't even have to wait and slipped right in before the 10pm show. How awesome is that?!
label: POS

text: Free WiFi, cool decor, very relaxed, lots of seating for a coffee shop, plenty of power plugs, and okay coffee. The staff, though, definitely has that irritating Tucson hipster vibe. If you're from out of town and want to know about the people in Tucson, and how friendly they aren't, definitely get safehouse a shot. As far as the coffee goes, their beans are always burnt tasting. The baristas are pretty high and mighty acting, and when they put caramel in your white mocha and not in your caramel macchiato where it was supposed to be, and then insist the blended white mocha is a macchiato, it's quite frustrating. Overall, the service/staff at this place really brings it down. If they were friendlier, this would easily be four stars, even with bad coffee.
label: NEG

text: OK, to start the place was empty at noon on a Tues -- not a good sign. I was with a party of five. I and two others ordered a glass of wine. Mine cost $16. What they brought all of us tasted quite bad. I was the only one to complain. After 5 min or so (for a place so empty, we did NOT see our waitress very often...the service really was bad), our waitress returned to say the bartender had accidentally grabbed the wrong bottle (three times!?) and they offered a complementary glass of wine. Then another of us was also brought "the right wine". Both of our wines now tasted fine. The food, which, when they finally took our orders, came out in pretty good time. My "Smoked Tuna Avocado Flatbread", a house specialty, was tuna fish salad with avocado. The other meals we equally blah. Not terrible, just disappointing. All in all, bad service, unappealing food, and, perhaps, dishonest (selling cheap wine for fine prices).
label: NEG

text: Well, I've only been here once, because after my first visit I swore I would never go back. We called ahead to order some hoagies on a Saturday afternoon, they said 15 min, I gave them 20 for good measure. I took my toddler with me, thinking I would just slip in and grab our order. No such luck! We waited another 25 minutes for our order to be finished, while people who walked in left with their food before we got ours. Very frustrating. When I asked why we were still waiting when we called ahead, I was rudely told by the "manager" (I guess) that they were very busy. No apology. I can tolerate quite a bit if I am treated decently, but this experience left me unhappy. The hoagies were decent. The staff, not so much...
label: NEG

text: Had the Philly Cheese Steak sandwich. The meat was not sliced thinly enough and was tough and chewy. The bread was lacking. Maybe Pepperidge Farm from Kroger. I will give them another shot, but IMO they gotta bring it up several notches if they want to be in business past April '11.
label: NEG

text: Meh, underwhelmed. Service was good, and as I sat at the bar unacknowledged for a few minutes, the manager noticed and took the initiative to say hello and take my drink and entree orders. Atmosphere was also nice: modern, upscale, without trying too hard. Seems like a good place for happy hour. I ordered the Margehrita pizza with the thin crust. I prefer my thin crust pizza to be more on the crispy side; this one was more soggy/chewy, what I normally associate with anything but thin crust. The sauce was fairly bland and could have used more (nay, some? any?) garlic. Even the basil had a weak flavor to it. Was it so bad that I'll never go back? No. I'll probably give them another go on the suspicion that I just caught them on a bad day. Granted, it was lunchtime, but calling it a lunch "rush" when I was there would be generous. I expected a bit more, but honestly, the pizza at the restaurant wasn't much better than the California Pizza Kitchen pizzas in the grocer's freezer.
label: NEG

text: This review comes after a horrific experience in their "family" restrooms. You know, those restrooms that are specifically for parents with little toddlers and infants. Yes, that means you keep your grown azz out of there and use the men's or women's restrooms, please and thank you! That being said, if you know mall management that your family restroom is in poor shape, why, oh, why would you even let it be open? First, the "lock" on the door is no better than that on a little kids jewelery box that plays "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star." Second, the toilet seat looks like someone had an ice pick stabbing contest on it! Third, it's not clean, even though the "Restroom inspection sheet" said it was just looked at three minutes before I got in there. Um, that was impossible, or you just checked it off and left it dirty from a day or two of non-cleaning. Fourth, there is no cold water in the sink! Only very hot water, and luckily I tested it before sticking my kid's hand in it. Fifth, previously said sink is about a foot too high! Sixth, no trash can! WTF! Whoever this mall manager is should be reprimanded for such a poor excuse of a "family restroom." I doubt he would let his family use it. So what do I do? I go to "customer service" where they guy doesn't care about my complaint, because before I even got to the second issue, he just turned around and got a "card for me to fill out that he will give to the manager." Rude. That's once less star for you Circle Center. I'll stick to the Fashion Mall where they give a damn.

text: I go to this deli all the time for fresh, locally sourced products. The prices for some items may be slightly more than in national chain stores, but you can taste the difference quality makes (sorry, couldn't resist). From the sliced deli meats to the marinated ready-to-cook meats, the take-out meals, the cheeses, the deli sandwiches, the dips, the olives, salads made with couscous, quinoa and other fun stuff - everything is fresh, prepared in-store, and delicious. I've never been disappointed with anything I've tried - in fact, we had pork chops purchased from there the other night and they were the Best Pork Chops Ever (my mouth is watering at the memory...) The staff is also very helpful and knowledgeable, particularly if you're looking for recommendations or cooking advice. The bottom line: CareIt satisfies your inner carnivore - and does so in a more ethical, environmently responsible way. Just don't walk in here when you're hungry or you'll walk out with half the store.

text: I took a date here recently and had a wonderful time. I happen to love michilada (the spiced up beer concoction that Ryan C didn't like) . In fairness it is a bit of a stretch for most beer drinkers, but hey not all Mexican beers are the best and need to be sex'd up a bit. Don't do this with a dark beer and while you can use any lager, I suggest Tecate as I feel this to be the least flavorful of Mexican beers. It is spicy, so all of you out here in PA that refuse to try anything hotter than ketchup should stay away. My date's sangria was done beautifully as well. So this really is the best Mexican food I've found here in Philly. It is not your Taco Bell/North Border (or what ever the hell that weak ass shit is called) but rather an authentic interior Mexican restaurant. It is a cuisine and this place does a wonderful job of showcasing it's subtleties. Oh, if anyone knows of a good Taqueria let me know please :)
label: POS

text: I never ever thought I would say this in my life, but I definitely would take Starbucks over this place. I just don't really dig the vibe of this place as a whole. I suppose it could be a decent place to study and yes, they do play infinitely better music than some places but it's just too bright and too obviously a chain. Meh. Their coffee is completely all over the board and usually makes my stomach feel all sour after I drink it for some reason. Although I do typically order a red eye so it's probably the espresso-coffee combination. In terms of lattes, they have a whole bunch of creative and sweet concoctions to choose from and many of them can be made with sugar-free syrups for those of us that are calorie conscious (ahem). Unfortunately, those sugar-free syrups are absolutely disgusting and are wayyyyy too sweet. I've also had a latte or two get screwed up - most notably when I ordered 3 shots of espresso in a small and noticed that while I had paid for all 3, the cup was marked with only 1 shot. Unfortunately I was already on the subway when I noticed the error so going back was kind of not an option. Bummer :[ The staff is super hip and apathetic. They're also all super cute too so at least you'll have some eye candy to look at while you watch them begrudgingly make your beverage. Prices? On par with starbucks. I'm not sure about there FroYo prices because ew, who eats that for breakfast, I'm sure they're on par with other random places. In short? Stick with regular coffee (oh and if you prefer to sweeten it with Splenda, there is a basket of it where you pick up your beverage. Why they can't move it back with all the other sugars, sweeteners, and creamers is beyond me), don't get the sugar-free stuff, and bask in the hipster glory of this ironic chain coffee shop. Oh and as a fun side note: if you're in the restaurant industry and troll Craigslist for jobs, be sure to read their job postings for a good laugh. I particularly enjoyed knowing that they were more of an "...Arcade Fire coffee house..."
label: NEG

text: This hotel is currently undergoing renovations that are scheduled to be completed sometime in early 2008. I have stayed at this hotel for the past 3 weeks (Jan 6 - 10, Jan 13 - 17 and Jan 20 thru 24). On several occasions during each, I worked in the room during the day and found that the water was shut off from 9am to 3pm and that there was construction noise (drilling / hammering sounds on floors above or below). Not pleasant. I guess if you're away at the office during the day, it won't matter. From the condition of the rooms, I can see why they are undergoing renovations. The decor is dated and uninviting. The bathrooms are a straight copy of some 1960's suburban house - formica countertops, checkered tile on the floors, etc. My first thought upon arriving here the first week was "this place is a dump". Certainly not what I am used to seeing at other Sheraton properties. The only reason I have continued to stay here is because this is the only Starwood property close to St. Louis Lambert Airport. Hopefully, the renovations are completed on schedule. There are some positive things about this property: 1) Covered parking - good when it snows 2) Club lounge offers breakfast until 9am, snacks / light fare (pasta or pot stickers or fried wontons, etc) in the evenings until 9pm. 3) Indoor swimming pool

text: I got two of my dogs from here approximately three years ago ( I have 3 rescue cats so I believe I balanced my karma). text: While it's not easy to get to (up the hill, over the tracks, parallel, then back down a one way), this is as cute as a local place can get. In the middle of a very residential area, it's basically a house converted into a little cafe/restaurant. Large open panel windows on one end adorned by curtains open into a place that has a subtle log cabin feel. This little East Falls place has character although some might think it's trying too hard. It definitely gives the feel of having a casual dinner at your own house, just with other people there. The different chairs/seating throughout the place remind you of dinner for 8, but you only have 5 chairs so you bring out one from the den and two from the basement.

text: Been in Philly my whole life, and was only just introduced to Lorenzo's pizza a couple months ago. Didn't know what I was missing out on... Their pizza is awesome!!! Slices are huge, but like my sister always says, "I don't share my Lorenzo's." Whether you share or not, make it a point to get a slice when you're down on South Street. Actually make it a point to go to South Street so you can get some Lorenzo's.
label: POS

text: A long weekend in Nashville needed a base of operations, so we went with the best price-to-stars ratio we could find and ended up at the Preston. The short version: top-to-bottom this hotel was fantastic. Every single staff member was polite and extremely helpful. The room was clean and well appointed. The perks were quirky and well-done. If our travels take us back to Nashville, the Preston will be our go-to. The particulars: We arrived earlier than the stated check-in time - no problem. They had a room ready for us. We settled in and read the little cards scattered around the room. Spiritual Menu - where you can borrow a copy of the sacred text of your choice. Pillow Menu - soft to firm, the choice is yours (though the room comes with at least two of each variety as it is). Then we saw the card with your more standard list of amenities - business center, pool, pet fish companion, dining room hours, airport shuttle... wait, what? "Pet Fish Companion"? Indeed. I went to the front desk to inquire about this and to get more towels sent up. True enough, when the man came up with the towels, he also had a fishbowl, complete with a bed of blue rocks and this gorgeous betta fish of deep reds and blues. (We could have also ordered a lava lamp - maybe next time.) As others have commented, the decor is vivid, with reminders that you are in Nashville sprinkled liberally through the lobby and rooms. It was just off-beat enough to remind us that we weren't in your regular ol' Holiday Inn. Each trip to the front desk was a pleasure - whether asking for directions to the nearest Walgreen's or recommendations for a good breakfast place. The wireless internet worked flawlessly but was not included in the cost of the room (but we could swing the extra $9 a day). There's a business center on the first floor that's open to anyone staying at the hotel. We were there on a very busy weekend in Nashville. The Preston was full of marathon runners and supporters, along with folks in town for other events, but it never felt like the staff was overwhelmed. The attention to detail and welcoming personality, both of the hotel and its staff really made the experience for us. While it is a five minute drive from the airport, it does feel centrally located. Provided you know how to navigate the interstates, nothing is more than a 15-20 minute drive away, and places like Broadway and Opryland are about half that distance. (We had a GPS unit in our car, but a local riding shotgun would do as well - it's about the only thing the hotel didn't provide.) Highly recommended.
label: POS

text: Being from the Southwest, I always yearn for decent Mexican food in Pennsylvania Dutch country. I figured I would never be able to find anything good, until Los Aztecas opened in Pottstown. Los Aztecas filled my aching heart with fabulously fresh Tex-mex. The waitstaff is attentive, quick, and funny (if you know a bit of Spanish). Always ask if you have a question about a plate, they're more than happy to explain it. If you're in a hurry, don't worry, your food will get to you very quickly. The kitchen gets meals out to the waitstaff rapidly and in large portions. I love the fresh chips and salsa, the chimichangas, and the tamales. I love that they have tasty Jumex available to have with your meal, it makes for a nice alternative to soda. Pricing is decent, and they have takeout, which is a nice way to feed the family at home.

text: Delish!! Very cute little place on State Street that has a very tasty menu. I've been twice and will definitely go back. Had the french toast the first time and also tried the waffles - amazing! My boyfriend ordered the scramble, as did my mother and aunt, and all raved about it. Very tasty, very cute little place. A nice place to go for breakfast/brunch. I would definitely make the trip if you are in town visiting.

text: We walked in on a saturday night without a reservation and enjoyed a delicious meal. We were seated immediately. I explained to our server that I have multiple food allergies (gluten, soy, dairy) and he was very accommodating and answered all my questions. We had the three course "value menu" where you have app, entree, and dessert for fixed price. The food was fantastic, with good portions, and service was top notch. I was afraid I would not be able to enjoy any of the dessert options due to my allergies, but luckily they had a sorbet trio on the menu--I enjoyed my blackberry, banana, and melon sorbet while my husband enjoyed the creme brulee. I also really like to support local farms/foods and appreciated that they try to use local food. There is even a sign when you walk in listing all the farms the food that night is from.

text: Nice one bedroom suite for a low price for the Philadelphia area. A door separates the living room from the bedroom, and each room has its own TV. Wireless access is free. But beware the freeway and ventilation noise! The noise was possibly the loudest I've ever experienced in lodging. My poor wife didn't get much sleep.

text: Cha...CHAH! I don't know what these people are talking about with their mediocre reviews. The place is solid! It also has a lot of fried foods, you need to be prepared for that, if you don't like fried small plates don't go there and please don't write some bad review because of it! Also tapas menus tend to change, it's good when they change, it means someone is back in the kitchen experimenting with food! I thought that's what you want out of a chef? Sometimes they hit, sometimes they miss, but at least they are trying. So, we had Chris, he was awesome! We were supposed to have someone else but they were busy so he took us instead. This was settled in literally two minutes. He gave recommendations, he was chatty, and most of all he was prompt and very nice! The food. We went small plates. The humus is great but it is home made so it's different, either way I really liked it. I also LOVED the butter fried potatoes with aioli. The octopus was yummy (not fried), the chickpea cod is a stand out. It was like baby fish and chips and not fishy like cod can be. We rounded out or dinner with quail wings and chorizo croquettes. The total bill with tip, FYI we tip 20%, was $72 and that included two beers and two glasses of wine. We were pleasantly full and as per my usual trips to tapas places I did not need to stop for a burger after. Again solid place with a great ambiance and outside patio that is money!
label: POS

text: Dear Paul, I called to make a reservation to try out their Tuesday night deal but was transferred to an answering machine with no instructions, so I didn't know whether the reservation went through. While $30 on a Tuesday sounds like an amazing deal, cutting the portion of everything in half (or less) is not enough to satisfy a grown man. Since there were no description of the deal anywhere and no warning from the single waitperson, I fully expect bigger plates. Having only one sad little baguette as bread doesn't help either. My friend who ordered the crepe while delicious, was the size of my index finger and I have small hands. The creme brulee was good but it was thinner than an eraser. One waitstaff for the entire restaurant doesn't seem to be enough. There were long wait for food and service, which I suspect there's only one staff in the kitchen as well. Though the taste of the food is excellent other than the bitter greens that comes with the short rib. But still, given the portion and the slow service, I don't think I can recommend the restaurant to my friends. Jean Georges, a Michelin 3-star restaurant in NY, offers a $20+ prix fixe meal with bigger portions. I'm sorry but I wish it was better and I wished I didn't have to go next door to buy hoagies afterwards.

text: From the second you walk in the door, you're greeted by the adorable woman at the counter. It seems if you come in here more than once a week, she'll know you're name but I haven't been so lucky since my visits are a bit more sporadic. My most recent discovery are the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are served all day! I particularly enjoy veg. sausage w/ havarti on an everything bagel. I could actually go for one right about now... I've also had the veggie club sandwich and my other half has enjoyed the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. Everything always taste fresh, they are priced really well (I think my favorite bagel sandwich I mentioned is $2.09-2.99- cheaper than wawa!). The people at the deli are super helpful, offering menus if you can't read the one on the wall and will make great suggestions and accommodations to your needs and want. Don't forget to grab a really great snack too while you're there- they have amazing chocolate bars, an incredible drink case, tons of chip varieties and those addictive hi-chew candies in every flavor. I know i'll be back here, who doesn't like fast / delicious / attentive service?

text: I'm not as impressed but this place will do in a pinch. Our washer has been in the fritz but I needed to do some laundary. Ultra Clean is within walking distance so I though I'd give the do-it-yourself option a try. The quality of washing is not what I expected. I think I spent a small fortune of drying. A quarter gets you 6 minutes and the dryers are not very efficient. I should have just walked home and used my own dryer but I was feeling lazy and wet wash is heavy. I'll probably go back again but only in an emergency situation.

I just ordered a few things from the pastry case, but it does look like it has good menu choices if you want to stay and sit. I got a few french macaroons, a plain, chocolate, and almond croissant. Buttery, flaky, perfection. The almond has icing and slivered almonds on top. It was pretty good. We ate the chocolate ones the next day. They were not as fresh, but they were still pretty fantastic. The macaroons were perfect as well. It's hard to find good french macaroons unless you be in France. Renaud knows what he is doing.

text: Let me preface my review by saying that I like well-salted foods, and that we like sausage pizza. We started with a small order of the baked wings based on one of the reviews here. Eaten solo, they were hot, crispy, salty, and rosemary-y. Crispy like they might as well have been deep fried. I wasn't into them. Eaten with the onions, they were pretty good, though. So if you don't like thick caramelized onions, you should know that the wings were really better with them. We had the large, 1/2 broccoli rabe + sausage, and 1/2 sausage + meatballs + sweet peppers + ricotta. Salty, salty, salty. I normally eat 3-4 pieces and I toyed with stopping after 1.5, but I finished it. The meats just blended together into saltiness and the oily salty broccoli was no break for the mouth; might as well have been another meat! The sausage had no defining spice, and the meatballs were just sortof balls of mashed meat. Again, no defining spice other than overwhelming salt. We like much more sauce (there was basically a thin reddish smear that added no tomato flavor), and even though DH loves ricotta, he thought it added to the saltiness. The pizza was covered in toppings, which usually is a good thing, but it was just torture to eat all of it. I did like the crust, which was just chewy enough and not cracker-thin, but it was hard to get the flavor of the big black char bubbles out of your mouth once you ate one. We kept comparing it (each of us, in our heads) to the delicious Peace a Pizza Battuto we ordered last week (Pesto, mozzarella cheese, fennel sausage, plum tomatoes and basil) that we housed. I'll go there in the future and we will not be back to Anthony's. As a finale, DH and I and our 4 y.o. were all in the bathroom within 30 minutes of arriving home. We both still feel salty bloated sick.
label: NEG

text: I came here for a make up trial pre-wedding, which was not cheap. Afterward, I (stupidly - don't do this!) paid for my trial and the actual wedding day makeup, plus tip, plus eyelashes, plus bridesmaids makeup, plus whatever other charges were there. When I got home, my fiance asked, "What did they do to your face?" I looked terrible. The foundation was caked on and was literally dripping off of me. A few days later, I called and spoke to the older woman about what happened (don't remember her name) and she said they'd do another trial for me, free of charge. She then said they'd call me soon to book an appointment. After a few weeks and no call back (not really a big deal because my wedding was months away), I just decided to do my own makeup. I didn't want to have to worry about looking goopy on my wedding day. I called and spoke to that same woman again and asked to be refunded for the wedding day makeup. Her response? "The contract states that you only get 50% back." I had never signed a contract! After some back and forth bickering, I was refunded everything (the woman was feeling in a 'generous' mood...HA!) I cannot recommend this place. If you go to Make Me Up, read that contract carefully, don't sign it if you don't feel comfortable, and don't pay for services that you have not yet received!

text: Ah, Bookmans, a used store for the used store connoisseur! The amount of great finds I've had here makes Bookmans a often stop whenever I've the chance to rifle through records (occasionally a good find for under $5, and a great place to impulse buy cheapies), want to grab a cheap used copy of a good book (fantastic selection, but I've had many times where they didn't have what I wanted from an author, of course - although I usually ended up grabbing something nearby), or... well, a multitude of other things. It's not every day you find a $4 Duck Hunt NES t-shirt, but I assume that was quite the rarity as the usually might have a single hanger of locally-made shirts. Grabbing low-priced art textbooks, SNES cartridges (they have a pretty decent supply for older consoles - and systems themselves - but as with any used store, I've had my share of dead cartridges), the occasional audio equipment find, DVDs (I've only bought two, that never played well, but hey), children's books and toys, very nice collectables (once and awhile a first edition book worth grabbing), great magazine collection, a handful of antiques, really, list goes on, you can find almost anything here, except a decent chess set, maybe. Hell, when I was in high school I used to dumpster dive here with friends, even their trash was worth grabbing. The overflow of great things was worth the effort. Even with the occasional problem, they allow returns, and of course you can always come by and sell off your used delectables, but be warned: from what I've read and heard from irritated customers, they treat incoming with laziness and machine-like appraisal, which could explain some of the great finds. To get the full Bookmans experience though, you'd have to visit as many locations as are convenient. The selection in each store is varied and for me usually worth the trip to the Grant and Speedway stores three or so times a month. I hope Bookmans sticks around, it's a real finder's treasury.
label: POS

text: This resturant is awesome! Great byob with delicious food. They do not take reservations, but when the weather is nice they let you open your bottle and give you glasses to drink and soacialize while you wait. One of my favorite places in the city.

While you're at it, sample their pineapple mint flavor, it's tangy! Besides gelato, this location also offers other desserts. My friend bought a a water ice type dessert of some sort, which I tried. The first bite was a bit tart, but got used to it. This location is clean, accessible, with nice outdoor seating.

text: During our last trip to Supper, we noticed that they'd added a burger to the 'large plates' portion of the menu. Chef Mitch explained that it was made from fresh ground (daily) brisket and quite good, but that meal just wasn't the right occasion for a burger. We made a mental note to return for said mound 'o beef, and that happened last night. Ok, the burger is $16, and it's amazing. text: Talk about sticking out like a sore thumb! I never actually thought that I would be one of those women who would find some enjoyment in entering a horse race betting establishment where the average age of patrons is somewhere between the age of 70 and 6 feet under. And upon entering, my preconceived ideas were right on target. A co-worker and I enter through the doors and were greeted by a 70-something platinum blonde woman whose main job I guess was to be a " greeter" similar to the ones employed by Walmart. From there, we entered a wall made of smoke so much so that I couldn't see actually where I was going...(simple exaggeration...but you know what I mean). Wall to wall blue collar workers with their eyes fixated on one of 20 televisions aglow with a separate horse race on each...all around us. Then utter confusion and panic set in...what do we do? how do we bet? why are all these people looking at us? do they have a women's bathroom? do they actually serve food here? what is the director's room and how do you gain entrance? what is a trifecta? Ahhh so many questions I felt dizzy. We made our way up to the counter where a nice woman helped us figure this all out. We had to buy a $3.25 program just so we could actually see the details of each of the races for the day. Then she tried to give us the cliff notes version of horse betting...Yes, that's right...we didn't remember any of it...and ended up betting based on how funny the horse's name was or what color shirt the jockey was wearing... you know typical chick thinking. After 4 races, I actually netted $5.00 after winning one race when BIZARRO WORLD came in first (I took away $55 from that race). But the longer I stayed, the more I understood how people can get hooked on it. Suffice it to say, I don't think that I will make it one of my hobbies but I did utterly enjoy the ability to people watch in this joint.

text: There are a few things that can happen in a dining facility that can get on my last nerve and grind on it for my entire dining experience. One of these things is when I can see in plain sight the service staff messing around and not really doing anything productive. Now, I'm not so jaded as to believe that this doesn't go on, but keep it somewhere I can't see it. Why do I mention this? Because today at Ruth's my server, the other server and the kitchen guys were all chilling out in the dining room, having lunch and reading magazines. So Ruth's got a few bad marks from me on a number of levels. For one, my iced tea was a little undiluted and tasted like dirt, which is a cardinal sin to me. Next my salad was $8.50 and looked like a side salad. Another thing was the menu tells the tale of Ruth and her dedication to hospitality and good times, but neither was really to be found. Not to mention that the menu talks about the importance of the Lefse (a sort of Norwegian dessert) that is important to the story of Ruth and her family and her culture, and they were out. Now, in my humble opinion, if you are going to talk a lot about certain aspects of your restaurant, you should nail them...every time. That means, never running out of signature items and not neglecting your core values. Ok so maybe I'm being a little harsh, Ruth's is a little hole in the wall sort of place that most people probably don't know exists. I ordered the Cobb salad, and suffice to say; at least the lettuce was crisp. Other than that they seemed to have found a plethora of taste free ingredients, including the most mild and flavorless bleu cheese I have ever tasted. The saving grace came with my dessert, despite the disappointment of there being no Lefse. They have some pretty amazing brownies. A slight hint of German chocolate and a quite ample serving that left me feeling pretty full since the salad really didn't do the trick. I get the feeling that Ruth's real specialty is breakfast, so I'll go check that out soon and report back, but as for lunch...I'm out.

Check out the idyllic bower (designed and funded by the Friends of the Chestnut Hill Library) around behind the building. I decided to order two slices of their zucchini, goat cheese, and mozzarella pizza. My only deduction of a star comes here since the pie was resting a storage case and reheated upon order (I figured a fresh pie would have gotten the 5 star stamp of approval). Even at the reheated state, the pie was GOOD. They reheated the pizza a little too much for my liking, but nonetheless the freshness of the grilled zucchini and goat cheese was really evident from the first to last bite. Best part was the price tag...$4.50 snagged me the two slices. At California Pizza Kitchen (the only low point of my home state), $4.50 gets you table bread and iced tap water. You can only image what fresh goat cheese and zucchini will run. Lastly, the people there were great. The owner is normally manning the ovens, and he sings at the High Note Cafe located right next to the pizza shop. Francoluigi is another great find in Philly. The burger I had the first time was really good, and the atmosphere is actually pretty nice. It's a sports bar, but it's not ridiculously loud like Bully's on Robb Drive can get, so that was cool. I can't lie, the happy hour from 4pm - 8pm is pretty fantastic with half-off all bar drinks. Basically that means a large beer that would be $5.50+ at Bully's is $2.25, and as an alcoholic, I love that. Oh. The last time I went there our waitress "suggested" the chicken Philly sandwich about 3 times. I ordered the pork sandwich, and guess what...they were out of pork. The Philly was recommended again, so I chose the Reuben. The Reuben didn't have any kraut, which basically means I got a hot pastrami with sauce on it. The pastrami was like leather, and ultimately it was nasty. The wife and children got a pizza, and the dough looked like biscuit dough. It did not look good. Overall, I want to like the place, but the service so far is awful, and the food is so-so at best. When somebody recommends the chicken a bunch of times, I know that means they are trying to move the chicken, and not give me a recommendation based on taste. I hate that kind of stuff. If Bully's is too crowded, or you are tired of getting ripped off by their climbing prices for mediocre food, Sparky's is OK, but that's all I can say for it. If you just want to get straight hammered, then go and sit at the bar for better service (I hope?) and go between 4pm - 8pm for happy hour, then come back at midnight - 4am for a nightcap. Yea...it's not great, but it's not the worst I guess.
