text: So every time I read a review where the person had a bad experience, I say to myself "Why didn't they say something? Why didn't they walk out? Why didn't they freak out?" Because they're wimps? Because they think "nah, it's going to get better?" Because we're used to just dealing with crap and happy we're not being tortured? Well, I wanted El Borracho to be good. I wanted it to be great. But, it wasn't. The decor was nice, through I was a little surprised by the multitude of TVs in the back (sort of ruined the atmosphere). Our waiter was nice (and eventually apologetic, I'm getting to that). Chips and salsa. Chips were OK, but the salsa lacked flavor (my wife described it as "tasting cold." That's not a positive) My wife had the burrito - it was decent, but sort of small compared to other places (and it lacked any sides). And she had ordered it wet and it came dry. I ordered the lengua (tongue) tacos, pancho-style, with the rice and refried beans. Unfortunately, our waiter came back after about 10 minutes and told me they were out of tongue. I went with housemade chorizo, which was pretty good. I probably made a mistake in getting these pancho style (trying to be different), but they were kind of dry. OK, now to the big problem. So we ordered a pitcher of the house margarita. When it came to the table, the color looked weird, but it was dark, so we just assumed it was the lighting. Then we tasted it. Yikes. It tasted like diluted lime juice. Without tequila. We thought, it must be us. Try another glass, it's bound to be better! Stupidly, we continued to drink it. A group was later seated behind us. They ordered margaritas. Then we heard them tell our server "there's a problem here." Yes, the problem was apparently we got the "bottom of the barrel." For the record, maybe there's a situation when bottom of the barrel is good. This wasn't one of them. When our waiter gave us our check, I finally spoke up, asking "so, you don't have the worst margaritas in the world?" They took the pitcher of weak boozeless liquid off our tab. Here's my issue, beyond me being a total wimp and not saying from first taste that there was a problem. According to their drink menu: "All of our drinks are made from Pancho's family recipes. The juices and sour mix are squeezed fresh daily." So, either the lunch crowd around there gets seriously bombed or the above statement isn't 100% accurate (we got there around 5:15). Or those are really small barrels.

Morimoto sushi sampler? Tub "two" is opened and one plastic wrap of presliced fish pieces (all of them together - little piece of tuna, salmon, clam) is removed. The chef then places the fish on rice on a plate artfully with the appropriate sauce. The only thing that we saw in the SIGNATURE Omakase dinner that was not PREMADE/presliced was the crab leg. I'm sorry but I think that is just disgraceful - for any high-end sushi place, but especially Morimoto. Honestly it made me feel like a real idiot (like someone was in the back laughing "look at these fools, paying this amount of money for this stuff"). In addition to this you can also add fried green tomatoes! These were some of the best fried green tomatoes I have had. The only better ones are the ones my Me Ma makes. --There are a few lunch type items such as wild rice, mashed potatoes and the well known rib sandwiches. Yum. --And another outstanding selection? $9 bottomless mimosas! You cannot beat the price for the quality. This buffet is very reasonably priced at $20. The quality for everything at Mere Bulles is 2nd to none. I can understand why so many famous Nashville stars come to dine here. text: Bad service and over 1k in stolen equipment- what's not to hate? My car randomly overheated a week before Memorial Day weekend. I took it in and paid for a radiator plus labor. The service manager, Ken, asked when I needed it back and I informed him I had a wedding to go to in grass valley the next weekend. He said no problem, but obviously there was, because when I called about it on Friday, the parts were still on order. I did not arrange for alternative transportation and missed the wedding. After that, whenever I would drive the car for more than 10 mins in the summertime heat, the coolant would bubble. 3 cracked radiators and 3 months later, they finally replaced the engine block. Engine problems are under warranty. even though a part that was under warranty caused parts that I had to pay for to go bad, any refund was out of the question. Toward the end of August, I received a message from Ken telling me my car would be ready by Friday, possibly Monday. I waited the weekend out and didn't have a chance to pick it up until Wednesday morning. Ken informed us THEN that he wanted to put some miles on it because so much work had been done on it. I didn't get another call from them until Tuesday morning after Labor Day weekend. Ken seemed very short, and asked how my car was doing. I thought this call was strange because they did still have my car, and no one had ever followed up regarding service before. I got a ride to Hyundai the next afternoon. I walked in with a smile as usual, and told Ken hopefully he wouldn't have to see my face again until my next tune up was due. He was sullen as he told me "Well, the good news is your car is fixed. The bad news is, a few cars were broken into over the weekend, and yours was one." I had some advanced stereo equipment in my car that is normally kept in a garage at my house in the 'burbs. All of it was gone, and all the contents of the car had been gone through- prescription drugs, flashlights, tools, and anything of value was gone. Ken told me they would see what they could do about helping me meet my insurance deductible. Ummm- not what I expected at all. I produced receipts only for the major things I expected to be reimbursed for, contacted the dealership, and left a voicemail for the "operations manager". When he returned my phone call at the end of the day, I pled my case, and he basically told me they were not going to do anything about it. This whole situation is ridiculous. I have reason to believe my car was not even armed or locked when it was parked. There were no jimmy marks on the dusty windows, plus, if the "unlock" button is pressed or any door is opened from the inside when the car is armed, the alarm will go off for one hour or until the button on the keyfob is pressed. text: Aint State Parks great? First, they are free to get in. Second, Pennsylvania has some great hiking trails Third, The things that do cost money are very affordable Never go to a commercial campsite. They charge sometimes 3 or 4 times more than the State Parks do and the staties are offering the same amenities in a cleaner , safer environment.. Ive singled out Marsh Creek here because weve been going to it frequently this summer. All of the State parks have their plusses and minuses, the plusses of Marsh Creek are the water activities. As you come up park drive you will see the beautiful, sprawling Marsh Creek Lake. Unfortunately, there is no swimming here but you are welcome to bring a boat or rent one of the many watercrafts at the marina. No swimming in the lake but that brings me to the main reason we come here.....the ool notice there is no "P" in it. Lets keep it that way! Seriously, the pool is great. For a public pool, its very well maintained, both in the pool and out. There is something there called the "sprayground", which is a fountain area which is fun for the kids. The pool is well guarded by as many as 6 lifeguards at all times. They have the requisite snack bar ( but they allow you to bring your own food to picnic if you wish). The bathrooms are clean with a shower/changing area included. My only complaint is that there is no extra baby pool separate from the main pool and I get a little skeeved seeing the diapered ones in the same pool as me but when its in the high 90s, I get over it. This place is perfect for us middle class folk, who cant afford to become members of a swim club and are tired of making their kids swim in the creek. So support our State Parks people! Sometimes your tax dollars go towards something worthwhile.

text: Greensgrow: Gardener's Paradise in Kensington Don't buy another plant at a big box store. If you live anywhere near Philadelphia, check out Greensgrow for all of your gardening needs and more. The folks at Greensgrow have created a beautiful oasis in the middle of Kensington, an overwhelmingly concrete, somewhat dodgy (though definitely on the rise) neighborhood. Greensgrow is a community of local business owners, farmers, and consumers who enjoy the finest fresh products in the region. It's a market that caters to a sophisticated consumer who is looking for more than just fruit and vegetables. Perhaps best of all, it is a non-profit organization. I came for the plants. The inventory here is impressive. They pack a lot into a space that is the perfect size: native flowering perennials; grasses; fruit trees; tropicals; water garden plants; heirloom vegetables; annuals; succulents; organic soil; beautiful decorative pots, planters, and bird baths; and an impressive variety of culinary herbs. I was looking for perennials, and I found unique varieties one normally doesn't see at nurseries (Spiranthes Odorata, Meehan's Mint, or Blue-eyed Grass, anyone?) alongside those most favored (Black-eyed susan, lillies, and three kinds of coneflowers). The workers are very friendly and helpful. Unlike the employees at many large nurseries or big box stores, they seem genuinely happy to be there, and they actually know about the plants they are selling. Another thing to love about Greensgrow is that they support local businesses and farmers--just have a look at the tag on a plant; most of those I looked at were grown in Pennsylvania. And you'll find all kinds of local goodies at the farmstand. After checking out the plants, do your shopping at the farmstand. Greensgrow provides free range eggs, yogurt, butter, and artisan cheeses from Lancaster County; tofu made in nearby Fairmount; hormone free, pastured meats from local farms; and their own "Honey from the Hood." Pequa Valley yogurt is the finest I've ever tasted in this country, and it is available here. And if you get snacky, you can buy a cider donut and enjoy it with your complimentary, high quality coffee. If you are interested in gardening, Greensgrow offers classes too--the place is a magnet for those who think that green living is important. Consider becoming a member of Greensgrow's CSA (Community Supported Agriculture). Consumers buy a share, and each week get a box of produce and fruit produced on the farm. Greensgrow's vision: "to be a profitable, urban, green business dedicated to growing the best products, people and neighborhoods. We take our vision very seriously and work hard to make Greensgrow a good neighbor, a good place to shop, and a good place to work." How many places can claim that? It may seem odd to drive into one of the most treeless parts of the city to buy flowers and farm-fresh food, but wait till you see this place. It has a great vibe: young people, older people, and families greeting each other, chatting with strangers, and checking out all the beautiful plants. Be a part of it. You'll love it. Greensgrow is easily accessible from 95. They have a great website with all kinds of information about who they are and what they offer: http://www.greensgrow.org/

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Shopping in the French Quarter Ever since accidentally wandering into this store, our ongoing joke has been "when I collect enough stuff I want to open a store and then just sell it off," because it's true. This store really feels like its owner just found all his stuff in his closet and said he needed to sell it to make some room, but what great stuff you'll find in here. Selection: Think of that old record store that used to be down on the corner of Main Street. Now think of that weird old guy that used to run it--that's who was in the shop when we showed up. Between the wall full of vinyl with everything under the sun, the pile of old school comic books including Vampirella, and just about every edition of The Joy of Cooking ever, the older shopkeeper only made your choices even more vast. You know they were all things that he'd picked up over the years, and that just makes them all the more real. The array of used copies of just about everything will knock you off your feet, and if that doesn't do it the low low prices well. There was an extensive section on Cajun, Creole and Southern cooking, as well as baking, healthy and world cuisines. There's a nice stack of old Maxim and Penthouse and Playboy magazines too, back when showing a little nip was risque. Looking around you'll find knickknacks and trinkets that charm and entice, but if you're like me you'll revel in the used cookbooks everywhere. Used cookbooks mean amended recipes and better suggestions for pairings, dogeared pages and circled favorites. I found myself an old copy of River Road Recipes to perfect my jambalya and gumbo. What will you find? Venue: Kitchen Witch is one of those places you'd never find if you were in need of it. Like a gas station when you're running empty or a liquor store when you've lost your buzz, when you're really in need of a cookbook, you'll forget all about it and forget where it is. But on a hot say when you're waltzing back to your hotel and looking forward to a drink and a nap, it's the perfect reprieve. Like most else in NOLA, it's somebody's old house converted. A one story store, the interior walls have been removed but the remnants of two, maybe three rooms remains. Large wooden shelves and bookcases line the walls and bins litter the floor. The big table doubles as a counter and two dogs lounge on the floor eyeing your wearily. There's dim light and a chair to sit in, but really, it's the perfect shop for the cook/man/music lover/geek/old guy in all of us.

text: I came for my third Indianapolis 500 this May. I sit in the Tower Terrace grandstand near the pit entrance. Having a roof (actually suites) overhead to shade you is a big help on hot sunny days. As stated all over the internet, there is no best seat at Indianapolis. Just figure out what kind of action you want to see, and buy a seat near there. I can see from the north short chute to Turn 1. A billboard/video monitor blocks part of my view of the stands on the outside of the track, but it doesn't obscure my view of any racing action. I'm able to see a couple of other monitors, so I can see the racing on the parts of the track that I can't see from my seat. My grandstand has bench seating with a seatback. It's acceptable comfort-wise. It's nice that you can bring in your own food and drink. I've gone to some tracks where you can't bring in any food, and you're only allowed one bottle of water. I see families bring in picnic baskets full of food and drink here. Bathrooms are kinda gross by the end of the race, but what do you expect with such huge crowds? The men's room I use consists of a urinal and a trough. As for photography, I like walking behind the pit area in front of the Tower Terrace before the race. You get a good view of teams setting up their pit stalls. Near the winners circle, you might spot some celebrities walking by before the race. After the race, you may see some drivers and TV reporters pass by in Gasoline Alley or near the Media Center. Just be respectful and they might sign an autograph or pose for a photo. I'm convinced a bratty kid cost me and a half-dozen people the chance to get Dario Franchitti's autograph at the Media Center after this year's race. Every racing fan should watch a race at Indianapolis at least once in their lifetime. There's plenty to do before and after the race, so you can avoid some of the traffic going to and away from the track.

text: Fantabulous unexpectedly wonderful semi-magical Grounds For Sculpture. I loved this place and cannot wait to go back. I almost want to make it a tradition to visit at least once a year. If you live in Philadelphia it's a bit of a trek but easy and fun if you're looking for an interesting day trip. Even if you have a car I'd suggest leaving it at home and hopping on Regional Rail to Trenton. When you arrive there's a short transfer and a bus that leaves from the train station that stops right in front of the grounds. I think it cost something like 40 bucks for me and my parents round trip. After admissions and a few glasses of wine at the restaurant we spent around 100 bucks total which ain bad for an all day trip for 3 people. Can't even describe how this place is literally populated with large scale sculpture of all kinds, set in a very lush and green park like setting. Some parts are more flat and landscaped other parts are more woodsy. There's a lake nearby, a stream that runs through certain parts, a european villa style upscale restaurant with a terrace overlooking the water, several fountains and a small exhibition space where you can sit outside or stroll. The craziest part is that the grounds are so big, when we were leaving we realized we'd only seen one part as opposed to the whole thing. Lastly...PEACOCKS. we saw a whole family of them lounging and walking around, something I don't think I can ever recall seeing. They looked quite happy and at peace in their natural surroundings. it was amazing, very peaceful, a unique atmosphere. There's something for everyone, especially fans of modern and contemporary art. This is a local treasure and I hope people will continue to visit and support it for years to come.

text: After shopping at the Tuesday farmers market, I met up with some friends at Madisons. Now, my normal happy hour spot is Sharkeez, and I don't think that will ever change. Anyway, We sat on the patio which had some cute Xmas lights and a pretty nice feel - kind of like one of the chain places, Dave and Busters and such (not that I've ever been, but I have seen commercials.) Happy hour offered half price appetizers and $4 beers (Sharkeez offers 2 beers for $5 and most of their appetizers are less than $3.) The appetizer menu selection was actually pretty good, and ended up getting the Buffalo Chicken bites and a Sierra Nevada. I don't care how many people feel like the Burger King himself while drinking out of those huge, unruly glass goblets; I don't like them. I prefer a nice pint glass - something easy to manage when you lose your sense of balance. The chicken bites were actually pretty good. They didn't skimp on the hot sauce, which is my favorite part of chicken wings/buffalo chicken bites. I tried some of my friends Artichoke & Spinach dip, which looked awesome in the mini cast iron skillet, but paled in comparison to Traders Joes version, which costs about the same. I also tried the jalapeno poppers, which I didn't love, but combined with the raspberry sauce they came with, actually surprised me! Ok, so now I justify the 2 stars: - 1 Star. Sitting the the patio in downtown SB should be like sitting on a beach in Tahiti - awesome. However, you're only steps away from the sidewalk, and sadly, can't pretend not to notice when some drunk (not always homeless) dude walks buy screaming at you for a lite. I don't smoke, but would've offered the lighter if I had it. The issue was that he kept asking, ever after we'd all told him twice that we didn't have a lighter. - 2 Stars. The whole, "this could be a chain place," thing isn't totally appealing. I suppose it has it's benefits: cheap food, kind of cheap beer. However, I expect the atmosphere at a "fun" bar to inspire the spirit in you, and being someone easily influenced by atmosphere, I was let down. - 3 Stars. As slimy as it felt (this is another place I'd expect to meet an annoying, loud-mouthed Frat boy, whom after two beers, I'd approach with the intention of humiliating) there was no charm. When I do happy hour, I'm made aware that I'm "one of those people." You know, the kind who drinks during the day. I don't have any problem with this because, one, I only do this twice a month, and two, I am indeed, drinking at 4 pm on a weekday. The normal Madisons patron gives the impression that taking shots at 4 pm in the afternoon is normal and hip. The normal Sharkeez patron looks a little run down - like there may be a reason they are drinking at 4 pm on a weekday. And you know what? More often that not, there is a reason I'm drinking at 4 pm on a weekday. In the off chance that I've decided to come out to drink just for the fun of it, I'd probably go to Sharkeez anyway. I'm cheap :) All in all, this isn't my favorite place, but I'd go again.

text: My husband and I had dinner here several weeks ago and I decided to wait to write a review, thinking it would be fair to let some time go by and soften the memory. I'm surprised the restaurant is still open, to be frank; our experience was so miserable from beginning to end and we're evidently not the only ones to have been let down. We'd decided to go to to dinner her after walking by one night and hearing wonderful music. We were charmed by the atmosphere, too. We came back a week later, arriving just before the dinner crowd. We placed our order and asked for a mojito. We should have known immediately that this evening wasn't going to be pleasant, but we were looking forward to fun night out. The whole night we probably let too many things go with a shrug, but the thing is, we're really easy to please. Our server, who never introduced herself so I don't know her name, was at moments too friendly and others completely condescending. When my husband asked for his steak to be cooked medium-well, she explained, her nose a new inches higher in the air, that they never cook it more than medium as it is such excellent meat. This was off-putting, but we assumed it was just pride in the restaurant's food. Fair enough. Our ceviche appetizer was grey and flavorless. We shrugged. We shouldn't have ordered ceviche from an Argentinean restaurant, we said! My mojito arrived. The lime wedge on the outer rim had browned completely on the edges, showing it had been sliced hours, if not days, ago. Not very appetizing, but the drink was otherwise fine. Again, we rationalized, if the rest of the food is good, and surely it will be, that will make up for this. But then the food did arrive: steak for my husband and Cuban-style shrimp for me. The shrimp was barely edible. Frozen for who knows how long and then overcooked, they crunched unpleasantly in my mouth. The coconut rice was fine, however. I ate it, the three dollops of sweet plantains on the edge of the plate, and one shrimp. My husband's steak was even worse. It arrived unevenly cooked, but generally well done. It was tough, gamey, and flavorless. I tried a bite of it and I was immediately reminded of dinners at Sizzler when I was a kid. It was exactly the steak you'd get at Sizzler. The chimichurri sauce served on the side was completely bland and didn't add anything to the steak. It was totally different from the amazing chimichurri sauce left on the table, presumably to have with bread. That was the one yummy thing we had here and what we tried to fill up on. Unfortunately, this wasn't the low point of dinner. As bad as the food was, the service was even worse. My husband and I looked longingly at Opal across the street, wishing we'd gone there for dinner, but decided to make the best of what we had. I would have liked another mojito, but our server had disappeared after dropping off our plates. We waited for about 20 minutes after finishing eating, but no one came by to check on us. We pushed our plates to the other side of the table thinking it just wasn't obvious that we were done. For the remaining HOUR we waited, no one picked up our plates. It was quite a bit busier now, but we still saw our server around. It appeared some of her regulars had come in. We tried to catch her eye, but to no avail. We had to ask two other waiters, at different times, if we could please get our check. They agreed. But as I said, an hour after we had finished eating, our plates were on the table and we had no check. We probably should have made a bigger scene, but we wanted to give everyone the benefit of the doubt. Even if our server was a lost cause, surely someone else would help us? One of the busboys hanging out with the other waiters off to the side? No one seemed to be too busy. We contemplated leaving without paying, but bad service certainly does not excuse theft. We finally left our table to ask the hostess what was going on. As we approached, she wished us a good night and started walking away. It was so very tempting to walk off into the night. But we explained how long we'd been waiting for the check and could we please get it and leave? Miraculously, she returned with our server. She acted surprised that we had been waiting! She was keeping an eye on us and it looked like we were just enjoying the music! So, were we off the see the show at the Lobero? She reached out and stroked my husband's arm as if they'd been best friends for years. The lack of professionalism demonstrated by everyone we interacted with was shocking. It's clear the management is absent and has no interest in maintaining this restaurant. If our server had just apologized as we were leaving and explained that she'd become distracted with her regulars, we really would have understood. But it's obvious she had no reason to care. I can't imagine why anyone would dine here. Go across the street to Opal and enjoy.

text: Cute Italian BYOB at a convenient location in Medford with plenty of parking. I'd say the other reviews have done a pretty good job painting the picture in terms of the atmosphere, so I'll limit mine to my opinion of the food. If you order the right thing, there aren't many better values in local dining, especially since you can bring your own bottle of wine. Yes, this does imply that the menu can be hit or miss here. But the hits are great enough to garner a 4-star review from me. Favorites: - The Garlic Knots: love those, sometimes ask for extra - Involtini Di Melenzane (Stuffed Eggplant): this appetizer you could make a meal of. They also offer it as an entree with pasta - but to me all that spaghetti in red sauce just gets in the way of my delicious stuffed eggplant. - Spaghetti Carbonara: If you REALLY want to try and kill yourself with a super heavy dish, try ordering the Carbonara with Gnocchi instead of spaghetti. I did it once and barely survived the experience, but it was so good. Proceed at your own risk. - Gnocchi w/ Vodka Sauce - Linguini w/ White Clam Sauce Not So Much: - Calamari Fritti: The fried calamari appetizer is the most disappointing thing on the menu for me. It's average at best; not good for an Italian spot like this. To qualify my opinion, it's one of my stupid little missions in life to find the best fried calamari out there. Whenever we go out to eat at a new restaurant and they have fried calamari, I order it. Had it from Italy to throughout New England to Arizona (where I had a very good Buffalo Calamari). It's average here. At best. - Vongole Casino: The Clams Casino were terrible, especially for the $8.99 price tag. - Crab Cakes: I'd ballpark these at below average. They're huge, I'll give them that, but if you are craving them you are much better off at a good seafood restaurant. They have a lot of dessert options, but with the portion sizes (one order of the Gnocchi w/ Vodka Sauce is enough for me to get 3 meals out of - and be full for all 3), you'll probably never dream of it unless you go in with the gameplan to eat conservatively and take home a massive doggy bag. Bonus - they do catering trays for parties at very reasonable prices. We did that for our Super Bowl party this year and it was SO worth it. Cut down on our work immensely. Again though - heed the portion sizes here. Yes, a tray of Pasta Tarantella for 5 will feed 5 adults ... if those 5 adults are intent on eating the entire tray and then passing out at the table. All in all, good place, good food, great value!

text: Armor Concepts is a company that specializes in door and window security. The majority of their products are designed to strengthen your door jamb and door and make it impossible for a burglar to kick your door in. I found Armor concepts after three houses on my street were robbed within a single week. In each case the thieves kicked the door in and were gone within a few minutes. I decided to do something about my house and was thrilled to find a local business that had exactly what I needed. I purchased their EZ Armor product to strengthen my doors. It is basically a four foot piece of metal that replaces the kick plate for you deadbolt. The biggest difference is that it has eight 3 inch screws holding it in versus the two wimpy 1/2 inch ones that most deadbolts have keeping your door secure. I also installed the Hinge protectors and door protector. I was actually angry when I was replacing the screws holding my door into place. They were all 1/2 inch or smaller. It is no wonder doors get kicked in so easily. There is literally nothing sturdy holding the door in. All of the Armor screws are 3 inches long and actually connect to the framing of the house. The product was fairly easy to install, but I would highly recommend having a power drill handy to make it go much faster. A competent handy man can have one door done in roughly 30 minutes. The location and building are extremely nondescript, there is not even a sign to speak of. It is more of an industrial office than a retail shop. The staff is extremely helpful however and it is still the easiest place to get the product in Nashville. I was very happy with the product and the company providing it. They are a local business and all the products are made here in Nashville. If you have concerns about your security, and you probably should, then this company can be a great help to you peace of mind.

text: I tried this place for the second time the other night after going for happy hour about 6 months ago. My first experience wasn't great, but it's a cute space so I decided to give it another try. We got there during happy hour which for the night we went advertised 1/2 price flights. The special was actually $13 for a flight (three 2 oz glasses of either red or white) and a cheese plate. The only wine option for happy hour was $3 house wine which I had the first time and was served Chanti from the bottle with the straw on it - you know the one I mean - you'd expect to find it in an old school Italian restaurant in South Philly... So, I didn't opt for the $3 wine this time. My friend and I shared the cheese plate which was fine, but aside from the sharp provolone with whole peppercorns (not a favorite) the others - gorgonzola, goat cheese and fontina, are pretty much staples in my fridge. Nothing too exciting, but very reasonable on the happy hour deal. We wanted dinner, but decided to split a bunch of appetizers instead of entrees. We ordered the grilled vegetable platter, calamari, and tuna mango maki roll. The grilled vegetables comes with onions, peppers, zucchini and eggplant. Unfortunately that's all it comes with, so if you're inclined to want to put your veggies on something, a fork is your only option. The flavor was very good, but eating a forkful of grilled onions doesn't do it for me. It did have two pieces of bread with bruschetta on the side, but the bread was really dry, and since it was already topped it didn't help solve the veggie problem. The calamari was fine - a little on the chewy side, but I appreciated the variety of sauces it came with. The maki was not like anything I (or anyone I know) would call maki. The plate had fist sized rolls of raw tuna wrapped loosely around guacamole with a mango salsa on the side. It was served with two giant fried wantons that we were told to use to eat the tuna and mango. I tried cutting through the tuna, but realized the white membrane part was still attached which I ended up having to pull like a string from my mouth after taking my first (and last) bite. We sent it back. I really wanted to like this place, but for the money there are too many other better options nearby :(

text: I still for the life of me can't understand why this place does not get better reviews across the board; they are always crowded when I have been and the food is always amazing. Some of the menu items even include soup or salad at no extra charge, which is an increasing rarity these days. Their queso, in my opinion, ranks 3rd after San Antonio Taco and Chili's in that order. Then, out of every place I have been to, their onion rings are just flat out Amazing, the best in town. The mark of a good onion ring? The onion stays in the batter coating when you bite into it. Their batter, which is not crumbly or crumby like other places, is a very much like a tempura batter and oh so good. I have not yet tried on single bad thing on the menu, from their fried mushrooms with horseradish sauce, chicken n buttons and Monterrey Chicken breast. Then there is the amazing mac n cheese (only second to Cracker Barrel, still need to try Loveless and Rotier's on that) and their awesome burgers. There is the one dish that is sure to make any lover of Mac n Cheese outright soak themselves in drool... The Ultimate Pasta, which is so good; think mac n cheese on steroids and this is what you get. Also, if you are a fan of Chicken Parmesan and are really hungry, they have the largest serving of Chicken Parm anywhere I have seen. Now while it is not the best in town, it is still very good. Finally, I must say, they have the best Chicken Tortilla soup I have ever had anywhere (even back home in Texas), as it has the perfect amount of cheese, tortilla strips, chicken, corn and seasonings in it. As for there Caesar salad, it is consistently good every time I have had it. I could go on and on about all the tasty menu items there, but there are to many to name. However, I will say that they also have some very good shakes. Now, my only complaint is that I wish they would bring back their coupons! They used to have coupons where, among other things, when buying two entree's you got the lesser of the two (cost wise) for free.

text: I've only been here once, so try not to take anything I say as concrete for the venu. The Rathskeller is located in an absolutely gorgeous antique building. The decorations are over-the-top German, yet extremely elegant, and not hokey in any way, shape or form. There are several rooms, including an outdoor Biergarten, with fine dining tables, and each has its own personality. A fun place to get up and explore! The beer selection is superb, especially if you like German beers, which I do. The dopplebock they had on draught was some of the best I've had. Straight from Germany. Can't beat it. Unless you come for lunch, the dinner prices are quite high, typically about $20 a plate, if not more. Most dinner plates are quite large, though, and you can split with a friend for an extra $10, which includes an extra plate, 2 sides for each person, and a soup or salad. Appetizers are unnecessary since freshly baked bread (including german rye and pretzels) are served with dinner. The wienerschnitzel I had here was thin (which is a good thing), tender and extremely flavorful. I enjoyed every mouthful. The sides of red cabbage and potato salad were a bit acidic for my tastes, even for German food. The spaetzle with gravy on top has to be your best bet. But the best thing here is the German chocolate cheesecake. A hybrid of the classic chocolate treat on top of a chocoalte cheesecake was extremely worth the mere $4.95 I paid for it. Desserts at "less expensive" restaurants are at least $6. I guess they're banking on people being extremely full from the copious amounts of food they serve!

text: Yes, it's a bit of a haul. Every time I head out west to Wiethop, I feel like I'm in the country. But even though it's certainly out of my way, it's a fabulous place to visit if you're up for some gardening. I've made the trip to Wiethop six or seven times since mid-April. That first trip, I was astounded by the size of the greenhouses, just filled to the brim with colorful flowering annuals, hanging baskets and overflowing prearranged pots. Wiethop also has another greenhouse devoted completely to perennials. After the cold, grey winter months, just stepping into the greenhouses' riot of color was restorative to my soul and inspiring. I helped my mother-in-law plant her flowers. I helped her sister. I moved on to Justin's offices. And then finally, FINALLY, we bought our house and had our own yard to plant. Unfortunately, buying a house meant I was also out of money, so I had to exercise extreme restraint on my last trip out to Wiethop. Luckily, their prices aren't exorbitant and if you're willing to forgo some blooms this year, you can buy starter perennials for far less than the grown up flowering ones. So I had to exercise restraint AND have patience. This home-owning stuff is really turning me into a grown up... If you're looking for trees and shrubs, you won't find them here, but for your annuals, perennials and vegetables, Wiethop is a great choice. You can always head next door to Sherwood Gardens for the shrubs and such afterward. Parking can be rough, especially on nice sunny afternoons, but Wiethop opens up early--take advantage of their hours if you don't feel like waiting for a spot and standing in line at check out!

If you're looking for an inexpensive, tasty, filling meal, this is the sure thing. I really wanted the biscuit, but I'm also a huge pulled pork sandwich person, and wanted the platter, because I saw the mac and cheese was offered as one of the rotating sides today. So, I got a pulled pork sandwich, mac and cheese, and sweet cabbage for $12. Also, I think it was nearing the end of her day, so the sweet lady at the counter threw in that biscuit for free. PLUS, sweet tea. I never tried sweet cabbage before, and it was peppery and spicy done right! I'm also not usually a cold tea drinker, but it cooled off the spice of the cabbage. Everything, actually complemented everything else. Plus, I had leftovers. Plus, they had cheddar-pepper biscuits, as well. Plus, the lovely lady dishing it all out was super friendly and, while we raved, told us about the food and how business was going so far. She mentioned that even vegetarians were liking Bebe's because of the vegetarian sides. 3 sides = vegetarian platter. We saw no ribs today, but I don't doubt their deliciousness! text: I made this trip to Reno with my parents to celebrate my mother's 65th birthday. Upon arrival we were given two double bed rooms and not two kings as requested at time of booking. After a wasted few minutes of haggling with a very unhelpful customer service clerk I spoke with the manager who informed me that all of the king rooms were sold out (hard to tell given the lack of activity in the casino). I again explained that I had made the reservation days ago and that no my aging parents would not prefer to "squeeze" into a double bed as he suggested. I had requested two king rooms and that was what I expected to receive. After much back and forth, the manager and I came to a compromise and I was able to get a king room for my parents and keep a double for myself. Needless to say, not a good start to the weekend. Harrah's in Reno used to be a grand hotel. Unfortunately now, like most of Reno it is falling into disrepair. The hotel looked as if it hadn't been updated since the late '80's, the air conditioning in the casino was lacking and the unit in the room rumbled throughout the night disturbing my sleep. The bed (a double since I wasn't given the king that I requested) was too hard. Reno itself has become quite the ghost town as evident by the various boarded up businesses and casinos (se la vie Fitzgerald), I suppose proving that this once Boom Town is not immune to the weakened economy or the strength of the Indian Casinos now peppered throughout northern California. At this point, I see no reason in returning unless there is a specific event going on. And if I do, it will NOT be to Harrah's.

text: Santa Barbara Roasting Company, known as RoCo to locals and fans, is the only coffee shop in Santa Barbara I know of that roasts their own coffee beans as well as serves coffee. Most of the others ship it in from elsewhere, like Starbucks and Peet's. RoCo kicks their butts, even with the foo-foo drinks (you know, the more milk than coffee, with tons of flavorings)! The original location, where they roast, is in a little shopping center (State St and Guiterrez St) next to a Time Bike shop and an art gallery, with a great bakery (D'Angelo's) around the corner. The coffee, people, atmosphere and charm of the original location can't be beat. The Paseo Nuevo location serves great coffee, but lacks the space and charm, but what can you expect for being in the middle of an upscale shopping mall? Besides coffee, espresso, and hot and cold coffee-based drinks, RoCo also serve a variety of pastries from a local bakery which are really good. They offer free Wi-Fi Internet, which can be a little poky at time, but hey, it's free, so no complaints. Honestly, the only place I've ever had better coffee than RoCo's is at Barefoot Roasters in Santa Clara. But RoCo is more fun, funky, and has a way cool logo, so I still consider it my favorite coffee shop of all time. Coffee lovers, tourists, beach bums, and college students all converge at RoCo in harmony. Join them and see why I miss it so now that I moved back to Silicon Valley.

text: I really, REALLY wanted to recommend these people, because Silvia herself is very nice, and I have always been sweet and polite in my dealings with her. But after they DESTROYED my record of my children's heights written on the wall, I could not, in good conscience, keep working with them. It was like pouring acid over a cherished photo album, and I will confess I was and am still heartbroken. A year ago, they cleaned the knobs on my toaster oven, and in the process, scrubbed all the numbers off! It is hard to use a toaster oven with all the degree markings obliterated. They also cleaned a garage sink and completely flooded my garage with 30 gallons of water when they failed to replace a washing machine drain. To this, I would add that they do not clean ON TOP of anything above about 4 feet high, and routinely miss dirty fingerprints around light switches, etc. Remarkably, I had these folks clean my modest, 1,100 square foot tract home for TWO YEARS! Trust me - it's NOTHING fancy - more Jeff Foxworthy than Beverly Hills. So this was NOT a one-time aberration. I had to remind the cleaners to clean stuff like light switches, dirty windows, dirty venetian blinds, etc. EVERY SINGLE TIME - probably THIRTY TIMES, the same set of reminders. In fairness, they **ALWAYS** made the bathrooms shine. But they have zero clue about how to clean houses. I think most of their business is offices, not houses, and they are apparently a one-trick pony who cannot adapt to the unique requirements of homes. I detect from our conversations that Silvia has a "poor little me" mentality. For the record, Silvia owns a fleet of cars, has about 30 employees, a full office staff, and a huge commercial contract portfolio. She has far more employees than I do. When I have [on more than a dozen occasions] told her that her staff did not, for example, clean on top of the TV, which is about 5 1/2 feet off the ground, she explained that her cleaners were not very tall! Come on! I'm "only" 5'10" tall, and I when I clean my house myself, I have to stand on something to clean the top of the door jambs, which are nearly 7 feet tall. When I knock down cobwebs, I use something with a long handle. She needs to get a clue. Her explanation for grinding the numbers off my toaster oven dials was that her cleaners did not know anything about toaster ovens. WHAT?? This is a friggin TOASTER OVEN, not a nuclear reactor. Her cleaners may not be English literate, but they thought it was OK to scour until "ON/OFF" was gone??? ...till "100", "200", and "300" were gone from the temperature dial?? Last time I checked, Mexcio still used the decimal system and Arabic numerals!!! For the record, my hugely capable college intern spoke fluent Spanish and English, so language was not a problem. I speak a modicum of Spanish myself. When I hired Silvia's the first time, I gave them a full checklist to work with in resoundingly good Spanish - which they routinely ignored. I suspect Silvia hires people who represent themselves as good cleaners and does not spend a cent on training them, on standards, or on mid-level supervision or accountability. Her services are not cheap, and I suspect she has a good expense ratio, so I cannot believe she cannot afford training. She has zero concept of checklists, quality control, management, or organization, except for a grueling, metronome-like schedule. I assume most of her employees are recent immigrants, and no one has more appreciation for the difficulties faced by recent immigrants into a foreign culture than I do. However, Silvia bears the responsibility for educating her people in what the job requires. If your employees do not know what a stove is, that is YOUR problem as the employer, not theirs, and certainly not mine. I should be able to EXPECT your employees to know what a stove is. As an employer with nearly 3 dozen in your workforce, you should provide that kind of training. Don't know how to provide training? There are, like, a zillion companies who do it, and for competitive prices. You don't do your own tax, I'll bet. See - you already know how to hire outsourced services! For the record, Service Master, Coverall, and a zillion other cleaning services who hire recent immigrants DO train their workforce! I have had these people do a poor job for years, and all they flooded my garage, destroyed my toaster over, and destroyed my cherished records of my children's height as they grew up. I work 12 hour days, but will probably clean my home myself before I ever let someone in to do it for me again.

text: First off, this hotel has an excellent location. It is directly across from the airport and you can drive right in from the airport access road. The bad news is that the location is the only thing going for this place. Otherwise, the hotel is a joke. I'm reminded of the episode from "I Love Lucy" where the gang stays in a hotel and are bothered by train noises all night long, nothing working, etc. It seems to me that this hotel just seeks to get by and not much more. For starters, there's a very busy train line running behind the hotel. By regulation or whatever, the trains around N.O. seem to constantly blare their horn. Since trains pass by the hotel 24/7, expect your sleep to be interrupted several times a night by the noisy train. Other than that, there's the fact that things just don't seem to work in this hotel. They completely forgot to clean up my room after the first night. So not only was my room not clean, but I was short on clean towels, cups, toilet paper, soap, etc. I called down and advised them of that. They didn't even bother to apologize. They just said that someone would be up with the supplies. A half hour later - nothing. I called again, and then it took them maybe another 10-15 to bring up the supplies. As if that weren't bad enough, one of the paper cups they brought up was actually used (had dried coffee all over). The next morning, I advised the front desk that my room was not cleaned before and once again, there was no apology. They just said "I'll make sure it's cleaned today". Well, the next day they did clean it but, instead of hanging up the towels, they left a pile of towels partially-folded up on my bed. The other big problem is the internet. Internet service at the hotel is a complete joke. During my stay, the internet went down 4 separate times. What's more, it was for different reasons. Twice, the wifi service went down. The two other times, the hotel's server crashed. There's not much you can do except grin and bear it. DO NOT CHOOSE THIS HOTEL IF YOU'RE STAYING FOR WORK since you very well may not be able to get your work done thanks to the very unreliable internet service. Also, parking at the hotel is a joke. Since the hotel rents out 85% or so of its lot for an airport parking service, guests have to park all the way at the front of the hotel - which is a LOOONG walk if your room is on the back side which mine was. It may be that the hotel guests can access the airport parking lot (which is behind a gate). If so, they didn't not inform me of that possibility so I assume that it is not an option. Noise is also an issue. Besides the literally blaring problem of the train, the walls at the hotel are paper thin as are the windows. I had the misfortune of having a room next to someone who apparently gets up at 6:30 and sees no trouble in pacing around the corridor talking loudly on his cell phone. It sounded like he was actually inside my room! All the while, I could hear his TV playing in his room. Then there were other things. A wall lamp became unanchored and fell off the wall during my stay. It just completely fell off with a thud. I notified the maid so that they wouldn't be under the impression that I broke it since I didn't. The maid said that someone would come by and fix it. Well, it wasn't fixed. They just left it where it fell. Then there's the coffee service. They do not consistently refill the instant coffee bags for the coffee maker. One day, all I got was decaf coffee bags - as if they had run out of regular coffee and just decided that they could make up for that by only giving me decaf.

text: I stumbled upon Asian Fusion while running errands this week and am glad I did! The chandelers are breath-taking (check out a pic in the gallery) and of course I'd notice them, they're shiny, sparkly and glass! I stopped in for lunch and everything on their lunch menu is under$10. I had the lemon grass chicken along with a Vietnamese coffee. I was surprised at the serving size as it was certainly worth more that $7. The veggies were fresh and crisp, the chicken wonderfully marinated and the rice good and sticky, with just enough punch to tingle your taste buds. I like trying different thing so I gave the Vietnamese coffee a try and was something I don't think I'd have next time. It was tasty, very sweet (contains sweetened condensed milk) and I loved the drip apparatus at the top of the mug. It was too sweet for me but I know my husband will love it. The service was good - should be I was one of 2 groups there. I was told by the server the restaurant has been there for just over a year and they are always busy in the evenings and on the weekends and the lunch crowd is usually regulars (I can totally understand that!). Asian Fusion is nearing the end of a renovation which includes updated interior and inclusion of a private dining room. It is certainly worth your time checking out. I know I'll be back.

text: After 5 years of faithful cuts at the Beehive, my stylist, Amy, suddenly disappeared off the circuit. Feeling stranded with 8 weeks of agonizing overgrowth that led me to get creative with bobby-pins and headbands, I went to Yelp and started hunting around. I wanted a laid-back salon where I didn't feel rushed, a stylist who didn't ask me endless questions just to fill the silence, and a cute short haircut that didn't age me by 20 years. So I decided to check out Fringe. The salon is instantly recognizable by the enormous pair of glitter-encrusted scissors dangling above the door. The inside is casual, comfy, and spacious. The friendly cat made me a feel a little more at home. I was quickly seen by my stylist, Roberta. The first haircut with someone new is always the hardest as it takes a few visits before a stylist can anticipate what exactly I want and what my hair is willing to do. She played around with my hair for a bit, asked some questions about my cowlicks and what I was looking for. She got out a new razor and went to work. She took her time on me. We talked about our neighborhoods, getting used to helicopter search lights through our windows, and being harassed by kids on the street. I learned that the natural part in my hair is highly unusual - who knew?! While it unnerved me a little bit that she cut herself twice during the appointment, thankfully my hair wasn't an additional casualty. It turned out great. She asked for my opinion a few times during the cut and made sure that I was happy with it. While the 45 minute commute from North Philly wasn't ideal for me and the parking was tight, I'd rather sing in the car for a little while than have to pay to wear a hat for the next month and a half. As I told Roberta on my way out, "My head loves you!" Thanks, Fringe!

text: If some out-of-towner who's never been to our fair city gripes about it being dirty, or dangerous, or any of that oher crap that can go part and parcel with most any frickin' big city on the planet, then be sure to tell them that they are, in fact, correct, and take them straight to The Gallery as soon as their precious safe and clean feet step on the Philly asphalt. Sure, there are stores like Old Navy, Burlington Coat Factory, and Kmart (see accompanying review for that turd as well), but you don't really want to go into any of them at The Gallery. All the versions of those stores at this weirdo excuse for a mall (really it seems more like the reality of some lousy urban planner's lunch that he vomited up one day) came straight from Hell. If you've ever seen the movie Jacob's Ladder, you'll instantly know what I mean. This place is just skeevy beyond belief. Of course, seeing the big mural thingy smack dab in the middle featuring Bill Cosby's likeness is well worth the free admission. The only reason I'm usually at this place is because one of the trains I take plops me off at Market East Station, which is featured in the very bowels of The Gallery. But it's actually the nicest thing there, because you know you'll be getting away from there soon when heading outbound. There's a terrible excuse for a food court down there as well, featuring such craptastic selections as Subway and Popeye's and some weird-ass Asian joints serving up smoothies and chicken wings galore. What is it with the Chinese places and chicken wings in this city? Someone needs to look that up. So just remember, take all your pals to The Gallery to scare the hell out of them and make their big city fears come true. text: This place gets 2 stars for dedicated ownership and potential. And the elements keeping it from being a great market seem so obvious. The attraction of a farm market are the freshness of all of its stuff and the inevitability of always finding something new. The best way to achieve zero growth is to offer same old same old. Go to the Market at Head House Square during the summer and you see the farmers trucks on the street being unloaded. The produce still has dirt on it, the cheeses are made in small batches, the peaches have fuzz on them and they all scream freshness. Go to the Farmers Market in Ardmore or Strafford and you'll find great fish and meats, a produce market with treviso, white asparagus, Belgian endive, mandarinos from Sicily, icicle radishes and cactus pears. The Amish concession is manned by an entire Amish family and you know that their chickens, produce, relishes and shoo fly pie came off their farm and from their kitchen. This straightforward no frills approach to food retail, bringing the best possible fresh foods to the city is the reason that a farmers market flourishes. Wine stalls, beer tastings and cooking lessons are fine but completely secondary to what is truly important. Fitting this perfectly adequate space with a dynamite fruit and produce section with interesting greengrocer items is key and no one runs these types of markets better than Korean operators. Additionally, a dynamic meat and poultry section is also mandatory for the growth of a market of this type. Further, if it is a year round market and not summer only, a fresh fish stand is if not a necessity, would leave a shopper no reason to go to the big stores. People who go to farmers markets know they will pay more but do not want to see most of the stuff there that they see in an Acme. Definite potential for 5 stars but never without the pieces necessary to attract patrons and put the market on their must-go-every-week list.

text: I'll be honest: The Gelateria is one of the reasons I moved downtown a year and a half ago. Well, the Gelateria and other locally owned businesses, that is. I wanted to be part of a neighborhood that had food and entertainment I could walk to, and where owners/workers would get to know me and be proud of their offerings. The Gelateria is a shining example of all of this. Both before and after the ownership change, customer service and great food has been a huge part of what makes the Gelateria special. Today's Gelateria Tavolini offers about a dozen delicious gelatos, some of which are available nearly all the time, and others of which are available only as holidays/ingredients allow. My favorites are the caramel and the pineapple -- a take-home pint of these flavors have combined to form my dinner on more than one occasion. All of the fruit flavors, including strawberry and raspberry, also are delicious -- the actual fruit really shines through and is so much better than store-bought treats that use that fake chemical fruit flavoring. You can enjoy the gelato in cups or shake form right there in the cozy cafe or to go. A bonus is that most of the dishes/utensils/containers are reusable or recyclable. Gelateria Tavolini also offers a large variety of hot drinks, most of which are coffee and tea. I'm not a coffee drinker, so I gravitate toward the hot chocolate. The hot chocolate at Cafe Cioccolato always will be my first love, but the choc at the Gelateria is good when CC isn't open and is MUCH better than any Swiss Miss you might make for yourself at home. You might want to dunk a pastry into your hot beverage, and Gelateria Tavolini can help with that. There typically are fresh scones, tarts, cookies and brownies for sale. On my latest visit, I sampled a flaky, sugary apple dumpling and was in heaven. As mentioned before, the counterfolk at the Gelateria are friendly and will make suggestions based upon your taste or mood. I usually visit on weekends and see the same young man during most of my visits. He's always smiley and chatty and has great taste in pastries. He also deals really, really well when the place is crowded with youth groups or convention people. A barrage of people might be exhausting or annoying for some people, but this guy manages to keep smiling even after dealing with 13 straight orders. The Gelateria Tavolini really is a perfect example of what people invested in St. Louis' and downtown's future can do.

text: Here is a synopsis of my experience at Osteria: We arrived for our reservation about 15 minutes early, and were delighted to hear they could seat us. We expected to have to have a drink at the bar first, which we did not mind at all. We were seating in a back room that lacked ambiance. Unfortuantely, she wasn't crazy about it, so she asked if she could try one more. She enjoyed the second wine and ordered it, but the sommolier acted as if she was being unreasonable and rude. Normally, I am overly polite and just take what is first offered, even if I am not crazy about it. But as a sommolier, is it that big of a deal to offer a second small sample? It wasn't even as if we were bothering our server asking her to do a million things when she needs to take food orders from the other tables. Her job is to assist tables in chosing wines. It seemed like a reasonable request. But we moved on. The sommolier was annoyed but we were there to have a lovely time. We all ordered, and two of my companions ordered a $36 special - a 1/2 pound of lobster and pasta. Appetizers came and were delicious, although the antipasta is charged per person and was not a lot of food. When the entree came, the two companions that ordered the lobster dish looked suprised. They were literarly fishing around to find lobster. Soon, the four of us were trying to assist, to try to find the lobster because we were so afraid of asking for the server. All in all, pieces that add up to about 1/2 the size of my tiny palm were found. We did not ask for the server or even steal glances across the room to find her. She stopped back to see how things were and we said everything was very good, and they hated to complain, but there was barely any lobster in the pasta. Immedietly she became very annoyed. She pointed to a small piece and said "There it is!" My companions said they understood, but they have ordered lobster many times in their lives and 1/2 a pound never looked so small. She said there was nothing they could do and if they wanted she would get the manager. What were we to do? We said OK. The manager arrived and said basically the same thing. He said they weight each lobster and it is always 1/2 a pound. We decided to let it go and just ate. Then things became incredibly embarassing. I was facing the room and saw our server, the manager, the sommolier and the bartender talking and pointing at us. I felt like that "nightmare" table, like I was in some kind of Twilight Zone episode. I always consider myself to be a great restaurant customer. I myself worked in the industry for two years. text: The Belcourt Theatre is, without a doubt, the most authentic and, well, neat establishment in the Hillsboro area. Independent little artsy movie houses are an absolute staple in any community, and fortunately for Nashvillians, this one is about as unpretentious as is possible when it comes to indie cinemas. The theatre was open as a silent movie house back in the 20's, and the Belcourt's current management still keeps the dream alive with classics, foreign films and documentaries that you often can't view anywhere else in Middle Tennessee. The Belcourt's full bar and intimate atmosphere give it an air that is far more welcoming than that of most sticky, towering multiplexes. The theatre also holds art shows, film festivals, special screenings and concerts that are consistently charming and entertaining. In fact, the Belcourt is renowned for holding concerts for huge acts that like to stage occasional intimate shows--think the White Stripes, Yo La Tengo, Feist, et cetera. Prices are about the same as you'd find at a typical chain cinema: $6.25 for matines and $8.50 for evenings. The only difference here is that you'll probably see a better film and get to have yourself a cocktail while doing so! The Belcourt typically only shows two films at a time, but they maintain their website regularly and rotate films on a consistent basis. And it's perfect for first dates.

text: Sushi Fune is my go-to place for sushi due to its proximity to home and always having exceptional tasting fresh fish. I have been going there for the past 15 years or so and while its location at the Bardmoor Publix Plaza strip center isn't anything special the interior is perfectly acceptable and befitting anyone's expectations of a sushi restaurant. Fune means small boat in Japanese and the central sushi bar features a wrap around mini river with tiny "boats" containing plates of sushi. The same chef and hostess/waitress are usually there every night and they are both friendly and very attentive. Some of my favorite items they have are the mackerel, fresh salmon, eel, conch, clam, yammy rolls (tempura sweet potato yam), miso tofu rolls, and samurai lobster roll. The Samurai lobster roll is huge and is beautifully plated with a lot of intricate details including part of the tail shell! The lobster meat is tempura fried and there is a lot of spicy sauce and it is one of the better high end rolls being priced at $16-17. I uploaded a picture of it. The miso soup and ginger dressing salad are pretty straightforward but good. They carry unfiltered cold sake that really tastes great and has a cloudy milky appearance and a very different taste than the hot sake you are accustomed to at japanese restaurants. Lastly, they also have a good TonKatsu which is a fried pork cutlet dinner entrée. Overall I think that Sushi Fune has tastier fish than fancier places like Sushi Rock Grill, and proves that a strip mall sushi restaurant can out do other local standalone places which may provide better ambiance not better tasty nigiri and rolls.

It was great, and the berry jam it came with was sooo good! - (boyfriend) Dungeness Crab Cake & Potato Hash w/Avocado Salsa, Poached Eggs & Lemon Butter Sauce - $17 He loved it. Everything was cooked perfectly and looked great. Prices: Kind of pricey? Our bill was $53.00, including tax and tip. But for an experience like this, I would say it was definitely worth it. My budget unfortunately won't allow me to visit this restaurant as often as I'd like, but I know I will be back soon... Especially if I can get my parents to pay for me :) Recommendation: Go! text: Though it's billed and priced as fine dining, the food I was served at Oh Yumm Bistro wouldn't have been fit to serve at any restaurant. The menu gives the appearance of creativity, but the dishes were unimaginative and poorly executed. Even if the food had not been carelessly prepared, there is little hope that even properly cooked it would have been worth spending time and money on it. My party ordered 'Shrimp and Grits', 'Tostada Carne Asada', 'Duck Breast with Paella', and 'Chicken Pot Pie'. The puff pastry topping the uninspired chicken pot pie was burnt imbuing the whole dish with a slight charcoal flavor and the filling was mushy in an unappealing rather than comforting way. The Tostada was built on what appeared to be store bought tortilla chips (hopefully nothing so terrible was made fresh in the kitchen, but it wouldn't be suprising if it had) and was tough, dry flavorless beef with a shockingly pedestrian and overly large pile of iceberg lettuce and shredded cheese. Although the duck breast and shrimp on the paella were competently cooked the paella underneath them was foul and almost inedible. It was comprised mostly of undercooked, gritty rice that would be more at home in Rice-a-Roni; overcooked, cheap, greasy chorizo; and what appeared to be frozen peas. Bizarrely, it was littered with whole black peppercorns that discouraged me from eating a bite without first carefully screening it. Noticeably lacking was any sign of the prominently billed saffron; admittedly it might have been present and was simply overwhelmed in flavor and color by chorizo grease. The shrimp and grits were the brightest point in the meal, although they rose to the level of adequacy and nothing more. The shrimp were wrapped in bacon and well prepared and the sauce on them added a pleasant salt and acidity that was completely absent from the other dishes. However, the grits were alternately tasty then fatty and bland depending on whether a pool of bacon grease was lurking on that mouthful. Even the bread and butter served before the meal were terrible. The rolls were room temperature and suspiciously similar to the ones served on my last flight. There was parsley and cinnamon butter offered; the parsley butter was bland, unsalted and unpleasant and the cinnamon butter tasted like children's cereal. In addition to the poor quality of the food there were several other problems that I would normally excuse or ignore, but cannot because they exemplify the atrocious carelessness of the entire operation. We had reservations and the restaurant was near empty, but we were seated directly next to the kitchen at a wobbly table with wobbly chairs. We asked to move to a different table, that was also wobbly and ultimately stabilized with a wine cork. The waitress couldn't seem to remember the specials even though they were written on a chalkboard above the table and she was uncertain which dishes they were or were not out of. They were out of the first several dishes that we ordered and she returned to tell me that they were also out of the wine that I had ordered. I should note that this was seven o'clock on a Saturday night, which makes it somewhat confusing as to how and why they would be out of so much, so early on what should be the busiest night of the week. Adding insult to injury, fine dining prices were being charged for food and service that would be unacceptable in a truck stop. I will not return to Oh Yum Bistro and I advise that for fine dining you try Elements instead.

text: OK, if you have read any of my other posts you know that me have big luv for rice plates and cheap and tasty grub. HK Diner is in a strip mall adjacent to the Atlantis casino and hotel and open until 3AM as advertised to catch the late night munchie crowd. All the dishes are Cantonese/Hong Kong style, with Won Tons that your Chinese Granny would be happy with. The soup has the right amount of salt and MSG, though the veggies in the wor won ton soup are more adjusted to the non-Chinese clientele (American broccoli, with bamboo shoots, and mini corns and a few snow peas.) The egg and shrimp over rice is a whole plate full of white rice covered by a huge egg omelet with many large shrimp-a real tasty dinner for $6.75. The Spicy Crispy Wings at $7.50 were tasty chunks of chicken wing dusted in cornstarch, seasoned generously with salt and then deep fried, quickly sauteed with jalapenos and scallions. A little over-fried to a deep brown, and I prefer whole wings not chunked/halved bits. They probably cut them to make you feel like you got more pieces, but they were harder to eat when cut into nugget size. You can take a pass on the potstickers-definitely forgettable. They were deep-fried-but I prefer my potstickers to be browned on the bottom then steamed until done. The pork and preserved egg rice porridge (Congee) was too thin, and should have more rice and/or add cornstarch to give it a creamier texture. The "jook" here is more like what you would get as a result of cooking it at home. Not bad, but not many places serve this dish so it does in a pinch. The deep-fried donuts with the congee was fine. Combo plates at $4.95 include rice or chow mein and you get to choose two a la carte items (e.g. Beef Broccoli, Sesame Chicken, Cashew Chicken, Sweet & Sour Pork, etc.) The fried rice dishes, the sauteed wide rice noodles (Ho Fun) and fried Mei Fun (thin rice noodles) are all tasty. Good sized portions for $5.25 to $6.50 depending upon your selection. I've had the roast duck and the beef stew (aka. braised beef brisket) and they are also reliable favorites. We come here for a visit each time we come to Reno (after getting gas at Costco up the street) and the food is consistently good. Service on styro with plasticware combined with the bright fabric covered ceiling tiles and kitschy baby pictures makes it fun. If you are looking to get a filling, tasty meal to make up for all your losses at the gaming tables the Hong Kong Diner is a real winner!

The mussels were plumb, tender and cooked perfectly. Charbroiled oysters - they were charbroiled in a cast iron skillet that had 6 mini cups to hold the oysters. This is where is gets bad: Entrees: Wood oven grilled crusted Drum - the breading/stuffing that came on top of the fish was waaaay too salty. I just scraped it off and squeezed tons of lemon on it. The dish came with string beans, pecans, potatoes and bacon...I killed that part of the dish! Duck - it was tender and juicy, but the fat could have been rendered off a little bit more. My gf liked it, so that's a plus. My sis ordered the Drum as I did and she liked it and was okay with the breading on top of the fish. My other two gfs ordered the Gumbo with Ham Hock and Sausage. They said that there was no ham hock to be found and the gumbo was waaay too salty. One gf ordered a side of the roasted potatoes and OMG.....the potatoes were parbroiled in salted water that was waaaaaay too salty. I think the kitchen accidentally messed that up bc they should not serve something soooo salty.... Dessert: We were so disappointed with our entrees that we just opted for something that cannot be screwed up - we ordered the creme brulee trio. It was a vanilla creme brulee, coconut, and coffee. Dessert came out looking gorgeous and tasted delicious. You know, I would like to give this place another chance, but there are so many other restaurants nearby that have the same so-called reputation.....that I just would not go back......sorry Emeril!!

text: We just recently celebrated the 1st birthday of our baby daughter at the Oystercatchers Restaurant. I decided to pick this location for the event as it happens to be just 9 minutes from our residence. it happens to be one of my favourite places for really good sea food especially for their crab cakes and it was my default choice. The Oystercatchers Restaurant branch is very conveniently located for just anyone to reach and is much easier to go to.Booking was easy and hassle free. Just a phone call couple of days prior to the big day had been enough. We were all together nine of us and they had arranged a table and seating accordingly. I really liked that knowing that it was a birthday celebration they had reserved for us the raised sitting area with comfy seats and decorative lightings and nice paintings on the wall which make the videos and photos extra special. All of our guests arrived on time as they had no difficulty locating the place. Everything was nice the wood chairs, the glossy floor and the neatly attired ever present attendants. Even though we had not made any special requests it was really nice that the staff played the birthday song when I had my daughter cut the cake and that made her the special person for the evening. The restaurant was quite full even though it was not a weekend which I felt was a good sign and also it added to the event. After the candle was blown and the cake was cut and everyone had their slices, the attendants were quick to get us a container to pack the remaining cake to take home. And all this without even making a request and it really made us feel pampered and special. Overall the service was excellent, the glasses were always filled up with chilled water without ever asking for and the meat dishes were to die for and that pretty much makes up for the not so great vegetarian dishes.I highly recommend the Oystercatchers Restaurant to anyone who would like to enjoy a wonderful seafood at a convenient location without having to pay a lot.

It's sugar coated magic with a side of alcohol. We've never strayed from our cheese fondue selection - I mean how can you turn your back on cheese fondue with beer in it? We'll be friends forever Cheddar Cheese Fondue - cross my heart. Salad. I prefer the California Salad EVERYTIME but my fiance switches it up every chance she gets. This past week she chose the Caprese special. I wasn't a fan of their vinegar so i'm glad I stuck to my classic selection. For the entree we typically go with the Signature Selection but we had my fiance's sister with us this time, who prefers chicken to beef or pork so we decided to see if we could entice her into trying something new so we strayed from our norm and got the Pacific Rim entree selection. Not our wisest choice to date. The potstickers are def best left to an asian bistro and not The Melting Pot. The duck was excellent but HEAVILY coated in pepper and needed to be scraped off before cooking and enjoying it. As always, the teriyaki sirloin was the best of the selection, but the pork tenderloin was a strong contender. As for dessert - i'm not a big fan of chocolate. I know... *gasp*. That said, I enjoy eating the "dipper" selection without the dip. My favorite has to be the marshmallows rolled in graham cracker. Superb. As for the dip - I'm a Bailey's fan, so when opting for a desert fondue I usually con my fiance into the milk chocolate with Baileys. I dip 3 or 4 items and then she eats the rest! Eventually she may try something else... in the meantime, i'll be the one in the corner hogging all the graham cracker marshmallows.

I also asked about ventilation given the humidity. I was reassured that they do this all the time and that I had nothing to worry about with regard to rain or ventilation. text: This place is a real mixed bag. I'm looking at it only as a cinema venue, not a convert venue. First of all, it has no permanent seating. That's fine for lots of what they do there, but for a movie or a "sit down" concert, it sucks. They use ordinary padded folding chairs on a sloped concrete floor that end up making your butt and back really HURT because they are tilted forward, not level. Solving that challenge is going to be huge. I went to a movie there - "Mine with the Iron Door" (or some similar title). It was filmed in the 1920s in 4x3 aspect ratio, but the projectionist showed it as 16x9 on the theater's 16x9 widescreen screen. As a result, a significant portion of the top and bottom of the film was on the masking of the screen. How amateur is that?! And we paid $20 for the admission but were given a $3 bargain matinee show. The projection was bright and well focused and well done in that respect. Then there was the alert window that popped up on the screen in the middle of the movie because they were playing it into the digital projector from a MAC laptop, not a DVD player. Never show a movie from a laptop that is "live" to the internet or a wifi hotspot. Things like that are going to happen, for sure. Professional cinema presentation requires extreme attention to the details. The Rialto staff fell on their sword this time. I love downtown Tucson and the Rialto and the Fox entertainment bookends. But for now, my vote for cinema goes to the Fox. They've got their act together for showing movies. Maybe the Rialto should stick to rock concerts and leave cinema to the Fox.

text: I haven't had Papa John's piss-poor excuse for pizza since 2003 but I would rather be force-fed that garbage than ever again eat the soggy, sad nonsense Pie-Face Pizza Co. has the audacity to serve. I ordered a small (which is also their medium) pepperoni for delivery and it came to $18. Under the impression Pie-Face is striving to make gourmet pizza, and knowing better ingredients often cost more, price didn't bother me. It wasn't until I opened the box and saw the flat, tepid, greasy disc of disappointment that I became livid. Perhaps I'd be more understanding if the driver had to travel twenty minutes to bring me the pizza but I literally live a minute away; there's no defense. Then I thought, what if I was some poor college student, strapped for cash but still wanting to support local? How cheated and angry would I feel when this overpriced circle of suck arrived at my door? According to Pie-Face's Facebook page (their website doesn't work), they claim to "uphold the principles of incredible pizza." They don't. Not even a little bit. If they're trying to do "Brooklyn" style, Brooklyn would be appalled. In comparison, however, they do make Domino's seem like it is crafted by the hand of God himself. Maybe Pie-Face will be able to survive on hungry, late-night drunks who don't care about taste or quality, but if you want thin crust pizza and you're lucid, do yourself a favor and walk across the street to Imperial Bar + Lounge. They know how to make edible things there.
