text: Well, it seems much has changed at this Bella Vista gastropub since my glowing 4 star review of The Wishing Well 6 months ago. And not for the better. What does the Wishing Well intend to be, because I can't figure it out. Upon return visits, their cuisine has been wildly inconsistent in both offerings and even within the same item. Specifically, the Shame burger. Apparently, The Wishing Well has started a food challenge. It involves eating two full Shame burgers(see my original review for details on this), two orders of fries and two beers in 45 minutes. I was there the nite this glutinous endeavour was first attempted. It was really fun and interesting. Since I loved the Shame Burger so much the first time I got it, I ordered another one to eat alongside the eager competitors. The burger I got resembled nothing of the one I got my first visit or, for that matter, the burgers that were served for the challenge. There was only one patty, and it was a pathetic imitation of the delicious burger which I (embarrassingly) called the best in the city previously. The service barely acknowledged my fiance and I, far more interested in taping and documenting the in-progress challenge. I ordered a beer which sat waiting to be delivered to me for (literally) 10 minutes. When i sent it back, the waitress snarled. it was the most reaction my fiance and I got all nite. This experience is only one example of an inconsistent and unreliable menu. Twice, I have looked at the menu online before going and seen "New and Improved Menu." Looked it over. Got excited! Went in and... Different menu. Different beers. "Sorry, we dont have that tonight." "Sorry, we haven't updated the website." How difficult is it to updated a website? Think about it: This place has changed its menu 2 or 3 times in less than a year. Changes have been stewed over, considered and ultimately decided. Menus were printed, then laminated. Yet the most simple part, updating the site for diners, has been ignored. Both the menu and beer list are consistently wrong. What a SHAME...

text: A few years ago my girlfriend asked if I wanted to join her for an authentic Italian meal. I thought we were heading to a restaurant but she brought me to the local Italian community hall. I recall surprisingly well what we ate: salad, meat and cheese, fresh pasta, veal parmesan, chicken, prime rib, deep fried frittata stuffed with spinach, mushroom and cheese and puffed pastries filled with fresh cream. We hobbled out of there, patting our bellies. The food was fantastic, but one of my favourite parts of the brunch was that we dined with people we didn't know. Gino and his wife shared our table, and it was such a lovely way to connect with a community that has such a strong pulse - and penchant for divine cooking. Forget Sorrentino's or Italian Pasta Kitchen - this is the best home-cooked Italian food in the city. Everyone needs a friend named Gino whose mama makes a mean plate of pasta!

text: check another one off the list!! A friend and I went to miro district for dinner last night and had a lovely meal! the service was great, and our waiter was accommodating and helpful with suggestions. i had E. My friend got the crabmeat beignets which were fluffy and the right amount of sweet (not too much) to go with a savory beignet... we both felt a little cheated like we were getting an airy crabcake. the flavor was good though. the bread basket included tiny corn muffins, biscuits with dots of orange jam (i think), and slices of baguette. i chose the salmon with pistou, red potatoes, spring peas, and chervil. it very good and interestingly paired well with my wine.... it was a little salty, but cooked well, and the plate was warm which i love. My friend again seared his tongue on the chicken pot pie right out of the oven (the beignets had come right out of the fryer! haha), but after a few minutes we both were able to appreciate the homey chicken and dumplings flavor. we agreed it was on the light side for a pot pie, more brothy and not overwhelmingly rich or creamy. he got a glass of Coppola's Director's Cut Zinfandel which was much richer than my glass but perfect for dessert. all of the desserts sounded good to me, so to go along with the rest of our meal i chose the most southern, Apple Pan Dowdy a la mode. YUM!! it was like a baby apple pie, complete with a small lattice crust that was crunchy and flaky. they know how to make all different kinds of great dough here! the apples were warm but not mushy, and the vanilla ice cream was in the perfect amount and high quality. i would love to come back as i enjoyed the food and the atmosphere, the bar area looks cool with a lot of outside light and black and white checked tile floor. i want to try the pork chop with ginger, thyme, sweet potatoes and spring veggies, the steak frites (smelled like wonderful steak grilling when we walked in!) and the chicken adelicia with fontina and tomato chutney aioli. and of course i want to try all the desserts. :) particularly the chocolate sheba, described by our waiter as a fudgy thing with dried fruit and nuts.

text: Very very disappointed! I feel like there had to be something off on the night my friend and I went (Sunday) because most of the recent reviews were awesome and our experience was just terrible. So we sat down and were given menus and told the specials. We actually thought that the $20 (or $25 on Sunday) price fixe was just on Tuesdays, so when our server told us that they had a "neighborhood appreciation special" ($25 for 3 courses) we were impressed. The thing our server forgot to mention was that the portion sizes would be at least half of the normal size. My friend and I had no problem splitting a salad and getting our own entrees, but under the guise of this appreciation thing, we thought you would be getting the same food (or at least something similar). The salads were really good- mixed bibb lettuce with bacon and tomato in a buttermilk dressing. And really big! When we were brought our entrees, we thought it was a joke. I ordered the bass, and I eat a lot of fish so I know what it is supposed to look like. Bass is a meaty, thick white flaky fish. The thing that came out on the plate looked like a piece of scrap they give you at the fish store to cook with your food and give to the dog. It was so tiny and thin that you literally had to scrape the fish off the skin so you wouldnt eat the skin. To top it all off, the portion was two small bites and it was under seasoned and borderline overcooked. The side dish, kind of like a vegetable hash with corn and asparagus, was bigger than the fish itself- really sad. Also, compared to the salad it was really inconsistent. My friend's chicken dish was fine, but it was one really thin chicken cutlet served with a side of romaine salad and one fingerling potato chopped into four tiny rounds. Thats it. One baby potato. Those things are tiny. The chicken was so thin that it was also undercooked. I mentioned to the server that I didn't like my dish and she suggested I try the cod. I tried it and it was slightly thicker than the bass, but once again the plate was covered in leaves and garnishes. The summer rolls didn't have an assortment of vegetables, just lots of lettuce and tiny pieces of pineapple. There were also mounds of microgreens all over the plate. The poor little piece of fish got lost in all of those leaves. We decided to stick around for dessert since it was part of the meal. The cheesecake was disgusting. The pan they cooked it in was too wide for the amount of filling they put in it and it probably immediately fell when it started to cool and was thin, but thick dense and really eggy. I guess the server felt bad for my friend who was clearly still hungry so she brought out this HUGE strawberry rhubarb "cobbler" for her. It must have been four to five cups of the stuff in this huge ramekin, and sprinkled with crumbled oats, not cobbler. It was ridiculous and kinda sickening after such little food for the entree. I am so disappointed with Paul and can't believe that this is how they do business. I don't think that it's right at all to cut down portions and quality as much as they do and call it "neighborhood appreciation." Even if they had doubled or tripled the portion of meat they served it still wouldn't be of the same cut and quality as other BYOB's such as Fond. I prefer to eat at places like Paul instead of patronizing Stephen Starr restaurants on a regular basis, but the inconsistency and outrageous price will make me re-think ever returning here.

text: Husband, Toddler, and I stopped in here yesterday for a treat, and unfortunately we fall into the ranks of Yelpers that find this place vastly overrated. I was immediately turned off by the smell of the place...it didn't smell like heavenly baked goods--more like burnt sugar. The atmosphere is pretty fancy for a bakery, which I guess is supposed to help justify the prices you are about to pay for cupcakes. Toddler was VERY excited to pick out her cupcake, a process made even more lengthy by the fact that they kept pulling trays out of the display to fill a large order in back. Not a huge deal, but something that made me feel like they don't much care about the customers in-store...I think they probably make most of their money on outside orders, which would explain a lot of the problems previous reviewers have had with the customer service. But this would all have been forgiven if the cupcakes had been good. I had the Dark Night, Husband had the Red Velvet, and Toddler had the "Bugs in Mud." Three very different cupcakes, and yet somehow they all managed to taste the same. The Dark Night had little chocolate flavor, and certainly not the deep, rich flavor of dark chocolate. The red velvet had no cocoa flavor. The "Bugs in Mud" was a white cupcake, so of the three, it tasted like it should--that is, bland. Like Justin says below, if you are going to do just one thing, it should be done extremely well. I was left feeling that I could easily make far superior cupcakes at home for a fraction of the price. Or, for that matter, I could go buy a dozen doughnuts for the price of three cupcakes at Batch.

text: Tortilla Press NEVER disappoints me! The staff is friendly and very helpful (we hosted a party there and they went above and beyond). The food is fresh, tasty and unique. I've been there for brunch and dinner as well as for a birthday party. They are willing to work with your budget on their menu for parties and as I said the staff is fantastic. Brunch - I've been 3x for their Early Bird brunch and it is a serious value for what you get. $6.00 before noon on Saturday or Sunday and you get a smaller menu that packs a flavorful punch. I've had the Cheese Chilequiles as well as the Quiche of the Day and they are amazing. You can add on things like fresh squeeze orange juice, chorizo coins, chorizo hash if your meal doesn't come with it for an additional cost, but it is really not necessary as the portion sizes are generous and when you sit down they bring you a basket of cinnamon/sugar tortillas with their signature sweet yogurt honey dip. DELICIOUS!!! Dinner - I've been there twice for dinner. My own meals ordered were the coconut habanero shrimp - great flavor, not TOO spicy, but just enough to compliment the creamy coconut sauce. The mashed potatoes and sauteed veggies that came with it were good too. I've also had the Pork Enmoladas and WOW was this flavorful. The portion is huge, and everything complimented each other very well. I'd never had a mole sauce before and it was a very nice first experience. I've also tasted the smothered shrimp and scallops burrito (HUGE and very good) and the carne ranchero and rainbow shrimp (tender steak, and the shrimp had a great flavor). Tortilla Press is located in the dry town of Collingswood, so it is BYO. We ordered delicious virgin mango margaritas and added tequila at the table. I would recommend dining here any time.

text: Oh Dive Bar, how I love thee. With your disheveled looks and your old man-who-smokes-too-much smell you're hard for me to dislike. You're like the neighborhood hooker that everyone knows a little too well. You wave your cheap drink about in such a tempting fashion and I do drink them while perched on a barstool checking out the regulars and not-so-regulars. You sashayed in front of me with your dangling Dive Bar sign and drew me in for life (or as long as I'm in Philly). Oh Dive Bar, how I love thee. Seriously folks... The bar: It's one of the few bars in Philly where a smoker can light up and have a stiff, quickly poured drink by a really, really, reeeeeaaally happy bartender. If you're not a smoker, be ware, yes there is a wall of smoke. If you complain about the smoke, know you're probably out numbered. The drinks: Ssssssssssstiff and poured with a smile and quickly too! Magically quickly. Priced fairly too. That's always a good thing. The crowd: I see some people here have described the crowd as hipsters. Far from it. The regulars mostly live in the neighborhood. It's the place they go when they're sick of staring at their own walls and maybe, just maybe they'll run into someone they know for a good conversation. The people I've met there are everything from artists to IT guys, those who no one is really sure what they do to make money to nurses. People from jeans and t-shirts to polo shirts and khakis. Middle class hipsters? I think not. Some are poor, some are rich, some are middle class but hipsters? Not so much. They just *like* the bar because it's not some pretentious, overpriced, meat market. It's a dump with some OK folks and a few douchoise as patrons but hey, that's any neighborhood bar. All in all, I like this place and will keep going back as long as it's there.

text: So not impressed by this supposed "Best Of Philly" perennial. My first attempt at trying Shank's was shortly after it opened in this new location on 15th St. I happen to work on 15th Street and not too far from Shank's...combining that with the fact that a coworker of mine does nothing but rave about the place saying it's his favorite (of it's kind) in the city, I was admittedly looking forward to trying it out for myself. So, one morning after getting settled in at work, a different coworker of mine and I went to get ourselves some breakfast sandwiches there (again, at the recommendation of the first coworker I mentioned). It was only shortly after 10 in the morning and we got there to the door and the place was closed! Sign said that they open at 11! So much for getting that breakfast sandwich! I love me some breakfast sandwiches so naturally I was a bit upset at this predicament. BUT, I chocked it up to them having just opened and that they hadn't necessarily gotten their feet on the ground just yet. So this review isn't (wholly) based on that one experience. However, it IS based on the experience I had today. I went there for lunch (again with the same coworker who tagged along for breakfast) today and was immediately dismayed once my order left my lips... "I'll have a turkey & Swiss hoagie, please." The girl's reply?... "We don't have swiss." STRIKE 1! I'm sorry, but if you're a place that's known for it's sandwiches and hoagies and such, you should at least carry a variety of meats and cheese that includes but is not limited to the combination of turkey and Swiss. I mean seriously, Swiss cheese is one of the most popular cheese in the world! Get with the program! ME: "Uh...ok, provolone?" The girl nods, and I continue... "Mayo, lettuce, tomato, onions...pickles, sweet peppers and a little bit of oil and vinegar." Then I pay and I wait. Now, it was after 1pm, so the lunch rush in Center City is starting to die down a bit and it really wasn't too packed in Shank's...but my friend and I waited quite a while. Orders taken after ours were served before ours...that's never cool. I finally get mine and wait around even longer for my friend and his cheesesteak (that he ordered before me, actually). We get back to our workplace and I unroll the poorly wrapped hoagie and discover the following... 1. it's not cut. ok, whatever...not TOO big a deal. 2. no pickles. again, disappointing, but whatever... 3. i asked for a "little" oil & vinegar... i got a ShamWow's worth of oil & vinegar...which does nothing but drip and pool on to my desk at work and just make things messy. 4. the "sweet peppers" are nothing more than HUGE chunks of soggy green bell peppers...THAT HAD ABSOLUTELY NO FLAVOR TO THEM! not sweet, not sour, not spicy, NOT GOOD! I ended up taking them off the hoagie altogether. This just does not make for a good hoagie experience whatsoever. It's like my sandwich was made by a blind person with cerebral palsy. Luckily, the turkey and cheese were fine, as well as the roll. Other than that? Horrible. Even my coworker complained about his cheesesteak...which isn't something you wanna complain about in PHILADELPHIA of all places. But, live and learn I suppose. I'm tempted to never go there again and if I hadn't witnessed them making some of those chicken cutlet sandwiches...I wouldn't. But those did look pretty tasty, so maybe sometime down the road, I'll hop in again and order one of those. Though I'll never get a hoagie or cheesesteak there for as long as I live.

text: Ommmmmm..... Tucson Yoga was voted the best yoga place in Tucson for the year of 2005-2006. I will start off with that simple comment. I'm new to yoga and found this place roaming through the Internet trying find ways to make my stalky body leaner. My first priority was to find something CHEAP! And for only $5 a class, I think this place constitutes. Because I am not familiar with yoga, styles of yoga, yoga etiquette, I will simply give you a synopsis of my first visit: 1) Its a downtown location that is hard to find if you use the directions given on their website. I drove around downtown, 4th avenue and through the UA campus about 2-3 times before I decided to use my inherent body compass to find it. Yes, it was a Monty Python/Benny Hill comedic event if anyone was there to witness. 2) Please get there ahead of time as suggested. The classes fill up quickly (I think its about a max capacity of 40) . Because it took me forever to find the place, I stumbled in there late and as I reached into my purse to pull out my $5, all of my pennies fell onto the cement floor disturbing all of the peaceful yoga masters during their warm up. 3) Mats and blankets are provided, which is a plus for those who are new to yoga and are not sure if they want to invest in their own mat. 4) I found a place in the corner, next to a wall, so I would successfully bump my head into it every once in awhile during the learning of poses. (Don't get a spot next to the side wall across from the bathroom !). 5) Wear clothes that are comfortable, but won't expose your cha cha's and mid-drift because you get to do some nifty little acrobat stunts at times. 6) Expect to be in pain the next day, if you're doing everything right. At the end of the day I was really satisfied with my yoga experience. For a lab rat like myself, this was a good 2 hour work out which uses your own body as resistance in toning and using those unused muscles. Unlike many other workouts I've done, this was the most complete. I felt all of my muscles being used (feet, buttocks, hamstrings, arms, delts, pects, etc.). I couldn't move the next 3 days. The instructors are really friendly and passionate about their craft,. However, there's this one that isn't so friendly. Well, lets say she's friendly to everyone else, but not to me. She comes across frigid and lacking warmth BUT I enjoy her class the most. WARNING, this next comment is going to be a hippie/psychedelic moment.: she brings all of her internal beauty into her instruction, her chanting, and musical skills. The other instructors are also good as they have been on Oprah show or teach at Canyon Ranch, etc. Guys, if you attend any class you will find yourself with other men, but a majority of the class is composed of ladies who don't believe in shaving. There is always those 4 or 5 hot chicks in the class, but they will not date you. People of all sizes and abilities attend these classes and no one feels inferior, intimidated or uncomfortable. After one session my posture greatly improved and my back was elongated giving that catwalk stance. After a few sessions my boyfriend told me I looked like I was losing weight. (that's the power of secretly feeding your boyfriend barbiturates because yoga doesn't make you lose weight unless you combine it with something else, but it does improve your posture making the weight appear to be redistributed). What I rave about yoga is that after a session with the school marm instructor (she just comes across cold to me, but very attractive, and I think my aura sends her off or something because people always usually run to me, not away from me) is that you feel really at peace and at ease. I don't do drugs (never have, never will) but its a strange drug induced effect you experience. Your legs are wobbly, you're in another dimension of time and space, its like you're numb to everything that was bothering you before you came. If I can get that mood altering experience after every workout without having to run 5-10 miles, I think its worth it.
label: POS

text: If you are looking for where the locals go, this is one of the places. The atmosphere is comfortable but not fancy. Although better lit than a bar it has kind of a bar feel to it. The service will make you feel like a non-local at first but if you are friendly to them they warm up quickly. And once they do, you will get great service. The food is very, very good and is made to order. What does that mean, you might ask...it means that they make EVERYTHING fresh for your plate. They don't have any food sitting around waiting to be thrown on a plate. This means that if you get potatos with your meal they are cut up and cooked right then, not pulled from a batch made earlier. You will need to keep this in mind if you try to go in for breakfast on Sat or Sun since it can often times takes quite a while to get your meal. Normally that would keep me from going back but the food is so good we either tolerate it or try to hit them for one of our non-weekend mornings like Friday or Monday. Other than not having pancakes their breakfast menu is pretty broad and the portions are hearty. There are definitely more than just egg or omelet combos, as mentioned by another reviewer. Heck, you can get bisquets & gravy (some of the best I have ever had), chicken fried steak, pork chops, etc. If you are in Reno for breakfast do yourself a favour and hit up Big Ed's! It beats the crap out of the hotel buffets (and I am a huge buffet fan).

text: First I am basing my review on two things, the customer service and the quality of the repair. I would give the customer service, Aaron, big marks. He is friendly, he is very knowledgeable and he was extremely helpful. The only mark against Aaron was that he never called me back when he said he would, but its a busy shop and hes probably busy so I can forgive that. I would give Aaron 4 out of 5 stars. The Repair, however was really bad. I brought my 62 Ranchero in with a transmission needing an overhaul. They reassured me that the guy who fixed them was an expert with older cars. The first thing I noticed when I crawled under the car is that they didnt even clean the transmission when it was out! Thats just amature night if you ask me. You always clean parts when you take them out and you know they are going back in. When they dropped the transmission, the engine block itself, was jerked (or possibly it was loosened to get the tranny out) however the "expert" did not bother to disconnect any wires to the engine. This resulted in damaging my original wiring harness. The wires to my oil pressure sensor and my temperature gauge were damaged. The "expert" also installed an after market transmission cooler. First the the cooler was put in a temorary location. However instead of tapping a few holes in the frame they welded nuts over drilled holes (hardly temporary). The cooler was mounted a mere 6 inches from the ground (may as well be dragging on the ground) THe cooler was also mounte point from side to side and not Front to back as the instructions say. Speaking of my instructions for the cooler, I never got those back, but its not like he used them. Because the instruction said to use AN fittings. Instead he used bung fittings and they werent even NEW bung fittings they were old used bung fittings that leaked. My car left the shop leaking. not a little leak, a major leak. and since I was not there to pick it up (it was towed) the tow truck driver noted a huge puddle on his flat bed truck after only an hour tow. This car was not driven after the work was completed. It may have been turned over, but It wasnt drive. The mistakes in the job were easy to spot and easily fixable, and if it had been driven they would have been found. I paid 2400 for this job that is still costing me money. Just because a place claims to be an expert on transmissions, doesnt mean they are. Avoid this place like a rash. 4 stars for Aaron, 0 stars for the work = 1 star

text: Excellent location is pretty much where my 5-star rating would end. I was happy about trying this one, since it's older and therefore has more interesting architecture and much more wide open space inside the restaurant. Sadly, the booth fabrics are torn, there are major quantities of crumbs between the booth cushions, and dust all over the back shelves of the booths. The food arrived lukewarm with that "glaze" over it like it had been sitting far too long before being delivered. The gas lamps on the exterior, as well as the fireplace, were all off, and on a very cold, rainy night. The experience makes me want to try one of my local locations for comparison's sake, but basically management needs to do a thorough cleaning and retrain the servers and cooks on better QC.

text: I've been a member at the Brandon location shortly after they opened. The facility was superb at that time as are most gyms when at the start. Right now though the location is starting to get pretty rough. The carpeting through the place is becoming so stained I am not sure why they didn't use more of the rubberized surface for all of downstairs and not just the free weight area. If you are an early morning workout fan (like myself) the place often smells terrible (remember the last time you left your old gym clothes in your bag for a few days??) and it even by 8 am the funk is still lingering. The men's locker room suffers from the same maladies, as well as ceiling tiles missing due to what looks like roof leaks or condensation issues w/ the HVAC system. The shower area suffers from blown lights and cheap light fixtures that are rusting very badly. I've also experienced some security issues w/ a locker break in and car burglary in their lot as well. This place has plenty of life in it if the management would address these glaring problems that make working out here worth less than what I am paying per month in fees. I am now eyeballing the new gym down by Channelside if they can't get their act together.

The food was oustanding, including the pâté board, onion soup, hanger steak, and pomme frites. The reason the fries are so rich and buttery is because they are fried in beef lard and canola oil. They may not be good for your heart, but they will make your taste buds sing!

text: Ended up here for one night as a result of a last minute Hotwire reservation, in advance of moving into our new apartment the following day. I'm surprised to read all the negative reviews, as I had a great experience, starting with the Hotwire rate that was less than a quarter of the regular nightly rate. Our room had two double beds and was very clean, as was the bathroom which looked new and just plain gorgeous. We didn't eat or park there, so I can't comment on those, but $20 for overnight parking in this part of town is actually very reasonable. The staff were quite friendly, and did their best to help us find a cab that would accommodate our oversized luggage. I am floored that anyone would complain about there being no airport shuttle, when this hotel is nowhere near the airport. My only real complaint is that there was no hair conditioner in the bathroom. As for the location, it's safe and vibrant, with many restaurants and bars a short walk away. I probably wouldn't recommend it at their regular prices, but if you can get a bargain then by all means.
label: POS

text: This has been one of my local favorites for around 13 years. Away grom the more boisterous parts of the FQ, it has been consistently good food, fast service and friendly staff. Prices stay within reason compared to other Italian restaurants. I am glad they finally got their liquor license, but miss the days of bringing in your own bottle. Wine by the glass is nice and keeps your bill down. On weekends I'd advise getting there a little before dinner hour, as the line can get long and there's no waiting area. Low-lit and good for a romantic local night out. Delivery is nice too! Oh, couldn't forget the neato collection of paintings of Mona Lisa and your opportunity to draw your own, right on the table with crayons provided!

text: The walk up and drive up were scarier then the actual haunted tour. text: Had I written this review immediately after our wedding over Memorial Day weekend, it may have contained expletives that perhaps I would have regretted. Having had a month to gain some calm, I still feel like I need to put my two cents on Hotel Palomar Philadelphia out there, for what it is worth. As I said, we married at the end of May (yippee!). In preparation for said bring-em-all-to-Philly fest, we contacted HPP around January 2010, at which time they offered us a group discount that was reasonable and competitive (about 20% less than the rack rate at the time) with those rates found elsewhere. We were satisfied.. flash forward to end of March, April when rates both on discount websites AND the kimptonhotel.com/ HPP website itself were markedly lower than those previously offered to us. I contacted the staff person assigned to our event, asking her if it was possible to adjust the rates that we were offering to our guests to just MATCH those now offered. She essentially said "no" and sent me an attached screen shot of a kayak.com search that she had done "proving" to me that I was wrong (when, in fact, it was not the case). I was infuriated with her condescension-through-a-grin (that makes one just want to climb out of one's skin) attitude and, only when I responded that, fine, I was going to have our guests cancel their reservations under our wedding block and book them on their own via the internet did she concede and say that they could change the rate, it made me doubly filled with distaste that she could have made the change all along but willingly chose not to do it. On hearing my story, my bridesmaid, in solidarity said, f@$! em, let's stay somewhere else (there are, in fact, so many great hotels in Philadelphia), but I was swayed by my curiosity and appreciation for the Kimpton aesthetic (some of which is really great design and some a bit overkill and doesn't know when to stop) to stick with it. Other pluses of our stay did include the daily wine reception and coffee/tea/lemonade offerings throughout the day. Our friends hung out in the restaurant/ bar post-wedding and loved the food. But, all in all, in thinking it over, our otherwise extraordinary weekend full of love, family, and friends was marred only by goings-on that I had with HPP. My story above along with other mishaps along the way and lackluster to completely unprofessional behavior from the staff (front desk in particular, valet staff were way cool) make me apprehensive at best to ever set foot in Hotel Palomar Philadelphia again. In good news, we did give our feedback to management who has acted with utter professionalism in efforts to rectify the situation(s). Maybe HPP is great for individual or family travel, but in our experience of using them for our wedding, it did not succeed. As an aside, we also worked with the Crowne Plaza Downtown Philadelphia on 18th and Market in order to offer our guests a range of price points. Their staff was OUTSTANDING-- from helping us set up our trolley transportation to the wedding site to distributing our welcome bags to guests with enthusiasm and at no charge (HPP wanted to charge an extra fee to hand them over when guests checked in) to alerting one of our guests when he left something behind in his room and holding it for him with security after he had checked out! We wholeheartedly endorse the Crowne Plaza for any group/ wedding. It was a pleasant and unexpected surprise that the more "modest" hotel had far superior client services than the supposedly higher end establishment. OK, I said my piece, good luck.
label: NEG

text: Brutal food. Went on the recommendation of a local who said its popular with the young professionals. I forgot to put on my normal "average people have no taste buds" filter, and got suckered into NOLA. The short version is: "Cheesecake factory with a New Orleans twist, but worse execution". This is southern food like PF Changs is Chinese food. Shrimp and grits were the most disappointing version I've ever had. I've spent the majority of my life in the South and these grits SUCKED. The grits were really sweet and mushy. too smooth (more like mashed potatoes in texture). There were also barely any grits. The shrimp preparation was terrible -- they were pan sauteed then tossed in a sweet BBQ sauce (KC masterpiece flavor). It was topped with limp bacon pieces, and didn't have any gravy aside from the BBQ sauce. Basically it wasn't "Shrimp and grits". Sausage and Chicken gumbo was terrible. Like most mass produced food, it lacked subtlety and was way overseasoned. It didn't have any body and we were just eating salt gravy with dry chicken bits. The stuff to rice ratio was off. I thought if there was ONE thing we'd get right at Emeril's restaurant in the FQ, it'd be gumbo but we were disappointed. Smoked duck was smokey, but very dry. Portion size was way too big (not a complaint, just another indicator that the restaurant is run by a clueless kitchen). Came out at room temperature and the skin was limp and the texture was terible. Points for smokey flavor, but nothing else. Fried chicken was AWFUL. Popeyes is better and 1/10the price. The crust was soggy and steamed, not properly coated, and the falling off. The chicken breast was inedibly dry and the entire thing was underseasoned. Another note on Southern food failure from this subpar establishment. Stuffed chicken wings (appetizer) -- amusing. Basically chinese egg roll stuffing in a chicken wing. The stuffing was overseasoned (surprise!). Basically it was breading and white pepper. The chicken was fried much better than the fried chicken though. Crabcake -- very delicious if you like eating breadcrumbs and eggs. Garbage if you want crab in your crabcake. All my stars on Yelp are strictly food reviews. 1 star food (literally, rather have Burger King for the same price), and it was stupidly expensive to boot (29 bucks for crappy shrimp and grits!). Waitstaff was very friendly and give them 4 stars for effort. I go to dining establishments to eat, not to socialize with waitstaff though, so that doesn't save the review.

When we finished our meal and received our grossly overpriced bill, I asked Scott Clayton to comp us the two pitchers of sangria that we consumed while waiting for the table for an hour and a half. One time I walked in at lunch time, and they weren't that busy. Plus, it was the buffet, so everyone was getting their food themselves anyway! They maybe had 4-5 tables with people at them. It was relatively quiet, and slow. The sign "wait to be seated" was at the front, so I waited. And waited. I probably waited at least 10 minutes before they even acknowledged that I had stepped into the building. And they DID see me, they just chose not to greet me, or acknowledge me. When I finally was seated, the server was very rude, and barely spoke. He brought the whole pitcher of water to my table, so as not to have to refill my glass himself. He never came to check on me during my meal, he came only once to take my plate, and even then he didn't speak, even when I said "thank you." When he dropped off the check, again, no "thank you", nothing. Only silence. I went to pay my check and received the same cold, rude service at the front desk. The next couple of times we went back, we had friends from out of town. We are all avid lovers of Indian food. On any of these times, we never had more than 4 people in our party, so it's not like we had an insane amount of people for them to wait on. Also, myself and my friends are not people that are hard to wait on anyway. Once we went for buffet, and the other time for dinner. Both times were NOT close to closing time. Our server once again was not polite, and they acted like they were doing us a big favor by waiting on us. Anytime we asked them for anything, they acted like it was a big deal. Then, they dropped off the ticket WAY early, like we hadn't even been there 30 minutes, and they kept coming over and asking us if we wanted anything off of the buffet...that they were closing it in 10 minutes. We politely said no thank you, and that we wouldn't be making any more trips to the buffet. A few minutes later, they said again that they were closing the buffet in 5 minutes. Again, we said no thank you. By this time, we felt REALLY rushed, and they weren't being polite at all. Not even 2 minutes later, they came over and said "do you want anything else, we're closing the buffet in 2 minutes." That's a bit much in my opinion. We were fed up at that point, and paid our check and left. Again, they never thanked us or anything. My most recent bad experience happened tonight. I've started noticing their ad in the newspapers around town advertising that they now deliver around the area. So...I thought I could get the food without the bad service. I called, ordered a substantial amount of food, gave them my number, name, address, and even gave them very clear directions to my house when they asked. I looked up a google map, and they are exactly 2 miles away. They said okay, and that it would be 30-45 minutes. I said thank you and okay. 10 minutes later they call...I thought maybe they were needing to ask something about the order...instead, to my shock, the man on the phone said "I'm sorry, we can't deliver there. You can come pick it up, but we're not coming there." I was quiet and surprised for a moment, and said "okay...was there a problem with the directions I gave you?" he said "No, the driver doesn't want to go there." I said "okay...is it out of your delivering radius? do you only deliver within a certain radius of your business?" and he said "Yes, if you were in West End or Green Hills..." and I said "Well, my house is only 2 miles from your location, I checked. Green Hills is just as far if not farther." He said "Well, the driver just doesn't want to go to that area." I replied "I really don't understand, it's not a bad area..." He said "No, it's not a bad area, the driver just doesn't want to go." And I said "Okay, well, I'm sorry that you're going to lose my business over this." And I hung up. That is seriously the last straw for me. I have tried, and tried, and TRIED to be kind, and overlook their past rudeness, but this is just too much. I honestly don't know how they stay in business. Unless they get new owners or management, I'm never stepping foot in there again. I've worked many serving jobs, and I know how hard it is and how you depend on your tips. So I'm a good tipper AND an easy customer. But it seems no matter how nice I am to the staff at Cuisine of India, they always treat me and my guests with either silence, or rudeness. That is unacceptable. There is no reason to be rude, especially to good customers. And now they're advertising that they deliver, but their driver just decides he doesn't want to go to a specific area for no reason? and they're okay with that? wow. If you want delivery,be prepared to be called back and turned down depending on the driver's mood.

text: What a disaster in a pretty box! As we pulled up in the torrential rain, I was excited to be getting somewhere where we could watch the football game between the wedding and the reception. I should have known something was up when there was no one directing traffic through the port-cochere and no one to help us with our bags. We finally got a somewhat covered spot, though the wind was blowing the rain under in sheets, and proceeded to unload our bags ourselves while still wearing our formal wedding gear. Fun times. So we waited in the lobby while Keith checked in, and then proceeded to one of the two elevators, and up to room 326. The set up of this hotel is not that user-friendly - the elevators are at one end, and you have to traipse all the way down the hall if you have a high-numbered room. If there were a fire, you'd literally have to go the full length of the hallway to the stairs... Anyway, we get to the room, and the keys don't work. Keith goes back to the front desk who advises him not to put it near a cellphone. Ok, while that will disable the keys, it doesn't do it that quickly. So as he's walking back with the "fixed" key, a woman is walking practically alongside him. He stops at 326 where the rest of us are waiting, and so does she. "I think this is my room," she said. Oh, really. Well, we tried Keith's key, and sure enough it worked, and sure enough, the woman's husband was inside. Thank goodness he was dressed! So Keith goes down to the front desk to get us an unoccupied room. We wait since we don't want to haul our luggage until we know where we're going. The man and woman came out a few minutes later to say that he'd gotten a call from the front desk and apologized saying that they thought they'd put them in 235 and that they would reduce the rate on the room. So we headed to 235 because sure enough, that's what they gave Keith. Jokingly, I said "make sure you knock a few times first" to Keith when we arrived at the door to 235. Well, good thing he did, because there was a guy asleep in his pajamas in this room, and he was none too thrilled that we'd awoken him. So at this rate, I'm livid, and so are the rest of us. We take all of our luggage down to the front desk and drop it in a pile in front of everyone else when Jimmy says "This is the most embarrassing hotel experience I've ever had!" Fortunately, that got their attention, so Keith could quietly say "yeah, that one was occupied, too. Is it really too much to ask for an unoccupied room?" Everyone cleared away from the desk. The Bellhop was so scared that he walked briskly away and left his cart, so I stole it for all our luggage. Finally we here "Ok, 220 was just cleaned, so I know it's open." So we head to 220. And yes it was open. And it was a decently nice room. The front desk called when we'd been there about 15 minutes to ask if the room was acceptable and to offer a $20 discount. Then they called again 10 minutes later to ask the same thing and offer the same discount. Clearly, there were communication issues at the front desk. When we took the shuttle to the country club for the reception, it got us there directly with no issues, and even a polite hello and goodbye from the driver. Best service we got from Normandy Farms all day. At the reception we learned that they wrong number of rooms for 2 members of the bridal party, so it wasn't just us. The bed ended up being quite comfortable, though I woke up stuffed up, indicating that the air was too dry or the place was moldy and activated my allergies. The brunch buffet was extensive and most of it was quite good, though the stuffed pancakes were not in fact stuffed with blueberries as advertised and were extra mushy as if uncooked in the middle. The salads were great, and I was impressed by the fresh oysters. So Normandy Farms, you get one star for comfy beds and one star for brunch. Service was atrocious. If you stay at NF so you're to Blue Bell Country Club (I can't imagine any other reason to stay), at least get the brunch so you don't leave with such a bitter taste in your mouth.

text: For those of you who don't know, Houlihan's is a medium small restaurant chain primarily concentrated in the Midwest. I used to enjoy it more than I enjoy it now. My last visit had some notable failings. This location in Fairview Heights could really use some managerial attention. The food was quite mixed. The Tuscan salad was a decent starter with lots of promise, but they failed to drain the beans fully so it was very watery. The main course was a stuffed chicken with a side of mashed potatoes. The stuffed chicken was decent with an herbed butter stuffing which was highly over-salted. If only some of that salt had made it to the potatoes which were woefully under-seasoned. Now, Midwestern chain restaurants are normally quite on top of service. However, we had one of the least professional waiters I've ever seen. She was way to casual, a bit rude, and spent most of the night seated at a booth nearby with fellow waitstaff. I used to enjoy eating here, but I think I'll take a pass from now on.
label: NEG

text: Sonobana Japanese Restaurant and Grocery is my favorite place in town to get Sushi. It is a small place but their are several booths which make it more private. Also, they have great Japanese style private rooms which you can reserve for your group or family. They have a great selection of Japanese appetizers, including fried tofu, seaweed salad, soybeans, and tempura among many other items. For the main course, I would definitely recommend their sushi. All the fish is very well prepared and extremely tasty. The Udon noodles soups are also top notch. The prices at this restaurant are really good for the quality of food you get. I would even go to say this place is a bargain. My only complaint is that sometimes the wait is very long on weekend evenings because they do a lot of carry-out business which seems to get priority over the people actually dining in the restaurant. Next door in the Japanese grocery you can pick up spices, and seaweed salad, and all kinds of stuff in strange packages. It's fun to look through the grocery after having a meal, to see all the ingredients that went into its preparation. Sonobana is the best for Sushi! I recommend getting there early, like around 5pm when they first open for dinner, that way you can skip the long wait, and get the great food.
label: POS

text: Good Mexican food, excellent picante salsa (we've actually ordered it online), but TERRIBLE service. No, let me correct that - THE WORST SERVICE THAT I'VE EVER HAD. We went to this restaurant three times in the week that we spent in Tucson. First time was great, second time was mediocre (in terms of service), third time was awful (again in service). See a pattern here? The last visit (and last we will ever make), we had to wait an hour for a table, despite multiple empty tables (???). Then the restaurant had booked a large party - we couldn't even get our drinks refilled by our server. Our food took another 45 minutes to come out (and no one ordered steak or anything like that). When we complained, the manager finally came over (about 30 minutes after we complained) and gave us 10% off the bill (gee, thanks). Not to worry, we'll be back to Tucson - but never here again!

text: Walked in last Friday night around 8 pm, no reservations, wearing shorts and a t-shirt. Hostess said she was booked inside, but we could sit at the bar or wait for a table outside to open up. We decided to eat at the bar, and boy, I'm very, very glad we did. We split the peach salad, which was served with house made ricotta, greens, and a raspberry vinaigrette reduction. It was spectacular. The ricotta and peaches were such a great combination that I went to the farmer's market on Saturday and picked up some myself. She had the bacon wrapped meatloaf, which was great! Perfectly cooked, well priced ($11!), and came with spectacular mashed potatoes. My wife was extremely pleased with this dish. I had the pompano. I couldn't resist ordering fish after hearing the raves about the chef's work with fish, and the raves were spot on. It was served blackened perfectly, atop some house made creamed corn, some kind of bread/biscuit, and with some tomato confit. Perfect all the way around. I loved this dish, and found the portion to be absolutely perfect. This is fine dining at its best, and very reasonably priced. Yays: - Great service, even at the bar - The food was outstanding. Some of the best I've had in St. Louis, and served quite nicely. - The pricing is kind of ridiculous. Our total meal, including a beer for my wife, was under $45. That's insane for fine dining. I've paid well more than $25 for a fish entree like I got here. - The portions are just right. Some might complain they're small, but I left pleasantly full from my meal, and we didn't even have dessert. - It's great to see some fine dining in this area that isn't overpriced italian. Nays: - It's a small venue. I think they should take over the rest of the block. - My pompano did take forever to come out from the kitchen. My wife had already finished her meatloaf by the time it showed up. I'm not sure if this was planned or just poor execution on a busy Friday night. I excuse it since the chef came out to let us know it would be a bit, then delivered the food himself, and THEN came back to see if it was OK.
label: POS

text: Great salad bar here! The selection is really nice, even though the salad bar looks like it is very small. Along with the usual salad bar-stuff, there's a great selection of other fun stuff like, roasted garlic cloves, roasted beets, baked salmon pieces, baked tuna, steak, roasted eggplant... really nice! Salad bar is sold by weight at $9.99/lbs. They also have premade sandwiches if you're in a rush, a sandwich counter, deli items, and an espresso bar. Fresh everything. Check it out! (I guess this place used to be a Cantwells at some point?)

text: I am a big rooter for all things East Nashvillean, as many people living in East Nashville tend to be. But I'm not delusional. Far East is just another restaurant with watered down Asian food that continues to litter the Nashville food landscape. To be totally immodest, I have eaten A LOT of Vietnamese food in my life. And, if I want Vietnamese food, I will have to continue heading to West Nashville instead of driving down the street to Far East. Now, the food isn't bad; it's just unremarkable. The food and the menu grasps for the Vietnamese flavor and taste, but doesn't quite get a hold of it. I'm not sure if it's because it doesn't know how to, or that it's catering to its diners. Regardless, as the rating goes, "meh, I've experienced better." The pho is not that great: it's too sweet, and it's expensive especially for the size of the bowl. It's a Vietnamese restaurant and not a strictly pho restaurant, so I don't penalize it for not having different types of pho. But, really, only one kind of pho?! The rest of the entrees I've tried have slight semblance to Vietnamese, but runs closer to something pan-Asian. For example, the flavor of the grilled pork (served with vermicelli noodles) was overpowering and totally missed the subtle flavors of the lemongrass and the smoked sweetness in the meat. However, I'm super glad that it's doing well and it has plenty of avid eaters there. It's always good to have a hip, hot and happening place in the hood. I just wish I could be one of them.
label: NEG

text: Yuck. We decided tonight to give it "one last try" after two previous visits with slow service and mediocre food. The service wasn't bad, but the food sunk far below our threshold of "mediocre." After starting on the clearly store bought chips and salsa, I looked past the salsa-smeared menu and ordered the combo, with refried beans clearly from a can, yellow rice mixed with canned vegetables, a deep fried flavorless recently-defrosted chicken flauta, a somewhat decent but still not fresh chicken enchilada and a "taco" - rather a cold flour tortilla stuffed with the same filling as the enchilada. I nearly forgot the dry and inedible beef tamale. I was able to eat the enchilada. My dining partner got the chicken enchiladas, and liked them less than I did. We were yet again the only people in there, and understandably so. Was anxious to tell the staff how unhappy we were, but our full plates were cleared without question. Obviously they know what they're serving.
label: NEG
